  • optimistic event-stream concurrency;
  • durable run, trial, work-item, usage, population, and experience projections;
  • stable idempotency keys and logical steps;
  • exact context bundles and experience-query results;
  • as-of search-state reconstruction;
  • explicit schema versions and migrations.

Object records are authoritative for object content. Events are authoritative for the fact that transitions occurred. Projections are disposable and rebuildable.

docs.title: Filesystem artifact store
docs.text:
.meta-evolve/
├── artifacts/sha256/...
├── runs/...
└── meta-evolve.sqlite

Identical payload bytes reuse content identity while distinct artifact occurrences retain trial, proposal, contributor, and parent lineage.

docs.title: Recovery scenario
docs.text: Terminate a deterministic run at each important transition, reconstruct a new coordinator from disk, resume from committed state, and compare it with an uninterrupted run. Closures are rejected in durable-local mode or cause an explicit capability error before execution; they never silently create a run advertised as resumable.

docs.title: Milestone 5: executable artifacts
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. Milestone 5 is complete through the M5.4 canonical clamp acceptance. The closure adds integrated assertions, an executed tour, and documentation only; it adds no production port, schema, registry, patch format, or authority claim.

M5.1 ships the first synchronous source-workspace vertical:

class WorkspaceProvider(Protocol):
    def materialize(self, artifact: object) -> Workspace: ...
    def capture(self, workspace: Workspace) -> object: ...
    def dispose(self, workspace: Workspace) -> None: ...


class ProposerRunner(Protocol):
    component: ComponentRef
    def validate_run(
        self,
        *,
        artifact_kind: str,
        artifact_representation: str,
        objectives: tuple[Objective, ...],
        budget: Budget,
        experience: ExperienceSpec | None,
    ) -> None: ...
    def execute(
        self,
        parents: tuple[Artifact, ...],
        context: ProposerContext,
    ) -> ProposalResult: ...

SourceTree uses the stable utf8-tree-v1 representation. PatchProposer accepts one exact-file command, while PatchResult carries the same evidence, usage, metadata, failure, and derivation information as an ordinary proposal. A decoded-value runner preserves the original callable path; the coordinator does not branch on either runner.

DirectoryWorkspaces copies immutable source into a fresh private directory, captures through the same source validation, and disposes before result commitment. A disposal failure is an infrastructure failure and prevents success commitment because M5.1 has no honest mixed success-plus-infrastructure-warning outcome.

M5.2 ships the synchronous SandboxProvider, immutable ProcessSpec and ProcessResult, and the clearly named DevelopmentSubprocessSandbox. The POSIX adapter enforces an absolute executable, workspace-contained normalized cwd, exact declared environment, timeout, independent raw-byte output bounds, whole-process-group termination, and lifecycle cleanup. Policy, timeout, resource, and infrastructure failures remain typed; ordinary nonzero exits are not interpreted. Narrow clock and process-operation seams make precedence and cleanup behavior deterministic under test. It makes no claim to secure arbitrary untrusted code. Add Git worktrees only as an optimization.

M5.3 ships CommandEvaluator, EvaluationEnvironment, and root-exported ProcessSpec. The evaluator is a declared local callable component and uses the existing callable-evaluator path. Its digest-backed component version commits the complete command, environment, scoring, adapter, and exit-protocol semantics. Task construction invokes a general optional evaluator validate_task hook after normalization; no concrete evaluator branch enters the coordinator.

The adapter materializes only a SourceTree, runs the declared process, and always disposes the workspace. Exit 0 and 1 produce passing and failing metrics; other exits become EvaluatorFailure. Existing process failures stay typed and non-rankable. Environment and bounded process-result evidence remain separate from metrics, and evaluator usage receives process wall time without claiming coordinator-owned evaluation counts. Cleanup failure overrides prior completion while retaining its classification, evidence, and usage.

The evaluator-owned grader remains outside the candidate mutation surface. The development sandbox still makes no hostile-code filesystem-isolation claim; stronger providers remain replaceable at the same structural port.

M5.4 pins deterministic content digests and semantic outcomes, while treating measured wall time as occurrence data. Reopened durable storage supports best-artifact and lineage queries; cold resume of these local live components fails explicitly and without side effects. SDK-backed proposers now remain user-owned local callables; portable reconstruction of patch, command, and live SDK components remains later work.

The M5-owned file audit splits patch-proposer core behavior from lifecycle/resume failures and sandbox declarations/contracts from process execution. Canonical design documents remain cohesive source-of-truth exceptions to the 300-line guideline, and unrelated pre-M5 suites are not refactored as part of this closure.

docs.title: Milestone 6: SDK proposer boundary proof
docs.text: Status: Shipped. M6 completed on July 28, 2026 by proving that native coding SDKs could participate through the ordinary proposer seam without a provider-shaped coordinator. The first-party adapters and extras were superseded on August 5 in favor of user-owned SDK callables; the obsolete provider capture archive was removed on August 6. This section records only the contract that remains part of the shipped architecture.

docs.title: Retained contract
docs.text:
• ProposerContext carries exact objectives, randomness, pushed context, and an optional scoped experience reader without evaluator, budget, permission, or promotion authority.
  • A structural propose(parent, context) object and a plain callable use the same runner path, validation, typed failures, usage, evidence, and derivation records.
  • SDK authentication, sessions, tools, permissions, retries, structured decoding, and provider telemetry belong to the user-owned wrapper.
  • Meta-Evolve retains candidate validation, external evaluation, effective budgets, durable records, lineage, audited experience, and promotion authority.

docs.title: Removed surface
docs.text:
There are no meta_evolve.claude or meta_evolve.codex modules, provider extras, compatibility shims, provider conformance fixtures, or generic live smoke directory. Current opt-in SDK demonstrations are milestone-owned experiments, such as the M8 harness driver, and add no core dependency.

The retired adapter implementations and live measurements remain recoverable from Git history and the closed M6 issues. They are historical development evidence, not current tests, documentation fixtures, or acceptance gates.

docs.title: Milestone 7: cross-domain local v1
docs.text:
Add the artifact registry and public extension contracts only after number, text, and code examples have exercised them.

The common artifact envelope contains semantic kind, representation, schema, interfaces, payload reference, content digest, parent occurrences, and provenance. Domain names such as TextArtifact, GitTreeArtifact, and SkillSetArtifact are typed constructors or views rather than a required inheritance hierarchy.

M7 P1+P2 formalized the SourceTree payload shape into an explicit codec protocol, ArtifactCodec (ports/codecs.py): every kind, including the default python-value, now resolves through a per-run CodecIndex (application/codecs.py) instead of a hard-coded dispatch. Declared interfaces resolve through the registered codec (Registry.artifact_interfaces), not through a new field on the Artifact envelope, so this added no durable schema bump — CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION is unchanged. Registry.register_artifact_type rejects every codec offered for an already-built-in (kind, representation) key — the built-in object included — so the then-four built-in keys (python-value/canonical-json, source-tree/utf8-tree-v1, text/utf8-text-v1, skill-set/utf8-tree-v1) remain non-overridable. The unit is the key, not the kind: a new representation of a built-in kind is a distinct key and registers like any other custom type.

P3 added skill-set (domain/skill_set.py), the first kind to reuse another kind's representation and the first codec with a non-empty interfaces declaration (skill-documents/v1). SkillSet wraps SourceTree construction and adds one rule, layout: every path matches skills/<name>.md. It carries no manifest — M8's HarnessArtifact defines those against a real consumer — and no content validation, since content meaning belongs to whoever reads the skills. Its codec is a fourth built-in rather than a registered custom type: the durable-local gate exists because a registered codec is a live object with no verifiable manifest, and a codec shipped with the library is verifiable exactly like the other three, so skill-set runs stay durable and resumable. That registration works for third parties is proven separately by tests/test_artifact_type_registry.py.

Proposed candidates route through the same CodecIndex as the seed, in application/proposal_completion.py — the original plan scoped only seed encoding — so a candidate the codec rejects becomes a typed InvalidOutput that fails its trial without raising into the run, and a custom artifact type now works through proposer output as well as input. application/runtime.py's durable-local validation block fails closed with CapabilityError when a task's (kind, representation) is not one of the built-in keys: a registered codec is a live object rather than a source function, so require_source_function cannot reach it, and a resumed run would otherwise rebuild payloads with unverified code.

The codec index is a per-run dependency. application/runtime.py and application/resume.py construct it once and return active results through the private Run._reopen(run_id, storage, codecs) path, preserving the exact codec objects used for that run. The public Run(run_id, storage, *, registry: Registry | None = None) constructor builds a read-only index with CodecIndex.with_extras(registry.artifact_types()) when a registry is supplied, merging its custom codecs with all built-ins while the built-ins retain precedence. This intentionally exposes every codec in that registry to decoding; the replayed run projection still selects the artifact kind read by each query, and the constructor grants no execution or mutation authority. Without a registry it remains the built-in reopening path. Codec declaration validation lives once in registry_support.validate_artifact_codec: kind, representation, and every interface name are non-empty and whitespace-exact, while an empty interface tuple remains valid. Both registry registration and the published codec suite call that same validator.

P4 demonstrated the milestone's exit gate. tests/test_four_domain_kernel.py drives number, text, repository, and skill-set runs through one meta.run call site; everything M7 permits a use case to vary lives in one Domain record, and no assertion is written for a single domain. The four leave an identical kernel record — same event sequence, usage, scores, logical steps, and audited experience — while declaring four distinct kinds over three representations, two of which share utf8-tree-v1. No domain needed a coordinator branch, special case, or workaround, and the phase changed no file under src/: the generality was already there to be measured, which is what makes the result a proof rather than a repair.

The purity allowlists are decisions, not accidents. Two properties are pinned by tests/test_application_purity.py, each with an explicit allowlist whose every member carries its justification in the test file itself, and each with a companion test that fails once a member stops being needed — so an exemption cannot quietly outlive its reason.

  • Imports. Application modules import no concrete adapter except storage.py (composes the default memory/filesystem/sqlite stores), unit_of_work.py (owns the atomic durable commit across both stores), run_support.py (constructs the callable-adapter runners for run and resume), and runtime.py (wires the public run() entry point). All four are wiring: something has to name the concrete implementations a default meta.run composes, and the allowlist exists to keep that set visible and small rather than to excuse it.
  • Type dispatch. Nothing calls isinstance against a concrete artifact type outside application/codecs.py and adapters/. The codec is the artifact-type dispatch — encode must refuse a value of the wrong type before it can become a payload — and adapters translate at the edge, where an external system's output first has to become a declared artifact value or a typed failure. The watched set is derived rather than listed: any class in meta_evolve.domain declaring string KIND and REPRESENTATION — the pair Task(artifact=...) reads — falls under the gate the moment it exists, and a guard test pins the derived set so a fifth artifact type is a visible decision rather than a silent widening.

P5a added the milestone's one new storage surface, the read-only listing Storage.runs() -> tuple[RunId, ...], so the CLI's list verb (and any caller whose ids have left the terminal scrollback) can reach Run, resume, and compare again. Two decisions are worth recording.

Enumeration is an optional capability, not a widened port. EventStore keeps exactly append and read; the listing is a separate one-method protocol, ports.RunIndex, that both bundled stores implement. Both required methods are run-scoped, so an implementation can be addressable without being enumerable — one stream handed in at construction, a backend exposing only GET /runs/{id}/events, a store sharded so that "all runs" spans shards. Requiring enumeration of every implementation would earn complexity from a hypothetical rather than the current gate, and would break the hand-built Storage(artifact_store, event_store) pair that LocalOnlyUnitOfWork exists to serve. Storage.runs() checks isinstance(self.events, RunIndex) and raises CapabilityError otherwise; it never reports a non-enumerable store as an empty one. This follows the is_durable principle — a capability is declared by the component, never inferred from a concrete type — but not its mechanism: durability needs a separate boolean because it is invisible in a commit strategy's method set, whereas here the capability is the method, so implementing it is the declaration and a parallel flag could only disagree with it.

Ids, sorted. The listing returns RunIds rather than a richer record: Run.summary() already owns per-run detail, and a richer listing would force the SQLite backend to decode every envelope just to enumerate. Ordering is lexicographic by id, not insertion — in-memory insertion order is a dict accident and SQLite has no insertion column short of rowid, an implementation detail unstable across VACUUM and interleaved appends. Sorting makes the two backends provably agree, which is the property callers depend on. Run ids are run-<sha256>, so the order carries no chronological meaning and is documented not to.

P5b added meta_evolve.cli and the meta-evolve entry point: five verbs — run, list, inspect, resume, compare — over the same public API, using stdlib argparse, no configuration DSL, and no capability logic of its own. A run takes an experiment module exposing one experiment() factory with no import-time side effects; the command line supplies only --storage and --mode. M10.1 made the factory's return a typed Experiment; dictionary returns remain supported with a DeprecationWarning, subject to the pre-1.0 policy. list is one verb beyond the milestone's four because run ids are content-derived digests rather than names anyone retypes from memory: without enumeration, every other verb is unreachable once an id leaves the terminal. Exit codes are 0 for success, 1 for a domain failure (RunError), and 2 for a usage or experiment-module error; anything else keeps its traceback rather than being flattened into a message.

Closed by the M7 defect-repair pass. compare_runs previously refused two incompatible runs with a bare ValueError from _require_equal (application/comparisons.py), which is not a RunError and so escaped the command line's typed-failure translation, reaching the user as a traceback. _require_equal now raises RunsNotComparable, a RunError carrying the declaration that differed as structured data rather than only in its message. The message text is unchanged, so prose matching still works; the command line now reports it as one error line and exit code 1 like every other typed failure.

The other four decisions of that pass. The surfaces themselves are docs/programming-model.md's; what is recorded here is why each landed the way it did.

  • One accessor, not a second view type. Run.trials() returns the existing TrialView, which gained a state field set from the projection records rather than re-derived from other view fields. failure was deliberately left alone: splitting it is breaking, and it still could not express "unevaluated", which is an authorization outcome rather than a fault. The seed trial is included, because three of the six workarounds it replaced depended on unpacking it.
  • CapabilityError is reserved abort control flow, escaping both the proposer and the evaluator boundary unwrapped. RunError is deliberately not in either escape tuple: a nested evaluator may legitimately hit a RunError subclass while reading its inner run, and a broad escape would turn that into a crashed outer run rather than a typed evaluator failure carrying the usage already incurred. (This rationale once cited three examples calling summary() inside their evaluator; issue #143 moved all three to the failure-safe inspect().overview.task_usage, so that evidence no longer holds even though the decision does.) Because CapabilityError is publicly exported, the contract binds user code and is documented, not merely implemented.
  • The name-only report keys on the run-local version sentinel, never on origin == "local". CommandEvaluator is local-origin and versions itself with a configuration digest; keying on origin would condemn exactly the local comparisons that are controlled. ComponentRef.configured_local refuses that sentinel for the same reason, and derives origin and the retained adapter rather than accepting them, since Task's declaration hook admits a component only when it is local and holds that exact callable by identity.
  • Declarable turn limits keep their existing defaults exactly. The defaults emit byte-identical native profiles, so no component.version and no Claude run id moves. native_profile takes the limit keyword-required instead of choosing between two constants, so a normalizer and a transport cannot silently disagree about what was sent. Rejected: max(requested, PULL_MIN) — silently rewriting a chosen number is the defect class being removed.

P6 published the conformance kit and the tutorial.

Published conformance covers all seven component types. meta_evolve.conformance ships subclassable pytest suites, on the pandas ExtensionArray model, for artifact codecs (ArtifactCodecTests), repository-editing proposers (RepositoryProposerTests, PullRepositoryProposerTests), evaluators (EvaluatorTests), search programs (SearchProgramTests), context policies (ContextPolicyTests), workspaces (WorkspaceProviderTests), and sandboxes (SandboxProviderTests), alongside the MutationSurfaceTests that M8 introduced and M9 generalized to four surfaces.

P6 shipped only the first two. M9 published SearchProgramTests, and the #98 follow-up closed the rest. Three of them existed as function-based suites under tests/ (policy_contract.py, workspace_contract.py, sandbox_contract.py) whose laws were already validated against a second implementation; converting those was exposure, not invention, and the function modules were deleted so a published suite and its retired twin cannot drift. policy_contract.py outlived M9's class suite because that suite took a policy instance, which cannot express a program built around the proposer; SearchProgramTests now takes either an instance or a search_factory, so the function module could go and MinimalPolicy runs through the published suite like everything else.

The two proposer suites are exercised by in-repository reference callables (tests/test_proposer_conformance.py) — no first-party provider adapter ships, and the docs say so rather than implying one. The earlier claim that tests/ covered "both providers" had been false since the user-owned SDK boundary removed those adapters; the reference callables are what make it true again at the level a test can honestly pin. Evaluators and context policies had no reusable suite. ContextPolicyTests derives its laws from what the kernel already enforces, in bundle_violation. ContextPolicy.select receives the root-exported ExperienceGraph, and the query, node, record, and state values its methods exchange are root-exported as one closed read-only surface. Construction through replay_experience_graph remains an internal application service. EvaluatorTests is only partly of that kind: the objective-coverage and typed-failure laws follow adapters/evaluators.py, but stability, order-independence, and non-mutation are not kernel-enforced — they are obligations an evaluator can break today, which is why the suite is where they are stated. Only the store suite stays internal in store_contract.py: store adapters are not one of the seven extension families.

The suites state their limits. ContextPolicyTests does not apply to NoMemory, which meta.run normalizes away before any policy runs, and asks a policy that selects nothing to declare it through expects_records — an empty bundle is accepted by the kernel, so refusing one outright would have been a law the shipped contract does not have. EvaluatorTests skips its typed-failure law visibly when a subclass declares no rejected_candidates.

EvaluatorTests also keeps a candidate-mutation law that was first removed on the argument that it could never fail. That argument was wrong, and the counter-example is now a test: decode is only required to return an equal value, so a registered codec that hands back the instance it encoded gives the evaluator the caller's own object to edit. The root cause is closed at the codec end too, by ArtifactCodecTests.mutable_values. That fixture has no default — () is a positive claim of immutability, the same shape as rejected_values — because an opt-in law still certifies a codec whose author never considered aliasing. It cannot simply apply to every value: requiring decode(encode(v)) is not v unconditionally would fail the built-in python-value codec on interned small integers, where sharing is harmless. The subclass declares its mutable values outright; the evaluator's mutation law observes through the kernel content digest and needs no shared helper.

The *_teeth test modules point a suite at a deliberately broken component and check its complaint, so a suite that stopped asserting would itself fail. They cover codecs, evaluators, search programs, context policies, workspaces, sandboxes, mutation surfaces, and — through broken reference callables such as a works-once proposer — the two proposer suites. They also pin the weaknesses review found: a workspace provider that leaks only when two workspaces are live, an evaluator whose drift hides in its uncertainty or evidence rather than its metrics, a sandbox that snapshots the environment in its constructor, a mutation surface that ignores the value it was asked to apply, a field that forges its own projection through __deepcopy__, a policy identity declared only for the kernel's read, a hidden random stream drawn only by the executed instance, an encode that special-cases the objects being watched, a value type whose __eq__ certifies a payload collapse, a sandbox that fabricates process results without executing, sandboxes that ignore timeout or either output limit, a sandbox that claims kernel-owned evaluation/trial/token usage, a random stream declared one decision late, a proposer that only works on its first call, a capture that re-reads only the paths it materialized, and a workspace backed by external symlinks.

tests/ subclasses the published classes for every built-in codec, all four mutation surfaces, every shipped search program, both workspace and sandbox providers, every selecting context policy, and — via the reference callables recorded above — both proposer suites, so those suites and the kernel's own conformance are the same code and cannot drift. pytest is imported by that subpackage and nowhere else in the package, pinned by an AST scan plus a subprocess check that importing meta_evolve never loads it, and surfaced as the package's one optional extra, conformance.

The codec suite checks round trips, rejection signaling, identity independence, repeated calls within one process, and common open/socket entry points. The last two are deliberately scoped evidence: they do not prove arbitrary purity or cross-process reproducibility. A separate built-in test creates artifacts in fresh interpreters under two fixed PYTHONHASHSEED values and compares their content digests.

The artifact-domain guide contains a complete notebook experiment. tests/test_notebook_lessons.py executes the displayed cells and verifies their adjacent output, including execution outside the checkout with the installed package. tests/test_add_a_domain_tutorial.py checks decoded recipe values, independent grading, rejected proposals, and fresh-process reopening with a rebuilt codec registry but no original proposer or evaluator. It also runs the displayed codec through ArtifactCodecTests, including rejection of bare strings, unordered containers, and blank steps. The guide imports only the public root and the standard library. Custom domains remain local-only; saving and reopening do not grant resume capability.

docs.title: Milestone 8: harness evolution
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. M8.1–M8.5 and #124 are implemented, and M8.6 is closed on retained authorized captures rather than on a claim about them.

The canonical deterministic implementation is examples/research/harness_evolution/. M9 uses the policy_evolution example independently of the M8.6 live proof.

The whole constructible family lives under meta_evolve.harness. The built-in codec owns agent-harness / harness-manifest-v1; the schema-v1 artifact has exactly planner: TextParam and context_policy: PolicyParam. Both implement the published MutationSurfaceTests contract.

ArtifactCodec.validate_successor is optional and discovered structurally by CodecIndex. Proposal completion invokes it after encode and before creating an Artifact. The hook sees parent and candidate frozen payloads and returns a typed failure or None; codecs without it are unchanged. This is the one generic seam, and no coordinator module imports a concrete harness type.

RepositoryEpisode and EpisodeSuite are portable namespaced values. The example owns their execution composition: fresh inner runs, isolated hidden test workspaces, captured evidence, and only token/spend/elapsed roll-up. Evaluator configuration identity covers suite digest, split, worker/model, inner budget, timeouts, environment, and scoring version.

Held-out comparison accepts only two seed-only Greedy(max_trials=0) runs and fails closed on any changed control or immutable harness declaration. Export is harness-specific rather than a speculative capability on every codec: it stages beside the destination, reconstructs and verifies the artifact digest, then atomically swaps only absent or valid prior harness exports.

The fixture TFD remains user code. The opt-in driver under experiments/08_harness_evolution_live/ reaches a provider through one boundary module per provider and adds no package dependency. Its first authorized result is retained as an unchanged tie after both proposal calls failed strict output-schema validation, so no native mutation reached the trusted successor boundary. A second boundary was added, and one authorized anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 run through it returned two complete manifests that the trusted successor boundary decoded and applied. Neither outcome is improved or discarded.

That second capture closes M8.6. Two authorized live calls returned complete manifests that reached native mutation decoding and the trusted successor boundary, which is the blocker the gate named. That is the whole of the claim: not a paper reproduction, not statistical generalization, and not a claim that the run should have exported. Its private split scored every candidate 0.0, so selection fell back to the seed and the held-out comparison tied — which is A4.5's rule working, not a failed live proof.

docs.title: Milestone 8.7: audited prior-candidate source inspection
docs.text: Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). This independent post-M8 program is tracked by

docs.title: 150 and does not widen the M8.6 closure gate or M9.5. It first proves value
docs.text:
through existing durable evidence, then locks a Git-neutral source-access manifest before adding audited path reads, canonical source diffs, and an optional disposable read-only Git projection.

The capability remains same-task, same-run, strictly prior, occurrence-based, and bounded by ExperienceGrant. Every returned source observation is audited and replayed from committed facts. Git metadata stays outside artifacts and durable identity; no coordinator branch depends on source artifacts or their presentation adapter.

docs.title: M8.7.2 — contract and serialization
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). This stage extended the port and durable contract without adding methods to AuditedExperienceReader; M8.7.3 implements listing and reads, and M8.7.4 implements diffing:

class ExperienceReader(Protocol):
    def list_source_paths(
        self, artifact_ref, *, as_of=None, limit=None
    ) -> SourcePathListing: ...

    def read_source(
        self, artifact_ref, *, paths, as_of=None
    ) -> SourceRead: ...

    def diff_source(
        self,
        older_artifact_ref,
        newer_artifact_ref,
        *,
        paths=(),
        as_of=None,
    ) -> SourceDiff: ...

domain/experience_access.py adds the operation names and the canonically omitted ExperienceRequest.paths default. Legacy requests and containing audit events therefore retain exact schema-v3 bytes. Only a non-tuple or non-string path is rejected before auditing; semantic path, kind, limit, and logical-time errors remain opaque denials. At this stage application/experience_operations.py explicitly denied all three source operations before legacy comparison dispatch.

domain/source_access.py owns SourcePathListing, SourceFile, SourceRead, SourceDiffEntry, and SourceDiff. Results carry verified digests, complete ordered entries, canonical text, truncation, and cumulative ExperienceUsage. Listing order is normalized lexicographic order; reads preserve caller order; paths are normalized and unique. Diff status is added, deleted, or modified under meta-evolve-unified-diff/v1. All records join the closed durable serializer and remain off the root surface.

Capacity resolution first authorizes and proves existence, then reserves one result for listing/read or two for diff, then retains the largest whole-entry prefix fitting record and character ceilings. Missing result capacity is ExperienceBudgetExhausted; a missing read path is atomic ExperienceAccessDenied. Neither consumes protected result, record, or character capacity. Each retained entry is one record and the character delta is exactly len(rendered). Listing uses compact JSON strings; reading uses compact JSON Lines with exactly path and source, stable keys, preserved Unicode, and no trailing newline. M8.7.3 implements resolution plus listing/read rendering; M8.7.4 implements unified diffs and their replay checks.

domain/source_history.py owns SourceHistoryBounds, SourceHistoryEntry, and SourceHistoryManifest. source-history-manifest/v1 requires a non-empty ordered entry tuple whose first artifact is head_ref. Artifact refs are unique while digests may repeat. Artifact, parent, proposal, and evaluation refs have exact kinds and one run; parents remain contained in the manifest. Entries retain logical step and non-empty selection rationale. No source bytes, Git IDs or refs, commits, trees, environment, or layout fields are present.

The later adapter declaration is fixed as:

meta.PatchProposer(
    edit,
    history=meta_evolve.adapters.GitHistoryView(
        max_ancestors=...,
        max_archive_members=...,
        max_chars=...,
    ),
)

GitHistoryView was not implemented in this stage. M8.7.5 now builds its manifest through ordinary audited traversal, listing, and reading, then records one mount fact without charging those bytes twice. Later Git commands are not independently audited. PullAccess remains outer authority and all history bounds are explicit.

M8.7.3 also owns an application-only ExperienceOperationUsage view. It omits zero totals and orders entries by search, open, ancestors, siblings, compare, list_source_paths, read_source, and diff_source. Their dimension-wise sum equals RunExperienceUsage.pull; there is no Git-mount usage category or new durable event.

Historical annotation. M8.7.5 narrowly supersedes the earlier “no new durable event” reservation with one SourceHistoryMounted fact because a truthful pre-execution mount must be replayable. It does not change the locked reader signatures, audit accounting, component/artifact identities, authority rules, or the claim that there is no Git-mount usage category. This final-stage repair is local to M8.7's projection contract and is not permission to reopen other shipped milestones.

docs.title: M8.7.3 — audited source listing and reads
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). A focused source-resolution edge accepts an already-authorized artifact occurrence, loads it through ArtifactStore, revalidates its content digest, and decodes only exact source-tree / utf8-tree-v1 payloads. The host supplies this dependency to AuditedExperienceReader; neither the coordinator nor generic experience graph branches on artifact type.

application/source_operations.py owns listing/read rendering and complete- entry prefix selection. Generic experience_operations.py dispatches those two operations there; M8.7.4 extends the same seam for diff_source. Authorization and tree resolution precede result reservation; every requested read path is proved before either content disclosure or charging. A successful operation consumes one result plus one record per retained entry and exactly the final joined rendering length in characters.

Both operation-ceiling and source result-ceiling exhaustion append the existing durable exhaustion fact with attempted cumulative usage. Event folding checks the result type, target occurrence, logical boundary, deltas, path order, and canonical rendering. Committed reader replay returns that result without live resolution. load_validated_run separately resolves the durable artifact and reproduces digest, selected prefix, file text, rendering, truncation, and usage for reopen, resume, and cross-process reconstruction.

Successful listing/read results add their exact artifact occurrence to the derivation observation ledger. The application view meta_evolve.views.ExperienceOperationUsage supplies canonical, non-zero per-operation totals on RunExperienceUsage.by_operation; their dimension-wise sum is required to equal the unchanged aggregate pull usage.

docs.title: M8.7.4 — canonical audited source diffs
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). The audited reader dispatches diff_source through the existing source-operation seam. It authorizes and resolves the older occurrence before the newer occurrence, then reserves two results atomically. The coordinator, artifact adapters, root surface, Experiment, and schema-v3 serializer require no special case or migration.

The pure application/source_diff.py renderer compares normalized logical lines with a deterministic Myers edit script and deletion-first ties. It owns sorted/filtered changed-path selection, three-line context and six-line hunk merging, JSON file operands, uniform ranges, and final-newline markers. It uses neither the human presentation diff nor difflib, Git, or subprocesses. source_operations.py applies whole-entry record/character prefix bounds and charges two results, one record per retained entry, and exactly the joined rendering length.

Event folding validates both refs and their logical visibility, canonical entry order and self-contained rendering, truncation shape, and cumulative usage. Successful operand refs enter derivation observations in order. Durable loading resolves both artifacts and rebuilds the exact diff, while ordinary reader replay returns the committed result without live artifact access. At this stage M8.7.5 remained the only open M8.7 stage and owned Git history projection.

docs.title: M8.7.5 — authorized read-only Git history
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). adapters/git_history.py owns the adapter declaration and explicit bounds. application/source_history.py owns the canonical audited request prefix, causal/archive selection, complete-tree character bound, and replay reconstruction. SourceHistoryMounted is folded only after that prefix resolves and before ProposalSubmitted; its transition checks trial authority, selected parent, observed version, exact operation prefix, ordering, refs, digests, and manifest equality.

adapters/git_projection.py owns only disposable Git plumbing. It builds blobs, trees, and commits parent-first in an external sidecar, supplies controlled absolute GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, and GIT_INDEX_FILE values through WorkspaceSession, creates deterministic archive refs, disables ambient configuration and executable extension points, freezes the result read-only, and disposes it before workspace capture. PatchProposer proves the callback did not mutate that workspace before applying its one returned TextPatch.

The adapter version and bounds enter configured proposer identity. With history=None, constructor behavior and identity remain byte-for-byte compatible. No generic reader, coordinator, experiment, root-export, or artifact-storage special case is introduced.

docs.title: Milestone 9: policy evolution
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The dependency is M8.1–M8.5, not #124 or M8.6. The deterministic implementation is examples/research/policy_evolution/.

meta_evolve.mutation owns only the generic MutationApplication result and MutationSurface protocol. Harness keeps compatibility re-exports and all harness-specific values. meta_evolve.policy owns the parallel policy domain: search-policy / policy-manifest-v1, schema-fixed ParentSelection and TrialLimit, one-surface PolicyMutation, portable PolicyEpisode and PolicySuite, captured EpisodeOutcome, aggregate PolicyEvaluation, and strict PolicyComparison. No generic episode/comparison framework was added.

The built-in candidate-policy@1 interpreter is registered with Registry.register_policy(). Its exact policy-manifest payload is frozen into the SearchSpec configuration. Seed selection always expands the original artifact; incumbent selection uses SearchState.incumbent_id; the voluntary trial limit never widens the run budget. Durable-local run and resume paths resolve it through the unchanged registry seam.

The published SearchProgramTests suite covers all four built-in policies. MutationSurfaceTests takes plural (mutation, expected successor) pairs and invalid_mutations, observes successors through an inert canonical-bytes projection rather than the surface's own equality, and runs unchanged against both harness and both policy surfaces.

Nested execution remains user-owned composition around ordinary meta.run() calls. Each outcome retains an inner RunId and storage location. Development may reopen an exact completed run and resume a permitted incomplete durable run; held-out execution creates a fresh empty namespace. Aggregation is recomputed from all outcomes, becomes non-rankable on any failed, incomplete, or missing episode, and rolls up only token, monetary-spend, and elapsed usage.

Separate outer Greedy(max_trials=0) runs capture held-out baseline and candidate evaluations. meta.compare_policies() requires equality of every external control and immutable surface declaration; only the two schema-owned surface values may differ. It returns improvement, tie, regression, or unrankable and reports strict promotion eligibility without promoting.

docs.title: Milestone 9.5: advanced search
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 17, 2026). M9.5.1 ships shared archive compatibility, M9.5.2 ships replayable specialist retention, M9.5.3 ships replayable tree search, and M9.5.4 ships the unified deterministic five-policy comparison. ArchiveUpdate.member_ids remains the complete ordered result, while the single-removal compatibility field is None for zero or multiple removals. This changes validation only: the durable schema, coordinator, commitment, inspection, recovery, and existing Population decisions remain unchanged.

meta_evolve.policies.Specialists now ships as specialists@1; it is not a root export. Its exact ordered metrics and trial limit are durable configuration, and the built-in registry reconstructs the bound preset. Committed successful evaluations reconstruct strict per-metric winners and ordered membership without a cache. Metric-uniform selection uses selection, proposal randomness uses trial, and archive membership remains authoritative for zero-, one-, or multiple-removal transitions. This is GEPA-style per-key retention, not Pareto ranking.

meta_evolve.policies.TreeSearch now ships as tree-search@1; it is not a root export. Its max_trials and exploration are durable configuration, and the built-in registry reconstructs the bound preset. A private immutable fold reconstructs one node per materialized artifact occurrence, visit counts, subtree Q values, the normalization range, and widening eligibility entirely from committed trial and evaluation facts. Selection widens a node with a new child while child_count < ceil(sqrt(node_visits)), otherwise it descends by normalized best-descendant UCT, breaking exact ties by ascending artifact occurrence ID. Only trial randomness is recorded.

examples/learn/policy_comparison/advanced_search.py ships the unified comparison. BestOfN, Greedy, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch run on the same specialist-retention and delayed-reward fixtures under identical task, seed, proposer, evaluator, root randomness, budget, and explicit trial limit, with equality verified pairwise through the existing Run.compare() gate. The specialist fixture shows Specialists retaining an aggregate-weak per-case winner that capacity-matched Population evicts, reaching the aggregate winner that equal-budget BestOfN cannot. The delayed-reward fixture shows Greedy plateauing on the immediately attractive branch while TreeSearch revisits the weaker delayed branch and reaches its descendant. Every result reports primary score, winning lineage and depth, every selected parent, evaluation and failure counts, archive behavior, and exact usage. No shared selector protocol, private policy engine, or coordinator branch is created in advance.

docs.title: Milestone 10: local author API and inspection experience
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 14, 2026; #149). This milestone does not depend on M8.6 or M9.5. Its nine one-PR stages are #151 (M10.0), #152 (M10.1), #165 (M10.2), #164 (M10.3), #153 (M10.4), #154 (M10.5), #166 (M10.6), #156 (M10.7), and #157 (M10.8).

The subordinate M10.0 design record owns the six journeys, vocabulary, measurements, and alternatives. Technical staging is:

  • Shipped — M10.1: the frozen declaration value lives in application/experiment.py without moving storage, mode, or the narrowing budget out of run(). Keyword calls lower to the same declaration. CLI parsing stays in cli.py; dictionary factories remain supported with a DeprecationWarning beside the typed alternative. The pre-1.0 policy revises the original through-1.x commitment.
  • Shipped — M10.2: application/improvement.py implements improve() in the application callable boundary. Its default declaration lowers through Task(evaluator=...), Experiment, Greedy(max_trials=trials), and local run(..., storage=...); it adds no second coordinator path and no durable-local claim.
  • Shipped — M10.3: policies/functional.py implements the curated @meta.search adapter and shares one private incumbent decision lowerer with Greedy. The callback never receives kernel state; immutable serializable configuration flows into SearchSpec identity, and DecisionDescription derives from the decorated name and cleaned docstring. Population actions remain on the full extension protocol.
  • Shipped — M10.4: application/inspection.py owns the immutable aggregate read model, while a shared application/views.py builder keeps artifact, evidence, trial-state, and lineage construction single-sourced. One Run.inspect() call performs exactly one validated replay.
  • Shipped — M10.5: Storage.read_only() wires dedicated read-only artifact, blob, event, and unit-of-work implementations. adapters/sqlite/ opens with mode=ro, enables query_only, validates without DDL or migration, and reads the maximum committed event sequence in a fresh deferred transaction. It does not use immutable=1, so one handle observes later WAL commits.
  • Shipped — M10.6: application/session.py owns the small public lifecycle, while one preparation boundary reconstructs fresh and resumed coordinators. run() and resume() exhaust Session; authority and budget are fixed at start, and recovery completes committed work rather than accepting injected decisions.
  • Shipped — M10.7: browser/reader.py owns a single-threaded read-only handle, exact-version catalog cards, and separate 32-entry inspection and comparison LRUs. browser/app.py supplies escaped server-rendered routes, same-origin polling, safe failure translation, and security headers over root-exported APIs only. cli.py conditionally delegates ui to a fixed loopback, one-worker Uvicorn lifecycle.
  • Shipped — M10.8: presentation/ owns dependency-free inert records, exact kind/representation dispatch, deterministic preview bounds, semantic direct-parent diffs, and canonical-payload-v1 bytes. ArtifactView retains its frozen payload without changing decoded value, equality, or repr semantics. Browser artifact/diff/raw routes resolve occurrences within one exact inspection snapshot; templates remain escaped, and the CLI's optional module contributes only its registry for custom-codec reconstruction. Notebook HTML is owned by the post-M10 presentation follow-up below.

The dependency order is M10.0 → (M10.1, M10.3, M10.4, M10.5), M10.1 → M10.2, M10.1 + M10.4 → M10.6, M10.4 + M10.5 → M10.7, and M10.7 → M10.8.

Core installation remains dependency-free. M10.7–M10.8 form the shipped bounded exception to the general dashboard prohibition, and only after M10.4 and M10.5 stabilize the public inspection, query, read-only storage, and version contracts. Its optional meta_evolve.browser package imports those public surfaces only—never Session, run, resume, proposers, evaluators, internal projections, or persistence implementations. cli.py conditionally imports it for the UI command. It binds to loopback, remains read-only, and exposes no operational, mutable, remote, collaboration, or distributed controls.

The browser extra contains Starlette, Jinja, and Uvicorn: Starlette supplies tested routing and lifecycle, Jinja supplies escaped templates, and Uvicorn supplies server operation without bespoke web infrastructure. They do not enter core dependencies. Presentation itself remains dependency-free.

docs.title: Post-M10 presentation follow-up
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. General artifact notebook representations and browser screenshot or visual-regression automation remain follow-up work over M10.8's inert records. The bounded #333 run-report slice below has its own gate outside the M10 closure gate.

docs.title: Issue #333: captured run display
docs.text:
The acceptance gate selects a nondurable extension to RunSummary. Its record and validation live in application/run_summary.py, re-exported through the existing paths. application/comparisons.py still captures one validated projection for each run; it adds the bootstrap measurement, distinct typed failed-attempt count, primary objective, recorded capabilities, and handle persistence metadata.

_run_display.py builds bounded PresentationField values from captured scalars, then renders text or escaped HTML. It stays outside presentation/ to preserve that package's stricter frozen-artifact boundary. No decoded artifact hooks, optional notebook/browser dependencies, or I/O enter display. Run repr remains an identifier-only hint; explicit queries retain their errors. Storage's private optional display path is capture metadata, never a backend protocol or persisted field. Existing ranking, CLI output, schemas, budgets, identity, and resume verification remain unchanged by this slice.

The plan records the constructor and display choices; the verification record records completed automated checks and manual visual acceptance. This follow-up does not expand #313/#319's release scope.

docs.title: Saved-run reopening (#335)
docs.text:
The author-UX gate adds one application composition in application/reopening.py: a standard-library context manager owns Storage.read_only(), selects an explicit identity or the only recorded run, calls load_validated_run(..., require_existing=True), and yields Run. Entry failures and context exit close the handle. RunSelectionRequired exposes available IDs when selection is ambiguous; empty or missing runs retain RunNotFound. String IDs use the existing opaque-identity validation.

No replay cache, schema, event, coordinator, or adapter change is needed. Subsequent queries retain live WAL visibility and their existing custom-codec requirements. The read-only contract preserves committed facts while permitting SQLite sidecar bookkeeping. The API contract owns behavior; the plan and verification record record the choices and evidence. This follow-up does not expand #313/#319's release scope.

docs.title: Issue #163: finite trial-budget inheritance for search presets
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. Tracked by #163 under release parent #268. This section records the original opt-in implementation; #320 subsequently changes omitted/None resolution to finite inheritance or fallback.

policies/_trial_budget.py is a private helper with no public exports and two functions. declared_trial_limit(value, label) validates a constructor argument and passes None through unresolved; it is the single place that widens the existing type error to "<label> max_trials must be an integer or None". resolve_trial_limit(declared, budget, label) returns declared when it is an integer, returns budget.trials when declared is None and the budget is finite, and otherwise raises BudgetUnavailable naming the preset and both remedies.

Preset binding is the only trial-limit resolution boundary and needs no new plumbing. prepare_start resolves the effective run budget and hands it to prepare_search, which binds the preset before it reads configuration and identity_key. Each preset's bind already rebuilt itself through its own constructor, so substituting resolve_trial_limit(...) for self.max_trials at that one call site puts the resolved integer into SearchSpec.configuration, into RunStarted.search, and into run_id_for by way of the unchanged identity key. Reconstruction — Registry.resolve_policy(spec, budget=recorded_run_budget) — rebuilds from spec.configuration, which already holds an integer, so no replay or resume path can re-inherit against a different budget. Rejection is therefore structurally before commitment: prepare_search runs well ahead of coordinator.start, so a run that cannot resolve leaves no events, no artifacts, and no run id.

Stopping order is unchanged and keeps authority separate from voluntary narrowing: policies check usage.trials >= max_trials before budget_exhausted, so an inherited N under Budget(trials=N) reports trial_limit_reached while an explicit limit above the budget reports budget_exhausted. max_trials=0, declared or inherited, stays seed-only.

Manifest honesty is explicit rather than incidental. No policy factory imports _trial_budget, so the resolution code would be invisible to implementation_digest unless declared. The registry therefore lists trial_budget_support in dependencies for exactly greedy, best-of-n, population, specialists, and tree-search; tree-search keeps _tree_search alongside it, and best-of-k and candidate-policy do not gain it. Factories, policy versions, configuration shapes, and identity-key formats are untouched, so existing integer records keep their exact bytes and ids.

improve() is deliberately outside this scope and stays integer-only. It exposes no budget and builds an unbudgeted Task, so trials=None could never inherit anything; left to forward into Greedy it would have turned the façade's long-standing TypeError into a bind-time BudgetUnavailable, an exception-family change for callers that never opted in. The façade therefore rejects None itself, before constructing the preset. Every other invalid value still falls through to Greedy unchanged, so the façade's "fails exactly as Greedy fails" contract continues to hold for the values it covers. The one observable delta is the message text for None, which now names the façade and the remedy instead of repeating a claim about Greedy that is no longer true.

docs.title: Issue #334: one objective and explicit context on the small path
docs.text: Status: Shipped. The author UX gate and implementation plan select two optional keywords on application/improvement.py: objective lowers to the existing Task.objectives tuple, and context passes into Experiment.context. Omitted values retain the default task and disabled pushed feedback. Validation, Greedy search, execution, identity, and accounting retain their existing owners. The implementation uses #332's evidence contract without changing its source dependencies. No new record, policy, coordinator branch, or schema is needed. This additive API belongs to a subsequent release, outside #313/#319's retained 0.2 scope; it does not select a version or publish a package. The verification record separates source equivalence and historical checks from publication.

docs.title: Issue #336: practical journey integration
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The existing routing driver consumes bounded evaluator reports through #332, captures #333 summaries before closing storage, and uses #335 for fresh-process inspection. The short SDK notebook retains its three-request bound and recorded environment; the credential-free feedback lesson uses #334's small declaration. No coordinator, schema, provider abstraction, or public keyword is added.

Source snippets and generated three-file downloads share their implementation. Installed rehearsals cover an imperfect seed, failed rewrite with known usage, improvement, final separation, and reopening. The verification record owns actual checks, SDK-glue inventory, and the #275/#277 handoff. Live examples remain Experimental/live-only; independent sessions, review, and publication retain their existing owners under the author UX gate.

docs.title: Issue #332: bounded evidence lookup and recent ancestor context
docs.text: Status: Shipped. The selected author UX gate authorizes this slice, specified in the feedback plan. ProposerContext.evidence exposes a storage-free view of its committed bundle and explicit policy declaration. latest(kind) preserves occurrence provenance and selected order; disabled pushed context raises a typed capability error, while a declared policy with no match returns None. RecentAncestors uses the existing bounded policy/registry seam with its own identity. Existing ancestor and sibling selection semantics remain intact. Automatic proposer source dependencies cover the view and construction wiring; no new durable schema, ambient query, or coordinator branch is needed. This follow-up does not expand #313/#319's release scope. The verification record retains the pre-change durable capture, explicit digest changes, and acceptance checks.

docs.title: Author API revision
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. The named roadmap gate and foundation decision authorize these bounded seams:

  • Resolve execution budgets once in session_preparation, before policy binding. Replay and resume use recorded resolved values.
  • Keep plain-callable binding in the adapter and automatic invocation source dependencies at the registry/manifest boundary. Preserve structural dispatch and user dependencies; verify before reconstructing executable components.
  • Build summary, inspection, and usage from coherent validated projections, including admitted history before bootstrap. Keep strict winner queries and existing comparison controls; migrate CLI rendering and exit behavior.
  • Resolve budget-led defaults in the existing preset trial-limit helper. Store integers, retain preset-specific fallback bounds, and leave custom policies and BestOfK outside this rule.
  • Normalize author-facing Resources into existing zero-count Usage at component adapters; retain durable accounting records and engine counts.

No coordinator branch, new scheduler, generic procedure class, package-tree reorganization, or schema change is authorized merely by these declarations. The comparison record rejects objectives, procedure, and counting rewrites for this release. Exact source-manifest drift is expected; historical evidence separates readability, matching-runtime continuation, and incompatible-source refusal. Implementation children own production tests; #318/#319 own integration and one release. The following #315 section records its existing source slice.

docs.title: Issue #317: winner-independent reporting
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The acceptance gate keeps summary and comparison in application/comparisons.py. A private builder loads one validated projection and reuses ViewBuilder for ranking, decoding, and causal lineage. It returns the nondurable summary plus captured declaration and seed metadata for comparison. No public snapshot object or query framework is introduced. Comparison requires each measured score before reading the next side or checking declaration compatibility.

The private domain.search._recorded_usage fold preserves the existing arithmetic and aggregation order. SearchState, summary, inspection, and Run.usage() use it; reporting no longer requires policy readiness. RunProjection.search_state retains its execution guard, including during pending distributed bootstrap. The CLI uses one private text/status report, with summary formatting in its existing renderer and stream writes only in main.

No execution, admission, recovery, identity, event, or serialization schema changes. The migration guide covers the required keyword-only record fields and changed CLI failure output. The verification record tracks source, historical reads, manifest effects, integration checks, and publication limits.

docs.title: Issue #315: partial execution budget overrides
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The Author API revision gate adds one private _resolve_run_budget(task_budget, override) helper in application/session_preparation.py. It first rejects each explicitly supplied finite value above its finite task ceiling, then uses the unchanged Budget.narrow() intersection to inherit missing dimensions. Missing whole declarations resolve to the other budget or Budget().

prepare_start calls this helper after its existing budget type check, before proposer validation, search binding, distributed admission, identity generation, or run commitment. Typed and keyword run() calls and Session.start() share that boundary. Resume, recorded-budget validation, event schemas, accounting, and policy defaults remain unchanged. No override object enters run identity or persistence; equivalent resolved budgets produce identical durable facts.

The migration guide and verification record cover the changed authoring behavior and historical-store checks. The broader API foundation and coordinated release remain tracked separately under #314 and #319.

docs.title: Issue #316: explicit callback context
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The acceptance gate uses private adapters/_proposer_invocation.py for signature selection and single invocation. CallableProposer selects plain or structural binding by entry route and retains failure normalization. application/run_support.py preserves route precedence and configured identity; its callable type accepts keyword inputs without introducing a public protocol.

registry_support.resolve_component automatically adds the invocation and proposer-adapter modules, covering imports, registered construction, and dispatch. Lazy imports avoid a registry/adapter cycle. User dependencies keep their deduplication semantics; evaluator dependencies are unchanged. Resume verifies these manifests before constructing runners or invoking their preflight hooks. Run identities and stored schemas are unchanged; exact source drift refuses continuation instead of rewriting history.

The migration guide distinguishes plain callbacks from structural and patch interfaces. The verification record owns historical capture provenance, implementation checks, and remaining release work.

docs.title: Issues #320/#321: budget-led presets and component resources
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The acceptance gate uses the existing policies/_trial_budget.py bind-time helper for all five presets. Each declares max_trials=None; the helper selects explicit integer, finite effective trial ceiling, or finite fallback in that order. TreeSearch passes 100; the others use 20. Recorded configuration stays an integer, and registry reconstruction keeps consuming it. No coordinator or schema changes.

domain/resources.py defines the immutable three-field author value, validation, and addition. Usage.resources projects it without changing serialized Usage. ports/callables.py requires Resources for both rich results; constructor validation rejects the old author Usage convention, including zero counts. Ordinary callable normalization keeps costs on valid successes and failures.

The existing proposal encoding and evaluation-fact boundaries share private application/work._resource_usage to convert once into zero-count Usage before engine counts are added. These boundaries cover custom runners as well as callables, so no parallel normalized-result classes or coordinator dispatch branches are needed. Patch and process adapters project their structural Usage into Resources when producing rich author results. Domain outcomes retain Usage.

Examples project method totals only at rich-return boundaries; policy and ACE keep their retained histories and phase accounting, while AutoResearch retains its declared outer-only total. The migration guide and integration evidence own the upgrade and source verification. Package release remains #319.

docs.title: Issue #195 B2: systems-optimization example
docs.text: Status: Shipped. The B2 acceptance gate is implemented entirely under examples/research/systems_optimization, using the existing public callable and durable-storage boundaries. Process confinement, the scheduler protocol, evaluator-owned simulation, post-search selection, and decision-record validation stay local to the example. No coordinator branch or new core protocol is required. Tests cover terminal failures, accounting against kernel usage, retained evidence consistency, and replay without re-execution; the docs notebook runs the same fixture command.

docs.title: SoL-Pi: harness efficiency experiment
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. The roadmap gate owns scope, sequence, and acceptance. Keep the first implementation under examples/research/sol_pi/, using existing callable, artifact, evidence, and storage seams; create that directory only when implementation begins.

  • Start with validated Text JSON containing only declared mechanism settings. Keep runtime/model identity, pricing inputs, task splits, evaluator code, permissions, and budgets in experiment-owned declarations. Later code evolution can use an allowlisted SourceTree with independent validation.
  • Use one narrow runner boundary with deterministic and opt-in Pi implementations. Pin the upstream extension and run each evaluated configuration in a fresh isolated workspace/session. Runtime tool and conversation handling belongs there; Meta-Evolve's ContextPolicy selects inter-proposal evidence.
  • Keep capability filtering, nondominated retention, and deterministic final choice in an example-owned selection component. Use ordinary SearchProgram extension points if retention must guide parent choice; add no coordinator branch, built-in Pareto preset, or change to compare_harnesses semantics.
  • Publish measured outcomes through EvaluationResult, detailed call and cache observations through evidence, and counted costs through Resources. Include reducer and compaction calls; preserve incomplete accounting explicitly.
  • Record selection inputs, dispositions, and the frozen winner beside the committed run evidence. Reuse durable history for replay and the existing harness example's separation of development from later evaluation. Keep upstream runtime dependencies optional and outside the core package.

docs.title: SIFT: judge-guided agent evolution
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. The roadmap gate owns sequence, scope, and acceptance. Keep the sequential implementation under examples/research/sift/; create it only when implementation begins.

  • Represent editable agent code as an independently validated SourceTree. The shipped HarnessArtifact text/configuration surfaces do not express arbitrary agent-code changes. Reuse proposer workspaces and independent evaluator execution, with benchmark and model dependencies outside the core.
  • Keep comparison orchestration and immutable decision snapshots example-owned. Use a custom SearchProgram for rank-based sampling only after proving that its inputs reconstruct from committed observations. If the existing search view cannot expose those inputs, compose local runs through an explicit experiment-owned driver retaining run and artifact-occurrence references; do not hide mutable archive state in callbacks or call a live judge in next.
  • Derive the win matrix and Bradley–Terry strengths from retained pairwise records. Recompute rankings without rewriting earlier evaluations. Publish actual measurements through EvaluationResult, observations through evidence, and incurred resources through Resources; retain decision snapshots beside run history when existing records cannot represent them directly.
  • Keep the sequential driver synchronous. Neither Session.step() nor current distributed cohorts provide evaluation-only scheduling or speculative expansion. A later runtime proposal must define staged evaluation identity, pending-node eligibility, provisional estimates, priority changes, completion ordering, recovery, and budget settlement before asynchronous work begins.

docs.title: Milestone 11: trusted distribution
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. Tracked by #10.

The subordinate M11 design record owns vocabulary, the consistency model, and the durable rules. Only after local semantics are stable:

  • add WorkAttempt and durable lease acquisition, renewal, expiration, cancellation, and completion;
  • retain one logical Trial across delivery retries;
  • introduce trusted worker identities and capability matching;
  • add atomic budget admission and settlement, derived by folding committed events rather than stored in a ledger;
  • make idempotent result submission explicit;
  • define consistency requirements per state type;
  • generalize the batch grammar into a dependency grammar keyed by trial, and add generational cohorts behind a declared policy capability;
  • load-test simulated populations before paid agent fleets.

Work, lease and worker state live in durable tables outside the run event stream: renewals are clock-driven control-plane mutations, and putting them in the stream would make policy-observed versions depend on heartbeat frequency. Cohort width is declared on the search policy, not as an execution overlay, so it reaches run identity. The staged package additions are domain/work.py, a work broker port with in-memory and SQLite adapters, an application dispatcher, and a small advanced distributed surface — none of them root exports, and none created before a slice needs them.

M11.1 notes. The durable-fold half landed single-process, in two parts. The stream grammar splits in two: application/batch_grammar.py owns what one batch may look like, application/stream_grammar.py what an order of batches may look like — and only the second is what concurrency changes, so it keys on trial identity rather than position. application/decision_transitions.py owns the decision barrier and derives cohort_members once, so the barrier and the cohort-base rules cannot acquire different notions of base, adjacency or width. The writer lives in application/decisions.py, where commit_decision is the cohort of one, so every production run drives the same code the wide path uses.

Two additive fields carry it: PolicyDecisionMade.cohort_base, omitted at its default so no recorded stream moves, and a derived evaluation_dispositions pin on the projection. The pin is deliberately tri-state — an evaluation is owed, terminally skipped, or the question is ill-posed because the trial overran its own allocation. Collapsing the last two would force a choice between refusing an evaluation for a skipped trial and keeping historical overages replayable.

The canonical reservation is examples/research/trusted_workers/.

Worker liveness and queue estimates are ephemeral. Accepted outcomes, evaluations, budgets, and promotion decisions are durable. Out-of-order wall-clock completion must not alter logical random choices or reveal future experience.

docs.title: Milestone 12: contributed and federated network
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. Tracked by #11 and dependent on M11.

Add signed manifests, scoped contributor identities, task-specific trust policies, visibility, licensing, embargoes, attribution, retraction, disputes, and reputation. Exchange policy-filtered subgraphs rather than assuming universal access.

References may be redacted, tombstoned, or inaccessible while preserving enough metadata to maintain causal structure. Untrusted execution, evaluator collusion, poisoning, sybil attacks, reward hacking, and correlated replication remain separate threats with separate controls.

The canonical reservation is examples/research/federated_exchange/.

docs.title: Interface staging
docs.text: Capability First implementation Later implementation Proposer local callable SDK agent, human workflow, composite harness Evaluator pure callable isolated grader, simulator, proof checker Artifact store in-memory payloads content-addressed filesystem or object store Event store in-memory list SQLite, then durable service Search greedy and best-of-N populations, Pareto, islands, learned allocation Experience no memory exact graph traversal, then measured semantic retrieval Workspace absent directory copy, Git tree/worktree, remote volume Sandbox absent development subprocess, container, hardened remote sandbox Identity absent or local stub trusted worker, then signed contributor identity

docs.title: What not to build first
docs.text:
• every module in the destination package tree;
  • a custom graph or vector database;
  • a peer-to-peer protocol or token economy;
  • a thousand-agent deployment;
  • mutable, operational, or remote dashboards, and any browser before stable public event and query contracts;
  • universal agent communication;
  • learned scheduling without strong baselines;
  • unrestricted self-modification;
  • a template DSL when local closures and typed durable manifests suffice;
  • scientific-discovery claims without domain evidence and replication.

docs.title: Near-term definition of done
docs.text:
Meta-Evolve has a credible first release when a user can define a task, seed artifact, proposer, and evaluator through the canonical small API; choose a search and context policy; run callable and SDK-backed proposers in appropriate execution profiles; evaluate immutable successors; inspect exact causal experience; resume durable runs after failure; and compare runs under equal budgets.

Everything beyond that should extend the same contracts rather than replace the kernel.

docs.title: User-owned live SDK track
docs.text:
Status: Experimental/live-only. Meta-Evolve ships no provider client or credentialed launcher. Use the shipped SDK-integration guide to wrap your own client as a callable or structural proposer.

The current examples are credential-free and deterministic. Their injection points can be used by an opt-in maintainer driver:

Exercise Injection point Maximum wrapper calls Repository proposal examples/agents/user_owned_sdk 1 Experience A/B examples/agents/experience_ab 4 Held-out skill evolution examples/research/context_evolution 6 Playbook context evolution examples/research/context_evolution 14

The ceiling is a declaration for a driver, not permission to spend. The driver must identify its wrapper and behavior-affecting configuration, authenticate outside Meta-Evolve, require explicit opt-in, and preserve SDK-specific tools, permissions, timeouts, and telemetry at the edge.

Only shared Meta-Evolve facts are comparable: task, seed, evaluator, effective budget, search declaration, durable usage, failures, lineage, and audited experience. A provider or infrastructure failure, timeout, invalid candidate, missing derivation, or grader failure carries no score and must never be converted to zero.

There is no official provider capture pending. A user may perform one authorized run with their own wrapper. Any published capture must name the wrapper declaration and retain ties, failures, and regressions honestly. CI uses deterministic fixtures and performs no credentialed execution.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This roadmap grows Meta-Evolve through small, testable vertical slices. Every milestone must produce a runnable demonstration, preserve the contracts established by earlier milestones, and add only the infrastructure required by its acceptance tests.

The first product target is a local, extensible improvement system in which a user can define an artifact, task, evaluator, proposer, search policy, and context policy; run a bounded experiment; let agents inspect prior work; replay or resume the run; and compare results under equal budgets. Harness evolution, meta-evolution, trusted concurrency, and federation build on that local product.

The harness-evolution demonstration (milestone 8) is the flagship product demo — "point this at your agent and eval set, get a measurably better agent, and inspect exactly why each change was kept." Earlier milestones should keep that demonstration in view rather than treating it as a distant capstone.

Before the numbered milestones, a disposable API spike validated the user-facing interface against both deterministic code and a real model. The spike is a design probe, not a shortcut into the durable implementation. It is complete; see its status below.

docs.title: Development rules
docs.text:
1. Every milestone has one canonical example that runs with a documented command.
  2. Every new port has an in-memory or deterministic reference adapter and a conformance suite.
  3. The coordinator contains no branches for particular artifact types, proposers, evaluators, or search policies.
  4. Durable behavior is specified through domain events and observable results, not adapter internals.
  5. New infrastructure is introduced only when a milestone's proof requires it.
  6. Failures remain typed: poor task performance, invalid output, timeout, resource exhaustion, policy violation, and infrastructure failure are not interchangeable.
  7. Tests are deterministic by default. Tests requiring credentials, network access, or hardened infrastructure are explicitly separated.
  8. Each milestone updates examples, tests, and user-facing documentation together.
  9. The programming model is the canonical public API contract; other documents link to it rather than redefining signatures.
  10. Canonical examples are first-class user-facing documentation, not test fixtures: each must be short, copy-pasteable, and runnable from a clean checkout, and the simple callable path never requires or surfaces kernel vocabulary such as Trial, OperatorSpec, or ProposalWork.

docs.title: Pre-milestone API spike
docs.text: Status: Shipped (July 16, 2026). Both demonstrations ran through the same small public surface under experiments/00_api_spike/, including a real gpt-5.4-mini Codex SDK prompt-optimization run. The exit gate passed: findings are recorded in real_model_findings.md and folded into the programming model's evidence section. Closed by #23.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Exercise the smallest declarative API before durable domain models and package boundaries are fixed.

docs.title: Demonstrations
docs.text:
Build a disposable one-to-three-file implementation that runs:

  1. deterministic integer improvement with Greedy and BestOfN;
  2. one real-model prompt-optimization task whose proposer and evaluator each require only a small user function.

The spike should test the canonical Task, meta.run, proposer, evaluator, search, and Run.best()/lineage() surface from the programming model.

docs.title: Questions it must answer
docs.text:
• Can a plain callable be used as a proposer and evaluator in local mode?
  • Is the distinction between task, seed, proposer, evaluator, and search obvious in working code?
  • Does changing search policy require no change to task or proposer code?
  • Can failures and multi-metric evaluations be represented without exposing orchestration machinery?
  • Which values must become durable records, and which abstractions are premature?

docs.title: Exit gate
docs.text:
• Both examples run through the same small public surface.
  • The programming model is revised from observed use rather than aspiration alone.
  • Any deliberately unsupported capability is named explicitly.
  • None of the spike's internal structure becomes a kernel contract without Milestone 1 justification.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Replay, crash recovery, ports and adapters, stable schemas, experience grants, workspace isolation, provider portability, and production-quality model integration.

docs.title: Common definition of done
docs.text:
A milestone is complete only when:

  • its canonical example runs from a clean checkout;
  • its acceptance tests pass locally and in CI where the required capabilities are available;
