docs.title: Coordinated acceptance gate
docs.text:
• Adopted preset-default (#320) and component-resource (#321) changes land as separate children under #313. Counting names, ordered objectives, and Experiment remain; a new Improver class is outside this gate.
  • Separate implementation PRs do not constitute separate package releases. Keep the package version at 0.1.0 until the coordinated release step.

The verification record distinguishes design/engineering evidence from production implementation and publication.

docs.title: 314 pins installed baselines, historical captures, selected contracts, and
docs.text: all four comparison dispositions. Its foundation unblocks #315–#317.

docs.title: 315 implements partial budget restrictions; #316 implements explicit plain
docs.text: callback context and automatic invocation verification; #317 implements   failure-independent reporting, including pre-bootstrap distributed history.

docs.title: 318 integrates every accepted change into examples, imports, canonical API
docs.text: documentation, and one migration path. #319 runs integrated tests and fresh installs, confirms the release version, publishes one package, updates meta-evolve-docs from that revision, and verifies the deployed site.

docs.title: Issue #317: summaries without a successful evaluation
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The source implementation of #317 separates reporting from winner selection under the coordinated author API gate. Acceptance requires:

  • One validated snapshot per summary, including all four lifecycle/rankability states and valid distributed history with pending seed evaluation.
  • Optional score and empty winning lineage when unrankable, truthful committed costs, unchanged evaluation counts, and explicit constructor invariants.
  • Strict winner queries and comparison, preserved compatibility controls and left-to-right error precedence, and at most one snapshot per compared side.
  • CLI summaries on stdout for unrankable run/resume with exit 1; successful inspection and existing browser refusals for valid unrankable history.
  • Read-only historical-store evidence, matching examples and canonical docs, focused and integration tests, and fresh installed-package examples.

The implementation boundary, migration guide, and verification record distinguish this source slice from coordinated release and publication in #318/#319.

docs.title: Issue #315: partial execution budget overrides
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The source implementation of #315 lets an execution budget tighten selected dimensions while inheriting the task's other ceilings. The programming model owns the public behavior; the implementation plan owns its single preparation boundary.

Acceptance requires:

  • All five resource dimensions distinguish omission, finite limits, and zero; explicitly wider values fail before component calls or committed run facts.
  • Typed run, keyword run, and paced Session agree. Partial and equivalent full budgets preserve identical identities, events, artifacts, usage, and bound search configuration.
  • Recovery consumes the recorded budget, including a store captured before the resolver change. Unknown spend and distributed admission retain their existing authority boundaries.
  • Current examples, reference, migration guidance, strict documentation build, and deterministic tests agree; installed-package examples pass outside the checkout. The verification record distinguishes local evidence from release and hosted CI claims.

Preset defaults, counting names, per-trial allocation (#206), callback dispatch (#316), result summaries (#317), and M11 concurrency are outside this slice.

docs.title: Issue #316: explicit callback context and verified invocation
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The source implementation of #316 separates ordinary Python defaults from framework inputs. The programming model owns the binding contract; the implementation plan owns the adapter and manifest boundaries.

Acceptance requires:

  • Plain callbacks receive parent only unless named keyword-only context opts in. Signature errors precede validation hooks, seed evaluation, and committed facts; callback bodies are never probed or retried for binding.
  • Structural proposer and runner routes, configured identities, context grants, failures, usage, and explicit patch callbacks retain their contracts.
  • Registered proposer manifests automatically verify invocation source and adapter wiring in addition to user dependencies. Same-runtime recovery preserves deterministic events; incompatible invocation refuses before work.
  • Real pre-cutover optional/variadic functions retain readable histories and matching-old-runtime continuation evidence. The new runtime refuses their proposer manifest specifically, with evaluator and policy manifests equal.
  • Current examples, notebooks, source docstrings, reference cases, and migration guidance agree with the tests. The verification record separates local implementation evidence from release and deployment.

No historical invocation engine, coordinator branch, public adapter, store schema, or change to evaluator/authority semantics belongs to this slice.

docs.title: Issues #320/#321: integrated author allowances and resources
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. These source slices complete the adopted #314 comparisons. Acceptance requires:

  • All five bare/None presets resolve against the effective partial budget, use finite fallbacks when unbounded, and preserve explicit voluntary limits, targets, exact counts, cohort restrictions, and concrete recorded limits.
  • improve, BestOfK, custom/functional search, and candidate-policy semantics remain unchanged. Failed proposals cannot evade finite fallback stopping.
  • Immutable Resources contains only tokens, billed/unknown spend, and elapsed work. Rich results reject Usage; Usage.resources projects costs losslessly.
  • Completed billable work survives typed failure, invalid output, and overage. Nested reports charge intended work once without importing logical counts.
  • Policy/ACE/AutoResearch retain their actual authority, history, and phase accounting. Historical Usage remains readable and exact-source continuation is verified or refused before further work.

docs.title: Issue #318: documentation integration
docs.text: Status: Shipped. The source docs integrate #297 and all five adopted changes through one migration entrance, source-generated reference, and runnable examples. Acceptance covers the first loop, SDK and feedback, search comparison, failed-run diagnosis, reopen/resume, and nested composition journeys. Existing migration routes and historical evidence remain. The verification record binds checks and installed artifacts to source. Coordinated package publication is still #319's separate gate; this does not claim M11 concurrency or empirical RSI.

docs.title: Issue #195 B2: systems-optimization example
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The ADRS-inspired fixture, tracked by #195 B2, revises a bounded scheduler, measures it independently, selects on a separate post-search workload, and retains the final comparison. This is an example-level proof using shipped callable, source-artifact, policy, and storage seams; it adds no kernel behavior.

The acceptance surface includes confinement of proposer and candidate child processes, typed failures, exact evaluation and scenario accounting, and replay of the retained decision without execution. Entirely failed searches retain their evidence and usage. Scenario observations must agree with their attempt's split and outcome. The fixture and executed notebook establish a local simulator result; live model search and production speedups are outside this slice.

docs.title: SoL-Pi: harness efficiency experiment
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. This research follow-up translates SoL-Pi, v1 into a bounded local experiment. It builds on shipped harness evaluation, source artifacts, experience, and resource accounting. M11 remains the runtime build boundary; this item adds no concurrency or release prerequisite. The implementation plan owns its technical composition.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Use execution evidence to propose agent-harness changes that reduce cost while keeping each capability metric within a fixed tolerance. Evaluate the frozen selection against the unchanged baseline on held-out tasks. The experiment owns metrics, tolerances, splits, models, environments, budgets, and promotion.

docs.title: Ordered scope
docs.text:
1. Deterministic local proof. Reserve examples/research/sol_pi/ for a small callable experiment with a fixture runner. Version a validated configuration, retain development observations, and demonstrate capability-constrained efficiency selection. Exercise Action Fusion (edit plus follow-up command) and ObservationPack (bounded context with exact output recall) before adding other mechanisms.
  2. Opt-in runtime integration. Wrap a pinned version of the authors' Pi extension through user-owned execution code. Compare the baseline, individual mechanisms, and their combination under equal external controls. Add Evidence-Preserving Reducer and Online Context Compact only with verified evidence handling, compaction lifecycle, and complete auxiliary-call accounting. Live results remain Experimental/live-only and retain ties, regressions, and failures.
  3. Later research scope. Evolve allowlisted harness source after the configuration experiment passes. Large concurrent campaigns depend on M11 and its paid-work reservation/settlement gate; they are not part of the local proof.

docs.title: Acceptance gate for the local experiment
docs.text:
• Candidate configuration has an explicit allowlist. Independent validation rejects changes to evaluator controls, permissions, budgets, or promotion.
  • Selection first checks every declared capability tolerance against the fixed baseline, then requires improvement in at least one declared efficiency metric. Retain nondominated eligible candidates under explicit metric directions and deterministic tie-breaking; do not substitute Specialists or the primary-objective compare_harnesses verdict for this rule.
  • A cheaper candidate outside a capability tolerance is rejected. A cheaper candidate at equal quality can be retained. Invalid, incomplete, or failed executions remain typed, non-rankable outcomes with their incurred costs.
  • Development evidence alone informs proposals and selection. Freeze the selected artifact, metrics, tolerances, and comparison rule before fresh held-out baseline/candidate executions; held-out feedback never returns to search, and rejection cannot trigger another optimization round.
  • Retain per-task quality, raw usage, billed spend when known, model and runtime identities, and mechanism activations. Preserve cache-read/write and auxiliary-model breakdowns when available; estimates remain evidence, unknown spend remains unknown, and nested work is charged exactly once.
  • Tests cover fused-action failure boundaries, exact observation recall, selection and dominance cases, split isolation, and accounting. Committed candidate lineage, evidence, failures, and selection decisions replay without provider execution. An entirely failed search still has an inspectable report.
  • A short runnable example, documentation, and an unchanged-baseline comparison establish the mechanism. Neither a positive live gain nor replication of the paper's savings is required to demonstrate the local boundary.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: A first-party agent runtime, new built-in HarnessArtifact surfaces, a generic Pareto framework, unrestricted self-modification, automatic deployment, the paper's full benchmark scale, and claims of compounding recursive improvement. Create no placeholder example tree before implementation begins.

docs.title: SIFT: judge-guided agent evolution
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. This research example adapts Self Improvement via Fast Tree-search (SIFT), v1 to the shipped local engine before pursuing the paper's asynchronous pipeline. M11 remains the runtime build boundary; this example adds no release prerequisite. The implementation plan owns its technical composition.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Evolve versioned coding-agent source using pairwise judge preferences and independent development measurements to guide parent selection. Compare the frozen selected agent against the unchanged baseline on held-out tasks, retaining the evidence and costs needed to assess whether judging helps search.

docs.title: Ordered scope
docs.text:
1. Deterministic sequential proof. Reserve examples/research/sift/ for an allowlisted SourceTree experiment with fixture proposers, pairwise judgments, and independent execution. Include an easy-task gate, bounded comparison-target selection, regularized Bradley–Terry fitting, and parent sampling from judge rank, measured accuracy rank, and parent visit counts. Complete each admitted candidate's development evaluation before the next expansion. Label this a sequential adaptation, without asynchronous speedup or full SIFT reproduction claims.
  2. Opt-in live experiment. Supply user-owned model wrappers and a pinned benchmark adapter with isolated execution. Compare judge-guided search to an accuracy-only ablation under equal external controls and total budgets, including judge costs. Live results remain Experimental/live-only; report ties, regressions, failures, and unknown spend.
  3. Deferred asynchronous reproduction. Separate expansion and evaluation queues, speculative descendants, provisional inherited accuracy, and priority updates require an explicit runtime acceptance gate beyond M11's generational cohorts. Depend on trusted concurrency and paid-work reservation/settlement where applicable; completing M11 alone does not supply these semantics. This stage is outside the local proof.

docs.title: Acceptance gate for the local experiment
docs.text:
• Candidate changes are confined to declared agent source. Evaluators, task splits, judge configuration, budgets, permissions, and promotion remain experiment-owned. Judges receive candidate implementations or recorded diffs, without benchmark tasks or outcomes; proposers may receive declared development diagnostics.
  • Retain comparison targets, pairwise outcomes, model/configuration identities, artifact occurrences, and decision order. Recompute archive-wide strengths from recorded wins and losses; pin regularization, convergence, rank ties, visit accounting, and named randomness so selection can be reconstructed.
  • A deterministic fixture demonstrates that the judge signal changes parent selection against the accuracy-only ablation. Tests cover sparse comparisons, ties, gate rejection, judge failure, and disagreement with measured accuracy. Failed measurements remain typed outcomes, never synthetic scores or wins.
  • Keep judge preferences, derived strengths, and measured accuracy distinct. Final local selection uses a declared measured-development rule; freeze the winner before fresh held-out baseline/candidate evaluation, with no feedback from held-out tasks into search.
  • Account for proposal, gate, judge, and benchmark work exactly once, including failures. Retain per-phase observations and benchmark task counts separately from kernel trial/evaluation counts. Replay recorded decisions without model or benchmark execution; an entirely failed search remains inspectable.
  • Deliver a short runnable example and documentation stating the sequential limitation. Positive live gains and the paper's reported savings are not prerequisites for the deterministic mechanism proof.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: A built-in SIFT preset, changes to existing TreeSearch semantics, unrestricted self-modification, automatic promotion, and the full benchmark campaign. Create no placeholder example tree or speculative runtime protocol before its gate.

docs.title: Milestone 11: trusted concurrency and distribution
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. Concurrent execution is the deliverable and it is not shipped: a distributed run executes its work serially, one worker at a time. M11.0 (the design record), M11.1 (the concurrency-ready fold, single-process, every durable fixture byte-identical) and M11.2 (the work table, the dispatcher and generational cohorts, reachable through meta.run(mode="distributed")) are shipped, and the subissue list below records which. Tracked by #10. The subordinate M11 design record owns vocabulary, the consistency model, the durable rules concurrency changes, and the compatibility promises.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Execute work concurrently on trusted workers without corrupting history, budgets, search state, or promotion decisions.

Scoped to what the milestone delivers: concurrent execution for any search policy that declares the cohort capability and passes its conformance suite — of which BestOfN is the only shipped example — for experiments declaring neither pushed context nor pull experience, under budgets whose finite dimensions are trial and evaluation counts. Population search does not gain concurrency here. Paid concurrency depends on #206 and is refused until it lands. Every restriction above is a CapabilityError at distributed start, never a silent degradation. The environment fingerprint is a worker's property, not a declaration, so it will be checked when a worker claims and refuse that worker; the comparison is not implemented yet.

docs.title: Ordered subissue program
docs.text:
• [x] #199 — M11.0: lock the design record, narrow this goal, and amend the implementation plan's prohibition on leases and retry-attempt identities.
  • [x] #200 — M11.1: make replay, budgets and ranking concurrency-ready, single-process, leaving every durable fixture byte-identical. Its "live execution and recovery agree on evaluation disposition" criterion is what the overrun reconciliation below satisfies; the tick was here one commit before that landed, which review caught.
  • [x] #201 — M11.2: add the work broker, dispatcher and generational cohorts, reachable through meta.run(mode="distributed"). Execution remains serial: what ships is the structural concurrency — cohorts, the durable work table, leases, fences, retries and their terminal facts — with one worker running each call inline. It also ships single-process resume and the terminal duplicate exemption, both amended out of M11.3. Concurrent workers arrive with M11.3. The boundary with M11.1: the cohort writer, the cohort base and the trial-keyed grammar are M11.1, because its acceptance criterion — an interleaved stream replays — cannot be met without something able to write one. What M11.2 adds is the producer: next_cohort on the policy, the dispatcher that calls it, and the broker that hands members out. So M11.1 leaves a writer exercised at width one on every production run and above one only by tests, and M11.2 is what lets a user reach it.
  • [ ] #202 — M11.3: add cross-process claiming. Amended in M11.2: this slice originally also owned "the durable work ledger", and M11.2 takes it. The forcing constraint is ATOMICITY, not resume: enqueue and acceptance ride the same transaction as the logical batch that authorizes them, and an in-memory ledger pair cannot be atomic with a durable event append at all. (An earlier wording argued from "Leases cannot be ephemeral — a restart must retain the fence, deadline and accepted result" plus "distributed resume is M11.2's". The second half is false at the time — prepare_resume refused a distributed run — so the argument is restated on the reason that actually holds. The conclusion is unchanged.) Amended again in M11.2: SINGLE-PROCESS distributed resume moved to M11.2 and ships there — prepare_resume admits a distributed run and Session.drive() rolls the epoch over as the explicit recovery step. What stays here is cross-process claiming, the submission seam that answers a worker Duplicate or Stale, and the abort-poison path that stops a resumed run re-driving an item that aborted because it was impossible.
  • [ ] #203 — M11.4: add trusted-worker administration.
  • [ ] #204 — M11.5: add multi-process load and fault injection.
  • [ ] #205 — M11.6: ship examples/research/trusted_workers/ and flip the documentation.

The dependency order is a single chain:

M11.0 → M11.1 → M11.2 → M11.3 → M11.4 → M11.5 → M11.6

Each slice is a superset of the last and ends green. M11.1 changes only single-process behavior. M11.2 owns everything its own normative rules require — the durable work ledger (amended from "the in-memory atomic ledger pair", for the reason given under #202 above; the in-memory broker is retained as the deterministic test double), the environment fingerprint and a minimal worker-generation model — so it can never run in a state the state machine forbids.

That amendment has a user-visible consequence a milestone earlier than planned: bumping the store schema means every store written before M11.2 must be reopened once through writable Storage.durable(...) before Storage.read_only(...) or the browser will open it. The refusal is loud and names the fix, but it belongs in the release notes rather than in a user's first surprised traceback.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Several worker processes claim bounded work through leases under a count-only budget. Workers finish out of wall-clock order, one lease expires, and one result is submitted twice. The reconstructed logical run preserves one trial across delivery retries, contains one accepted outcome, and has correct budget accounting.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Durable work states and atomic lease acquisition, renewal, expiration, cancellation, and completion.
  • WorkAttempt identities that remain distinct from their logical Trial and WorkItem.
  • Worker capability and resource declarations.
  • Idempotent result submission and retry policy.
  • Atomic budget admission and settlement, derived by folding committed events.
  • Scheduler matching work requirements to trusted workers.
  • Explicit consistency rules for durable facts, leases, heuristic frontier statistics, and promotion.
  • A dependency batch grammar keyed by trial, and generational decision cohorts behind a declared policy capability.
  • Multi-process load and fault-injection test harness.
  • examples/research/trusted_workers/.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• At most one completion has logical effect for an idempotency key.
  • Expired workers cannot overwrite an accepted result.
  • Named random choices and decision identities reproduce from committed history; trajectories are schedule-sensitive when an outcome varies or an attempt is abandoned.
  • A cohort barrier makes the set of results visible at the next boundary independent of arrival order.
  • Durable events and evaluations are strongly inserted; heuristic statistics may tolerate documented staleness.
  • Promotion and budget accounting use authoritative state.
  • Local and distributed runs preserve the same task, artifact, trial, work, evaluation, and event semantics.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Competing lease claims.
  • Lease renewal and expiration races, including a concurrent renewal racing expiry.
  • Duplicate and late result submission.
  • Worker termination separately during proposal and during evaluation.
  • Exact budget admission under concurrency, with consumption exact only over accepted completions.
  • Two concurrent claims exceeding one worker's declared capacity.
  • Projection rebuild after out-of-order events.
  • Load test with simulated trusted workers before paid agent fleets.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Arbitrary untrusted community code, Byzantine workers, public federation, reputation economies, universal strong consistency, multi-dispatcher high availability or automatic failover, and distributed context or pull experience.

docs.title: Milestone 12: contributed and federated network
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. Tracked by #11 and dependent on M11's trusted-worker boundary.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Allow independent installations to contribute and exchange authorized agents, evaluators, artifacts, evidence, and experience subgraphs with verifiable provenance.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Two Meta-Evolve installations exchange a signed, policy-filtered experience bundle. The receiving installation verifies identity and content, imports only authorized records, preserves source provenance and restrictions, independently evaluates a promoted candidate, and processes a later retraction.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Signed manifests for contributors, agents, evaluators, tasks, environments, and artifact schemas.
  • Scoped identities and task-specific trust policies.
  • Canonical export/import format for policy-filtered experience subgraphs.
  • Verification of signatures, content digests, schema compatibility, causal closure, and access labels.
  • Provenance, licensing, embargo, attribution, and retraction propagation through derivation edges.
  • Independent or redundant evaluation for promotion-sensitive results.
  • Minimal dispute and reputation projections based on recorded evidence.
  • examples/research/federated_exchange/ using two local installations.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• Import never grants broader access than the source export policy and receiving trust policy allow.
  • Missing private ancestors can be represented by verifiable redacted references without fabricating lineage.
  • Invalid signatures, digests, schemas, or causal references are rejected.
  • Imported evaluations are evidence, not automatic local promotion.
  • Retractions and permission changes identify dependent artifacts, datasets, skills, and checkpoints.
  • Operators may keep private events while publishing permitted claims and artifacts.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Successful signed export/import between two installations.
  • Tampered payload, signature, digest, and causal-edge rejection.
  • Private, embargoed, and redacted source handling.
  • Conflicting evaluator results and independent verification.
  • Retraction propagation through derived records.
  • Duplicate import idempotency and schema-version negotiation.
  • Threat-model review covering code execution, evaluator collusion, poisoning, sybil behavior, reward hacking, and correlated replication.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Token economies, unrestricted peer-to-peer execution, global consensus, claims that containers alone secure untrusted code, and scientific validity without domain-governed evidence and replication.

docs.title: Architecture gate across all milestones
docs.text:
The following test should remain true throughout development:

new use case
  = artifact codec and schema
  + task and evaluator
  + agent or mutator
  + search/context configuration
  + optional infrastructure adapters

new use case
  ≠ coordinator branch
  ≠ new durable semantics
  ≠ bypassed authority boundary

When a new domain does not fit, first determine whether it needs a general protocol capability or whether it lies outside evaluated artifact-improvement loops. The kernel should grow only for the former.

docs.title: The smallest useful mental model
docs.text:
Start with an artifact, a function that proposes revisions, and an independent function that measures them. To run these cells, first run Start here. It defines meta, SEED, propose, evaluate, and load_parser without an SDK or credentials. With those definitions, the smallest run declaration is:

The first run
result = meta.improve(
    seed=SEED,
    proposer=propose,
    evaluator=evaluate,
    trials=1,
)

improve() assembles a task, an experiment, and bounded Greedy search. It evaluates the seed, tries up to trials proposed revisions, and returns a Run containing the history. An attempt need not improve the score; the seed can remain the selected result.

The keyword-only signature is improve(*, seed, proposer, evaluator, trials=20, storage=None, random_seed=0, objective=None, context=None) -> Run.

objective accepts one Maximize or Minimize; None uses Maximize("score") without a satisfaction target. A scalar evaluator measures the selected objective's metric. A mapping or EvaluationResult must contain that exact metric; missing measurements become typed evaluation failures. A seed meeting an explicit target stops after one evaluation with no proposals, even at trials=0; an unsatisfied seed at that limit stops at the proposal allowance.

context accepts an explicit bounded policy, such as RecentAncestors. None and NoMemory() supply no pushed feedback. A proposer requests (parent, *, context) and reads context.evidence.latest(kind) from the selected bundle; disabled access raises ContextDisabled, while an enabled policy with no match returns None. This setting does not enable pulled experience. See the single-objective example and feedback lesson.

These optional keywords preserve existing calls and lower to Task.objectives and Experiment.context. trials remains a nonnegative integer (not None or a boolean); storage defaults to isolated memory and randomness to seed zero. Malformed declarations fail before evaluation or committed run facts. Saving local history does not make a run resumable.

The objects below let you configure and control that same loop. Each execution starts from the same seed in separate default in-memory storage; it does not continue the previous run.

docs.title: Task: define what better means
docs.text:
A Task defines the evaluation contract for an artifact. It requires an evaluator, which measures a candidate, and uses objectives to interpret those measurements. The default objective maximizes score, without a satisfaction threshold. Here the evaluator checks six parser inputs:

task = meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate)

You can also declare the artifact type, evaluation environment, and budget ceilings on the task. The task is reusable across seeds, proposers, and search strategies; constructing it declares the rules without running an evaluation. The evaluator owns the checks and expected answers. Proposed artifacts cannot revise that contract. See evaluation and limits to change measurements, objectives, or ceilings.

docs.title: Experiment: choose how to search
docs.text:
An Experiment combines a task with a seed and a proposer. Its search policy chooses which version to revise and when to stop. Bounded Greedy search is the default; here we give it the same allowance as the first run:

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed=SEED,
    proposer=propose,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=1),
)

The declaration is immutable and starts no search. Optional context and experience settings control what prior observations a proposer can receive. Recording a score alone does not send it as feedback; the feedback guide shows that configuration.

Pass the declaration to run() to execute until search stops and receive the recorded result:

expanded_result = meta.run(experiment)

docs.title: Session: control execution
docs.text:
A Session is the active execution handle for an experiment. Use Session.start(experiment) when you want to inspect progress between decisions. For local execution, the seed is already evaluated when start() returns. Each step() completes one search decision and returns its immutable view. A decision can attempt a revision, update an archive, or stop; a step does not promise a better candidate.

session.run provides recorded results: best_trial() gives the selected attempt, and usage() reports work consumed.

with meta.Session.start(experiment) as session:
    print("Evaluations after start:", session.run.usage().evaluations)
    first_decision = session.step()
    score = session.run.best_trial().metrics["score"]
    print(f"After one step: {score:.0%}")
    print("Evaluations so far:", session.run.usage().evaluations)
    while not session.stopped:
        session.step()
    paced_result = session.run
# Output:
# Evaluations after start: 1
# After one step: 100%
# Evaluations so far: 2

run(experiment) completes this lifecycle for you. Stepping gives you control over when execution advances; the declared search still chooses the decisions. The experiment and effective budget stay fixed for the session. Leaving the with block closes this execution handle; session.run remains inspectable. Leaving early does not finish the remaining search.

docs.title: Run: inspect what happened
docs.text:
A Run gives you access to recorded results and history. improve() and run() return it after execution stops; session.run also lets you inspect work already recorded while a session is active. Reading its methods does not advance search.

You want to know… Use Which value was selected? best().value What happened, and which versions led to the selection? trials() and lineage() What is the current state and work consumed? summary() and usage() Why did attempts succeed or fail? inspect() 
scores = [
    f"{attempt.metrics['score']:.0%}"
    for attempt in paced_result.trials()
]
print(scores)
selected = paced_result.best().value
parse_seconds = load_parser(selected)
print("4m:", parse_seconds("4m"))
# Output:
# ['33%', '100%']
# 4m: 240

These are the same measured results as the original improve() call and the expanded run() call. Failed attempts remain inspectable; when no evaluation succeeds, best() raises NoSuccessfulEvaluation. Use result inspection to examine that case.

docs.title: Summaries and comparisons
docs.text:
Run.summary() reads one validated snapshot of an existing run. Its frozen RunSummary reports:

Field Meaning lifecycle complete when a stop is committed; otherwise incomplete rankability rankable when a successful measurement can be selected; otherwise unrankable stop_reason Recorded stop reason, or None while incomplete primary_score Selected primary measurement, or None when unrankable winning_lineage Decoded causal lineage, or an empty tuple when unrankable evaluation_count All committed evaluations, including failures and the evaluated seed primary_objective, baseline_score Primary objective and successful seed measurement; failed or pending seed measurements are absent failure_count Distinct attempts with a committed typed proposal/evaluation failure, including a failed seed storage_is_durable, storage_location Durability and optional location of the handle at capture; a custom durable store may have no path capabilities Recorded execution mode and resume capability, without verifying current compatibility or permission

The seed can win, zero and negative scores remain measurements, and a stopped run can still be unrankable. Usage, declarations, experience totals, decoded seed, and component provenance remain available in every state. Pending work does not contribute a guessed charge. Summary, usage, and inspection also work before a distributed seed evaluation completes. Missing runs raise RunNotFound; invalid history retains its typed integrity error.

Capture while storage is open: snapshot = result.summary(). print(snapshot) produces bounded text; a notebook displays escaped HTML when snapshot is its cell's final expression. Both remain usable after storage closes or disappears. They omit decoded artifact values, evidence bodies, and manifests. Programmatic fields retain their full values; a frozen summary does not make arbitrary decoded custom objects deeply immutable.

The report separates completion, successful measurement, and improvement. It compares the baseline and selected scores in the primary objective's direction; a tie is no improvement, and an absent measurement means improvement is unavailable. Proposal counts exclude the seed; evaluation counts include it when evaluated. Typed failures keep their costs. Task spend and context/pull usage remain separate, and unknown spend remains unknown.

History is reported at capture: memory-only history is not saved durably, and a saved history does not grant resume permission. Recorded resume support is not a current compatibility check; a complete run has no continuation pending. repr(result) shows its identifier without I/O. Explicit queries, including another summary(), still require accessible storage and retain their real errors. See result inspection and storage lifetime.

best(), best_trial(), and default lineage() still require a successful evaluation. compare(other) requires one on each side, reading left then right, before applying its existing declaration checks. Incomplete runs may be compared if both rank; two missing scores never constitute a tie. Each side uses one validated snapshot, without promising an atomic read across independent stores.

Direct RunSummary construction requires keyword-only lifecycle, rankability, and stop_reason; existing positional fields keep their order. The six report metadata fields above are optional keywords defaulting to None (unknown). Supplied facts participate in record equality; an old-style manual summary can therefore differ from a fully populated captured summary. See the summary migration guide for constructor invariants and CLI behavior. A returned summary certifies neither improvement nor resumability.

docs.title: Choose what to change
docs.text:
Change you want Where it belongs Measure candidates differently improve(evaluator=...) or Task.evaluator Prefer one metric or set a target improve(objective=...) or Task.objectives Supply bounded feedback improve(context=...) or Experiment.context Generate different revisions Experiment.proposer Choose different parents or a proposal allowance Experiment.search Pause between decisions and inspect progress Session.step() and session.run

To change a declaration, construct a new value, reusing the components that still apply. Search demonstrates reusing a task and proposal rules with another policy. The routing lesson applies the same callable path to instruction text.

docs.title: Execution contracts
docs.text:
Evaluation, budgets, and permissions remain outside candidate authority. External SDKs are user-owned callables; Use your model SDK shows their request wiring, execution limits, and accounting. No first-party provider adapter is shipped. Simulated tutorial responses are not live-provider evidence.

For existing callers, the source-compatible declaration-keyword spelling of run() remains available. New examples use the typed declaration. The pre-1.0 release policy supersedes the earlier through-1.x promise; this spelling is retained in the selected 0.2 scope:

Supported keyword form · with the same declared experiment
result = meta.run(
    task=experiment.task,
    seed=experiment.seed,
    proposer=experiment.proposer,
    search=experiment.search,
    context=experiment.context,
)

Experiment owns the eight declaration fields and defaults. Storage, mode, and a narrowing call-level budget are execution overlays on run(), never experiment fields. In a supplied budget, omitted or None dimensions inherit task ceilings. Finite values may tighten or introduce ceilings; exceeding a finite task ceiling raises ValueError before work starts. Budget() preserves all task ceilings. See the budget override example.

The returned Run supports inspection, trials, lineage, evidence, usage, failures, summaries, and comparisons. Rich ProposalResult and EvaluationResult reports take immutable Resources with tokens, billed spend, and elapsed work. Trial/evaluation fields and the old author Usage value are rejected. Plain candidate/scalar/mapping returns remain direct. Run.usage() returns Usage, including engine-owned counts; forward nested work with inner.usage().resources. Structural PatchResult, process and durable domain records retain Usage.

Resources.spend_micros and recorded Usage.spend_micros accept a billed integer or None for unknown; its default 0 describes known free work. Unknown totals remain unknown, and monetary ceilings stop further work when spend cannot be verified. Estimates remain evidence. See evaluation and budgets. Safe frozen-payload presentation, direct-parent diff rules, and exact current canonical-payload-v1 bytes are specified by the browser guide.

In local and durable-local execution, run() exhausts the synchronous Session. Session fixes components and authority at start. Each step() commits one decision or completes one owed by recovery; it accepts no injected decision. Bootstrap is complete before Session.start() returns and is not a policy step. Distributed execution uses a different pacing boundary; see execution profiles.

Durable storage has two independent axes: is_durable means committed facts live on durable media, while is_read_only means this handle has no commit or execution authority. Storage.durable(path) is durable and writable; Storage.read_only(path) is durable and read-only. Storage.run_version(id) returns the maximum committed event sequence, or 0 when that well-formed id has no events. The latter is a polling result, not authoritative run loading: opening a required missing run still raises RunNotFound.

docs.title: Reopen saved history
docs.text:
open_run(path, *, run_id=None, registry=None) owns a read-only storage handle and yields the existing Run in a with block. path is the directory passed to Storage.durable(). An explicit RunId or ID string selects only that run; a missing selected run raises RunNotFound without fallback. ID strings must be nonempty and have no outer whitespace. Other ID types and invalid registries raise TypeError; malformed strings raise ValueError.

With run_id=None, an empty store raises RunNotFound, a single run is selected, and multiple runs raise RunSelectionRequired. Its run_ids tuple lists available identities lexically, not chronologically. Selection occurs once; later additions do not retarget the handle. Argument validation, opening, and authoritative history validation happen on context entry. Incomplete and unsuccessful histories remain readable; missing, corrupt, and incompatible storage retain their existing typed errors.

Storage closes on normal exit or error. Capture summary(), inspect(), or usage() inside the block for use afterward; the live Run still requires open storage for queries. Queries can observe later commits, while each summary or inspection captures one validated frontier. registry= supplies custom artifact codecs for decoded queries; entry validation and usage() do not require those codecs. A missing codec raises CapabilityError when decoding is requested. Reopening neither executes components nor resumes or migrates a run. Committed history is unchanged; SQLite may maintain WAL sidecars. See the durability guide for lifetime and storage details.

docs.title: Selected evidence
docs.text:
context.evidence.latest(kind) returns the last matching evidence in the already selected bundle's canonical order. Its immutable item exposes data, kind, uri, ref, logical_step, and event_sequence; ref can be cited in an explicit ProposalResult.derived_from. Same-step matches follow bundle order. Both proposer and evaluator evidence qualify; a label does not certify authorship, success, or a relationship to the current parent.

context.evidence.enabled reports the pushed-policy declaration. None and NoMemory() are disabled: calling latest() raises ContextDisabled, a CapabilityError, at use rather than repeatedly failing proposals. An enabled selection with no matching record returns None. Use an explicit enabled check when feedback is optional. Manually constructed ProposerContext values must supply context_policy to enable this accessor; bundle contents/reason are not proof of a declaration. Separately declared pull access does not enable it.

RecentAncestors retains the newest accessible ancestor records within max_records, returning them in canonical order. AncestorsOnly@1 still retains the oldest records, and BestSibling keeps its existing ranking. No preset promises matching evidence under every bound. context.evidence.truncated mirrors the committed aggregate flag: omitted records or clipped rendering. max_chars bounds rendered text, not item data. Lookup performs no I/O, grants no access, and never merges pull observations. See the feedback lesson and source/migration implications.

docs.title: Proposer callback arguments
docs.text:
Plain callbacks receive the parent positionally. Only a named keyword-only context requests ProposerContext, even when that keyword has a default. Ordinary defaults such as factor=2 remain Python configuration. Variadics alone do not request framework inputs.

def propose(parent, factor=2):
    return parent * factor

def propose_with_context(parent, *, context):
    return parent + context.rng.choice((-1, 1))

Preparation inspects and binds once, before seed evaluation or committed facts. An additional positional context, unbound required arguments, or an uninspectable plain callback raises TypeError. A body that raises TypeError is invoked once and normalized as a proposer failure; it is never retried to guess a signature. Local bound methods, partials, and callable instances follow their effective signatures; durable registration still requires source-verifiable module-level functions. Structural .propose(parent, context) objects retain their explicit port and parent-only convenience. See the callback migration guide for route precedence, optional aliases, wrappers, and historical resume consequences.

docs.title: Canonical public surface
docs.text:
This is the canonical contract for the shipped public API available from the current package. The generated API reference owns signatures and parameter details; the guides teach task-oriented usage.

The reference partitions root exports into four tiers. Root imports are public; kernel records remain internal unless a guide describes an extension protocol.

The constructible harness family stays under meta_evolve.harness: HarnessArtifact, HarnessMutation, MutationSurface, TextParam, PolicyParam, MutationApplication, portable repository episodes, comparison views, and export views. Only compare_harnesses, export_harness, and load_harness are root conveniences.

The neutral MutationApplication and MutationSurface contracts live under meta_evolve.mutation; harness keeps compatibility re-exports. The data-only meta_evolve.policy family contains PolicyArtifact, its two fixed surfaces and mutation, CandidatePolicy, portable episodes/suites, captured outcomes/evaluations, and comparison views. compare_policies is the single root convenience.

docs.title: Task guides
docs.text:
• Choose a guide — task-oriented routes through the public API.
  • Define what better means — evaluators, named metrics, and objectives in a fresh notebook.
  • Set limits and stopping conditions — proposal allowances, satisfaction, and evaluation ceilings.
  • Choose what to try next — a standalone notebook comparing a handwritten loop, Greedy, and TreeSearch, with recorded parent choices and saved history.
  • Inspect results and failures — a standalone notebook guide; Runs and results owns detailed query views.
  • Evaluation and budgets — objectives, evidence, usage, and typed failures.
  • Learning from experience — no memory, pushed context, audited pull, and derivation.
  • Save and reopen a run — a standalone notebook guide; Durability owns recovery and resume.
  • Use your model SDK — a standalone notebook; SDK accounting and tools owns detailed wrapper patterns.
  • Improve an SVG with visual feedback — a self-contained Jupyter notebook with a live Codex generator, separate grader, Greedy, and recorded feedback.
  • Command line — run, list, inspect, resume, compare, and browse.
  • Local run browser — optional server-rendered read-only inspection.
  • Extensions — codecs, registries, component identity, and conformance.
  • Improve a search policy — a standalone notebook with nested runs, retained outcomes, and held-out comparison.

docs.title: Execution profiles
docs.text: local accepts live Python components and defaults to a separate in-memory store. Local execution does not itself isolate untrusted code; see the source execution boundary. durable-local requires durable storage plus registered, reconstructible components and records enough identity to resume honestly through Session.resume() or resume(). Persisting a local run keeps history; it does not make its callables resumable. distributed adds a durable work table and uses Session.drive() instead of step(). It currently executes work serially, one worker at a time, and supports single-process recovery. Multiprocess concurrency remains Design—not shipped. See current status for supported scope.

docs.title: Authority and failure boundary
docs.text:
Candidates may propose artifact content. They cannot change the evaluator, effective budget, permissions, hidden data, audit history, or promotion rule. Invalid output, proposer/evaluator failure, timeout, exhaustion, policy violation, and infrastructure failure remain typed, inspectable outcomes. A failure with no valid measurement is never ranked as a low score.

Harness candidates receive a second, trusted check after codec encoding and before artifact creation. The built-in harness codec compares the encoded successor with its one parent and rejects changed component references, interfaces, parameter names or types as PolicyViolation; malformed and no-op transitions are InvalidOutput. Wrapper-side mutation helpers are convenience, not authority.

Bounded list_source_paths, read_source, and diff_source operate on exact, prior same-task/run occurrences. Successful observations may be cited in proposal derivation. PatchProposer can project a bounded committed manifest through adapter-only GitHistoryView; its callback receives meta_evolve.ports.WorkspaceSession. These observations do not widen candidate authority or change artifact identity. See audited pull for access and charging rules.

meta.PatchProposer(
    edit,
    history=meta_evolve.adapters.GitHistoryView(
        max_ancestors=4,
        max_archive_members=2,
        max_chars=128_000,
    ),
)

All bounds are required non-negative keywords. history=None preserves prior identity and behavior. In a history-enabled callback, defaulted ProposerContext.workspace contains root, the complete controlled subprocess environment, and the committed history manifest.

docs.title: Composable policy pieces
docs.text:
The search presets share the task's external allowance. For Greedy, BestOfN, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch, omitted/None max_trials inherits finite effective Budget.trials, otherwise using 20 (100 for TreeSearch). Explicit integers are voluntary stops. The resolved integer is recorded once; replay never re-inherits. improve, BestOfK, functional search, and custom/candidate policies retain their own limits. See migration for changed defaults.

For bounded single-parent refinement, an author may declare the parent choice without receiving kernel state or constructing trials:

@meta.search(max_trials=20)
def incumbent_refinement(search):
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)

The callback sees only opaque seed and optional incumbent occurrence handles, immutable declared configuration, expand(), and stop(). The adapter owns proposer binding, the unit budget, the objective and exhaustion envelope, named trial randomness, and durable explanation. Behavior-affecting configuration belongs on the decorator; closure capture is rejected because it would be invisible to run identity. Population-shaped actions and archive decisions remain on the full SearchProgram.next() extension protocol.

docs.title: Specialists and per-metric retention
docs.text: Specialists (meta_evolve.policies.Specialists, not a root export) retains one winning artifact occurrence per configured metric and expands a uniformly sampled metric's owner, weighting parent selection by how many metrics an occurrence owns. It is GEPA-style per-key frontier evolution, not a Pareto archive. See the search guide.

docs.title: TreeSearch and value-directed tree allocation
docs.text: TreeSearch (meta_evolve.policies.TreeSearch, not a root export) reconstructs one node per materialized artifact occurrence from durable history. It widens a node with a new child while child_count < ceil(sqrt(node_visits)) and otherwise descends by normalized best-descendant UCT, breaking exact ties by ascending artifact occurrence ID. See the search guide.

docs.title: The simplicity test
docs.text:
A common first run should remain improve(seed, proposer, evaluator, trials). A common expansion should remain one Task, one Experiment, and one meta.run(experiment) call. New internal protocols must not make that public story larger.

The small path accepts individual declarative values with obvious defaults and existing owners. Every additional keyword needs an explicit requirement and acceptance gate. The selected extensions are one objective and pushed context. Multiple objectives, artifact/environment declarations, budgets, custom search, registry, execution mode, and pulled experience use the expanded path. A budget on improve() would require a separate decision about its interaction with trials; there is no generic options bag.

docs.text: Status: Experimental/live-only. These are small teaching mechanisms, not paper reproductions or an official SealQA evaluation. The complete curriculum contains at most 12 sessions.

docs.title: The common experimental substrate
docs.text: All labs consume a structural SessionRunner. The repository supplies orchestration and deterministic injected-runner tests; users supply any live SDK wrapper. The wrapper owns authentication, structured decoding, tools, permissions, model configuration, and provider telemetry.

docs.title: What is frozen and what may change
docs.text: The fixture questions, documents, evaluator-only answers, schemas, and session arithmetic are frozen. Candidate prompts and recipes may change. The wrapper declaration and all behavior-affecting configuration must be recorded before a live run.

docs.title: Leakage boundary
docs.text: Solver views contain only public document ids, titles, dates, and text. Gold answers, source URLs, split roles, evaluation rules, permissions, budgets, and promotion decisions remain outside candidate authority.

docs.title: Failure and scoring semantics
docs.text: Malformed structured output, missing candidates, timeout, exhaustion, SDK or infrastructure failure, and protected-control edits are typed and unrankable. They are never converted into a low score. Deterministic graders alone produce rankable measurements.

docs.title: Evidence, lineage, and identity
docs.text: Each session retains its label, decoded value or typed failure, wrapper evidence, token and elapsed usage, and experience counters. Derived artifacts name their source evidence. A wrapper configuration change changes declared identity and prevents uncontrolled comparison.

docs.title: How the shared components actually work
docs.text: UserSdkSessionRunner invokes a user-provided proposer inside an ordinary one-trial meta.run(). A successful wrapper returns ProposalResult, puts the schema-decoded value in sdk.structured-output evidence, and reports only shared token and elapsed usage. The lab validates that value again before using it.

docs.title: How to run the curriculum
docs.text:
Create an opt-in driver outside the shipped examples. Implement build_agent(request), identify its declaration, and pass it to UserSdkSessionRunner; then call run_selected. Review the maximum call count, SDK permissions, and spending limits before setting META_EVOLVE_LIVE_SDK=1.

No official provider capture is pending. Users may perform one authorized run with their own wrapper. Any published capture must identify the wrapper declaration and preserve ties, failures, null results, and regressions honestly. The notebooks contain illustrative code and no fabricated live output.

docs.title: Start here: improve a duration parser
docs.text:
Our time tracker thinks four minutes means four seconds. In five short cells, you'll measure the bug, try a correction, and use the selected parser. The correction is handwritten; Python runs the checks. No model or API key is needed.

Start with a version → propose a change → test it → inspect what happened.

Open in Colab · Download the notebook

Or copy the five Python blocks into a fresh Jupyter notebook.

Run the five cells in order. Every definition is below. After installation, the example runs offline.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
Use a fresh notebook environment running Python 3.12 or newer. Install directly from the published documentation:

%pip install https://sentient-xyz.github.io/meta-evolve-docs/downloads/meta-evolve.zip

If you already imported Meta-Evolve, restart the kernel after installing. Then run the remaining cells in order.

Archived or offline docs: use the ZIP included with that build. Put meta-evolve.zip in the notebook's working folder (%pwd shows it; hosted notebooks let you upload files), then run %pip install ./meta-evolve.zip instead. Installing from source may still download build tools.

docs.title: 2. Try the starting parser
docs.text:
SEED holds the parser's Python source. load_parser executes that source and returns its function. Try "4m": this version reads the number and ignores the unit.

import meta_evolve as meta

SEED = '''def parse_seconds(text):
    return int(text[:-1])
'''


def load_parser(source):
    namespace = {}
    exec(source, namespace)
    return namespace["parse_seconds"]


print("4m:", load_parser(SEED)("4m"), "seconds")
# Output:
# 4m: 4 seconds

docs.title: 3. Measure it with six checks
docs.text:
evaluate returns the fraction of correct answers; higher is better. Only the two seconds cases pass. These expected answers stay fixed while we try a revised parser.

CASES = (
    ("30s", 30),
    ("90s", 90),
    ("2m", 120),
    ("3m", 180),
    ("1h", 3600),
    ("2h", 7200),
)


def evaluate(source):
    parse = load_parser(source)
    passed = 0
    for text, expected in CASES:
        actual = parse(text)
        if type(actual) is int and actual == expected:
            passed += 1
    return passed / len(CASES)


print(f"Starting: {evaluate(SEED) * len(CASES):.0f}/{len(CASES)} checks")
# Output:
# Starting: 2/6 checks

docs.title: 4. Propose a correction
docs.text:
The missing step is converting minutes and hours to seconds. propose receives the current source and returns a proposed revision. Here it always returns this handwritten correction; you can replace it with a model call later.

def propose(source):
    return '''def parse_seconds(text):
    quantity = int(text[:-1])
    seconds_per_unit = {"s": 1, "m": 60, "h": 3600}
    return quantity * seconds_per_unit[text[-1]]
'''

docs.title: 5. Improve, inspect, and use it
docs.text:
meta.improve evaluates the starting parser, tries one revision (trials=1), and keeps the version with the better score. result.best().value gives you its source, ready to load and call. You set the checks and the attempt limit; the run stops after that one revision attempt.

result = meta.improve(
    seed=SEED,
    proposer=propose,
    evaluator=evaluate,
    trials=1,
)

summary = result.summary()
print(f"Starting: {evaluate(SEED) * len(CASES):.0f}/{len(CASES)} checks")
print(f"Selected: {summary.primary_score * len(CASES):.0f}/{len(CASES)} checks")
print("Selected source:")
print(result.best().value, end="")

parse_seconds = load_parser(result.best().value)
print("4m:", parse_seconds("4m"), "seconds")
# Output:
# Starting: 2/6 checks
# Selected: 6/6 checks
# Selected source:
# def parse_seconds(text):
#     quantity = int(text[:-1])
#     seconds_per_unit = {"s": 1, "m": 60, "h": 3600}
#     return quantity * seconds_per_unit[text[-1]]
# 4m: 240 seconds

Four minutes now gives 240 seconds, and the selected parser passes 6/6 checks. A tie or a worse revision keeps the earlier winner. These checks cover whole-number durations ending in s, m, or h; passing them doesn't establish correctness for every possible input.

result keeps the attempted versions and their outcomes in memory. To keep that history after Python closes, save and reopen the run. Selecting a parser does not deploy it.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Change trials=1 to trials=0 in cell 5 and rerun that cell. Predict the answer before running it: 2/6 checks, and "4m" gives 4 seconds again. With no proposal attempts, the starting parser stays selected. Restore trials=1.

To try another check, add ("4m", 240) to CASES in cell 3 and rerun cells 3 and 5. The starting score becomes 2/7 and the selected score 7/7. Rerunning all five cells repeats the experiment from the starting parser.

docs.title: Build a SQL schema migration
docs.text:
Complete SQL walkthrough · Shipped · Python 3.12+ with standard-library SQLite. Extend an ordered tuple of SQL statements; the evaluator executes it in a fresh in-memory database and counts required table/column names.

docs.title: Improve a repair harness
docs.text:
Canonical Meta-Harness walkthrough · Shipped · Python 3.12+; macOS sandbox-exec or supported Linux Landlock confinement. Change planner/context settings; bounded repository-repair episodes provide independent development, private, and final checks.

uv run python examples/research/harness_evolution/main.py --output /tmp/meta-evolve-harness

Use a fresh output directory for a new study. Existing compatible stores resume. Fixture gains demonstrate this mechanism, not model performance; export does not promote the candidate. Unsupported confinement causes an explicit refusal.

docs.title: Find a slug-generation defect
docs.text:
Complete defect-discovery walkthrough · Shipped · Python 3.12+. Change a JSON-encoded title; the fixed evaluator checks the title's input contract, runs slugify, and scores violations of its promised output format.

uv run python examples/domains/adversarial_inputs/main.py

There is no maintained creative/simulation application in this catalog yet. See Application ideas for proposed uses, Research for method mappings, and the complete example inventory for learning exercises and operations commands.

docs.title: Application ideas
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. These sketches have no maintained runnable application or measured result in this repository. The working applications are a separate catalog. A related mechanism or proposal is a starting point, not an implementation of the application described here.

Each idea needs its own data, independent evaluator, bounded editable artifact, and execution path before it can enter the working catalog.

docs.title: Document and workflow automation
docs.text: Extract invoice fields with source evidence. Evolve extraction instructions; grade amounts, currencies, missing fields, and supporting text against annotated invoices. The meeting-notes example shows JSON grading, but invoice parsing, document loading, and provenance checks are not implemented.

docs.title: Support and knowledge systems
docs.text: Answer support questions from a maintained knowledge base. Evolve retrieval instructions or context entries; grade answer correctness, citations, and refusal when evidence is absent on a fixed question set. The ACE mechanism and structured-memory proposal are related. A support corpus, retrieval integration, and grounded-answer grader still need implementation.

docs.title: Software development
docs.text: Tune a team's repair workflow. Evolve permitted harness settings; grade repairs against repository-owned tests, regressions, and reported cost. The Meta-Harness mechanism and workflow research proposals provide starting points. Integration with a team's repositories, representative tasks, and rollout requirements is unimplemented; passing fixture tests does not supply it.

docs.title: Data quality
docs.text: Normalize inconsistent imported records. Evolve transformation source; independently check field preservation, normalization, and rejection of malformed records on development and separate final cases. The duration parser is a smaller working example. Dataset ingestion, transformation rules, and the record-level evaluator are missing; there is no dedicated application proposal yet.

docs.title: Creative and simulation uses
docs.text:
Revise an illustration's SVG source. Evolve SVG text against a fixed brief; measure rendering validity and rubric-based composition with an independent judge. SVG Feedback Descent implements this with a Codex generator, a separate visual grader, and Greedy search. It is Experimental/live-only; creative quality remains sensitive to the rubric and judge, and improvement is not guaranteed.

Improve a scheduler in a simulator. The ADRS-inspired example evolves scheduler source against evaluator-owned workloads and a trusted simulator. Its deterministic fixture measures imbalance and probe work with separate development, selection, and final workloads. Production scheduling, latency measurement, and a live model proposer remain unimplemented.

Discover a model of a simulated world. Evolve a bounded discovery procedure; measure predictions on evaluator-owned observations. The Model Discovery Agent proposal records the research direction. The target world, observations, prediction grader, and application execution path remain to be built.

In all cases, data splits, budgets, permissions, and promotion remain outside candidate control. These ideas add no execution capability or evidence claim.

docs.title: Extract action items from meeting notes
docs.text:
Improve a reusable extraction prompt, measure its responses against annotated JSON, and inspect why an earlier revision stays selected after a regression. Adapt the prompt, responder, and development cases to your own extraction task.

Status: Shipped. This case study runs offline with handwritten revisions and response fixtures. No SDK, credentials, or model requests are involved.

docs.title: The concrete problem
docs.text:
A note says “We still need someone to check the pricing.” The starting prompt, Extract action items from the meeting notes as JSON., produces an invented owner and deadline in the fixture:

[{"task": "check the pricing", "owner": "Maya", "deadline": "Friday"}]

The independent expected answer preserves the action and missing information:

[{"task": "check the pricing", "owner": null, "deadline": null}]

We improve the reusable instruction. The meeting note and expected JSON belong to the evaluator; they are not edited by the candidate.

docs.title: The complete entry point
docs.text:
main.py · complete entry point
import meta_evolve as meta

from extraction_evaluation import evaluate
from meeting_cases import DEVELOPMENT
from prompt_variants import SEED, rewrite


def rewrite_prompt(parent):
    return rewrite(parent)  # Handwritten revision; replace with your model call.


def evaluate_prompt(prompt):
    return evaluate(prompt)  # Grades fixture responses on six development cases.


result = meta.improve(
    seed=SEED,
    proposer=rewrite_prompt,
    evaluator=evaluate_prompt,
    trials=2,
)

print("Handwritten model fixtures; no live LLM calls.")
best = result.best()
print("\nPrompt          | Development cases passed")
print("----------------|-------------------------")
for index, attempt in enumerate(result.trials()):
    name = "Starting prompt" if index == 0 else f"Revision {index}"
    passed = round(attempt.metrics["score"] * len(DEVELOPMENT))
    selected = " — selected" if attempt.artifact.id == best.id else ""
    print(f"{name:<15} | {passed}/{len(DEVELOPMENT)}{selected}")
print("\nSelected prompt:")
print(best.value)
usage = result.usage()
attempt_word = "attempt" if usage.trials == 1 else "attempts"
print(f"\nUsage: {usage.trials} revision {attempt_word}, {usage.evaluations} evaluations")
Component Role here Artifact / seed The initial extraction prompt string Proposer rewrite_prompt supplies a handwritten revision Evaluator / objective evaluate_prompt checks responses against six independent JSON answers Search improve uses bounded Greedy; two revisions after seed evaluation Feedback None in this first run; explicit feedback variant below External controls Notes, expected outputs, fixture responses, attempt bound, grading

rewrite_prompt changes instructions. evaluate_prompt runs all six fixture responses and measures correctness. A later revision can regress; selection keeps the best measured prompt rather than automatically keeping the last one.

docs.title: Setup and run
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12+. Download the source package and complete extraction example.

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./meta-evolve.zip
python -m zipfile -e extraction-example.zip .
python examples/learn/meeting_notes/main.py

Alternatively, use Python 3.12+, Git, and uv with a checkout:

git clone https://github.com/sentient-xyz/meta-evolve.git
cd meta-evolve
uv sync --locked

Run the following command from the repository root. Its adjacent output is executed by the documentation evidence checks:

uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/main.py
Output
Handwritten model fixtures; no live LLM calls.

Prompt          | Development cases passed
----------------|-------------------------
Starting prompt | 2/6
Revision 1      | 5/6 — selected
Revision 2      | 3/6

Selected prompt:
Extract agreed or explicitly needed action items as a JSON array. Use task phrases from the notes with fields task, owner, deadline. Use null for unstated owners or deadlines. Exclude unaccepted suggestions.

Usage: 2 revision attempts, 3 evaluations

The seed passes 2/6 development cases, the first revision 5/6, and the second 3/6. The selected instruction adds rules for unstated fields and unaccepted suggestions. These are eighteen graded fixture responses, with no live calls.

The six development cases cover assigned work, unassigned work, missing deadlines, unaccepted suggestions, mixed notes, and no actions. The grader requires source task phrases, stated owners/deadlines, and null when missing. Row order, whitespace, and terminal sentence punctuation may differ; arbitrary paraphrases and duplicate actions fail. Expected annotations are independent of the handwritten response fixtures.

The selected prompt still omits the unassigned dashboard check in this note:

Nina will publish the release notes by Monday. We need someone to verify the dashboard. Ava suggested redesigning the homepage, but nobody agreed.

Its response keeps Nina's action and excludes Ava's suggestion, but misses:

{"task": "verify the dashboard", "owner": null, "deadline": null}

That omission explains the remaining failed case. The first command does not execute the three reserved final cases. The companion below runs them only after selection.

docs.title: Supply recorded feedback
docs.text:
The same case study also demonstrates explicit feedback and a reserved final check. The proposer reads published failed development cases; reserved answers remain unavailable to rewriting and selection.

uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/prompt_feedback.py
Output
Without feedback: 5/6 development cases
With feedback: 6/6 development cases
Separate final check after selection: 3/3 reserved cases
Handwritten fixtures demonstrate separation, not generalization.

docs.title: Adapt and inspect
docs.text:
Replace the handwritten response/rewrite functions with your model calls, keeping case grading independent. model_integration.py provides the example-owned integration seam; a real wrapper must report usage and retain typed failures. The entire supporting source is below, including the case data and grader.

In a scratch checkout, change trials=2 to trials=1 in main.py. Predict the same 5/6 selected prompt, with one revision and two evaluations; the regressing second attempt disappears. Restore the limit afterward. Arbitrary prompt edits have no fixture responses and fail explicitly. A wrong response is a valid low score; a failed model call has a typed failure and no measurement. Fixture improvements are not measurements of a model learning or generalization to unseen meeting notes.

docs.title: Continue the same example
docs.text:
These companions keep the same prompts, meeting notes, and independent grader. Run the commands from the repository root. Every command runs offline with handwritten fixtures.

Companion Run Expected result Define better uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/define_better.py Stop at 5/6 after one revision and two evaluations. Inspect results uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/inspect_results.py Retain the 3/6 regression; compare the winner's actual and expected JSON. Change search uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/search_prompts.py Greedy reaches 6/6; BestOfN reaches 5/6 under the same attempt limit. Use feedback uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/prompt_feedback.py Development improves from 5/6 to 6/6; the selected prompt then passes 3/3 reserved cases. Inspect failed calls uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/failed_calls.py Wrong responses score zero; failed calls retain typed failures without scores. Keep a run uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/keep_run.py Reopen saved history, then resume a separate unfinished run from one attempt to two.

Define better. The first run uses all two allowed revisions. This companion adds a satisfaction threshold of 5 / 6 through Task and Experiment, the expanded declaration path. The first revision reaches that threshold, so search stops before trying the regression. A limit says how much work may happen; satisfaction says when the measured result is good enough to stop.

Inspect results. All measured attempts remain in result.trials(), while result.lineage() follows only the selected prompt's ancestry: seed -> improved. The command reads retained evaluation evidence to print the mixed notes, actual JSON, and expected JSON. Comparing those arrays reveals the missing verify the dashboard action without running the response fixture again.

Change search. Both runs use the same varied proposer, grader, initial prompt, and recorded random seed, with four revision attempts and five evaluations each. Greedy builds on its current best prompt; BestOfN always revises the starting prompt. The output shows each parent-to-revision step and names the comparison winner. This fixture demonstrates how parent selection changes the available revisions; it does not establish that one policy always performs better. meeting_components.py records the evaluator's configuration so comparisons keep the model, data, and grading implementation fixed.

Use feedback. Feedback is off in the first run. This companion explicitly supplies bounded, recorded ancestor evidence to the proposer. It builds a report from the latest observation of each development case and keeps only failures. After the first revision, that report contains only the mixed-notes omission. The handwritten rewriter uses it to choose the complete prompt. After selection, a separate evaluator call runs the three reserved final-check cases. Those cases never enter the search or the rewrite report; their fixture results make no generalization claim.

Inspect failed calls. A completed response containing prose instead of JSON can be graded and earns zero. An unavailable evaluator supplies no measurement, so the run has no winner; result.inspect() still exposes its failure. A failed rewrite creates no candidate artifact. The example prints these distinct outcomes instead of turning a call failure into a low score.

Keep a run. Saving a local improve() run permits read-only reopening but does not make that run resumable. The companion then creates a separate durable-local run with registered deterministic components, closes its session after one revision, closes storage, and resumes the remaining work. It checks that the complete event history equals an uninterrupted fixture run. Storage lives in a temporary directory and is deleted when the command exits.

docs.title: Bring your own model
docs.text:
Run model_integration_demo.py from the repository root with uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/model_integration_demo.py. Its example-local fake client replaces both functions without credentials or an SDK. All responses and telemetry are synthetic, with no actual charges. It prints 6/6 development cases, 18 response calls plus two rewrites, and usage of 148 tokens, 64 spend-micros, and 5.5 seconds. After selection, its separate 3/3 reserved check adds three calls, 21 tokens, 9 spend-micros, and 0.75 seconds; development history stays unchanged. Inspect FakeClient.requests for the inputs at both boundaries.

model_integration.py composes two user-owned functions: respond(prompt, notes) and rewrite(parent, report). Both return meta.ProposalResult with text or a typed failure plus reported usage. See SDK accounting and tools for result fields and usage reporting. The three final-check calls are separate from the 20-call development bound. No SDK is installed or called by import.
