At the flagship's second proposal that is nine operations, ten results, and ten records against a declared ten, ten, and ten — the caps are reached exactly, with one operation slot spare, and a third proposal fails closed rather than widening a limit.

Encodability is decided before any byte length or digest, because both begin with the same encode. A lone surrogate cannot become UTF-8, and a validator that raises on it is not a validator — the producer never emits one, which is the reason only a hostile payload reaches that check.

Nesting is bounded too, and separately, because a byte count does not catch it: roughly 1,800 bytes of nested arrays sits under every size limit and still exhausts the stack in parsing, in the canonical re-encode, and in freezing. The bound is enforced on both sides — the producer refuses to publish a view its own reader would reject — and the reader keeps a recursion guard behind it so the refusal does not depend on the interpreter's limit.

The character cap is measured against what the schemas permit rather than what the flagship spends. Canonical serialization expands a control character roughly six-fold, so two complete 40 KiB views of adversarial-yet-legal surface values render to about 500,000 characters against a declared 512,000. Crossing it truncates an open, which is refused, so the failure is closed and typed — never a leak and never a low score. The arithmetic is derived from the declared limits in a test, so raising a limit or indexing another file fails loudly instead of silently overflowing a live run.

docs.title: Identity has to cover the code, not only the constants
docs.text:
The fixed registry records what a component reaches as a dependency closure and hashes the modules, so splitting or editing a source module moves the proposer's version. A live component has no registry behind it: configured_local hashes a version string and nothing else. Declaring the schemas, renderer, paths, limits, and granted access is therefore not enough — all of that can hold still while the code reading through it changes.

So the same closure is declared for the live path and hashed by the same shipped helper. Its own proposer is a closure over the SDK client, which implementation_digest refuses by design, so the digest is taken over the module-level adapter that closure delegates to and the modules it reads through.

The driver's own module is in that closure too. Rendering the prompt and reading the SDK response are as much the proposer's behaviour as the trusted adapter is, and neither shows up in a schema or a limit. The live evaluator gets the same treatment for the same reason: its suite digest, budget, timeouts, and published channels can all hold still while its code changes.

docs.title: What this is not
docs.text: It is not a filesystem, a Git history, or a generic source-view seam. The shipped list_source_paths, read_source, and diff_source operations are not widened to accept a harness artifact, and the local parent/prior comparison the prompt carries is example-owned rendering over two values the adapter already holds rather than an audited diff operation. It is a Meta-Harness-inspired evaluator-owned mechanism retrieved through Meta-Evolve's audited experience reader, not a reproduction of that paper's system, benchmarks, or reported gains.

docs.title: Author API comparison decisions
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

September 18, 2026: #314's optional decisions, following the foundation. The executable study and evidence record retain the baselines, assertions, receipts, and limits. These engineering traces establish semantic properties; they are not independent usability measurements.

docs.title: 1. Adopt budget-led preset defaults; retain counting names
docs.text:
The duplicate ordinary allowance is avoidable:

# Current: repeating 25, or knowing to opt into max_trials=None.
task = meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate, budget=meta.Budget(trials=25))
experiment = meta.Experiment(task=task, seed=seed, proposer=propose,
                             search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=25))

# Selected 0.2 declaration; not available merely because this design is published.
experiment = meta.Experiment(task=task, seed=seed, proposer=propose,
                             search=meta.Greedy())

Both forms still require choosing a proposer, evaluator, and external ceiling. The alternative removes one duplicated amount and the need to know an opt-in sentinel. It adds no public import, callback wrapper, or authority-bearing object. Experiment(search=None) follows the same ordinary Greedy rule.

Selected rule: for Greedy, BestOfN, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch, omitted/None max_trials uses the effective finite Budget.trials. If no finite trial ceiling exists, resolve to the existing finite fallback: 20, or 100 for TreeSearch. Keeping TreeSearch's established fallback avoids an unrelated search change. Explicit integers keep their voluntary-stop meaning; they never widen external authority. improve(trials=20) retains its current small, bounded contract. BestOfK, custom search, and candidate-policy programs keep their own meaning; do not inject an ordinary preset limit into them.

Resolve once in shared preset binding after #315 resolves the execution budget. Persist a concrete integer in search configuration before work; reconstruction uses that recorded integer. No new event, coordinator branch, or storage schema is needed. Exact policy manifests will change; historical replay does not.

Evidence: with a 25-attempt task budget, bare Greedy currently performs 20 attempts; the alternative performs 25. This is an intentional default change, not a claim of an algorithmic improvement. Explicit equivalent configurations produced identical histories. Zero, two, and unbounded task allowances were exercised across all five presets; failed proposals still terminate when only evaluation/token ceilings exist. Custom search stopped at one attempt and BestOfK at its own two-attempt limit. Wide cohorts remain refused locally; the separate serial distributed capture establishes their admitted recovery path.

Migration: write an explicit old limit to preserve an old declaration's work amount. max_trials=None without a finite task/run ceiling changes from an error to finite fallback; document this alongside bare-default changes. Keep existing stop-reason precedence when budget and voluntary limit coincide.

Retain Budget.trials, Usage.trials, improve(trials=...), max_trials, and Run.trials(). The experiment did not establish a benefit sufficient to rename all of them together. Teach that attempts exclude the seed, the history includes its bootstrap record, and evaluations include authorized seed evaluation.

docs.title: 2. Retain ordered objectives
docs.text:
# Retained public form: primary objective first.
meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate,
          objectives=(meta.Maximize("quality", satisfy=2), meta.Minimize("cost")))

# Compared alternative, isolated in the study.
primary_task(evaluator=evaluate, objective=meta.Maximize("quality", satisfy=2),
             metrics=(meta.Minimize("cost"),))

The alternative makes primary intent explicit but adds another keyword and a factory; it still needs both metric directions, required-measurement rules, and primary-only search semantics. No wrapper or required author decision disappears. Keeping Minimize under a keyword called metrics also needs an explanation that it configures alternate queries, not mixed-direction search.

Both declarations selected quality 2 and cost 0 under the same history; scalar evaluation, threshold stopping, missing required metrics, and Specialists were checked. Specialists still uses the primary direction for its metric frontiers. Neither spelling establishes Pareto optimization. Retain the tuple and teach its ordering beside the declaration. No migration or new durable identity is needed; a future objective change requires new evidence and a new issue.

docs.title: 3. Adopt resource-only component reports
docs.text:
# Current SDK result and nested forwarding.
meta.ProposalResult(candidate=candidate, usage=meta.Usage(tokens=7, spend_micros=None))
meta.EvaluationResult(metrics=metrics, usage=inner.usage().without_counts)

# Selected 0.2 authoring surface.
meta.ProposalResult(candidate=candidate, usage=meta.Resources(tokens=7, spend_micros=None))
meta.EvaluationResult(metrics=metrics, usage=inner.usage().resources)

Introduce one immutable Resources(tokens=0, spend_micros=0, wall_seconds=0.0) value. It has no trial/evaluation fields. Run/domain Usage retains its current counts and serialized meaning; Usage.resources projects the three resource dimensions. Rich author returns use Resources; plain candidate, scalar, and mapping returns remain direct. Keep structural/kernel outcome records on their existing Usage boundary.

Normalize Resources to zero-count Usage once at the adapter boundary. Rich result construction must reject engine-count fields rather than silently give components the impression that those counts are authoritative. Preserve all current value validation and failure accounting. The study converts explicitly only because it runs against 0.1; authors must not need to_usage() wrappers in the shipped alternative. Migrate rich Usage returns in the same release; retaining durable/domain Usage does not imply retaining two author conventions.

This adds one public type but removes two irrelevant component fields and makes the nested projection state what it returns. Both SDK and nested policy evaluation need that distinction. It does not remove the author's decision about which work to charge. Retained inner history must not charge again; forward inner resources plus the evaluator's own resources exactly once.

Evidence: two SDK proposals retained 14 tokens with unknown spend; two billed failures retained 10 tokens and 6 micro-USD with only the seed evaluation. Resources rejected a trial-count constructor argument and preserved unknown spend through aggregation. Policy evolution retained ten inner stores while its development outer run recorded two attempts, three evaluations, and 14 tokens. Resource projection equalled the existing count-stripped total.

Keep spend_micros=0 as known free and None as unknown. The frozen old histories retain both unknown-spend cases, including refusal of further work under a monetary ceiling. Summed elapsed work is not wall-clock duration or hard preemption. The implementation child must add integrated fresh/resumed resource conversion, partial-failure, overage, and unknown-spend tests.

docs.title: 4. Retain Experiment; do not add Improver in 0.2
docs.text:
# Retained reuse.
other = dataclasses.replace(experiment, task=other_task, seed=other_seed)

# Compared alternative: one extra object, with the same external authorities.
procedure = Improver(proposer=propose, search=search, context=feedback)
other = procedure.experiment(task=other_task, seed=other_seed,
                             experience=grant, registry=registry)

The sketch groups proposer/search/feedback selection. Task, independent evaluation, hard budget, seed, access grant, random seed, and registry remain explicit outside it. It does not remove their required decisions or turn live callables into serializable candidate data. Freezing an outer object does not freeze its functions or mutable registry.

Reusing across two tasks/seeds produced equivalent results using both forms. The study then reconstructed each real declaration through the sketch while running the actual methods: 15 ordinary runs in AutoResearch, 13 in policy evolution, and 15 in ACE, per comparison side. Values, counts, failures, lineage, budgets, selected evidence, and retention agreed. Independently allocated storage paths were normalized explicitly; that is not an assertion that every storage-bearing event byte is identical.

The class did not remove the existing recipe interpreter in AutoResearch or the policy-suite/episode protocol in policy evolution. ACE still required development, search, consolidation, and final checking. Its 14 wrapper sessions included six during search; the fixture bills zero resources, so equal zero resource totals do not prove that those extra sessions are free in a live run. AutoResearch retains score summaries of inner work; policy evolution retains inner histories; ACE retains search history plus in-memory phase outcomes. Do not flatten those distinctions into a generic run result.

The requirement for demonstrated simplification in two compositions was not met. Retain Experiment and explicit Python orchestration. Teach the conceptual procedure as composition of existing values; data-only candidate configuration still selects permitted behavior through trusted interpretation. No new core class, registry placement rule, serialization, or coordinator is authorized.

docs.title: 315–#317 implement the frozen foundation independently. The two adopted
docs.text: comparisons have separate children under #313: #320, preset allowances and #321, component resources.

docs.title: 318 integrates their examples,
docs.text:
imports, and one migration guide; #319 releases them together. Ordered objectives, procedure objects, count renames, root-export pruning, and changing the default meaning of unknown spend are closed as retain current behavior for 0.2, not unresolved requirements that block the release.

Keep ordinary imports at the root and advanced APIs in their existing namespaces. The study needed Specialists from meta_evolve.policies; hiding ordinary declarations behind additional namespaces did not help any journey. Preserve strict Run.compare() controls: a different-proposer scientific study needs its own explicit protocol, not a weaker comparator.

docs.title: API contracts and release decisions: plan for #314
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 18, 2026 for #314, under #313. This page owns the work order and evidence needed for the decision issue. The program plan, behavior contracts, and comparison specifications own their existing detail; this page does not duplicate or supersede them.

Execution is recorded in the foundation decision, comparison decisions, and baseline and verification evidence. This page retains the work order; those records own the resulting decisions.

docs.title: Two checkpoints
docs.text:
Foundation checkpoint: identify the baseline, adopt the release policy in the canonical roadmap, freeze the three behavior contracts, and preserve the evidence needed to test migration. Record a dated decision with revision links in #314 and link it from #315–#317. Those three implementation issues can then start while optional comparisons continue.

Design completion: decide allowance/counting, objectives, component resource reports, and a reusable procedure using the same real journeys. Record both adopted and rejected alternatives. Create implementation children only for adopted changes; every deferred question needs an explicit release disposition. Close #314 only after both checkpoints, not when the foundation alone is ready.

This issue produces reviewed contracts, runnable comparisons, historical fixtures, and an implementation handoff. Production behavior belongs to its implementation children. It does not ship a package, publish the documentation site, or complete M11 concurrency.

docs.title: Selected release direction
docs.text:
The user explicitly selected a pre-1.0 compatibility reset and one coordinated breaking release on September 18. Use 0.2.0 as the working release target; confirm the tag/package inventory before reserving the final version.

The earlier through-1.x commitments must be revised explicitly as part of the foundation checkpoint. Do not treat 0.1.0 as implicit permission to ignore them, and do not require an artificial 1.x/2.0 sequence after this policy choice. No intermediate compatibility release is required. Useful migration diagnostics remain in scope; a permanent legacy dispatch mode does not.

The reset permits a deliberate removal or default change; it does not select one automatically. Inventory keyword run(), dictionary CLI factories, positional callback context, preset inheritance/defaults, result fields, and public imports. For each, record retain, replace, or remove, with replacement code and the release boundary. Avoid removing an unrelated spelling merely because a breaking release is available.

Existing source/storage facts remain historical truth. Keep read-only access to supported histories and fail closed on incompatible resume. Do not promise cross-version execution simply because Python syntax or stored schemas match. The coordinated release is gated by #318/#319 even when its implementation PRs are reviewed separately.

docs.title: 1. Pin the baseline before experiments
docs.text: The September 18 read found local HEAD and remote main both at c04ec6b4b949b8a2702779107e25acd24feb8020; pyproject.toml declares 0.1.0.

docs.title: 297's documentation/source-docstring patch and the API design documents are
docs.text:
still uncommitted. GitHub returned no release entries; this does not establish whether a package has been uploaded to another registry.

Preserve existing work and distinguish these baselines:

Baseline Purpose Identification Main before #297 Historical source and manifest behavior Commit, exact package, lock/environment, import location Reviewed #297 integration Reference/current-behavior baseline Separate commit or complete patch/file hashes, package hash, verification record Each API comparison Proposed declaration or normalization Its source revision, baseline used, and configuration delta

Use an isolated checkout or source snapshot and non-editable installations for cross-version checks. Do not let checkout imports supply missing files. Keep the baseline components and their import paths available to reconstruct the old environment. Store generated captures outside the source checkout until they are reviewed; exploratory notebooks stay in gitignored notebooks/.

Publish the reviewed design documents and baseline evidence with a dedicated

docs.title: 314 PR once #297's exact integration state is identified. #297 retains its own
docs.text:
scope and remaining acceptance checks; this issue does not silently mark them complete or claim publication. Use revision-specific links in the GitHub issues once those files exist remotely.

Output: one concise baseline record containing source/package/lock hashes, Python and installation details, current issue/merge state, fixture inventory, and links to reused verification. Link the #297 verification rather than copy its historical test counts as if they certified the new work.

docs.title: 2. Capture the compatibility cases
docs.text:
Start with existing tests and freeze only missing historical evidence. The checked-in tests/fixtures/v3_durable_run/ covers an older store/record case; its directory name is not proof of its physical store version. Most other tests generate stores with whichever package is currently running, so those tests alone do not establish compatibility with an older adapter.

Case to preserve Existing starting point Required observation Complete success and failed seed test_run_comparisons.py, reference cases Old values/counts/cost remain readable; failure has no invented score Interrupted registered run test_resume.py, tests/_faults.py Legal committed frontier, matching-runtime continuation, explicit upgrade outcome Optional second callback argument / variadics test_callable_adapters.py, manifest tests Unchanged function source cannot hide changed invocation behavior Inherited proposal limit test_preset_budget_inheritance.py, resume tests Recorded integer and stop behavior survive changed defaults Pushed feedback test_resume_context.py Recorded observations and context manifest remain attributable Unknown spend, with and without a monetary ceiling test_unknown_spend_resume.py Unknown remains unknown; no lost cost or newly authorized evaluation Admitted serial distributed run test_distributed_resume.py Real Session.start(..., mode="distributed") capabilities and recovery frontier Older schema and read-only access test_durable_format.py, test_read_only_storage.py Preserve supported migration behavior and verify that read-only access does not migrate/write

Capture with the identified old package before production semantics change. Keep stores closed and copy their complete committed state; do not truncate an event stream or synthesize a dispatcher fixture that production admission would reject. Record exact source dependencies, configuration, IDs, capabilities, stored schema versions, effective budget, resolved search, expected outcomes, and content hashes. Exclude credentials and live provider data.

For each capture, distinguish old-runtime resume, new-runtime read, and new-runtime resume. The latter may correctly refuse. Schema migration, when already supported, is a separate explicitly writable operation on a copy; never call it a read-only check. Test new-runtime interruption/resume separately as a positive case rather than requiring the new adapter to execute old code.

Output: a small reviewed fixture set plus a compatibility matrix with expected pass/refusal and its reason. Reuse existing fixtures where sufficient; do not build a general fixture-management framework.

docs.title: 3. Freeze the foundation decisions
docs.text:
Use the proposed contracts as the starting text. Resolve the following details into explicit decisions before marking the foundation checkpoint complete:

Decision Recommended contract Evidence to attach Partial ceilings Inherit omitted dimensions; reject explicit widening; resolve once before policy binding Per-dimension cases, zero/mixed overrides, pre-work refusal, normalized facts Plain callback invocation Parent positional, named keyword-only context opt-in; normal configuration defaults preserved Signature matrix, migration inventory, structural-dispatch trace, one-call failure cases Invocation verification Automatically include the framework binding/dispatch implementation in registered proposer verification Same-function/different-invocation digest probe and pre-work resume refusal Run reporting Existing RunSummary gains lifecycle/rankability/stop reason; score becomes optional; empty winning lineage when unrankable Four valid lifecycle/rankability cases, existing field consumers, one-snapshot query trace Winner/comparison behavior Keep strict winner queries, comparison controls, error precedence, and actual tie semantics Existing comparison tests and explicit no-measurement cases CLI outcome Run/resume reports unrankable outcomes and returns 1; successful inspection returns 0; usage errors remain 2 Command/exit-code table, including seed-selected and incomplete histories Compatibility surface Adopt the pre-1.0 reset and enumerate actual retained/replaced/removed forms Before/after calls and fields, affected tests, migration scope, release note outline

Source tracing already locates the invocation seam: registry_support.resolve_component() hashes the registered function and its declared dependencies. Registry.manifests_for() assembles the manifests; prepare_resume() verifies them before run_support.resolve_registered_components() constructs the callable adapters. run_support.component_proposer() gives a declared runner precedence, then structural .propose() over __call__. CallableProposer.declared() currently serves both structural methods and callable objects carrying a component declaration. Choose invocation by the selected role, not merely by that constructor name; include wrapped component references in the dispatch inventory too.

The verification proposal belongs at that registry/adapter boundary. Prototype the smallest sufficient binding/dispatch source dependency set; do not hash the entire repository or require users to declare the library's own dependencies. Keep caller configuration dependencies separate and preserve source checking. An isolated digest probe is useful evidence; integration belongs to #316.

Add the named Author API revision gate to docs/milestones.md and its technical staging to docs/implementation-plan.md in the foundation PR. Explain explicitly which previous compatibility promises the pre-1.0 policy supersedes. The programming model continues to describe executable behavior; point readers to the release policy without advertising future signatures as shipped.

Review the current promise sites in docs/programming-model.md, the M10 and preset-inheritance roadmap sections, their implementation-plan entries, docs/design/m10-local-author.md, and cli.py's documentation. Preserve dated historical facts; amend current commitments and link the new policy instead of rewriting history. Update contract tests that encode promises deliberately.

Output: a dated foundation decision linked from #315–#317, the exact contracts/release treatment, the historical fixture matrix, and a focused implementation/test/migration handoff for each child. Keep unchecked work in

docs.title: 314 visible; publishing a plan alone does not complete this checkpoint.
4. Compare the broader designs in order
docs.text:
Run the six journeys against the existing API and the alternative. Use offline components and real example composition; no paid calls or new runtime branch is needed. Start with the baseline code before writing an adapter for a preferred design.

Order Comparison First concrete exercise Decision boundary 1 Ordinary allowance Same Greedy/search comparison with current preset limits and one external proposal allowance One resolution site, recorded finite defaults, no loss of voluntary stopping; counting renames are a separate decision 2 Primary objective Quality/cost metrics, scalar evaluator, threshold, and alternate winner query Primary intent clearer while required metrics/directions and policy capabilities remain explicit 3 Component resources SDK success/failure and a nested policy evaluation Fewer opportunities to double-charge or inject engine counts, without forcing wrappers around simple returns 4 Reusable procedure Reuse across two tasks/seeds, then policy evolution, AutoResearch, and ACE Better than dataclasses.replace in at least two real compositions, with no authority expansion or forced flattening of stages

Stabilize the first three decisions before the procedure sketch so its example does not bundle four untested improvements into one apparently better API. Then perform one combined journey pass to expose interactions. A rejected optional change does not block the accepted ones.

Keep comparisons bounded: existing API plus one credible alternative per question, expanding only to resolve a demonstrated failure. For each, retain before/after code, required decisions, setup/imports, duplicated declarations, wrappers, error diagnosis, authority mapping, and migration cost. Check the same outcomes/counts/retention under equivalent configuration. Present any intentionally changed default/trajectory as its own experiment.

Output: one concise decision per question with observed evidence, selected spelling/semantics or reason to retain the existing API, compatibility impact, test gate, and linked implementation issue when adopted. Do not add root exports or production abstractions during the comparison merely to make the alternative importable. Prototype lowering is not evidence that durable registration or resume is already implemented.

docs.title: 5. Review and hand off
docs.text:
Use two reviewable changes within #314 rather than one large implementation:

  1. Foundation: publish baseline/fixtures, record the chosen pre-1.0 policy, add the canonical scope gate, and freeze the three behavior contracts. #315–#317 can proceed after this checkpoint.
  2. Design decisions: retain the runnable comparisons and conclusions, open adopted implementation children under #313, and update the parent dependency map. #318 consumes the final choices; #319 owns integrated release evidence.

For the foundation, verify fixture provenance, schema/read-only expectations, manifest sensitivity, the existing focused baseline tests, and documentation ownership/routes/build. For the comparisons, execute the retained deterministic scripts and their semantic checks from the identified environment. Full runtime and Docs CI belongs to the eventual integrated release; repeat broader checks earlier only when changed code or failures justify it.

Each record names its revision, environment, commands, actual results, and limits. Keep mathematical notation linked to the concept owner; keep studies of use separate from engineering traces. Selection, private evaluation, observation access, budgets, and promotion must retain their current owners.

docs.title: 314 is complete when both checkpoints are evidenced, all four optional
docs.text: questions have a disposition, accepted changes have actionable children, and no proposed API is presented as shipped. A production implementation or deployment is not part of closing this design issue.

docs.title: API documentation integration: plan for #318
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 18, 2026 for #318, under #313. This develops API-9 of the parent plan into a documentation integration slice. The foundation and comparison decisions settle the API choices; this issue makes their implemented result discoverable, coherent, and runnable.

docs.title: Baseline and dependency boundary
docs.text:
The inspected checkout is c04ec6b4b949b8a2702779107e25acd24feb8020 plus substantial local work, including #297 and #314–#317. Those changes are not represented by the base commit alone. At the September 18 check, #314–#318, #320, and #321 were open; the #314 review PR was open at 6465779ca6b26dda5e15d5453e72546969ccc28b. Do not interpret an open issue as absence of local implementation, or a local verification as a merge.

Dependency Observed state Required handoff to #318 #297, reference foundation Local generated entries, executable reference cases, and verification record exist. Keep their source/rendering ownership and current edge-case coverage. #314, contract decisions Foundation and comparisons select one coordinated 0.2.0 target; PR review remains open. Identify the accepted revision and retain/replace inventory. #315, partial budgets Resolver, tests, migration guide, and verification record exist locally. Integrate the implemented per-dimension rule and its exact baseline qualification. #316, callback context Invocation adapter, registered verification, migrated examples, and guide exist locally. Preserve role-specific dispatch and the actual cross-version resume refusal. #317, reporting Summary/CLI changes, tests, and guide exist locally. Cover reportable failure, strict selection, and pending seed history consistently. #320, preset defaults Selected; inspected presets still default to 20/100, and explicit None still requires a finite ceiling. Require implemented binding, signatures, migration cases, and focused tests before teaching the new default. #321, resource reports Selected; Resources is absent from the inspected root package. Require the implemented export, result types, conversion, examples, and tests before generating its reference.

Planning, route inventories, and review of existing pages can start now. Finish the current-release examples and reference only against a source revision containing all five accepted behavior changes. Do not import proposed APIs into the runnable documentation or substitute a compatibility shim to simulate them.

The roadmap gate owns release scope and the revised pre-1.0 compatibility policy. #319 owns version confirmation, package publication, and the deployed meta-evolve-docs check. #318 supplies verified source documentation and its installable examples; it does not bump the version or claim the release has already happened. M11 concurrency remains outside this gate.

docs.title: Target reader story
docs.text:
Keep the progression: run one loop, configure it, inspect its outcomes, compose several stages, then evaluate a procedure as the candidate. The parser remains the complete credential-free entrance. improve(trials=...) stays the small path; expanded examples use Task, Experiment, Session, and Run.

The integrated 0.2 documentation must explain these five changes:

  1. Execution budget overrides inherit omitted task ceilings and refuse explicit widening. Show the effective budget, not just the sparse request.
  2. Plain callbacks request framework input through keyword-only context. Structural proposer, runner, and PatchProposer interfaces keep their own explicit contracts; ordinary configuration defaults are not framework input.
  3. summary() reports lifecycle, rankability, stop reason, cost, and an optional score. Winner queries and comparisons remain strict; zero is a valid score.
  4. Bare/None limits for the five selected presets inherit a finite effective trial ceiling, otherwise falling back to 20, or 100 for TreeSearch. Explicit integers are voluntary limits; improve, BestOfK, and custom search retain their contracts. Recorded limits never re-inherit during replay.
  5. Rich author results report Resources; Run.usage() still reports Usage. Nested authors use inner.usage().resources and charge intended work once. Plain candidates, scalars, and mappings need no result wrapper.

Keep the decisions to retain ordered objectives, Experiment, counting names, keyword run, dictionary CLI factories, and existing import namespaces. No Improver, singular-objective constructor, attempts rename, root pruning, or change to known-zero/unknown spend is part of #318.

Notation stays optional and links to its existing owner: I is the procedure, E independent evaluation, B external allowance, H authorized observations, and R retained results. An Experiment is a declaration; it is not a new universal procedure artifact. A composed method may retain several runs or a method-specific result.

docs.title: Findings that determine the edits
docs.text:
Inspected surface Finding Integration action Three migration guides Budget, callback, and summary guides exist, but there is no common migration entry in mkdocs.yml or the guide index. Add one versioned entry point and retain the detailed routes. Preset descriptions Programming model and reference examples correctly describe the current opt-in inheritance behavior. Replace that account when #320 lands; keep before-behavior only in migration/history contexts. Provider/reference examples Usage(...) constructs author reports; nested examples use without_counts. Migrate rich author boundaries after #321; retain domain/structural Usage where it is still the contract. Component composition reference It says Experiment combines a Budget, which can suggest a constructor field that does not exist. State precisely: task ceiling, experiment components, execution-time partial restriction. Root reference Four tiers cover 79 actual exports; ordinary and advanced routes already exist. Add the implemented Resources entry once, with no new export-count target or competing inventory. Status and evidence Source implementations, the unchanged 0.1.0 package metadata, design decisions, and publication are described on different pages. Use one consistent account of source availability versus coordinated release; preserve dated evidence. Long canonical/editorial files Programming model is already 488 lines; editorial conventions are 299. Replace outdated passages, link detail owners, preserve anchors, and avoid append-only duplication.

These are integration targets, not a claim that #320/#321 behavior is already available or that every matching old spelling is erroneous.

docs.title: 1. Create one migration entrance
docs.text:
Add docs/guides/migrate-to-0.2.md as the versioned migration owner once the accepted behavior is available in the documentation's package. Keep it normally below 300 lines. Its opening identifies the source/release it describes and links to the roadmap's release policy instead of redefining that policy.

Use this order:

  • Choose the right package: documentation and downloaded source must describe the same revision. Do not prescribe installing a published 0.2 package before publication or infer source equivalence from a 0.1.0 version string.
  • Review the five changes: one before/after/action table, with retained spellings listed briefly so callers do not perform unnecessary rewrites.
  • Update plain callbacks and rich returns: show a small complete example using keyword-only context and Resources, plus the parent-only alternative.
  • Check how much work runs: demonstrate partial overrides and the 25-attempt preset case. Explain explicit old limits for callers retaining old work amounts, and the newly valid max_trials=None fallback without a finite trial ceiling.
  • Handle results and commands: check primary_score is not None, retain strict winner handling, and show the CLI's stdout plus exit 1 for unrankable run/resume results. A selected seed does not establish improvement.
  • Open old history deliberately: separate read-only access, supported schema migration, same-environment continuation, and incompatible-source refusal.

Retain budget-override-migration.md, callback-context-migration.md, and run-summary-migration.md with their existing URLs and useful anchors. They own the detailed edge cases; the versioned guide links to them and they link back. Coordinate detailed preset/resource guidance with #320/#321 rather than creating duplicate guides if those owners already supply it. The migration entrance is one route through the material, not a concatenation of every contract table.

Add “Migrate to 0.2” under Guides, an upgrade link in guides/index.md, and concise links from the programming model/reference and README's relevant setup section. Avoid adding five top-level navigation entries or reorganizing unrelated menus.

docs.title: 2. Reconcile canonical, reference, and example owners
docs.text:
Owner Concrete work and acceptance programming-model.md Keep the core-object story and ordered objectives. Replace preset inheritance/default text; distinguish component Resources from run Usage; link detailed callback and result contracts. Retain compatibility forms selected by #314. architecture.md Check counting, authority, failure, snapshot, and replay wording against the final behavior. Do not copy constructor signatures or add a new layer for a documentation category. milestones.md, implementation-plan.md, project/status.md Reconcile source availability and selected release scope using actual implementation evidence. Keep M11 serial restrictions and publication boundaries explicit. Preserve historical decisions as historical. reference/api.md, _includes/api-authoring.md, public docstrings Put Resources with rich author result construction and describe Usage with returned run accounting. Render its three fields, result usage types, preset defaults/resolution, and optional summary score accurately. Preserve the four-tier partition and namespaced extensions. reference/api-examples.md, examples/learn/reference_cases.py Extend existing extracted cases for inherited/fallback limits, Resources, nested forwarding, and combined migration. Keep exact printed outputs sourced from executable cells; preserve failure/counting cases already added by #315–#317. Limits, evaluation/budgets, and runs/results guides Distinguish external ceilings, voluntary policy stops, seed/evaluation counts, failed attempts, and post-call resource overages. Teach one ordinary allowance declaration without changing custom-policy semantics. Providers guide, reference/sdk-boundary.md, current SDK examples Migrate rich author reports to Resources; keep user-owned clients, actual billed/unknown spend, typed failure, and explicit feedback. Do not introduce Resources into the first plain-candidate example merely for completeness. Feedback guide/reference and current callable examples Audit by invocation role, including direct calls. Do not globally rewrite every two-input method or callback: structural ports, runners, and patch callbacks remain explicit interfaces. Result lesson, CLI/browser guides, durable operations Explain complete/incomplete separately from rankability, strict comparison, pending seed history, new required summary fields, and actual CLI streams/exit codes. Reporting never implies resume eligibility. reference/components.md, composition worksheet, contributor tour Correct declaration/allowance ownership; map roles to actual source/test owners. Teach reuse through existing declarations and explicit Python orchestration.

Use existing snippet extraction and method catalogs. Keep runnable guide code owned by one source; small illustrative signatures must be identified as such. If a reference fixture grows too large, split by independently executable case rather than moving the duplicate code into a second documentation harness.

Audit searches are discovery tools, not automated rewrites. Classify hits for Usage, without_counts, positional context, old defaults, and old compatibility promises as current author code, structural/domain code, migration before-code, or historical evidence. Preserve frozen fixtures, recorded component source, durable bytes, and explicitly historical notebooks. Current maintained notebook supplements migrate with their source and output checks.

Source docstrings participate in exact-source manifests. When changing them, record affected manifest differences and validate the final installed source; “documentation-only” does not by itself establish executable-resume compatibility.

docs.title: 3. Walk all six journeys on the integrated source
docs.text:
Journey Primary surfaces Evidence of completion First loop README, Start here, parser source, core-object example Fresh install runs the complete parser with two successor attempts/three evaluations; no new mandatory object or credentials. SDK and feedback Providers, SDK boundary, feedback guide, simulated SDK tests Keyword context and grants are distinct; rich report types are correct; successes and typed failures retain billable/unknown resources. Search comparison Search lesson, limits guide, preset reference, policy examples Show 25 budget-led attempts versus explicit old limits, finite fallback, zero work, and exact seed counts; policy-specific behavior remains stated. Failed-run diagnosis API cases, result lesson, summary migration, CLI/browser Valid unrankable/incomplete histories report costs without a winner; absent score differs from zero/tie; commands preserve documented outcomes. Reopen/resume Persistence guide, durability reference, registered examples, migration hub Old supported histories are readable; same-runtime recovery works; incompatible manifests refuse before new work. Package/source identity is discoverable. Composition/meta-evolution Policy, AutoResearch, ACE, nested-evaluation and composition guides Preserve actual stages, private/final checks, retained evidence, and one-time resource forwarding. Avoid new procedure-class or RSI claims.

For composition, verify the three distinct contracts explicitly:

  • Policy evaluation keeps reopenable inner histories and forwards intended physical resources without importing inner logical counts. Inspect the actual PolicyEvaluation.outer_usage boundary after #321; do not change that record's type merely to simplify a guide.
  • AutoResearch keeps inner score summaries, performs final work in report(), and currently reports outer-only usage. A new resource type does not silently make its totals include nested or post-selection work.
  • ACE has development, search, consolidation, and held-out stages, including work outside its search run. Preserve phase accounting and partial failure evidence; equal zero-cost fixtures do not prove live work is free.

Maintain the notation's actual result boundary and external evaluation/grants. The strict Run.compare() control over the authorized proposer remains; a different-proposer study needs its own declared comparison protocol.

docs.title: 4. Verification and handoff
docs.text:
First identify one stable integrated checkout or isolated snapshot containing the selected implementations and documentation. Record all relevant patches and untracked source, not just HEAD. Preserve other ongoing work and do not fold unrelated changes into this issue's claimed verification.

  1. Run focused snippet, reference, navigation, and affected guide checks during editing. Extend existing tests for reader-visible changes: Resources/default rendering, optional summary score, actual migration actions, and fresh setup. Keep __all__ as the export-coverage owner; do not assert an arbitrary count.
  2. Run the maintained Docs workflow selection and strict MkDocs build against the final snapshot. Validate old routes/fragments and new cross-links without freezing prose or adding a parallel route registry.
  3. Install the exact generated source ZIP into a fresh environment outside the checkout. Execute the documented downloads and SDK fixtures with simulated HTTP responses, and confirm imports/source hashes come from that install. Reuse workflow owners rather than copying a stale command list into this plan.
  4. Inspect changed pages at desktop and narrow widths: long signatures, tables, required setup expansion, code copy, migration navigation, optional scores, and offline links. Capture actual observations; an unavailable browser check remains an unmet check, not an inferred pass.
  5. Recheck focused production cases only where documentation/fixtures exposed a gap, or changes invalidate prior evidence. The full integrated runtime and release gates belong to #319; the same exact-revision evidence can be reused when its scope suffices. No paid provider experiment is required.
  6. Add docs/project/api-documentation-verification.md after execution, linked from maintained project/evidence owners. Identify revision/patches, lock, package hash, manifest effects, counts/skips, logs, and manual-review limits. Preserve existing per-slice verification records instead of rewriting them into a misleading claim that all slices shared one compatibility baseline.

docs.title: Completion gate and first implementation pass
318 is complete when all five implemented changes have a coherent migration
docs.text:
route, each of the six journeys executes as documented, reference/imports match the installed package, historical URLs and evidence remain accurate, and the verification record identifies what was actually checked. Package publication, version confirmation, and hosted-site verification remain #319's completion gate; a passing local documentation build is not evidence of those actions.

Start by reconciling #320/#321's final source and collecting their migration notes. Then implement the migration entrance, reconcile the owner table, execute the six journeys, and finish the verification record. Treat these as passes within #318; no additional implementation abstraction or issue hierarchy is needed merely to carry out this documentation work.

docs.title: Author API foundation decision
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Decision date: September 18, 2026. This is #314's foundation handoff under #313. It freezes the behavior contracts; it does not make their proposed APIs available. The roadmap owns release scope and policy. The evidence record identifies both installed baselines and the historical captures. The separate comparison decisions finish the optional review.

docs.title: Foundation contracts
docs.text:
Slice Frozen decision Implementation owner Partial ceilings Execution overrides inherit every omitted/None dimension; explicit widening raises ValueError before work or committed run facts; zero is a real ceiling. #315 Plain proposer callbacks Parent positional; framework input only through named keyword-only context. Normal configuration defaults stay Python defaults; no probe calls or retry after body TypeError. #316 Registered invocation Automatically verify framework binding and dispatch source with the proposer implementation; refuse incompatible resume before any component work. #316 Run reporting Extend RunSummary with lifecycle/rankability/stop reason; optional score and empty winning lineage when nothing ranks; one coherent snapshot. #317 Selection/comparison Winner queries remain strict. Comparison requires two measurements; an absent score is neither a tie nor a losing score. Preserve controls and error precedence. #317

The contract tables own the signature matrix, per-dimension budget rule, comparison controls, and error cases. These are decisions, not open recommendations. Implementation can refine private seams without changing the public rules; a changed rule needs a recorded decision.

The callback distinction is by selected role. The explicit structural port still receives .propose(parent, context). Preserve declared-runner precedence, structural versus callable-object selection, wrapped registered references, validation hooks, and exact context identity. The binding/dispatch dependencies must cover all these routes while retaining the user's declared dependencies. Do not hash the entire library or ask users to register its own adapter code.

The digest experiment establishes that a new dependency changes the manifest of an unchanged callback, and that the existing resume verifier refuses it before work. It is not a replacement for #316's actual adapter integration and route tests. Do not weaken source verification to make old runs continue.

docs.title: Reporting and command outcomes
docs.text:
Situation Summary run / resume CLI exit Successful inspect exit Complete, rankable; seed may still win Measured score and selected lineage 0 0 Complete, unrankable Score None, empty winning lineage, retained costs 1 0 Incomplete, rankable Measured score, incomplete lifecycle, no stop reason Same rankability rule if rendered 0 Incomplete, unrankable Score None, incomplete lifecycle, retained costs Same rankability rule if rendered 0 Missing/corrupt history or execution error Existing typed error; no fabricated summary Existing domain-error exit Existing domain-error exit Invalid command usage Argument error 2 2

Do not claim the execution commands return normally after every interruption. The table defines rendering of a valid returned result; execution exceptions keep their existing behavior.

The distributed capture adds a required case: admitted genesis before seed evaluation. It is a valid incomplete, unrankable history. In 0.1, inspect() and usage() raise SearchNotStarted there. #317 must derive committed usage without requiring projection.search_state, and make summary/inspection/usage agree. The capture reader uses validated replay for this one historical state and identifies that limitation explicitly. Pending work is not completed usage.

docs.title: Release treatment
docs.text:
The selected boundary is one coordinated 0.2.0 release, subject to #319's final version/publication check. There is no mandatory intermediate compatibility release. The user explicitly authorized revising the former through-1.x promises. The following inventory determines what this release actually changes:

Surface Disposition in 0.2 Migration run(task=..., seed=..., proposer=...) Retain; typed Experiment is the documentation default. No forced rewrite. Dictionary CLI factories Retain with the existing deprecation warning. Returning Experiment remains preferred; no removal is scheduled by #314. Positional inferred callback context Replace with explicit keyword-only opt-in for plain callables. def propose(parent, *, context); review optional ctx/_context and variadics manually. Structural proposer port Retain. Do not rewrite adapter methods as ordinary callbacks. Whole-budget override interpretation Replace with partial restrictions. Omitted fields inherit; some previously rejected calls now execute. Winner-dependent summary Replace with reportable unrankable outcomes. Check rankability / primary_score is not None; migrate direct dataclass construction. Preset allowance defaults Replace, as specified by the comparison decision. Set explicit max_trials=20 (100 for TreeSearch) to retain the old voluntary limit. Rich component resource reports Replace their author-facing resource value with Resources; retain run/domain Usage. usage=Resources(...); forward inner.usage().resources. trials, history methods, objectives, Experiment Retain. No counting rename, Task rewrite, or Improver migration. Existing root/advanced imports Retain; add Resources with its implementation. #318 organizes discovery by author role; no export-count target. SearchProgram.next() / functional search / BestOfK Retain their extension and algorithm contracts. No unrelated coordinator or policy migration.

No unrelated public spelling is removed just because a breaking release is available. The optional additions are specified separately; the foundation fixes do not wait for them. Their implementation owners are #320 for preset defaults and #321 for resources.

docs.title: Compatibility evidence and handoff
docs.text:
Seven physical schema-4 stores capture old complete and interrupted runs. The matching installed runtime resumed every case with identical final events and usage to uninterrupted execution. The #297 reference package read all seven unchanged and refused every resume before work because exact policy/context source changed, despite those package changes being docstrings only.

Supported old histories remain readable. Supported schema migrations are explicitly writable operations on a copy, never a read-only side effect. An old callback's unchanged source is insufficient evidence of invocation compatibility. Resume requires compatible verified components and, where the execution mode requires it, the recorded environment.

Foundation work is ready for #315–#317 implementation review. Each child must still prove its production behavior with focused tests, examples, and canonical documentation. #318 owns the combined migration/import journey; #319 owns integrated tests, fresh installs, release artifacts, and the deployed docs check.

docs.title: 314 neither publishes the package nor demonstrates M11 concurrency or RSI.
Author API release verification matrix
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This page specifies the checks for the #319 release plan. It is an implementation checklist, not a record that a 0.2.0 package has passed. Reuse the maintained CI/Docs workflows and existing tests; add a test only for an uncovered distribution or release contract.

docs.title: Candidate and artifacts
docs.text:
Every receipt identifies the release source commit R, chosen version, clean source state, dependency lock hash, and resolved build/tool environment. Use SHA-256 for each wheel, sdist, documentation source ZIP, and retained docs archive. Record package source file hashes separately from archive hashes.

Required artifact checks:

  • Wheel and sdist agree on distribution name/version, Requires-Python, dependency/extra metadata, CLI entry points, README content type, license, and project URLs. Inspect rendered README links outside GitHub's context.
  • Core imports need no optional browser or provider package. Installing the browser extra supplies its actual dependencies and retains required templates, JavaScript, CSS, and py.typed in the installed distribution.
  • The sdist rebuilds outside the repository without .git, untracked files, checkout imports, or files absent from the archive. Its rebuilt wheel installs the intended same code/resources as the release wheel.
  • Source ZIP contents and package source match R; do not equate its bytes or hash with the differently structured sdist. The existing deterministic ZIP content check remains in force.
  • Installed meta_evolve.__file__ resolves inside the selected environment's non-editable installation. Report importlib.metadata.version("meta-evolve") and package file hashes; equal version strings alone do not establish equality.
  • Inspect expected archive contents, including optional package data. Do not use a build that accidentally includes local credentials, caches, or work directories; building a clean tracked revision supplies this boundary.

docs.title: Proposed environment coverage
docs.text:
The release owner must select and record the support matrix before claiming support. The existing >=3.12 metadata is an installation constraint, not proof that every future interpreter and platform has been tested.

Environment Proposed required evidence Ubuntu, repository-pinned Python 3.12 Existing full deterministic suite, compile step, five canonical examples, Docs workflow, and separate wheel/sdist installs. Ubuntu, Python 3.13 and 3.14 Separate wheel/sdist core, CLI, history, and browser-extra smoke checks. Add full runtime/profile coverage before claiming the same full-suite assurance as 3.12. macOS, Python 3.12 Separate wheel/sdist smoke plus relevant existing host/confinement checks; retain actual outcomes rather than treating Ubuntu results as macOS evidence. Other interpreters/platforms No new certification from this gate without corresponding evidence. Preserve explicit runtime capability refusals.

This is a proposal, not a new supported-platform declaration. If a smaller matrix is selected, narrow the claims explicitly. Installer success does not prove confinement, timeout enforcement, or multiprocess support. Serial distributed execution remains the only implemented distributed regime.

docs.title: Installed-package smoke
docs.text:
Run these in separate fresh wheel and sdist environments with working directories outside the checkout and no checkout PYTHONPATH. Copy the small required example/fixture inputs explicitly; do not let the test runner import the source package through its own development installation.

Check Expected outcome Core import and metadata Correct version/origin, expected public and namespaced imports, no browser/provider dependency needed for core work. First parser loop Credential-free callable example performs its declared attempts; seed/evaluation counts and selected value match the maintained example. Partial budget Sparse tightening preserves other ceilings; explicit widening refuses before work. Callback input Keyword-only context works, ordinary optional configuration retains defaults, positional framework context gives its migration error. Rich resource reports Resources is accepted, author Usage rejected with a useful error, nested resource projection preserves unknown spend and engine-owned outer counts. Summary and CLI Failed/incomplete runs remain reportable; score absence differs from zero. CLI run/resume/inspect exit and stream behavior match the migration contract. Durable history Create a registered run, reopen it in a fresh process, and resume an interrupted copy with the same verified environment/source. Browser extra Templates/static assets are present; the existing read-only browser path renders the installed run without acquiring write/execution authority. Documented downloads Maintained extracted parser/prompt and reference examples run with the installed interpreter. Simulated SDK cases retain usage/failure behavior without paid calls.

Use the existing META_EVOLVE_LESSON_PYTHON mechanism for downloaded lessons where applicable, and retain its proof of no checkout imports. A narrow shared smoke script is sufficient for new wheel/sdist coverage. Keep packaging tool dependencies out of the runtime library dependency set.

docs.title: Historical compatibility
docs.text:
Read frozen originals; perform resumptions and writable schema operations only on disposable copies. Record before/after file hashes and serialized facts. Keep fixture component source and import identities frozen.

Existing evidence Release assertion tests/fixtures/api_v01/stores and test_api_v01_history.py All seven captures remain readable: completed, failed, optional context/inherited limits/feedback, variadic, unknown spend, unknown capped spend, and pre-bootstrap serial distributed history. pre_315_budget_override and test_run_budget_override_history.py Historical effective budget and facts remain intact; current partial/full equivalent declarations agree; incompatible old source refuses. pre_316_invocation and test_proposer_invocation_history.py Changed invocation is detected for unchanged optional/variadic callback source, with no component calls or new facts on refusal. v3_durable_run, existing schema and read-only tests Supported old schema reading/migration follows the existing capability boundary. API migration does not make schema upgrades a read-only side effect. Current registered resume, interruption, resource, and distributed tests Same verified runtime continues exactly from recorded work; defaults and budgets are not recalculated and counts/costs are not duplicated.

The broad historical test permits verified continuation or an explicit mismatch so it can also run against its original package. A release receipt must pin the actual expected outcome for R; it must not pass merely because any refusal occurred. Record which manifest or environment check refused the run.

Current integration can encounter changed policy source before changed callback wiring. Preserve the separate direct proposer-manifest assertion so policy drift does not mask an untested invocation change. Do not edit recorded manifests to force a desired error order.

The 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 version change can itself alter the distributed environment fingerprint, which includes installed distribution versions and package source. An expected historical environment refusal is different from a current-runtime resume regression. Test same-package execution/resume in a stable environment; installing test tools or extras between those steps can legitimately change the recorded environment too.

Keep old environments/source artifacts reconstructible from retained hashes and patches. Do not regenerate old stores using the release implementation, replace source digests, or suppress environment verification.

docs.title: Runtime and authority coverage
docs.text:
Run the maintained suite on R; use these owners to investigate a failure, not as a second permanently copied command inventory:

Concern Existing starting points Partial ceilings and resolution test_run_budget_overrides.py, test_run_budget_override_resume.py, test_experiment.py, test_session.py Context and manifests Callable adapter/contracts, proposer seam, invocation history, manifest and source-verification tests Summary/query coherence test_run_summary_records.py, test_run_summary_snapshots.py, inspection, comparisons, CLI and browser tests Preset allowance test_preset_defaults.py, test_preset_budget_inheritance.py, policy manifest and cohort tests Physical resources test_component_resources.py, normalization, monetary/unknown-spend, nested policy and method-specific accounting tests Composition and authority Policy evolution, AutoResearch, ACE, experience grants, lineage, workspace, and conformance tests

Require factual cost and lineage preservation across failure/recovery; no candidate may change external caps, evaluator/private data, access grants, or promotion. Search selection is not deployment authority. Do not flatten method stages or describe AutoResearch's outer-only accounting as total inner spend.

docs.title: Documentation and public installation
docs.text:
Before publication, build strictly from R and execute the maintained rendered, route, source-extraction, downloadable-example, and installed-SDK checks. Revisit changed installation/version text, long signatures, migration links, code copying, and narrow layouts. Reuse #318's observations for unchanged surfaces with source provenance; do not relabel its old review as a new review.

After publication, check the real public artifacts:

  • Index version and each file hash equal the retained release artifact; install the pinned public version from a fresh environment with cache/checkout sources excluded. Force a source install separately rather than accidentally selecting the cached wheel. Preserve dependency provenance.
  • GitHub tag resolves to R; release assets/notes identify the same version and package bytes. Preserve the documented old-run compatibility restrictions.
  • Public .source-commit equals R; the Pages build names the recorded docs repository commit. An HTTP success alone is not revision verification.
  • Public install/start-here, API reference, 0.2 migration, durability and component-resource routes load. Download the actual source ZIP and compare its hash, package metadata, and source manifest to the candidate build.
  • The independent verifier required by the release-owner process records their own environment, public installation commands, result, and limitations. Automated checks and a familiarized internal walkthrough do not replace it.

docs.title: Evidence receipt and stop conditions
docs.text:
Keep a small machine-readable receipt plus a readable verification record. No new public model or release service is needed. Required receipt fields:

Group Retained data Candidate Version, tag, source SHA, clean/patch state, lock/source hashes, build tools and metadata Artifacts File names, archive SHA-256 values, package-file manifest, build/CI artifact IDs and retained locations Verification OS/Python/install source, package origin, exact commands, results/counts/skips, logs and hosted run links Compatibility Frozen fixture hashes, read outcomes, actual resume/refusal reason, event/call-count evidence and current-runtime recovery Publication Index URLs/hashes, GitHub release/tag, docs source/deploy commits and Pages result, downloaded public ZIP hash Acceptance Release-scope decision, residual limits, final publication authorization, independent verification and issue closure links

A failing required job, missing public artifact, hash/revision mismatch, missing applicable acceptance, or unexplained compatibility outcome prevents closure. Do not downgrade checks to warnings, silently add skips, or infer a waiver from earlier local passes. Rerun affected gates after a fix; a new distribution must receive fresh installed-package verification before publication.

docs.title: Verify and publish the author API release: plan for #319
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 18, 2026 for #319, under #313. This plans the coordinated 0.2.0 package release. It does not publish a package, create a tag, change package metadata, deploy documentation, or certify the broader MVP.

The roadmap owns the acceptance gate; the foundation and comparison decisions own the selected API. The release checks below own the concrete verification matrix. Use the current programming model and architecture for shipped meaning.

docs.title: What is already complete
docs.text:
Inspected September 18 Evidence and implication Clean main at 1607afbb81f7c5e457f97eb437b13ffb9ad63267 PR #324 merged the integrated API. Select a later release commit after version/packaging changes; this is the planning baseline. #314–#318, #320, and #321 are closed Their native issue states establish that #319 is the remaining API child. The parent body's older unchecked boxes are stale, not evidence of missing source work. Hosted CI and Docs passed on that main commit Runtime run and Docs run. These are baseline passes, not passes for a future version-bumped candidate. Public docs identify the same source Remote docs commit 8cf9810d864aeaf7c07b9945ebda5667f0a2bf00, successful Pages build, and the public .source-commit identify 1607afbb…. The adjacent local docs checkout is older and must not be used as the publication baseline. Package metadata and lock still identify 0.1.0 The version was intentionally held until this gate. Integrated source and published package availability are separate facts. No GitHub releases; no v0.2.0 tag found Recheck all matching release/tag forms immediately before release. No version has been reserved by this plan. Public PyPI project JSON returned 404 This is an inventory observation, not proof of name availability, account ownership, or upload authority.

The #318 verification record already covers the six authoring journeys, supported historical reads, fresh source-ZIP installation, and desktop/narrow rendering. Preserve it. Its local full run reported a process-cleanup failure followed by a passing sandbox rerun; the linked hosted main runs subsequently passed. Do not rewrite the earlier observation as a clean local full-suite pass.

The selected release keeps Experiment, ordered objectives, existing counting names and imports, keyword run, and dictionary CLI factories. It ships partial budget restrictions, explicit callback context, winner-independent summaries, budget-led preset defaults, and Resources. No Improver, new coordinator, concurrent worker implementation, or further API redesign belongs to #319.

docs.title: 0. Set the release scope and publication ownership
docs.text:
Recommended scope: a focused 0.2.0 author API release, with the full MVP tracked separately. This scope choice is awaiting Salah's response at plan preparation. It is not inferred from the pre-1.0 compatibility reset.

There is a real overlap with existing release work:

Owner Relationship to #319 #268 — MVP scope Requires completion of M11 concurrency, live-workflow evidence, environment claims, and independent acceptance beyond this API revision. Remains open. #272 — Distribution verification Owns wheel/sdist installation, browser assets, matrix CI, and a repeatable publishing procedure. Implement/reuse this seam rather than create a competing packaging system. #276 — Publication Names Salah as final acceptance/publication owner, Quancore as procedure owner, and Bhasker as independent post-publication verifier. Retain these responsibilities unless explicitly revised.

Before upload, record whether this is the narrow API cut or the full MVP and which existing acceptance requirements apply. If the narrow cut is selected, record that scope explicitly in the release-owner handoff; leave incomplete MVP issues open and make no concurrency/live-quality claim. If the full MVP is selected, #319 can prepare the distributions and verification but publication waits for that release's remaining gates. Do not silently waive them.

Confirm the exact PyPI project/version, publication account, and supported environment matrix with the existing release owner. GitHub administrator access was verified for both repositories; it does not establish PyPI ownership. Use the proposed matrix in the checks page as a concrete starting point.

docs.title: 1. Add the missing distribution and publication seam
docs.text:
Only ci.yml and docs.yml currently exist. Runtime CI tests the checkout; Docs CI verifies an installed source ZIP. Neither builds, validates, and tests both release distributions or uploads to PyPI. No existing release workflow or standalone publishing procedure was found in the source checkout.

Extend the existing CI packaging responsibility with a small, deterministic installed-package smoke entry point. It must work against an interpreter and artifact supplied by the caller, outside the checkout. Reuse examples and history checks; do not invent another acceptance framework.

Use one reviewed publication workflow or the existing owner's equivalent repeatable procedure. Keep build/verification separate from the upload step. The upload consumes the exact artifacts already checked, with the same hashes; it must not rebuild a different wheel or follow a moving branch.

For GitHub Actions, prefer a protected publication environment and PyPI Trusted Publishing, with OIDC permission confined to the upload job. This avoids a long-lived package token in the repository. Pin reviewed action/tool versions when implementing. See PyPI's publishing instructions.

If this is the first PyPI upload, configure and verify the appropriate pending publisher for the actual repository, workflow, environment, and account. A pending publisher does not reserve a project name; recheck before upload. See creating a project through Trusted Publishing. If access is missing, finish build/checks and the concrete handoff; identify the account/configuration action needed instead of improvising another index.

TestPyPI is optional for rehearsing the upload mechanism. It neither satisfies public-PyPI verification nor establishes ownership of the production name. Publishing remains an explicit later release action, never a side effect of ordinary PR tests or a docs build.

docs.title: 2. Prepare and freeze one release candidate
docs.text:
Use a focused release-preparation PR after the packaging seam is usable:

  1. Set pyproject.toml to the selected release version and update its own distribution entry in uv.lock. Review any unrelated dependency movement.
  2. Validate metadata, Python requirements, license, README rendering and links, CLI entry point, extras, and source/docs/issue URLs. Add missing public project URLs where needed; keep unrelated packaging cleanup out of scope.
  3. Replace current-install guidance that says the package still reports 0.1.0 in the migration/status pages. Preserve 0.1.0 inside historical captures, source patches, and dated evidence. Do not globally replace version strings.
  4. Prepare release notes from the existing migration guide: five changes, retained forms, externally owned authority, supported environments, and read-versus-resume limitations. Existing deterministic examples do not become live-model evidence in the announcement.
  5. Merge/reconcile the preparation and identify a clean, immutable commit R. Record the exact lock and source tree. Build all final artifacts from R.

R is a plan symbol, not a literal git ref. A source/version/docs change after freezing it creates a new candidate and invalidates affected evidence. A later verification-record commit can describe R; it must not silently move the tag or be substituted for the tested source in publication.

docs.title: 3. Build and verify the distributions
docs.text:
Build the wheel and source distribution through the declared Hatchling backend using a recorded toolchain. Record the resolved build backend as well as uv, Python, and runtime/test dependencies: the current unbounded hatchling build-system requirement is not pinned merely because uv.lock is recorded. Use a scoped build constraint if needed for reproducibility.

Validate both archives' metadata and included package resources. Install the wheel and sdist separately into clean environments, forcing the source path for the latter. Rebuild from the unpacked sdist outside git to prove it contains what its backend needs. Verify the package origin and installed source files, not only the reported version. Wheel/sdist compression need not be byte-identical to one another; their installed code and intended resources must agree.

Build the documentation source ZIP from R too. It is a third distribution route and must match the same package source/metadata, but its hash and archive layout are distinct. Preserve the deterministic ZIP test already owned by docs/hooks/entrance.py and test_lesson_downloads.py.

The checks page specifies fresh-install smoke cases, historical compatibility, supported profiles, and evidence fields. Run the maintained full runtime and Docs workflows on R; baseline passes on 1607afbb… cannot substitute. Reuse one successful result per exact revision and required environment rather than rerunning identical suites without cause.

docs.title: 4. Assemble the release handoff before publication
docs.text:
Produce one reviewable packet containing:

  • Commit R, version, proposed tag, final wheel/sdist/source-ZIP hashes, build-tool versions, source manifest, and exact installed-package receipts.
  • Hosted runtime, packaging-matrix, and Docs run links for R, with actual pass/fail/skip counts, reasons, supported environments, and residual limits.
  • Historical read/resume outcomes and explicit negative invocation/environment checks. Retain evidence that refusal performed no component work or new facts.
  • Release notes, rendered candidate docs, immutable documentation archive, public-index/project configuration, and the exact upload/deployment procedure.
  • The chosen narrow/full release scope and the existing owner's final claims and publication decision, plus the independent verification handoff.

Keep durable evidence beyond the existing 14-day Docs artifact retention. Attach receipts/checksums and necessary logs to the release or a maintained evidence record. Temporary /private/tmp paths alone are not release evidence that another contributor can retrieve.

The existing #276 explicitly says “Salah retains final acceptance and publication authority.” Prepare the complete packet first; request any still missing publication decision against these concrete artifacts. If Salah has already authorized the exact publication in the implementation session, retain that authorization rather than asking again. Planning #319 alone is not upload authorization.

docs.title: 5. Publish the exact artifacts and matching documentation
docs.text:
After the applicable acceptance and publication decision:

  1. Recheck tag/version/name availability and that R and artifact hashes match the approved packet. Create the version tag at R and prepare a GitHub release with the reviewed notes and assets using the selected procedure.
  2. Upload the verified wheel and sdist; record the actual index response and compare the index's file hashes. Do not rebuild between verification/upload.
  3. From a clean environment and outside the checkout, install the exact version from the public index, including a source-install check. Verify public asset hashes, metadata, imports, quickstart, CLI, saved history, and browser extra.
  4. Publish the reviewed GitHub release with its verified assets and notes. Keep staged release/docs material separate until the index check succeeds.
  5. Build/deploy docs from R, or use the verified R artifact. Update meta-evolve-docs/.source-commit to R; preserve the static repo's hosting files and README. Inspect its actual remote head first: the local sibling checkout observed during planning was stale.
  6. Verify the Pages build, public marker, migration/reference/install routes, and downloaded ZIP hash/metadata/source. Test real public responses, not just the deployment job or local files. Record source and docs commit IDs.

The current docs deployment is a separate static repository served from its main branch root through GitHub Pages. Reuse that arrangement; a new hosting service or cross-repository deployment framework is unnecessary. A moving homepage cannot retain all version-specific evidence, so keep the tagged source and reviewed docs archive available with the release.

docs.title: 6. Stop, recover, and close honestly
docs.text:
Failure point Required response Before upload: tests, metadata, permissions, or claims incomplete Keep artifacts staged. Fix the owning problem; create a new candidate if source changes. No tag or package claims imply a pass. Ambiguous/partial upload Inspect the public index before retrying. Account for each file/hash; do not blindly upload a rebuild or mark the release complete. Public install or asset mismatch Stop announcement/docs advancement, retain evidence, and use the approved correction/yank procedure if necessary. A fix requires a new published version; do not replace bytes behind an existing version/tag.
