Package works but docs deployment fails Keep #319 open, report the package/docs split, and redeploy the same reviewed documentation artifact. Do not conceal the successful package upload by calling the whole operation rolled back. A later defect affects saved runs Preserve old distributions and history. Reverting a package/docs pointer does not migrate stored facts or make an older runtime safe for newer stores.

Completion requires both public artifacts and matching docs, recorded fresh installation and compatibility evidence, and the independent verification required by the selected publication process. An automated smoke run cannot be reported as Bhasker's independent acceptance.

Update #319 and #313 with the evidence and reconcile their stale checklists. Close the API parent only after all selected children and publication gates are complete; leave broader #268/MVP issues open unless their own gates are met.

docs.title: Implementation slices
docs.text:
Slice Deliverable Exit A — Scope and packaging seam Record release cut/matrix/ownership; implement missing #272-compatible distribution checks and reviewed publication procedure. Wheel and sdist checks are reproducible and hosted; public-index configuration is known. B — Release preparation Version/lock/metadata, current install guidance, release notes, final candidate and staged assets. Exact R passes runtime, Docs, packaging, and historical checks; complete handoff ready. C — Authorized publication and verification Upload those assets, public-index installs, GitHub release, R docs deployment, independent handoff and closure record. All public artifact/revision/hash links and required acceptance evidence are retained.

These are review boundaries within #319, coordinated with #272/#276. They do not require a new family of speculative issues or additional runtime redesign.

docs.title: First-run documentation: plan for #331
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 19, 2026 for #331, the documentation entrance to #330. The intended result is a shorter route from opening the homepage to running a complete experiment, followed by a clear route to model-generated revisions, feedback, and saved history. This page plans the change; it does not implement the entrance or authorize unselected runtime behavior.

The implementation verification record now records the source checks, visual review, and remaining publication handoff.

The programming model owns executable API contracts, the architecture owns semantics, the roadmap owns acceptance gates, and the implementation plan owns technical boundaries. The existing documentation maintenance rules govern source ownership, historical routes, and useful checks.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. Keep the complete credential-free parser example. Move it above the two concept sections and discovery table in both entrances; retain the opening “Improve solutions. Improve the methods that produce them.” framing.
  2. Lead online setup with a direct install from the published documentation ZIP. Keep the matching local ZIP route for archived/offline documentation. A package-index command waits for actual publication under #319.
  3. Immediately after the first result, link the existing complete live parser journey. Offer the routing-prompt journey as the alternative domain. Reuse #269's examples rather than create another tutorial.
  4. Separate ordinary construction and inspection from extension protocols in the generated reference while preserving existing URLs and fragment IDs.
  5. Add a separate author-UX gate to the roadmap. Runtime work stays in #332–#335; integrated usability work stays in #336; #337 is a later design decision about SDK support.

docs.title: Inspected baseline and installation proof
docs.text:
The inspected source is 1607afbb81f7c5e457f97eb437b13ffb9ad63267. Existing local release-planning edits are separate work. The deployed site's .source-commit identifies that same source; the documentation repository's deployment commit was 8cf9810d864aeaf7c07b9945ebda5667f0a2bf00 at inspection.

Check on September 19 Observed result Public package availability PyPI's meta-evolve JSON endpoint returned 404; the source repository had no GitHub releases; #319 remained open. Published source ZIP HTTP 200; SHA-256 ff855074531015053e1e863a7f46b401d4a05b092ea5f17af257da09762911fd. Fresh installation Direct URL installed successfully in a new Python 3.12.13 environment on macOS, outside the checkout. Source identity Every archive entry matched the inspected checkout; all 211 installed package files matched the ZIP. Installed direct_url.json recorded its URL and SHA-256. Canonical quickstart Seed 33%, selected 100%, one proposal, two evaluations, and 4m → 240 seconds. Network access was rejected during example execution.

The tested command was:

python -m pip install https://sentient-xyz.github.io/meta-evolve-docs/downloads/meta-evolve.zip

Use its %pip install ... equivalent in the notebook entrance. The proof above used the command-line installer and canonical script, not a notebook UI or an independent newcomer. Package metadata still says 0.1.0; that string alone does not establish which API revision is installed.

The URL follows the current online documentation. Archived documentation must direct readers to its accompanying ZIP instead of silently installing today's source. Recheck the deployed marker, archive hash, package origin, and example when publishing the changed entrance. For a reproducible verification receipt, retain the tested archive and hashes rather than rely on a moving URL.

The ZIP avoids a checkout and manual upload for an online first run. Source installation can still download build tooling. “Local ZIP” does not promise an air-gapped installation; offline dependencies remain the installer's concern.

docs.title: Proposed entrance
docs.text:
Keep the same order in README.md and docs/index.md, with normal Markdown in the README and shared includes in the site:

Order Reader sees 1 Name, existing positioning, one short explanation, and a direct first-run link. 2 Python 3.12+ requirement and one online install cell; nearby local-ZIP fallback. 3 Complete existing proposer, evaluator, and run cells, in that order. 4 Expected output, what the score measures, and the zero-proposal exercise. 5 “Use your model next”: the complete live parser journey with feedback and saved history; routing prompt as an alternative. 6 Adapt the example, then the artifact/method diagrams, discovery table, and use/compose/evolve routes.

Do not make the first example look shorter by omitting definitions or adding helper imports. Reuse examples/learn/parser_quickstart.py unchanged unless a specific correctness issue appears. Preserve the existing explanation that its proposal is handwritten and its scores come from six actual Python checks. Keep setup visible and each displayed Python cell below 40 lines.

The live continuation should explain its value in one sentence: a model proposes revisions from evaluator feedback, and the example saves a history that can be inspected later. Link its prerequisites and dry run; do not imply it needs no credentials, guarantees an improvement, or has retained model-performance evidence. The small SDK guide remains useful for connecting a callable, but is not the only next link.

Update the shared setup and README's marked copy together. Remove the current unqualified “skip it if you already installed this package” instruction: equal version labels do not prove matching source. Recommend a fresh environment for the first run and explain restarting an already-imported notebook kernel. Do not introduce a download resolver, packaging workflow, or installer library.

docs.title: Wording and reference boundaries
docs.text:
Use these terms consistently in the touched entrance, feedback, and persistence prose without renaming public fields or constructors:

Reader-facing term Exact existing API meaning Proposal attempts trials= and usage().trials count attempts after the seed; an attempt may fail. Evaluations usage().evaluations includes the seed evaluation; do not promise every proposal reaches evaluation. Recorded history result.trials() includes the seed and attempted revisions; its length is not the proposal allowance. Feedback Evaluator observations made available to the proposer by the declared context policy. Experience The broader existing record/access vocabulary, including explicitly configured pull access.

The default example keeps history in memory. Say that saving across processes requires explicit storage, with a link to the persistence guide. A selected seed is a valid result; completion does not imply improvement.

For the reference, start with a small construction/inspection orientation, then render the ordinary author entries before the exhaustive export inventory and extension detail. Keep the existing four export tiers and generated signatures; do not prune root exports or duplicate manually maintained signatures.

Use per-entry mkdocstrings member selection to keep Greedy and BestOfN constructors readable. Render binding/cohort methods once in a later extension section on the same API page, retaining anchors such as meta_evolve.Greedy.bind and meta_evolve.BestOfN.next_cohort. Link the existing extension guide. Preserve useful limitations when moving detail; serial distributed execution must not start sounding concurrent.

Move milestone chronology out of beginner-facing prose. Do not rewrite Python component docstrings merely to hide design notes: source changes can affect recorded component identity. Prefer reference placement/configuration in #331; any necessary source edit needs its own explicit identity-impact review and focused verification. Avoid a global rendering filter or new template framework.

docs.title: Proposed roadmap gate
docs.text:
Add an “Author UX follow-up” section to docs/milestones.md, linked to #330 and the existing post-M10 presentation follow-up. Mark proposed capabilities Design—not shipped and record this bounded acceptance:

The roadmap should link child issues for detailed contracts, not copy their entire bodies. Each runtime child updates the canonical API/semantics and adds focused tests when its behavior lands. This gate does not expand #313/#319's selected 0.2 release, M11 concurrency, or candidate authority. It does not make

docs.title: 331 supplies verified installation, an earlier complete experiment, an
docs.text: existing practical continuation, retained reference routes, and a newcomer   handoff. It changes no runtime contract.

docs.title: 332 makes bounded authorized feedback usable and diagnoses disabled, empty,
docs.text: and truncated context. Latest means latest within the selected bundle;   broader access remains explicit. Deliberately disabled feedback stays valid.

docs.title: 333 presents detached, inert run summaries truthfully after storage closes;
docs.text: Run.__repr__ does not acquire an I/O dependency. Failure, absent scores, baseline counts, and persistence claims must remain accurate.

docs.title: 334 adds one objective and explicit context to improve() with demonstrated
docs.text: equivalence to the expanded declaration. Keep advanced search, registration,   execution mode, and pull access on that expanded path.

docs.title: 335 reopens an explicitly selected run, or the only run in a store, with a
docs.text: clear storage lifetime. Multiple runs require a choice; lexical IDs do not   define recency. Reopening does not promise resumability.

docs.title: 336 integrates the shipped results into the existing practical journey and
docs.text: #275/#277 evidence process. #337 then decides whether repeated SDK accounting   work justifies reusable support; a decision to retain current wrappers is valid.

docs.title: 337 a prerequisite for shipping the earlier improvements.
Implementation sequence and files
docs.text:
One #331 PR can contain three reviewable commits; no further issue split is needed for this slice.

Step Files and work Exit condition 1. Gate and entrance docs/milestones.md, README.md, docs/index.md, docs/_includes/notebook-install.md, and setup references in docs/start-here.md. Separate follow-up gate; complete code precedes concept sections; online setup and local fallback agree. 2. Reference and vocabulary docs/reference/api.md, docs/_includes/api-authoring.md, and targeted prose in the feedback/persistence guides. Add a small extension include only if it keeps each responsibility clearer. Ordinary inputs are easy to find; extension anchors and exact API meaning survive. 3. Verification and handoff Existing affected tests; docs/project/capability-walkthrough.md; a concise dated receipt linked from the PR. Built docs, installed examples, links, visual checks, and participant prompts agree with the final revision.

Change mkdocs.yml only if navigation needs an actual adjustment. A heading/nav label mismatch alone does not justify changing a URL. Reuse the historical route fixtures without regenerating them from the new site or removing old fragments. Keep existing docs owners under #274 involved; completed documentation issues stay closed. Packaging CI remains #272's responsibility, and publication remains with #319/#276.

docs.title: Validation and handoff
docs.text:
For implementation, run the maintained checks from the Docs workflow, starting with uv run --locked --group docs mkdocs build --strict. Focus review on the existing entrance, generated-reference, lesson-download, historical-route, redirect, feedback, persistence, and guide-navigation tests. Preserve source equality, useful constructor rendering, executable outputs, and unique anchors; avoid tests for exact marketing wording, line positions, or screenshots' pixels.

Rehearse the final rendered entrance in a fresh notebook outside the checkout. Use a non-editable install of the matching built ZIP; check imported file origin and package bytes, then execute cells in order. Check one proposal/two evaluations and zero proposals/one evaluation. Use the existing META_EVOLVE_LESSON_PYTHON path for the affected downloaded lessons. Exercise the model continuation's existing offline checks; paid model calls are not required to establish this documentation change.

Capture before/after README and rendered homepage views at desktop and narrow widths (for example, 1440 and 390 CSS pixels). Check the first-run link, setup, copy controls, complete cells, expected output, and continuation links. Document where the first runnable cell occurs; keep necessary context legible instead of claiming a fixed “above the fold” result across devices.

Extend the existing #275/#277 handoff rather than create another study:

  • Record documentation/source revision, install origin, environment, and help.
  • Measure installation separately from time to a first completed experiment.
  • Measure completion with the participant's own evaluator and an inspectable result; a positive score delta is not the success criterion.
  • Observe whether the participant encounters the feedback configuration trap without prompting; record the attempted route and any assistance.

docs.title: 331 supplies the changed entrance and measurable prompts. Independent human
docs.text: sessions and later accessor/journey results remain with their existing owners; agent execution is not evidence of independent usability.

docs.title: Difficulty and completion
docs.text:
Estimated implementation effort is two to three focused working days, including verification, excluding review queues and publication. The entrance and wording are straightforward; preserving generated-reference anchors and checking the installed package against the deployed docs require the most care. No library overhaul is needed for this issue.

Close #331 when its roadmap gate, documentation change, verification receipt, and handoff are reviewed together. Record source merge and site publication separately. Leave runtime children open until their own behavior and acceptance evidence exist.

docs.title: Fixed evaluation: plan for #352
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 21, 2026 for #352, D8 under #343. The dependency #351 is open. Its help-assistant lesson and verification record are present in the working tree; Salah's review and publication remain outstanding. Planning can overlap; acceptance follows the dependency order.

The implementation verification records the delivered lesson, installed Jupyter runs, and remaining review.

The programming model owns the API and refusal contract, the architecture owns authority, and the M8 acceptance record and implementation boundaries describe the existing harness mechanism. M11 remains the runtime build boundary. This work teaches shipped behavior.

docs.title: Reader outcome
docs.text:
Answer: “What stops a proposed change from changing the test instead of improving the answer?” Reuse D7's help assistant, password/invoice notes, and three fixed questions. Readers should point to the editable instruction, the protected checks, a permitted mistake, and a retained refusal before learning the broader ownership terminology.

Use one bounded run, one evaluator, and three proposed revisions. Keep the starting exact-match instruction and the same two supported worker behaviors. The second revision deliberately restores exact matching after the first revision broadens it; its missed polite question is an ordinary measured error.

Record Proposed change Expected measurement Evaluator called? Starting version Match exact questions. 2/3 checks Yes Allowed improvement Planner value becomes Match topic words. 3/3 checks Yes Allowed regression Planner value returns to Match exact questions. 2/3 checks Yes Forbidden declaration change Rename the planner surface to evaluation_checks, with a proposed always-pass rule PolicyViolation; no score or successor artifact No

The last proposal attempts to redefine what the editable field means. It does not obtain or modify the actual evaluator. Show the proposed renamed field beside the original declaration and the unchanged HELP_CASES; do not describe this as executing a replacement grader or protecting against arbitrary Python.

Expected work: three proposal attempts and three evaluations, including the starting version. The refused attempt adds one proposal and zero evaluations. Three questions within one evaluator call are three checks, not three accounted evaluations. The best measured instruction remains topic matching, even after the regression and refusal. Use no satisfaction threshold that would stop the demonstration after reaching 3/3.

docs.title: Enforce the actual boundary
docs.text:
Use the existing meta_evolve.harness.HarnessArtifact, with TextParam and PolicyParam. Schema v1 requires both planner and context-policy parameters; show both definitions. Explain that both values are declared mutable, although this example only exercises the planner value. Do not claim that this artifact declares a planner-only allowlist.

The permitted proposals can use HarnessMutation and HarnessArtifact.apply. For the forbidden proposal, deliberately bypass that convenience method and construct a successor with dataclasses.replace: change planner.name to evaluation_checks and its value to an always-pass instruction. The core's generic successor-validation hook calls HarnessArtifactCodec.validate_successor after encoding and before creating a successor artifact. It rejects the changed declaration with PolicyViolation and changed_declarations=("planner.name",) before evaluation.

This distinction matters: apply(HarnessMutation("evaluation_checks", ...)) instead returns InvalidOutput for an undeclared surface. That helper is convenience, not the authority boundary. Keep the main three-case demonstration on the core refusal; an existing helper test or a short explanation can cover the other failure kind without a fourth required case.

Use Task(artifact=harness.HarnessArtifact, ...), Experiment, and run(). improve() does not select this artifact codec. Declare a three-attempt allowance and up to four evaluations, permitting the seed and every proposal if all were admitted; the refusal leaves one evaluation unused. Use bounded Greedy search so the third attempt still has the successful instruction as its parent. Reset the authored proposal sequence when the run cell is rerun.

Keep notes, cases, evaluator callable, objective, and budget outside the candidate. The worker must interpret instruction text and return actual answers; the evaluator must retain question, expected answer, actual answer, and pass/fail evidence. Never assign quality from a revision label. Derive the displayed scores, failure reason, selected instruction, and counts from the returned run records. Display the failed record's lookup so readers can locate it again and inspect its .id, without treating a content duplicate as the same occurrence. This keeps the transcript readable without pinning an opaque identifier across package revisions.

State the limits beside the result:

  • This is a deterministic in-process simulation. Declaration validation supplies no process, filesystem, or Python security isolation.
  • The refusal protects immutable harness declarations on the normal proposal path. The actual checks remain experiment-owned; arbitrary malicious Python could access notebook globals and is outside this demonstration's protection.
  • Preventing this forbidden edit does not prevent all exploitation of an imperfect metric. Broader specification-gaming research stays in #216.
  • A path-valid SourceTree does not enforce a file allowlist. This notebook needs no source-tree variant, confinement setup, provider, or new framework.

docs.title: Notebook and page
docs.text:
Add one complete canonical source at examples/learn/harness_authority.py. Adapt D7's small worker and fixed cases directly, with no runtime sibling imports or hidden helper definitions. The page and downloads must use this source's snippet sections; avoid a second hand-maintained notebook program.

Target five required cells, including installation, each below 40 lines:

Cell Visible contents 1 Shared Python 3.12+ installation cell and fresh-kernel guidance 2 Imports, fixed notes/cases, and the complete two-instruction worker 3 Typed seed, both surface declarations, and evaluator with retained checks 4 The three explicit edits and proposer that returns the next successor 5 Reset sequence, declare/run experiment, inspect outcomes, protected checks, selection, and exact counts

Use readable definitions rather than compressed statements to fit the limit. Count output comments as cell lines too. If the full inspection is too large, keep the first measured result within five cells and make any additional required inspection cell explicit in the evidence; do not hide setup to meet the count. Prefer fitting all three outcomes within the five-cell target.

Put the example early in docs/concepts/authority.md, retaining its URL, keep-authority-where-it-belongs, ownership explanation, and promotion section. Preserve existing useful heading fragments. Add a D7 link next to its statement that the fixed checks stay outside the revised configuration; distinguish the plain mapping there from this typed declaration.

After the result, give one small “Change and predict” exercise: replace the forbidden edit with a permitted planner-value change and rerun. It should reach evaluation and use the fourth evaluation, even if its answers are wrong. Choose a non-no-op instruction relative to the current best parent. This makes the difference between admission and quality observable.

docs.title: Implementation slices
docs.text:
1. Prove the source and behavior. Implement the self-contained example, obtain the four retained outcomes above, and add focused regression checks before polishing the page. Keep src/ unchanged.
  2. Deliver the notebook. Include its source sections in the authority page; add the D7 link. Register authority-boundaries.ipynb and harness_authority.py with docs/hooks/entrance.py's existing generation paths. Use the existing concept navigation rather than a new guide hierarchy.
  3. Verify delivery. Add tests/test_authority_notebook.py and tests/test_authority_downloads.py, authority standalone coverage in tests/notebook_lesson_support.py, and their selections in the existing Docs workflow, including the isolated installed-package job.
  4. Rehearse and hand off. Execute the complete visible notebook, inspect the rendered page and executed output, and write docs/project/authority-lesson-verification.md from actual measurements. Record remaining dependency, audit, and publication gates explicitly.

No new artifact type, mutation framework, SDK adapter, coordinator branch, research study, automatic promotion, or public API change belongs to this work. Link canonical contracts rather than duplicating their signatures or changing their shipped status to describe a documentation delivery.

docs.title: Acceptance checks
docs.text:
• Execute the exact displayed cells: retained scores are 2/3, 1, 2/3, followed by policy_violation with empty metrics and no successor artifact/evaluation. The successful topic-matching version remains selected.
  • Instrument evaluator entry in a focused test: only the seed and two admitted revisions enter it. Prove the forbidden successor reaches the core check, rather than returning a manually constructed failure from the proposer.
  • Assert exact aggregate usage and per-attempt count changes. Confirm the second revision has its own artifact occurrence and parent link even though its content returns to the starting instruction.
  • Snapshot the fixed cases, notes, evaluator declaration, budget, and original harness declarations; verify they remain unchanged through every attempt. Every retained evaluation must use the same expected answers. Also cover direct component/interface declaration replacement with the existing harness regression suite.
  • Exercise the documented permitted replacement for the forbidden edit: evaluations rise from three to four; ordinary poor answers remain measured. Changing an expected answer as the experiment author changes the score in a separate control, proving the checks actually determine the measurement.
  • Whole-notebook and final-cell reruns reset the sequence and reproduce the outcomes without StopIteration or prior notebook state.
  • Check source, rendered Python cells, and generated notebook parity; visible definitions; cell lengths/counts; download links; and retained page anchors. The authority page contains a text diagram, so filter Python blocks rather than assuming every HTML pre is an executable cell.
  • Run downloaded Python, notebook cells, and rendered copied cells against a fresh noneditable install outside the checkout, with package-origin checks, no repository imports or provider keys, and no runtime network access.

Run those focused tests, existing harness artifact/notebook/download tests, standalone lesson checks, concept/navigation/route checks, and the strict MkDocs build. Use the existing META_EVOLVE_LESSON_PYTHON mechanism for tests against that build's downloads/meta-evolve.zip; ensure the workflow's -k selection actually includes the new installed-package tests.

docs.title: Evidence and closure
docs.text:
Retain the rendered page, executed notebook, clean copied-cell transcript, source revision and any dirty patch, archive hashes, installed package origin, installation command/receipt, Python and OS/kernel, required cell count, setup/run/total time, controls, and manual interventions. Exploratory notebooks and audit artifacts belong under gitignored notebooks/352-authority/. Keep the committed verification record concise and link its evidence.

Verify Jupyter and Colab independently before claiming support. D7's local Jupyter result is useful precedent, not evidence that D8 ran on either platform. Separate the exact-build install from a rehearsal of the public installation URL, whose package may lag. Do not borrow D7's timings, hashes, or test totals.

Salah's review is required before issue closure. Publication and the independent newcomer gate retain their existing owners under #343/#274. This plan does not close the dependency, publish documentation, or start participant outreach.

docs.title: Explicit callback context: implementation plan for #316
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 18, 2026 for #316, under #313. This specializes the proposed callback contract into binding, verification, migration, and test work. The programming model owns shipped behavior. Implementation is now recorded under the #316 source gate and verification record.

docs.title: Scope and entry gate
docs.text:
Use #314's selected pre-1.0 release direction: one coordinated breaking release, provisionally 0.2.0, without an intermediate compatibility release or permanent legacy dispatch mode. The canonical Author API revision gate is now present alongside the separate #315 slice. The foundation decision records reviewed contracts, compatibility policy, and historical evidence. This design record does not itself complete implementation or M11 workers.

The scope is plain decoded-value proposer callbacks passed through the ordinary execution path or registered for durable execution. Keep the evaluator, authorized context, result normalization, budgets, and coordinator unchanged. ProposerContext remains the same object with the same capabilities; this change governs how it reaches a callback.

docs.title: Findings that determine the change
docs.text:
The inspected checkout is c04ec6b4b949b8a2702779107e25acd24feb8020 plus the local #297 documentation/docstring patch and current design documents.

Existing behavior Implementation consequence _invocation_shape() tries two positional inputs before one. Replace plain-callback inference; factor=2 must keep its Python default. CallableProposer.__init__, .registered, and .declared share that inference. Select the binding contract by entry route; changing one helper globally would affect structural ports. component_proposer() prefers execute, then structural propose, then a callable. Preserve dispatch precedence and malformed-runner refusal. An explicit CallableProposer(dual_object) or local ComponentRef chooses the callable side first. Preserve that existing explicit-wrapper behavior; do not claim every entry route has identical precedence. Structural .propose(parent) is deliberately supported and tested. Preserve its parent-only convenience beside the explicit two-input structural port. A callable carrying .component currently uses .declared. Retain its identity checks but send its call through the plain-callback binder. Metadata must not select a different argument convention. Registered proposer manifests hash the function and user dependencies only. Include the actual framework binding/invocation implementation automatically. Resume verifies manifests before building runners or invoking their validation hooks. Retain that ordering so incompatible history cannot execute new callbacks. ProposerLike advertises positional callable signatures. Update the type alias to admit keyword context without adding a root export.

docs.title: 1. Bind plain callbacks explicitly
docs.text:
Use the effective inspect.signature() of the selected callable, including local bound methods and partials. Determine a call shape once per adapter construction with inert markers and Signature.bind; never call the callback body to discover its signature, and never retry after it raises TypeError.

  1. Inspect the signature. If inspection fails, raise TypeError explaining the inspectable-wrapper or explicit-structural-port alternatives.
  2. If a keyword-only parameter named context exists, bind a positional parent plus keyword context. A default on that parameter does not disable opt-in.
  3. Otherwise bind the parent alone. Reject an additional positional parameter named context, even when optional, with the keyword-only replacement. A first parent parameter named context is still a valid parent-only call.
  4. Reject any remaining unbound required inputs before seed evaluation or run commitment. Retain ordinary Python defaults for other optional parameters.
  5. Store the chosen private invocation shape and use exactly that call later.

Required examples for the new contract:

def propose(parent):
    return revise(parent)

def propose(parent, *, context):
    return revise(parent, observations=context.bundle)

def propose(parent, factor=2):
    return parent * factor  # factor stays 2

These are signature sketches; revise is not a library function. No annotation, parameter count, _context alias, or variadic parameter alone requests context. f(parent, *args, **kwargs) receives just the parent; f(*args, context=...) receives the parent in args and the framework context by keyword if it binds. Positional-only parents remain valid.

Inspect the effective signature rather than inventing a second partial-binding algorithm. For example, binding an ordinary required amount through a partial can produce a valid parent-only callable. If a partial still exposes keyword-only context, that name opts into framework delivery even if the partial supplied a default. An inspectable wrapper that hides a bound argument is the explicit alternative. Cover decorated local callables using their advertised signatures; registered decorated wrappers remain subject to the existing source refusals.

docs.title: 2. Preserve the other proposer contracts
docs.text:
Selected route Binding rule after this change Plain callable; registered function; bound method passed as a callback New parent-only or keyword-context rule Callable object with a valid configured local .component Same plain rule, preserving its exact declared component Object selected through .propose Existing structural two-positional-input binding, with parent-only fallback Non-callable local reference retaining a structural object Same structural rule Explicit callable adapter or local reference retaining a callable/dual object Preserve callable selection, then apply the new plain rule Explicit runner with .execute and valid component Existing runner contract; no callable rebinding PatchProposer's own callback Existing explicit (tree, context) adapter contract

Keep .declared(ref, method) as the structural adapter path. In application/run_support.py, change the configured-callable branch to use the plain adapter with the validated local reference; its .component attribute must not turn it into a structural method. Keep component retention/role checks and validation-hook discovery intact.

Structural binding may continue to prefer two positional inputs and fall back to the currently supported parent-only method. An uninspectable structural method has the explicit two-input port contract. Do not apply the new plain callback refusal indiscriminately to it. This is a separate port, not a legacy switch for ordinary callbacks.

Passing object.propose as a callable and passing object as a structural proposer select different declared interfaces. Explain that distinction in advanced guidance. Preserve explicit-adapter precedence instead of taking this issue as permission to redesign component selection.

docs.title: 3. Make invocation source part of verification
docs.text:
A function can keep identical source while receiving different arguments. For example, f(parent, option=None) can take a different branch when the old adapter supplies context and the new one preserves None. Verifying only its source cannot detect this change.

Prefer one small private module, proposed as adapters/_proposer_invocation.py, for signature selection and actual invocation. It needs no domain authority, registry, or new dependency; the adapter still owns failure normalization. This seam is justified by the separate binding contracts and the requirement to identify the framework's invocation source independently. Keep the existing adapter file below its normal size limit by moving this responsibility, not by adding a second public adapter class.

Automatically extend registered proposer source dependencies at the existing registry manifest boundary. The dependency set must cover the private invocation module and the registered adapter's construction/dispatch wiring (for example CallableProposer.registered and CallableProposer.propose). Hash actual source, including relevant module constants; a version string or a hash of the signature checker alone is insufficient. Keep user-declared dependencies and their existing deduplication/order behavior.

Resolve these library-owned dependencies without creating an import cycle; defer the adapter import until manifest resolution if required. Verify fresh imports in isolated processes. The same registry resolution constructs the manifest for start and resume. Evaluator manifests receive no new callback dependency, and no new persistent field, component role, or store schema is needed solely for invocation verification.

Keep prepare_resume()'s manifest verification before runner construction, preflight hooks, broker driving, and new proposer/evaluator work. Preserve typed CapabilityError mismatches without rewriting old facts. Policy factories may still be reconstructed during manifest resolution; do not overstate this as a guarantee that no Python setup code executes.

This intentionally changes manifests for all registered proposers using the new dependency rule, including parent-only functions. Recommend refusing old unverified invocation rather than shipping a historical execution engine in this issue. Supported history remains readable; old unfinished runs require their matching environment to continue. A component-source edit may cause an additional mismatch, which must be reported separately.

Keep the existing run/component identity rules. Manifests are not currently part of run_id_for; the same component reference/run ID is not proof of equivalent implementations. Do not overwrite an existing run, synthesize a component version, or relabel a new run as continuation. Explain versioning and fresh-run requirements when the author deliberately changes behavior.

docs.title: 4. Migrate by invocation owner
docs.text:
A September 18 AST inventory found 52 potentially affected positional-context forms across 43 example Python files, four plain conformance helpers, and many test forms. This is a discovery list, not an exact rewrite count: structural methods and adapter-owned callbacks appear in it too. Include parameters with other names, lambdas, partials, and generated code that a name-based scan misses.

Surface Migration and verification src/meta_evolve/conformance/{cohorts,context_policies,evaluators,search_programs}.py Change actual plain callback consumers; retain conformance coverage of their original laws. Learn/parser/SDK/feedback examples and executable reference cases Use keyword context when consumed; remove an unused second argument where parent-only is clearer; update real expected outcomes. Registered CLI, durable-operations, and crash-recovery examples Update source functions, versions where behavior changes, and source dependencies; record the resume consequence. Policy evolution, AutoResearch, and ACE Migrate inner/outer callbacks without flattening stages or changing evaluation, observation grants, retained results, or nested accounting. Structural SDK objects, runners, patch/history examples Trace the selected route first; keep their explicit port signatures and workspace cleanup behavior. Tests and historical captures Replace live old-convention tests with the new behavior; retain deliberate invalid/legacy cases and preserve old source bytes used by compatibility fixtures. Extracted snippets, downloads, notebooks, and live-only scripts Edit the owning source; execute supported current examples with deterministic substitutes. Preserve historical artifacts or publish a clearly versioned successor rather than silently rewriting provenance.

Do not mechanically add * to every parameter named context. Recheck direct Python calls to each migrated function: a framework callback may also have explicit callers that now need context=. A required _context can become keyword-only context or be removed if unused; optional aliases and variadics can change behavior without any startup error and need an explicit migration note. Never turn an ordinary setting into framework context just to pass a test.

Change ProposerLike's callable arm to Callable[..., object], retaining the structural and runner alternatives and exact runtime validation. This admits keyword-context callbacks without introducing a new root protocol or claiming that Callable[[object, object], object] describes keyword-only parameters.

Update improve/Experiment/run/ProposerContext docstrings, the programming model, callback/SDK/experience guides, and #297's reference cases together. Show before/after forms and startup diagnostics. Do not change evaluator signatures, preset defaults, budget resolution, result fields, or root exports as incidental cleanup. #315 and #317 retain those separate concerns.

docs.title: 5. Implement and verify in reviewable stages
docs.text:
Stage Deliverable Gate before moving on Foundation handoff #314 decision, exact baseline, fixture provenance, release treatment Contracts/gate evidenced; historical source remains available Binding and dispatch Private binder/invoker, route-specific adapters, type alias, focused migrations Signature matrix passes with no double calls or unintended route changes Verified invocation Automatic proposer dependencies and preserved resume ordering Unchanged callback source cannot conceal changed invocation; same-runtime resume works Repository migration Remaining live consumers, conformance, examples, docs, generated/extracted material Original outcomes and authority/accounting rules retained under explicit equivalent callbacks Integration handoff Focused and required broad checks, migration/compatibility record #318/#319 can consume one identified source revision

Treat these as review stages of #316, not independently published API releases. The production change should reach review with its migrations and source verification complete. No runtime behavior is implemented by this plan.

docs.title: Test matrix
docs.text:
Area Required proof Plain signatures Parent-only, required/optional keyword context, ordinary defaults, positional-only parent, first parent named context, additional positional context refusal, variadics, missing required arguments, and uninspectable refusal Local Python forms Bound methods, partials including exposed context, decorated callables, callable instances, configured local identity, and misleading advertised signatures producing one normalized invocation failure Port selection execute precedence/refusal, .propose precedence, parent-only structural method, explicit wrapper/reference behavior, and uninspectable structural invocation Admission Invalid plain signatures fail before seed evaluation, proposal execution, validation-hook execution, or committed run facts through improve, run, and Session.start Invocation/result handling Exact context object, one signature selection per adapter, one body call, no retry after TypeError, retained usage/evidence, and unchanged escaping infrastructure/capability errors Manifest sensitivity Framework binder, invoker, and adapter wiring source changes affect proposer verification; user dependencies still count; evaluator manifests remain unchanged; dependency ordering and repeat resolution are stable Positive durability New registered parent-only/keyword-context runs resume from legal committed frontiers and match uninterrupted logical results/events; cover pushed context and admitted serial distributed execution Historical refusal/read Exact old source still reopens; upgraded resume refuses invocation mismatch before additional work or committed facts, without masking the case with an unrelated mismatch Extended behavior Existing grant, derivation, workspace/history, unknown-spend, failure, and conformance checks remain green after their plain callback fixtures migrate

For the decisive historical case, use an unchanged module-level function whose optional second argument makes old positional delivery observable. Capture a legal incomplete run with the identified pre-cutover package and demonstrate matching-old-runtime continuation. In the upgrade check, keep evaluator and policy manifests equal so #297's policy docstring differences cannot be the actual reason for refusal. Assert the proposer mismatch specifically, and retain store/event/resource observations proving no further work occurred. Do not truncate logs or patch manifests to manufacture compatibility.

The shared checkout now contains #314's capture scaffolding under experiments/api_revision/ and frozen components at tests/fixtures/api_v01/components.py. Its optional-argument and variadic functions fit these cases. Reuse completed captures once their package/source provenance is verified; the presence of scaffolding alone is not that evidence. Preserve those source bytes instead of migrating the historical functions.

Start with test_callable_adapters.py, test_proposer_seam.py, registry/manifest tests, and existing resume/context/distributed suites. Add focused signature and historical-invocation test modules if their independent responsibilities would otherwise inflate existing long files. Use existing failpoint helpers for legal recovery frontiers and fresh processes for cross-version checks.

Run focused suites first; after all live callback migrations, run the maintained runtime CI and Docs selections because the affected examples/fixtures are widely shared. Verify installed downloads and fake SDK paths without checkout imports or paid calls. Strict documentation ownership/routes and rendered signatures must agree with the implemented behavior.

docs.title: Planning evidence and completion boundary
docs.text:
The inspected baseline passed 103 tests across callable adapters, proposer seams, registry, and manifests. Local probes reproduced the default-argument failure and keyword-context rejection, confirmed the distinct dual-object routes and parent-only structural support, and confirmed that the current registered manifest can equal the function-only digest. Probe results and the discovery inventory are under /private/tmp/meta-evolve-316-planning/.

These checks validate findings, not the proposed implementation. Close #316 only with migrated consumers/docs, passing behavior and compatibility gates, an identified implementation revision, and explicit old-history/read/resume outcomes. #314 owns the foundation decision; #318/#319 own final integration and publication.

docs.title: Manual, reference, and design destination map
docs.text:

This is the completed move ledger for the documentation split tracked by #121. A3 made these moves, preserved useful old anchors, and updated links without changing runtime API or semantics.

docs.title: Bounded feedback: implementation plan for #332
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 19, 2026 for #332, under #330. This records the accessor contract, recency policy, and verification plan. Implementation is now recorded under the #332 source gate and verification record. The programming model and architecture own shipped behavior.

docs.title: Scope and entry gate
docs.text:
Make selected feedback easy to read, explain disabled and missing feedback, and keep useful feedback available as a bounded history grows. Implement these as one complete vertical slice through the existing proposer and policy seams.

#331's entrance plan established the author UX follow-up gate before runtime work. The selected technical boundary is recorded in the canonical implementation plan. This design record does not expand the pending #313/#319 release or choose a version. Keep improve() additions, result presentation, reopen helpers, SDK adapters, and the newcomer study with their sibling issues.

docs.title: Findings and disposable probe
docs.text:
Inspected source: 1607afbb81f7c5e457f97eb437b13ffb9ad63267, with the existing local API/release and #331 design edits left in place. No runtime changes were made. The seven existing context-policy, replay, resume, conformance, proposer, policy-manifest, and feedback-lesson test files passed: 102 tests.

  • AncestorsOnly@1 walks ancestors oldest first; _bundle() retains the first max_records records. The accessor alone cannot repair that selection.
  • ContextBundle.truncated combines record omission and rendered-text clipping. It does not record which happened or how many records were lost.
  • None and NoMemory() normalize to no declaration and identical histories. A declared custom policy may legitimately return an empty bundle.
  • Evidence contains kind/data/URI but no producer role. Both proposals and evaluations can record it. An evidence label does not certify its producer.
  • ContextSelected persists the exact bundle. Replay loads that selection; registered source manifests govern whether execution may resume.

A disposable custom policy selected the last N accessible ancestor records, retained their original order, then applied the existing rendering rule. The probe used seed 0, six Greedy proposals of parent + 1, and an evaluator returning the value as score plus EvidenceDraft(kind="feedback", data={"value": value}). With max_chars=1_000_000:

Policy / record limit Feedback values seen by successive proposals Shipped AncestorsOnly, 20 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1 Recency prototype, 20 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 Recency prototype, 0 or 1 No matching evidence Recency prototype, 2 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5

At limit 1, the final record is the evaluation, not its evidence. At limit 2, both fit for this one-evidence evaluator; that is not a universal minimum. With 1,000 records and zero rendered characters, all structured feedback remains available while truncated is true. These are feasibility observations, not production tests or a promise that every bounded bundle contains feedback.

docs.title: 1. Read evidence from the selected bundle
docs.text:
Recommend context.evidence.latest(kind), with a required, nonempty exact evidence label. This follows EvidenceDraft directly and replaces the current lesson's two-kind filter and max(logical_step) expression:

def propose(parent, *, context):
    item = context.evidence.latest("failed-cases")
    failures = () if item is None else item.data["failures"]
    return revise(parent, failures)

# In the experiment declaration:
context=meta.RecentAncestors(max_records=20, max_chars=8_000)

This is a proposed API sketch; revise is user code. Retain context.bundle for callers needing the full structured selection. The accessor has no store, graph, evaluator, provider, or pull-reader reference. It performs no I/O, records no events, and consumes no additional usage.

Latest means the last matching evidence record in the committed bundle's existing canonical order. Scan that order in reverse; do not sort by step, deduplicate labels, merge pull observations, or query missing history. Multiple same-label items in one logical step follow their selected order. The result may be an older ancestor or selected sibling; it does not necessarily describe the current parent or the most recent attempted candidate. Selection and replay validation own authorization; the view reads their result without expanding or independently reconstructing access control.

Return an immutable EvidenceItem | None. The item exposes kind, immutable data, uri, ref, logical_step, and event_sequence from that selected record. ref stays the exact evidence occurrence usable in an explicit ProposalResult.derived_from. Do not invent a trial ID or parent relationship.

The spelling in #332, context.feedback.latest(...), was illustrative. Prefer evidence because a proposer-owned item with the same label also matches. The lesson can call its evaluator-owned observations feedback and reserve "failed-cases" for that evaluator. Do not imply that the accessor certifies authorship or measurement success. Selected failed-evaluation evidence remains readable without synthesizing a score. An evaluator-only lookup would need a separate rule for bundles missing the owning evaluation; defer that contract.

Place EvidenceSelection and EvidenceItem in a small ports/evidence.py module beside the proposer-facing records. This storage-free seam is directly testable and keeps application queries out of the port. Existing application.views.EvidenceView carries a run-query token and lacks occurrence provenance; leave it unchanged. Export the types from their module for typing; the common path needs no new root import except RecentAncestors.

docs.title: 2. Make disabled context explicit
docs.text:
The selection exposes independent enabled: bool and truncated: bool facts. The latter reflects the committed bundle flag exactly, including text-only clipping. It is not proof that evidence records were omitted.

State latest(kind) behavior context=None or NoMemory() Raise ContextDisabled with a declaration/optional-use remedy Declared policy, no matching selected evidence Return None Declared policy, matching evidence Return the last matching item Either enabled case with truncation Same result; truncated is true

No unconditional warnings, implicit policy, or fallback query. Missing evidence in a truncated bundle is not proof that the evaluator recorded none. Rendering and record limits stay separate: max_chars=0 does not erase records, and reading .data is not bounded by the rendered-character limit.

For an intentional feedback-off comparison, make the optional dependency clear:

if not context.evidence.enabled:
    return parent
item = context.evidence.latest("failed-cases")

Recommend ContextDisabled in meta_evolve.errors as a CapabilityError subclass, specifically for accessing disabled pushed context. The existing escape rule aborts on an unhandled configuration error rather than spending the remaining attempts on it. Authors may catch the specific type; the enabled check is the teaching path. The error occurs at accessor use, possibly after seed evaluation. Do not promise preflight detection or change exception normalization globally. An enabled lookup with no match is not an exception.

Add optional context_policy: PolicyRef | None = None to ProposerContext. Its evidence property builds the selection from this declaration and bundle. Sequential execution supplies trial.spec.context_policy; distributed execution supplies None, preserving its existing refusal of pushed context. Neither record contents nor bundle.reason determines whether context is on.

Existing manually constructed contexts remain constructible and bundle access works unchanged. Authors constructing one for a unit test or custom runner must supply the policy reference to exercise enabled evidence lookup. Document this new accessor requirement. Workspace dataclasses.replace() must preserve the declaration. Keep plain and structural callback invocation unchanged.

docs.title: 3. Add an explicit recent-ancestor selection
docs.text:
Recommend RecentAncestors(max_records=20, max_chars=8_000) with PolicyRef("recent-ancestors", "1"), registered through the existing ContextPolicy factory seam. No new ContextSpec field is needed.

  1. Obtain exactly the accessible ancestor candidates that AncestorsOnly considers, with the same strictly-prior cutoff and exclusions.
  2. Retain the last N eligible records, handling zero explicitly so [-0:] cannot accidentally select everything.
  3. Return that subset in its original canonical order, not newest first.
  4. Render selected records under max_chars. Set truncation when eligible records were omitted or rendering was clipped; report exact usage.

This changes retention priority, not access authority. Rejected siblings stay outside ancestry; hidden/future records never enter the candidate set. In branching or multiple-parent history, a finite limit cannot promise feedback for every parent. No matching evidence and incomplete history remain valid.

Alternative Disposition Reverse AncestorsOnly@1 silently Reject: changes recorded policy semantics under the same declaration Version AncestorsOnly and change its default Possible migration; unnecessary for an explicit additive route Add an order flag to AncestorsOnly Defer: the choice must survive declaration, identity, and reconstruction New RecentAncestors preset Recommend: existing seam, explicit identity, old policy remains selectable Fetch current feedback inside latest() Reject: bypasses committed selection and its authority

Teach RecentAncestors for iterative feedback. Document AncestorsOnly@1's oldest-record retention and preserve its semantics. Leave BestSibling ranking/selection unchanged; the accessor only sees whatever it selected. Keep aggregate truncation metadata for this issue. Precise historical omission counts or separate cause flags require new durable facts and migration work; do not manufacture them from the current boolean or reason text.

docs.title: 4. Preserve replay and verify executable semantics
docs.text:
The views and declaration pointer are invocation-time values. Persist no new view record, event, or schema solely for the accessor. Supported old bundles remain readable; replay must never rerun a selector to modernize them.

Registered proposer manifests include invocation/adapter source but do not transitively hash the context class, accessor, or construction. Extend their automatic dependencies to cover ports/evidence.py, ports/proposers.py, the ContextDisabled definition, and actual construction wiring in execute_trial and LocalProposalExecutor.propose. Keep user dependencies and evaluator manifests unchanged. Use lazy resolution if necessary and test fresh-process imports. Hash actual source, not just a policy name or version constant.

Register and fingerprint the new context factory and actual selection/rendering dependencies. If sharing policies/context.py changes existing context-policy hashes, record that drift explicitly; unchanged semantics do not make old hashes compatible. Do not suppress mismatches or silently rewrite digest tests.

Capture pre-change source/manifests and an interrupted durable fixture before editing runtime files. Verify historical read-only inspection, matching-runtime resume, and changed-source refusal separately. Resume checks manifests before runner construction/preflight and new proposer/evaluator work. Policy factory reconstruction during verification is not execution of a proposal. Add no historical runtime, rewrite no selections, and infer no new component version; an unchanged run ID is not implementation equivalence.

docs.title: 5. Implement in reviewable stages
docs.text:
Stage Changes Exit evidence Gate and baseline #331 canonical gate; this contract; pre-change durable/source capture Scope and compatibility baseline are explicit Accessor and invocation Evidence views, context declaration, typed error, construction wiring, automatic dependencies Lookup, disabled-state, authority, and source-drift tests Recency policy policies/context.py, policy/root exports, registry factories Growing-history regression, bounds, identity, conformance, durable reconstruction Complete teaching slice Feedback lesson, experience guide, canonical contracts, reference cases, executable downloads Feedback-on/off outcomes, documentation checks, replay/resume matrix

These are review stages within #332, not separate releases. Introduce tests and documentation with each behavior change; finish the full slice before handing its contract to #334 or integrating it into #336's practical journey.

docs.title: Acceptance matrix
docs.text:
Concern Required proof Disabled versus empty None and NoMemory() retain identical identity/events; declared empty policies are enabled even with default/misleading reason text; pull-only access stays disabled for pushed evidence Strict and optional use Unhandled disabled lookup raises the typed error at first access without repeated attempts; enabled guard retains the lesson's equal-work off comparison Exact lookup Current/older ancestors, no match, multiple same-kind records in one step, immutable payload/provenance, proposer/evaluator label collision, failed-evaluation evidence Authority and purity No unselected, hidden, future, or rejected-sibling records; authorized BestSibling evidence works; no store/graph/provider/pull calls or extra usage; exact refs remain valid derivation inputs Bounds and recency Six-step stale-history regression; zero/one/two record limits; multiple evidence items; zero/small character limits; text-only clipping with complete records; no unconditional current-parent promise Integration Parent-only and keyword-context callbacks, structural proposers/runners, manual contexts, workspace replacement, unchanged distributed admission Durability Policy factory round-trip and distinct identity; no reselection of committed bundles; crash/resume equivalence at every interior batch boundary; old readable history; accessor/wiring/policy drift refused before new work Teaching Lesson scores remain 2/6, 4/6, 1 with feedback and 2/6, 2/6, 2/6 when explicitly off, with two proposals and three evaluations in each

docs.title: Difficulty and completion
docs.text: Medium overall: lookup and recent-record selection are small. Most work is truthful diagnostics, durable verification, edge cases, and teaching. Estimate 3–5 focused engineering days plus review after the entry gate, assuming no new durable metadata or evaluator-only query contract. This is a planning estimate, not a release commitment.

docs.title: Harness lesson: plan for #351
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 20, 2026 for #351, D7 under #343. Its dependency #347 is closed. This plan changes the teaching path using shipped behavior. The programming model, architecture, milestones, and implementation plan retain their ownership. M11 remains the runtime build boundary; no runtime, SDK, or research expansion is needed for this issue.

The implementation verification records the delivered notebooks, executed results, and remaining review.

docs.title: Reader outcome and decisions
docs.text:
Readers should be able to identify the editable instructions, the worker's separate answer or repair, the fixed evaluator, and the stopping limit. Use D1's sequence and captions from docs/_includes/evolution-levels.md: change instructions/settings → run the same worker → independently test its output → retain the best measured settings. The starting settings can win.

Keep two explicitly connected examples:

Route Editable value Work being judged What it demonstrates Introductory help assistant One instruction in a plain mapping Returned help answers Instructions are measured through behavior; five required cells, no credentials or supporting imports Existing Meta-Harness study Typed planner text and context configuration Repository repairs executed against independent tests Governed edits, confinement, separate selection/final phases, accounting, and eligible export

Both workers and proposers are deterministic fixtures. The help assistant is a simulation, not a repository-repair agent or the research fixture. The advanced study executes real bounded repair/test processes, but does not reproduce the paper or establish general model improvement. State those limits beside results. Use only Shipped, Experimental/live-only, and Design—not shipped for status, following the existing convention for shipped lesson openings.

docs.title: 1. Shorten the introductory notebook
docs.text:
Maintain one complete source at examples/learn/harness_help.py, with snippet sections included by docs/guides/harness-evolution.md. Generate its notebook and Python download through the existing entrance hook. Keep every code cell below 40 lines; aim for fewer than 80 readable Python lines before the result.

Use {"planner": "Match exact questions."} as the seed. Keep both password and billing notes fixed outside the candidate. Preserve the existing three questions: reset password, please reset password, and download invoice. The single proposed instruction, Match topic words., changes the polite password answer from a missing-note response to Open Settings > Password. The expected measured result becomes 2/3 → 3/3, derived from actual answers. This replaces the old two-change 1/3 → 2/3 → 3/3 fixture; do not reuse its transcript or claim that the new score measures the same starting configuration.

Required cell Visible contents 1 Shared direct-install block, Python 3.12+, fresh-kernel instructions 2 Import, plain seed, fixed notes, complete assistant, and three fixed cases 3 Evaluator calling the assistant and retaining each question, actual answer, expected answer, and pass/fail 4 Handwritten proposer returning a new mapping with the changed instruction 5 improve(..., trials=1), measured starting/selected checks, changed answer, selected configuration, counts, and direct reuse

Show one proposal attempt and two evaluations, including the seed; explain that the declared attempt limit stops this run. Print observations from retained evaluation evidence instead of assigning scores to instruction names. Preview or reuse calls outside the run are not additional accounted evaluations. Reusing the selection on please download my invoice demonstrates adoption by the caller, not a held-out quality claim or deployment.

The main exercise sets trials=0: the starting configuration remains selected, the polite password request remains unanswered, and there is one evaluation. Also explain that changing an expected answer or adding an unseen phrasing can expose the simulation's limits. The evaluator stays independent of proposed instructions; unsupported instructions produce an evaluation failure with no score, while a completed wrong answer is an ordinary measured mistake.

Remove the initial HarnessArtifact, component fingerprints, expanded Experiment, held-out comparison, and export setup from the short notebook. Link to their concrete use in the advanced study after the first result. Ordinary mappings do not inherit typed harness mutation validation, resumability, or compare_harnesses/export_harness support. In particular, do not preserve the old typed no-op rejection test as a claimed mapping guarantee.

Preserve the guide URL and published fragment IDs. Old fresh-check/export anchors should lead to short, meaningful explanations and links to the matching advanced sections, rather than an unrelated next-step list.

docs.title: 2. Lead the research page with the actual repair
docs.text:
Open docs/research/meta-harness.md with the existing arithmetic example:

Observation Starting harness First revised harness Planner instruction Make a conservative change while preserving the interface. Diagnose requested behavior and repair arithmetic operations. Worker output in math_ops.py return value - 1 return value + 1 Independent check increment(3) == 4 fails The same check passes

Explain that the fixed worker interprets these instructions through authored Python branches. The instruction does not receive a score by itself: the worker produces source, and a fresh independent workspace executes the check. This first edit changes aggregate development quality from 0.0 to 0.5 across two repair tasks. A later context-setting edit reaches 1.0; keep it as a short continuation of the full study rather than a second prerequisite explanation.

Sources of truth for this example are flagship_declarations.py, fixture_responder.py, evaluation_core.py, and development_evaluation.py under examples/research/harness_evolution/. Derive/check the displayed instruction, repair, and measurement against their executed evidence.

Order the page as: concrete repair and two-level explanation; supported-runtime setup and result; mechanism worksheet and explicit typed declaration; diagnosis and citations; private selection, held-out comparison, accounting and export; paper comparison and evidence. Preserve the paper citation and the existing distinction between this bounded typed-surface study and Algorithm 1.

Keep short source excerpts where they explain a guarantee. Replace the supporting-source: harness directive and the full development-function dump with links to the complete source directory and existing harness-example.zip. Preserve the complete-supporting-source anchor as a useful source/download section. Essential expanded declarations remain visible, not hidden behind a new notebook helper.

Retain the existing study unchanged wherever possible: development diagnosis and authorized source reads; citation validation; private checks of all rankable occurrences; a frozen selection; matched seed-only held-out baseline/candidate runs; typed failures; separate inner/outer counts and resource roll-up; decision retention/replay; and export eligibility. Private selection may differ from the development winner. Exported settings are available for the user to adopt; neither selection nor export grants deployment authority.

Keep stopping conditions concrete: development allows two revisions, three evaluations, 100 fixture tokens, and 30 seconds, and may stop on satisfaction. Each private or held-out candidate has a seed-only evaluation with 40 fixture tokens and ten seconds. Print the phase report's actual usage and ceilings; inner proposal/evaluation counts remain separate from outer counts.

docs.title: 3. Supply an honest advanced notebook route
docs.text:
Generate downloads/meta-harness-repair.ipynb from the research page using the existing notebook exporter. Use visible Python setup/download/run cells and the existing complete archive; keep run_flagship as the execution owner and the existing CLI as the alternative terminal route. The introductory download is downloads/harness-improvement.ipynb, with downloads/harness_help.py as its canonical source download.

The advanced sequence is:

  1. Explain Python/OS requirements before setup. A small stdlib check rejects unsupported Python or platforms; a supported OS alone is not sufficient.
  2. Install the matching package directly and visibly download/extract the complete example into a fresh directory. No manual ZIP upload or checkout is required. Record matching archive hashes/revision for the audit.
  3. Before any study work, run a real confinement canary with the example's existing confinement_policy.launcher. Create a decoy in a protected output_root, pass that root to the launcher, and keep the allowed workspace separate. Confirm the parent can access the decoy, the child can read/write its own workspace, and the child cannot read/write the decoy. Show all definitions. Launcher failure must fail the check, not count as denial.
  4. Visibly import and call the downloaded study's existing run_flagship, which owns registration and all three phases. Print its report and inspect the retained first planner revision and episode-capture repair/check pair; do not rerun episodes to manufacture a separate demonstration. Locate the selected export. Explain fresh output directories versus compatible resume.

Use macOS with working sandbox-exec, or Linux with the example's required Landlock ABI 3 or newer. A failed canary stops before repair/proposal work with an actionable diagnostic. Do not disable protection or add a fallback runtime. No advanced Colab badge/support claim without an actual successful hosted run; a verified supported local Jupyter route satisfies the advanced requirement. The introductory notebook still requires fresh Colab and Jupyter verification.

The notebook exporter does not expand catalog source-function comments. Keep web-only explanatory excerpts within its existing web-only markers, with source links retained in notebook prose; executable notebook cells must be complete. Do not introduce another source renderer or duplicate the study.

docs.title: Acceptance and verification
docs.text:
Area Required observations Causal behavior Exact-to-topic edit changes the actual polite answer; removing/reverting it removes that improvement. Checks and expected answers stay fixed; seed remains immutable. Introductory execution Fresh notebook, final-cell rerun, whole-notebook rerun, downloaded Python, and rendered copied cells agree. Every required definition is visible; no sibling/test imports, credentials, prior state, or runtime network calls after installation. Limits and failures One attempt/two evaluations; zero attempts/one evaluation; malformed instruction is non-rankable with retained typed failure. No score table or version-name shortcut. Advanced behavior Captured increment repair passes the actual independent test, _meta_evolve_test.py is absent from captured candidate source, and unchanged controls preserve the full study's transcript and phase semantics. Grader diagnostics remain retained evidence. Confinement Positive workspace access plus denied access to an existing protected-root decoy; launcher/unsupported-runtime refusal stops early. Reuse existing adversarial confinement tests; do not imply all external reads are denied on macOS. Distribution and reading Strict build; historical routes/fragments; generated source/notebook parity; no full source dump; beginner and advanced links resolve from rendered pages and notebook prose. Installed runtime Exact built source ZIP installed non-editably outside the checkout, META_EVOLVE_LESSON_PYTHON used in the existing Docs job, import path verified. Both example archives match the tested build. Audit Source SHA and any dirty patch, Python/OS/kernel, install command/archive hashes, copied-cell transcript and control, required cell count, setup/run times, and manual interventions. Record Colab and Jupyter separately; agent rehearsals are not independent newcomer sessions.

Start with the changed lesson, notebook/download, catalog, route/navigation, and confinement/repair tests. Reuse the existing harness phase, accounting, private-isolation, failure, comparison/export, citation, and replay suites; broaden only as required by changed files and CI. Run strict docs and the installed-download checks from .github/workflows/docs.yml, including explicit selection of the new harness rehearsals. Finish with the repository's required CI checks. Tests should assert executed behavior and valid delivery, not prose spelling or an arbitrary section order.

Completion requires the evidence above and Salah's audit before #351 closes. Publication, independent newcomer sessions, research extensions, and paid runs retain their existing owners. Estimated implementation: 2–3 engineering days, plus hosted-notebook verification and review availability. The main uncertainty is confinement in a particular runtime, followed by download/source agreement; neither requires a core API change.

docs.title: Planning evidence, not implementation acceptance
docs.text:
Inspected HEAD: 9077011776a9b3cf6d2df57e798288e58a9c486c, with existing local documentation/example changes. No clean-commit, installed-notebook, or hosted acceptance is claimed by this plan.

  • The existing help notebook's nine tests passed in 0.34 seconds. It currently has ten code cells, with its first measured search result in cell seven.
  • The default Python-value codec already accepts a plain mapping. The proposed introductory declaration needs no artifact inference or API extension.
  • On Python 3.12.13, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, the current outer execution sandbox prevents sandbox-exec from launching despite supported() returning true. The same focused checks under native process permissions passed: four tests in 0.83 seconds, including real confinement and the flagship study.
  • A direct execution of the arithmetic episode confirmed the two captured repairs above and quality 0.0 → 1.0 for that episode; each run used one inner proposal, two inner evaluations, and three fixture tokens. Those tokens are fixture accounting, not model requests or billed usage.

These observations establish feasibility and the need for the early canary. Fresh-session timings, generated notebook execution, and rendered-page review remain implementation work.

docs.title: One objective and explicit context: plan for #334
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. This retained design record is subordinate to the canonical shipped contract. Source implementation and checks are recorded in the verification record; package publication is separate.

Prepared September 19, 2026 for #334, under #330. This selects a small extension to improve(); the selected contract is implemented. The programming model owns the shipped API and the architecture owns its execution invariants.

docs.title: Outcome and entry gate
docs.text:
A caller can minimize an error, set a satisfaction target, or supply bounded feedback without first constructing a Task and Experiment. The expanded declaration remains the reusable form of the same execution.

Implementation follows #331's author UX gate and uses #332's feedback contract. The accessor spelling, disabled-context behavior, and recency policy are covered by the dependency's tests and this slice's integration checks. Source integration does not close the GitHub issues or establish package publication.

Treat this as an additive API change in a subsequent release, outside the retained #313/#319 0.2 scope. The release owner assigns the version; this issue does not bump it, publish a package, or rewrite the frozen release contract. The selected boundary is recorded in the canonical implementation plan. Contract updates, executable examples, and tests accompany the behavior.

docs.title: Selected public contract
docs.text:
Append two keyword-only parameters, preserving the existing parameter order, defaults, exports, and concrete Run return annotation:

def improve(
    *,
    seed,
    proposer,
    evaluator,
    trials: int = 20,
    storage=None,
    random_seed: int = 0,
    objective: Maximize | Minimize | None = None,
    context: ContextPolicy | None = None,
) -> Run:

Use existing objective classes and the existing context policy protocol; no new root export or declaration type is needed.

  • objective=None inherits Task's default: maximize score, with no satisfaction target. A supplied Maximize or Minimize becomes the task's one-element objectives tuple. Strings, booleans, and sequences are invalid; a tuple containing one objective is not another accepted spelling.
  • context=None preserves disabled pushed feedback. Pass a supplied policy directly to Experiment.context. NoMemory() retains its existing equivalence to None. Structural local policies remain supported through existing validation; do not restrict this keyword to built-in classes.
  • trials still bounds successor proposals, including failed proposals. It must be a finite nonnegative integer; None and booleans remain invalid. Zero evaluates only the seed. Storage and random-seed behavior stay intact.

The call reads:

result = meta.improve(
    seed=seed, proposer=propose, evaluator=evaluate, trials=20,
    objective=meta.Minimize("error", satisfy=0),
    context=meta.RecentAncestors(),
)

RecentAncestors is the policy supplied by #332. The proposer requests feedback with def propose(parent, *, context) and reads context.evidence.latest("failed-cases"). That argument is an evidence label, not the objective's metric name. Keep the distinction explicit in the example.

docs.title: Stop rule for facade expansion
docs.text:
