Only consider individual declarative values with an obvious default and an existing canonical owner. This criterion is necessary, not automatic permission to add another keyword: every addition needs a named requirement and gate.

This slice admits exactly objective and context. Multiple objectives, artifact/environment declarations, budgets, custom search, registry, execution mode, and pulled experience use Task / Experiment / run. In particular, do not add budget until another decision settles its interaction with trials. Do not introduce **options, a procedure object, or provider options.

docs.title: Lowering and behavior
docs.text:
Keep the production change in application/improvement.py:

  1. Preserve the existing trials=None rejection.
  2. If objective is None, construct Task(evaluator=evaluator) exactly as today. Otherwise construct Task(evaluator=evaluator, objectives=(objective,)). Use an explicit is None check so false values cannot silently become defaults.
  3. Construct Greedy(max_trials=trials) and the existing Experiment, adding only context=context; preserve random_seed forwarding.
  4. Call the existing local run(experiment, storage=storage).

Do not duplicate Task objective validation, normalize policies in the facade, call select() early, or create an execution branch. The wrapper contributes no durable identity, schema, event, policy, or accounting logic.

Input or situation Required behavior from the existing engine Finite scalar evaluation Becomes the sole objective's measurement, including a custom name such as error. Mapping or rich evaluation Must contain the declared metric; extra diagnostic measurements are retained. No implicit renaming from score to error. Missing or invalid measurement Recorded typed evaluation failure, never a fabricated low score or preflight declaration error. All failures can produce a Run with no winner. satisfy=None No new target. A successful seed does not itself cause early satisfaction. Seed already satisfies One evaluation, zero proposals, objective_satisfied, including when trials=0. Unsatisfied seed, trials=0 One evaluation, zero proposals, trial_limit_reached. Ties or regressions Keep the earlier best result; preserve every committed attempt and its lineage. Declared context Select the same bounded records as the expanded path. Do not enable pulled experience or expose rejected siblings beyond the policy. Disabled context Valid when feedback is unused. Under #332's selected contract, attempting latest() raises ContextDisabled; do not catch it in the facade. Declared policy with no match latest() returns None; bounded selection and truncation do not trigger a hidden history query.

Preflight rejects malformed objective/context declarations before evaluation, proposal execution, or committed run facts. This is not a promise to execute arbitrary policy code ahead of time: selector errors happen at selection, and disabled-access errors happen when the proposer requests evidence. Preserve those distinctions and the expanded path's exception types.

docs.title: Compatibility and proof boundary
docs.text:
For the same callbacks, declarations, random seed, implementation revision, and isolated starting storage, the simple and expanded forms must agree on:

  • run ID and exact serialized events, including selected context;
  • artifact occurrences, decisions, selected measurements and winning lineage;
  • proposal/evaluation counts, reported resources, unknown spend, failures, lifecycle, and stop reason.

Compare declared context to the same declared context. Enabling feedback or changing the objective can legitimately change identity and behavior. Equivalence does not promise identical external model outputs across separate executions.

Keep handle metadata separate from run facts: #333's summary captures the storage location and durability. Two stores with different paths need not produce equal complete summaries. Assert each location independently and compare the shared summary facts; never normalize event bytes to obtain equality.

Capture default-call equivalence after #332's handoff, then compare before and after #334. Do not mistake #332's source-manifest changes for facade regressions. This wrapper is not currently an automatic registered-proposer dependency; verify that remains true and keep error/accessor implementation changes out of this slice. Historical reading and exact-source resume remain separate checks. Do not weaken source verification, introduce a schema migration, or claim that persisted local improve() runs become resumable. Registered durable execution still uses the expanded path.

docs.title: Focused validation matrix
docs.text:
Extend the signature/default assertions and baseline equivalence in tests/test_improve.py. Put the additional behavior cases in tests/test_improve_options.py, with feedback integration in tests/test_improve_context.py, so each file remains small. Reuse existing projection/serialization helpers where they already express the assertion; avoid a generic scenario framework.

Cases Evidence required Old calls; explicit objective=None, context=None; NoMemory() Same default declaration and committed facts; all eight parameters keyword-only, annotations resolve, existing export identity retained. Maximize / Minimize; scalar / mapping / rich results Correct direction and metric naming; diagnostic metrics, evidence, and resources preserved. Missing metric; invalid return; proposer/evaluator failure Identical typed outcomes, accounting, and no-winner behavior to expanded execution. Threshold absent, seed satisfied, later satisfied; ties/regressions; zero proposals Exact selected result, counts, lineage, and stop precedence. Bad objective type, objective sequence, bad context shape/bounds; retained bad trials Expected typed rejection and no seed evaluation or committed facts. Retain existing invalid-limit messages where contracted. Context off, AncestorsOnly, #332 recency policy, one structural local policy Same policy declaration, selected records and provenance; callbacks see the declared objective and no pull reader. Enabled empty/truncated bundle; disabled accessor use #332's None/diagnostic/error behavior propagates unchanged, including abort accounting. Do not duplicate its exhaustive policy tests. Memory and durable storage, then read-only reopen Exact facts across equivalent fresh runs and unchanged persisted history after close/reopen. Check persistence metadata separately. Typed Experiment, keyword run, and Session Retain their existing equivalence tests; add a representative new-options comparison only where the facade coverage leaves a gap.

Use deterministic evaluators and proposers; no paid providers or credentials. Run the focused improve/experiment tests first, then relevant reference/example, feedback, public API, annotation, historical reading, and registered-resume checks. The integrated implementation must pass the repository's required runtime and documentation checks; planning probes do not satisfy that gate.

docs.title: Documentation and example changes
docs.text:
• Update improve's docstring and the canonical programming model: signature/defaults, expansion stop rule, scalar metric naming, explicit feedback, and persistence wording. The generated API reference should consume that signature rather than acquire another handwritten copy.
  • Update the evaluation guide to show the single objective on the short path; retain the expanded example for ordered multiple objectives. The Task ordering contract does not change.
  • After #332 lands, update the feedback lesson with a short equivalent improve(context=...) declaration and the accepted accessor. Retain its expanded explanation and the disabled/empty/truncated distinctions.
  • Add small executable reference cases to examples/learn/reference_cases.py and API examples, covering scalar minimization and feedback. Extend tests/test_api_reference_examples.py to execute them. Keep files below the size guideline; split by example responsibility if needed.
  • Record the additive release treatment and revised compatibility guidance. The credential-free quickstart remains valid unchanged. #336 owns the full practical journey and newcomer study; neither is required to invent another SDK integration in this issue.

docs.title: Delivery sequence and difficulty
docs.text:
One focused implementation PR after the dependency handoff should suffice:

  1. Confirm #331/#332 acceptance and record the canonical technical boundary; capture the default baseline and retain #333's summary comparison distinction.
  2. Add the two parameters and direct lowering, with signature, failure-timing, default-preservation, and behavioral equivalence tests.
  3. Update executable examples, canonical contracts, and release guidance in the same PR; run focused checks and the required integration gates.

Difficulty is low–medium. The production change is a few lines of existing declaration composition. Most work is in deterministic equivalence coverage and consistent teaching. #332's finalized behavior and #333's summary equality are the integration risks; neither calls for a coordinator overhaul.

docs.title: Planning observations
docs.text:
Inspected committed baseline: 1607afbb81f7c5e457f97eb437b13ffb9ad63267, with concurrent #331–#333 and release edits left intact. Initial planning made no runtime changes; the subsequent implementation is recorded separately above.

The first improve/experiment baseline run produced 33 passed, 1 failed: the durable equivalence assertion compared complete summaries from different directories, including #333's new storage_location. A concurrent update to that test excluded this handle field; the repeat run passed all 34 tests. Preserve that distinction when extending the assertions for #334.

A disposable forwarding prototype outside the repository passed 22 paired runs across memory/durable storage, 2 comparisons with the current facade, and 7 malformed-declaration checks without evaluations or committed facts. It exercised scalar/mapping objectives, satisfaction including seed-only cases, missing metrics, disabled/empty/recent feedback, and reported resources. These observations used #332's local implementation and excluded handle metadata from summary equivalence; they demonstrate feasibility, not completed acceptance or a shipped API. Formal tests must repeat them against the accepted dependency.

docs.title: M10 local-author design
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This page is the subordinate design record for #151 (M10.0). The milestone roadmap owns status, order, gates, and exclusions. The implementation plan owns technical staging. Journey 2's Experiment declaration and dual-form run() call are shipped by M10.1, Journey 1's improve() call is shipped by M10.2, Journey 3's functional search is shipped by M10.3, and the aggregate Run.inspect() read model is shipped by M10.4. Journey 4's Session is shipped by M10.6. The read-only local browser shipped in M10.7; frozen-payload artifact presentation, previews, diffs, and canonical attachments shipped in M10.8. At the time of this record the parent M10 remained open; it has since shipped. Its current status is owned by the milestone roadmap.

The live examples were later reorganized by user journey under examples/learn/, domains/, operations/, agents/, and research/. Numbered paths below are frozen historical measurement evidence; the live functional-search fixtures now reside at examples/learn/functional_search/, and the live future reservation is examples/research/trusted_workers/.

The public story is: proposers create candidates, evaluators judge them, search decides what to try next, and Meta-Evolve records the entire process.

docs.title: Vocabulary tiers
docs.text:
The beginner tier names the seed, proposer, evaluator, and bounded trials=. The declarative tier adds Task, Experiment, search, context, experience, random seed, and registry. Storage, execution mode, and a narrowing budget are execution overlays. The extension tier retains SearchProgram.next() and the kernel records needed by advanced policy authors.

trials= is an author-facing cost and control limit, not exposure of kernel Trial records. Search state, trial specifications, operators, work items, events, and raw randomness stay off the simple path.

docs.title: Measurement rules
docs.text:
A physical line is every nonblank, non-comment code line. Imports and lines containing only delimiters count. Every counted line is classified once: algorithm expresses the limit, selection, stopping, or domain declaration; scaffolding adapts protocols, identities, execution, or syntax around those choices. Proposer, evaluator, and artifact-domain logic is held outside every search slice.

The shipped before-side for functional search is this runnable full-protocol shape, reduced from the repository's custom-search test without changing its protocol work:

from meta_evolve import domain
class IncumbentRefinement:
    policy = domain.PolicyRef("example:incumbent", "1", origin="local")
    def __init__(self, proposer):
        self.proposer = domain.ComponentRef.local_proposer(proposer)
    def next(self, state):
        if state.usage.trials >= 20:
            return domain.Stop(reason="trial limit reached")
        parent = state.incumbent_id or state.start.seed_artifact_id
        return domain.TrialSpec(
            task_id=state.start.task_id,
            parent_ids=(parent,),
            proposer=self.proposer,
            operator=domain.OperatorSpec(kind="rewrite"),
            budget=domain.Budget(trials=1, evaluations=1),
            random_seed=state.randomness.seed("trial"),
        )
search = IncumbentRefinement(propose)

It has 18 total lines: 3 algorithm and 15 scaffolding. It has one kernel import and constructs a trial manually. Changing only the name and limit for the two composition fixtures leaves those counts unchanged.

docs.title: Journey 1: beginner improve()
docs.text:
The smallest shipped declaration is bounded and can choose durable storage without claiming durable-local reconstruction:

run = meta.improve(
    seed=(),
    proposer=complete_one,
    evaluator=len,
    trials=3,
    storage=storage,
)

docs.title: Journey 2: explicit expansion
docs.text:
The shipped beginner call lowers exactly to this declaration and execution:

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(evaluator=len),
    seed=(),
    proposer=complete_one,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
)
run = meta.run(experiment, storage=storage)

docs.title: Journey 3: functional incumbent refinement
docs.text:
The shipped author-owned equivalent of the full-protocol before-side is:

@meta.search(max_trials=20)
def incumbent_refinement(search):
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)

The callback sees opaque occurrence-preserving seed and incumbent handles, immutable declared configuration, expand(), and stop(). The adapter owns budgets, proposer and operator binding, replayed stopping, and named randomness.

docs.title: Journey 4: uninterrupted, paced, and resumed Session
docs.text:
Uninterrupted execution remains one call:

run = meta.run(experiment, storage=storage)

Paced execution completes one committed decision per step:

with meta.Session.start(
    experiment,
    storage=storage,
    budget=budget,
    mode="local",
) as session:
    for decision in session:
        observe(decision)
run = session.run

Recovery continues the same authority and budget rather than accepting a new decision:

with meta.Session.resume(
    run_id,
    storage=storage,
    registry=registry,
) as session:
    for decision in session:
        observe(decision)
run = session.run

Uninterrupted and resumed execution must produce byte-identical durable histories. Human choices require a future declared component with recorded inputs; Session.step(decision=...) is prohibited.

docs.title: Journey 5: deterministic textual-feedback descent
docs.text:
This shipped functional-search fixture is derived from the deterministic development loop in examples/20_harness_evolution/; its proposer, evaluator, artifact domain, and held-out promotion check remain outside the slice:

@meta.search(max_trials=2)
def textual_feedback_descent(search):
    """Expand the incumbent after deterministic development feedback."""
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)

It is a deterministic, local, unpaid, unnumbered fixture under examples/functional_search/, not a new numbered example.

docs.title: Journey 6: deterministic AutoResearch composition
docs.text:
This shipped outer-search fixture is derived from examples/19_autoresearch/; private selection, public evidence, inner runs, and held-out evaluation remain evaluator- or user-owned:

@meta.search(max_trials=2)
def autoresearch_recipe(search):
    """Expand the selected recipe for the next bounded outer evaluation."""
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)

It is also deterministic, local, unpaid, unnumbered under examples/functional_search/, and outside the numbered sequence. Neither fixture creates or consumes the reserved examples/22_trusted_workers/.

docs.title: Friction scorecard
docs.text:
This is the historical M10.0 measurement, so its original proposed slice labels and line counts remain unchanged as later journeys ship.

Public names count distinct public API names in the slice; kernel imports count import statements from internal extension namespaces. A durability rewrite is an author change required to move from local execution to durable-local reconstruction. Reduction is the drop in scaffolding from the 15-line shipped functional-search baseline; it is published only where that comparison applies. The now-runnable Journey 5 and Journey 6 fixtures are statically recounted by the same rules at 3 algorithm lines and 1 scaffolding line each. Both therefore retain the published 93% reduction, well above the required 50%; the historical scorecard labels and measurements below remain unchanged.

Journey Slice Public names User-visible concepts Total Algorithm Scaffolding Kernel imports Manual trials First failure Durability rewrites Reduction 1 Beginner proposed 1 seed, proposer, evaluator, trials, storage, run 7 4 3 0 No invalid declarations fail before work; proposal and evaluation failures are typed outcomes graduate to Experiment and register components — 2 Expansion proposed 4 task, experiment, search, execution overlay 7 4 3 0 No duplicate or invalid declarations fail before work register reconstructible components and select durable-local mode — 3 Full protocol before 6 policy identity, state, trial, operator, budget, randomness 18 3 15 1 Yes malformed decisions fail at the protocol boundary provide a registered policy factory — 3 Functional proposed 1 limit, incumbent, seed, expand 3 2 1 0 No unsupported returns name expand() and stop() register the decorated policy for reconstruction 93% 4 Three execution forms proposed 2 experiment, overlays, decision, session, recovery 18 2 16 0 No start/resume validation fails before external work; later failures remain typed resume adds run id, storage, and registry, not new authority — 5 Textual feedback before 6 full policy and trial protocol 18 3 15 1 Yes malformed decisions fail at the protocol boundary provide a registered policy factory — 5 Textual feedback proposed 1 limit, incumbent, feedback-paced expansion 4 3 1 0 No unsupported returns fail with façade guidance register the decorated policy for reconstruction 93% 6 AutoResearch before 6 full policy and trial protocol 18 3 15 1 Yes malformed decisions fail at the protocol boundary provide a registered policy factory — 6 AutoResearch proposed 1 outer limit, selected recipe, expansion 4 3 1 0 No unsupported returns fail with façade guidance register the decorated policy for reconstruction 93%

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
These are the original M10 decisions. The September 18 pre-1.0 release policy supersedes their through-1.x / earliest-2.0 compatibility promises. The selected release inventory retains the keyword form, dictionary factories, and extension protocol in 0.2.

  • SearchProgram.next() remains the full 1.x extension protocol. Renaming it to decide() adds churn while @meta.search removes routine exposure.
  • Decorator configuration is immutable, serializable, and identity-visible. Hidden closure configuration is rejected. Lowering is exact and introduces no coordinator branch or special case.
  • Outer and inner loops, generations, and episodes remain relative explanatory terms, not new core types.
  • Dictionary-returning CLI factories remain supported through 1.x and now emit the M10.1 DeprecationWarning beside the typed alternative; removal is no earlier than 2.0.
  • M10.3 #164 shipped the docstring-derived DecisionDescription contract.

docs.title: Deferred and rejected alternatives
docs.text:
After M10, class-based harness surfaces may remove repeated field names and named search/context presets may improve discovery only when they lower exactly through existing validation, identity, authority, and durability contracts. Reflective proposer recipes remain user-owned.

Rejected alternatives are ambient configuration, execution-owning forward(), optimizer-owned compile(), hidden captured configuration, injected human decisions, fused proposer/evaluator/search layers, and any sugar that requires a coordinator, kernel, artifact, provider, or infrastructure special case.

docs.title: M11 trusted-concurrency design
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This page is the subordinate design record for #10. The milestone roadmap owns status, order, gates, and exclusions. The implementation plan owns technical staging and package boundaries. The distributed direction owns the longer arc through M12. This record owns vocabulary, the consistency model, the durable rules concurrency changes, and the compatibility promises.

Nothing here makes a name importable or an invariant implemented.

Longer than the other design records, deliberately: the rules below are one interlocking set — the outstanding-work definition, the decision barrier, the evaluation disposition and the reservation fold are four readings of the same predicate, and splitting them across pages would hide that they must agree.

docs.title: What distributed start refuses
docs.text:
The milestone roadmap owns the scope statement. This record owns the refusals that enforce it: seven configurations, each a CapabilityError naming its reason: six checked at start before any claim or lease, and the environment fingerprint, which will be checked when a worker claims. Single-process resume ships in M11.2: prepare_resume admits a distributed run (session_preparation.py, mode not in ("durable-local", "distributed")) and re-runs admission against the recorded values, with Session.drive() rolling the epoch over as the explicit recovery step. There is no Dispatcher.resume. What stays M11.3's is the CROSS-PROCESS re-read: the "Re-read on resume from" column below describes a worker rejoining a run another process is driving. Admission turns on a declared capability, never a named preset — checking for a specific policy by type would be the policy-specific coordinator branch the constitution forbids.

Refused Reason A declared context policy Pushed context binds a fact to an exact stream position, and its cutoff is strict where pull's is inclusive. A declared experience access Pull experience appends audit facts synchronously from inside the proposer, behind stream-global guards. A policy without the cohort capability The capability is a declared width and a producer, and only BestOfN declares the width. Greedy chains strictly, so each parent is the previous result and a generation has nothing to draw from. BestOfK is the natural second — _cohort_parent already freezes an incumbent for a whole cohort of k — but it neither declares a width nor produces a generation, which is #201. A finite token, wall-time or spend ceiling The shipped presets hand each trial the run's whole measured allowance — bind copies the declared token and wall-time ceilings, and narrow adds the remaining spend at decision time — so a second cohort member, computed from the same base where nothing is yet settled, has nothing left to allocate. Zero is refused with the rest; the budget section owns why. A custom codec Codecs carry no manifest; durable-local already refuses them. A worker with the wrong codec is worse than one with none. A component not declaring retry_safe Automatic retry of unsafe work is dishonest. Determinism is not required: that is durable-local's rule, for M4's interrupted-equals-uninterrupted guarantee, which a distributed run does not claim. An environment fingerprint mismatch See environment fingerprint. The comparison is unimplemented as of M11.2: the value is recorded and declared, never compared.

Every restriction is a refusal, never a silent degradation. Paid concurrency needs conservative per-trial allocation of measured dimensions, which M11.0 opened as #206 and which the measured-ceiling refusal above stands in for until it lands.

docs.title: Vocabulary
docs.text:
Four identities, none collapsed. The identity concept already establishes that equal bytes in different causal positions stay different occurrences; a work attempt is a third axis and folds into neither.

Term Meaning Identity Trial The logical experiment. Unchanged. Derived from its decision. WorkItem One deliverable unit. At most two per trial: proposal and evaluation. Stable from the trial and the kind. WorkAttempt One worker's bounded attempt at a work item. The work item and an ordinal, unique in the work table. Worker A trusted execution identity with declared capabilities and capacity. An operator-supplied id plus a monotonic generation.

docs.title: Execution terms
docs.text:
What runs work, and how its failures divide. None of these is an identity.

Term Meaning Worker process The operating-system process that hosts one Worker and connects to the dispatcher. Executor What runs a component on a work item's resolved inputs and returns its result, holding no coordinator, storage, clock or broker. Attempt failure Input resolution or the executor raised, outside the escaping set. The attempt is released and the retry bound decides. Completion failure A fault after the component returned: building its facts, validating them, or committing them. Its cause is recorded and it propagates; the dispatcher does not run the component again, though once the lease ends a later drain may. Input resolution The store reads that resolve a work item's inputs before its component is called.

docs.title: Semantics settled in M11.2
docs.text:
Four questions the vocabulary above left open. Each was answered because two adapters had answered it differently, and the shared contract suite could not see the disagreement.

A submission is the same when the fields ENQUEUE AUTHORS are the same — the trial, the kind and the retry bound. state and attempts belong to the broker, not the submitter, so a repeat submission of a work item that has since been leased is the same item further along, not a conflicting claim. Comparing them would make a retried commit of an already-partly-progressed cohort fail, which is the opposite of what an idempotent enqueue is for.

Enqueue is atomic across a generation. A cohort is enqueued as a generation, and a half-enqueued generation is the torn state the same-transaction rule exists to prevent. Every row is validated before any row is written.

An acknowledgment is opaque. It is bytes the broker records and returns without reading. A structured payload invites two writers to disagree about how to encode it, and two did.

A state and its justification are ONE fact. LEASED does not exist without the lease that justifies it; COMPLETED does not exist without the accepted attempt, its token and the acknowledgment. A lease also names its run, so a submission addressed to another run is refused rather than answered stale. States whose evidence is optional are how an orphaned row becomes permanently unclaimable in one implementation and silently released in another.

Attempt identity must be distinct, not secret. Authority comes from an opaque lease token, whose digest alone is stored, and from a monotonic fence. A derived attempt id therefore adds no risk and needs no entropy source. The result key is stable from the work item and is an idempotency key, never a credential.

The bootstrap trial has only an evaluation work item.

A dead attempt is released, not waited out. The broker gains release, fenced exactly as renew is and appending no fact: the scheduler already knows the attempt is dead, and letting the deadline expire instead idles the item for a whole lease duration to learn what it was told. The transition an unfinished lease leaves behind is released() / RELEASE_SQL, the same statement expiry and rollover make, so exhaustion goes terminal by the same rule in all three. The terminal LOGICAL fact an exhausted row then owes is the reclaim step's; a ledger edit does not discharge it.

Three outcomes. A raise that the adapters' own normalization boundary lets escape — the five infrastructure types plus CapabilityError, published as escapes_normalization — while resolving inputs or inside the executor aborts the run and is never retried; it records no cause. Any other Exception raised while resolving inputs or inside the executor is an attempt failure: released with its cause, and the retry bound decides. Reusing that boundary rather than writing a second taxonomy beside it is the point: retrying an escaping raise would spend the retry bound re-running an impossible preflight. And a fault after the component returned is a completion failure — building the facts, the provisional fold, the keepalive or the commit: the cause is recorded against the lease and the error propagates, because re-running a component that already answered spends a provider call to reproduce a coordinator fault. The row stays leased until expiry or rollover returns it to ready, after which a later drain may run the component again; closing that is M11.3's. Exception, not BaseException, so an operator's interrupt is neither released nor diagnosed.

record_failure writes a cause and moves no state. It follows the same diagnosis rule release does. The first writer wins per attempt, on every path. While a lease is held, only its holder may write. Once expiry has collected the lease, only the row's latest attempt may still diagnose, and only by proving the token it was issued against last_lease_token_digest, a verifier kept on the row through expiry and cleared when the lease is released or rolled over; a row with none refuses. Terminal rows are never rewritten.

A committed artifact missing from storage is corruption, not an attempt failure. Proposal parents and the evaluated artifact are ids the fold has already validated as committed, so a store answering "not found" for one raises DurableCorruption and aborts rather than spending the retry bound.

An inline call can outlive its lease. M11.2 runs one worker inline, and renewal happens only after the component returns. acquire stamps the deadline before the call runs, so a component slower than the lease -- 60 seconds by default, with no setting on Session.drive() -- expires its own lease and the run raises CapabilityError when it tries to commit its result (one that raises instead is released, with its diagnosis recorded). Renewal during a call, and configuring the duration, are M11.3's.

docs.title: Consistency by state type
docs.text:
Logical facts live in the run event stream; work, lease and worker state live in separate durable transactional tables. Leases cannot be ephemeral — a restart must retain the fence, deadline and accepted result — and must not live in the stream, because renewals are clock-driven: putting them there would make policy-observed versions depend on heartbeat frequency and make replay appear able to decide whether a historical lease is alive. The architecture separates committed facts from worker liveness; this record extends that into a second durable store rather than treating it as licence already granted.

State Home Writers Guarantee Logical run facts Event stream and artifact storage Dispatcher only Linearizable per run. No stale read may make or accept a decision. Outstanding work and reserved budget Derived by folding committed events — Exact at any stream version. Never read from the work ledger. Work item, lease, attempt, retry Durable work tables Dispatcher and scoped lease endpoints Serializable fenced transitions. Monitoring may lag. Trusted worker registry Installation-level table Operator authority only Strong on registration, revocation and claim. Worker liveness and free capacity Ephemeral, with a TTL Workers report, dispatcher observes Stale permitted. Can never authorize a claim. Queue and frontier statistics Disposable cache keyed by exact versions Dispatcher Staleness only for prioritizing already-eligible work. Archive membership Event stream Dispatcher only Strong and replayed. Sequential only — never inside a cohort. Promotion External governance record Governance Strong. Consumes only a drained, validated run.

"Strong" means one database transaction, not distributed consensus. Because attribution lives in the attempt table, the event envelope gains no actor field and no timestamp.

docs.title: The work and lease state machine
docs.text:
States are PREPARING, READY, LEASED, COMPLETED and CANCELLED.

The capacity inequality, which acquire names: a worker may hold at most its declared max_concurrent_leases leases at once, counted over rows in LEASED for that worker in the current epoch and generation, and the count is read inside the acquiring transaction so two simultaneous claims cannot both see room. That is the whole of it in M11 -- ONE dimension, a count of leases, not a resource vector. Per-item resource requirements and worker resource dimensions are deliberately not defined here: nothing in this milestone schedules on them, and the roadmap's acceptance case -- two concurrent claims exceeding one worker's declared capacity -- is a statement about this count and is testable against it. A richer inequality the implementation would not honour would leave that criterion with no normative behaviour behind it.

Every acquire, renew and complete precondition includes the current dispatcher epoch and the worker's current generation, read inside the same transaction — with one exemption, which is load-bearing. Terminal duplicate lookup on a COMPLETED item checks the accepted attempt and its token but not epoch or generation liveness. Without the exemption, "commit succeeded, acknowledgment lost, dispatcher restarted" would carry the prior epoch and be answered stale, contradicting the duplicate rule below. A terminal item is a stored fact, not a live lease.

complete is an INTENT, not a broker operation. M11.2 removed the broker's complete, whose own transaction could not be atomic with the logical batch, in favour of AcceptCompletion applied inside the writing transaction. The complete row above is unchanged in every respect that matters — the transition, and all four preconditions — because the intent carries the fence and the clock and checks them there. What moved is who applies the rule, not the rule. Moving it the first time DID drop three of the four preconditions to prose, which a review caught; they are enforced again.

An aborted item is not marked, and nothing distinguishes it. When the abort boundary fires before the component returns, _execute re-raises without releasing or recording a cause — but expiry routes the row through released() to READY one lease-duration later, so it does return to the queue, just slowly. In the interval it is neither claimable nor reclaimable (reclaim scans READY only) and carries no terminal fact, and afterwards no reader can tell an aborted item from a flaky one. Marking it needs the distributed-resume story — a run that aborted must not silently re-drive the impossible item on resume — which is M11.3's.

The terminal duplicate exemption ships in M11.2. AcceptCompletion answers a repeated completion by replaying the stored acknowledgment rather than refusing it, checking the accepted attempt and its token and deliberately not epoch, generation or deadline. The duplicate makes the whole commit a no-op: the intent unwinds the transaction, so the row keeps its bytes and the stream does not grow.

Duplicates remain unreachable through the dispatcher in single-process M11.2 — the batch and the intent share one transaction, a committed completion leaves the row terminal, and rollover skips terminal rows — so the exemption is exercised at the commit boundary rather than by a worker. Reattachment makes it reachable, because a Future dies with its process; M11.3 adds the submission seam that hands the replayed acknowledgment back, and the Duplicate answer with it. The stale half stays there too: a stale intent aborts its batch by design, because an intent rides the batch it authorises.

From Operation Preconditions To absent enqueue The authorizing logical batch commits PREPARING or READY PREPARING prepare This trial's prerequisites are committed READY PREPARING preparation failed Central preparation raised CANCELLED READY acquire Worker matches, including the capacity inequality above; attempts remain LEASED LEASED renew Same worker, attempt, fence and token; before the deadline LEASED LEASED expire At or past the deadline READY LEASED release Same worker, attempt, fence and token; before the deadline READY READY reclaim Attempts exhausted; rides the terminal logical fact CANCELLED READY or LEASED cancel Dispatcher or operator authority CANCELLED LEASED complete Exact worker, attempt, fence and token; before the deadline COMPLETED COMPLETED complete again Same attempt and matching token; epoch and generation deliberately unchecked COMPLETED any complete with a superseded or expired attempt, or a token mismatch — unchanged terminal any lease operation — unchanged

Enqueue inserts work rows in the same transaction as the decision cohort or genesis. Completion validates, appends the logical batch, enqueues dependent evaluation work, and stores an acknowledgment — all atomically.

The exhaustion edge was split in M11.2 (M11.2, implemented). This table originally read LEASED --expire at retry limit--> CANCELLED. Three broker-side transitions produce an unfinished lease — expiry, rollover and release — and none of them is committing a batch, so none can carry the terminal logical fact this record's sixth rule requires. A row terminated there would be terminal with nothing in the stream saying why, and nothing that would ever revisit it. All three now release to READY; the acquire guard (attempts < max_attempts) makes an exhausted row unclaimable, and the dispatcher's reclaim step terminates it with TerminateWork alongside the fact in one logical commit. The observable end state is unchanged; what moved is who owns the edge, so that it can carry its fact — and a crash between exhaustion and the fact now leaves a reclaimable row rather than a permanent silent hole.

The rules the table encodes:

  • The deadline is half-open. Completion and renewal succeed only strictly before it, read from the broker clock inside the transaction.
  • An expired but unreclaimed attempt may not submit a completion. Expiry follows from the clock read, not from whether a replacement exists. Its one remaining write is its own diagnosis, under record_failure's rule.
  • Duplicate is not stale. The same attempt with a matching token returns the original acknowledgment. Anything else is stale. Neither is an error, and neither writes.
  • Renewal racing expiry resolves in one transaction; the loser is stale.
  • Revocation bumps the worker's generation, invalidating its leases at the next transactional check.
  • Retry exhaustion, preparation failure and cancellation each append the terminal logical fact for their work kind — never a ledger-only edit.

Clock domain. Deadlines are absolute broker timestamps from a single authority; workers never decide expiry from their own clocks. The broker persists its last observed time and clamps its clock non-decreasing, so a rollback within an epoch cannot un-expire a lease. Across a restart the dispatcher epoch is bumped, and rollover is an explicit recovery step: every prior-epoch leased row moves back to ready, or is cancelled with its terminal fact when attempts are exhausted. Rows are never left unclaimable.

docs.title: Outstanding work and the decision barrier
docs.text:
Everything else keys off one definition. A trial is outstanding when it has a committed trial decision, or is the bootstrap trial, and either it has no completion, or its completion succeeded, its evaluation disposition is evaluate, and no evaluation has completed.

The bootstrap satisfies that second clause by exception, not by pin. It is never pinned a disposition — its evaluation is owed by genesis rather than authorized by one — so read literally the clause would exclude the very trial the first clause names, and a distributed genesis would leave no committed fact saying the evaluation is owed. The bootstrap is therefore outstanding while it has no completion, or a successful completion with no evaluation, and its disposition is not consulted.

The second clause is what distinguishes a trial that still owes an evaluation from one whose evaluation was terminally skipped as unauthorized. Treating every successful completion as terminal would accept a stop while an authorized evaluation is pending; treating none as terminal would reject a legitimate stop after a skip.

The disposition has three values, not two. Evaluate and terminally skipped are the two answers; the third is no answer — recorded for a failed trial, for the bootstrap, and for a trial whose own recorded usage exceeds its own allocation. The last of those is what makes the other two usable: with only two values, an overrun would have to be recorded as skipped, and the fold refuses an evaluation on a skipped trial, so every historical over-budget stream would stop replaying. Leaving the question unanswered where it is ill-posed is what lets skipped mean only "terminally skipped" and be enforced. A trial with no answer is not outstanding, so it neither holds a stop nor is owed anything — except the bootstrap, which is no-answer and outstanding at once. That is the one place the two come apart, and it is why the outstanding-work definition above names the bootstrap separately instead of relying on the pin.

A policy decision may be committed only when nothing is outstanding, or when the decision is a trial decision, every outstanding trial shares its cohort base, that base equals the stream head immediately before the cohort's first decision, and the decisions carrying that base form one contiguous run ending at this one.

A stop cohort has length one, so it can only be admitted through the empty branch. At width one nothing is ever outstanding at decision time, so the rule is today's sequential guard verbatim.

Consequently two shipped rules need no change at all: a committed stop remains an absolute terminator, and a run with a committed stop is complete. Observation cutoffs are likewise untouched, because context and experience are refused under distribution.

docs.title: Generational cohorts
docs.text:
An opted-in policy declares a cohort width and returns a cohort: a non-empty tuple of trial decisions produced from one complete committed history and committed as one atomic batch. Absence of the capability means width one and today's sequential decision.

Composition. Either a tuple of trial decisions bounded by the declared width, or a singleton stop. Mixed forms are invalid, and archive updates are never part of a cohort.

No truncation. The coordinator commits the whole cohort or refuses it entirely, as trial validation refuses rather than trims today. Sizing a cohort to what fits is the policy's responsibility, and it has the state to do it.

Width is declared, and reaches run identity by kernel derivation. A policy supplies its identity key independently of its configuration, so a conforming policy could record a wide cohort and still return the narrow key. The kernel therefore contributes the width itself, omitted at width one so every recorded run identity is unchanged. Any cohort-capable policy also exposes its width in durable configuration, likewise omitted at one, so the fold can bound cohort length with no live registry. The sequential path refuses a width above one, since without that refusal one declaration would stop early sequentially and run wide distributed under a single run identity.

Replay. Each decision still records the stream head immediately before it, so no field is ever false; what the policy observed is recorded separately as the cohort base. Consumers reconstructing a policy's input from the recorded head must switch to the base for members after the first, beginning with the search-program replay law. Replaying a cohort from its base must reproduce the committed tuple exactly.

Conformance. A published cohort suite carries the laws: composition and length, full-or-refuse, exact replay from the base, per-member randomness attribution, no member referencing another member's artifact, width present in configuration exactly when it exceeds one, and a width-one coherence law requiring a singleton cohort to equal the sequential decision. Passing a suite is a developer obligation, not a durable fact: the executable admission predicate is the structural declaration, and the suite is what makes it honest.

docs.title: Budget: one disposition, and a pure fold
docs.text:
Reserved budget is derived from committed events, never stored: any capacity freed outside the stream would make a later decision unreproducible.

One evaluation disposition, consumed by every caller. At a successful trial completion, over the prefix including that event, available capacity is the ceiling less settled usage less the reservations of every trial except this one. Excluding the completing trial's own allocation breaks the circularity — an incomplete sibling reserves its full allocation, and a completed one was resolved at its own earlier terminal event.

Two terms survive from the shipped calculation and are not replaced by the reservation fold. The trial's own remaining allocation still narrows the result, so a trial that exhausted its own budget is skipped even where the run's capacity is ample. And spend is adjudicated against the trial's own charge, so a free proposal under a zero ceiling still evaluates. The disposition is therefore the run's available capacity narrowed by the completing trial's remaining allocation, authorized when the narrowed budget leaves no zero among its evaluation, token and wall-time allowances and spend is not exhausted against that trial's own charge. The fold adds a term to the shipped rule; it does not replace it. Anything looser would flip committed skip decisions into evaluations and move durable bytes.

That rule is only consulted where the question is well-posed. A failed trial, the bootstrap, and a trial whose recorded usage exceeds its own allocation are pinned no answer instead — see outstanding work for why the third value is what makes the refusal on a skipped trial enforceable.

That value is pinned at one event, so it is stable for all later prefixes, which is what makes live execution and recovery agree by construction -- and agreement means every reader consults the pin rather than re-deriving it. A reader that recomputed the overrun instead would call a stream corrupt that this fold has just declared replayable, which is exactly the contradiction #217 resolves in the fold's favour. Five callers consume it: the live completion path, the resume tail, the recovery frontier classifier, the outstanding-work definition, and the dispatcher's atomic accept-and-enqueue path. The general remaining budget keeps its meaning for admitting new trials but is no longer a valid input to evaluation authorization.

A trial reserves its full allocation until it completes, its evaluation residual while an authorized evaluation is owed, and nothing once it has failed, been terminally skipped, or had its evaluation complete.

Erratum (M11.2). This paragraph originally continued "The bootstrap trial follows the same rule", and that is the same mistake the errata above correct in two other places: the bootstrap's evaluation is owed by genesis and is never authorized by a disposition, so under the unamended wording a completed bootstrap reserves nothing — which the table's own last two rows deny. The bootstrap reserves on the same schedule as any other trial but on a different authority, and the fold needs two explicit branches for it rather than none. What does carry over unchanged is the reason it needs no special allocation: no policy decision may be committed before the run is ready, so its reservation is never concurrent with a cohort.

Trial state Reserved Released by Decided, no completion committed Its full declared allocation Its own terminal fact Completed, evaluation authorized and owed, other than the bootstrap trial Its evaluation residual: the allocation less the usage already settled against it The evaluation completion, successful or failed Completed, evaluation terminally skipped Nothing Already released by the completion itself Completed, disposition unanswerable, and not the bootstrap Nothing Already released by the completion itself -- nothing can be owed against a question the fold refused to answer Failed proposal work Nothing Its trial completion carrying the failure Failed evaluation work Nothing Its failed evaluation completion, never a second trial completion Failed before any proposal — preparation failure, cancellation, retry exhaustion Nothing The full shipped failure batch Bootstrap, decided, no completion committed Its full allocation Its evaluation completion Bootstrap, completed, evaluation owed Its evaluation residual Its evaluation completion

These rows are a partition: every trial state matches exactly one row, and a failure releases through the one mechanism its work kind names.

The dimensions are not interchangeable, and the reservation fold governs only two of them:

Dimension Finite under distribution How admission uses it trials, evaluations Admitted — the only finite dimensions M11 serves The exact reservation fold above tokens, wall_seconds Refused finite at start Nothing until #206 defines a per-trial share spend_micros Refused finite at start, zero included Never a reservation. Budget.spend_micros is a ceiling that halts, not a hard cap, so it has no prospective form to reserve against

Every capacity release is a committed logical fact whose kind differs by work kind: proposal work terminates with a trial completion, evaluation work with a failed evaluation completion, never a second trial completion. Work that never produced a proposal — preparation failure, cancellation, retry exhaustion — commits the full shipped failure-batch shape rather than a bare completion.

Exactness, in three parts. Admission is exact over committed facts. A component may still overrun its allocation, which commits as a typed resource exhaustion with its actual figures and halts the run — shipped single-trial behaviour, not a concurrency regression. And consumption is exact only over accepted completions: a stale or orphaned attempt writes nothing by design, so what it consumed never reaches the run's usage. That gap is new to distribution and is documented rather than papered over.

A monetary hard cap additionally requires provider-side idempotency and bounded spend authority. Declaring a component retry-safe is necessary but not sufficient: it says reinvocation is logically safe, not that billing is idempotent.

A finite spend ceiling is refused at distributed start, zero included — and zero is the one monetary declaration with nothing to allocate, since spend_exhausted reads it as free-work-only and arms only once something bills. Refusing it therefore refuses a configuration cohorts could otherwise serve. The refusal stays blunt deliberately: at width N a zero ceiling admits up to N charges before the halt arms where the sequential path admits one, and weakening a declared prohibition by the cohort width is a worse thing to ship than a missing capability. #206 is where per-dimension allocation earns the right to separate them.

docs.title: Worked traces
docs.text: Each trace is a step sequence over the two ledgers, written so an implementation can be checked against it without re-deriving the rules above. W is a work item, t the broker clock.

docs.title: Lease expiry, and the replacement that supersedes it
docs.text:
Step t Event stream Work table 1 0 The trial decision commits W inserted READY, attempts 0, in the same transaction 2 0 — Worker A acquires: LEASED, attempt 1, fence 1, deadline 30 3 25 — A renews: deadline 60, same fence 4 61 — A is silent. The next transactional read finds the deadline passed: LEASED → READY, attempt 1 abandoned 5 62 — Worker B acquires: LEASED, attempt 2, fence 2, deadline 91 6 70 — A returns and submits under attempt 1, fence 1 7 70 — Stale: the fence does not match. Nothing written, nothing raised 8 80 The trial completion for B's result, and the dependent evaluation item, commit together W → COMPLETED, accepted attempt 2

One logical trial throughout; the retry created an attempt, not a trial. Whatever A consumed — tokens, and any charge it incurred — never reaches the run's usage. That is the documented consumption gap, not an accounting defect.

At step 4 expiry follows from the clock read alone. Had B never arrived, A's submission at step 6 would still be refused: an expired but unreclaimed attempt may not submit.

docs.title: Duplicate versus stale submission
docs.text:
Both arrive at a COMPLETED item. The columns are the two OUTCOMES, not a partition of the inputs, and the difference matters: the accepted attempt carrying a mismatched or absent token matches neither column as written. The state machine classifies it stale (complete with a superseded or expired attempt, or a token mismatch), and it must, because the token is what proves the submitter is the worker that earned the attempt. A duplicate is therefore the accepted attempt AND a matching token; everything else at a terminal item is stale.

Duplicate Stale Attempt The accepted attempt Any other attempt Token digest Matches Mismatched or absent Epoch and generation Not checked — the terminal exemption Not checked Answer The original acknowledgment, replayed A stale answer Writes None None Raises Nothing Nothing

The exemption is load-bearing exactly once — when the acknowledgment is lost across a dispatcher restart:

Step Event stream Work table 1 The completion batch commits W → COMPLETED, accepted attempt 3, acknowledgment stored 2 — The reply to the worker is lost in transit 3 — The dispatcher restarts; the epoch is bumped; prior-epoch LEASED rows roll over, and W is untouched because it is terminal 4 — The worker retries attempt 3 with its token 5 — Terminal duplicate lookup matches attempt and token, ignores the stale epoch, and replays the stored acknowledgment

Without the exemption step 5 would answer stale, and a worker would believe committed work was lost.

docs.title: Bootstrap evaluation
docs.text:
Step Event stream Work table 1 Genesis commits the run start, the seed artifact and the bootstrap trial The bootstrap evaluation item is enqueued in the same transaction 2 — The bootstrap trial has no proposal item; it is the one trial whose only work is evaluation 3 — A worker claims and completes it under the ordinary state machine 4 The bootstrap evaluation commits, and the run becomes ready W → COMPLETED

Between steps 1 and 4 the run exists and is not ready. Inspection is available and returns the shipped overview fields without raising; no policy decision is admissible. That is why the bootstrap reservation is never concurrent with a cohort, and why it needs no special allocation rule.

docs.title: Cohort admission refusal
docs.text:
Refusal has two independent shapes, and neither trims.

Step Declared width Policy returns Outcome 1 4 Five trial decisions Refused whole. Length above the declared width is invalid, and the coordinator does not keep the first four 2 4 Three trial decisions and a stop Refused whole. Mixed forms are invalid; a stop cohort is a singleton 3 4 Four trial decisions, one referencing another member's artifact Refused whole. No member may reference a sibling, which has not been committed

The barrier refuses on a different axis — the decision's provenance rather than the cohort's shape:

Step Stream state Decision offered Outcome 1 Nothing outstanding A trial cohort based at the head Admitted; this is the empty branch, and it is today's sequential guard verbatim 2 Two trials from that cohort outstanding A further trial decision on the same base Admitted only while the decisions carrying that base form one contiguous run ending at this one 3 Two trials outstanding A stop Refused. A stop cohort has length one and can only be admitted through the empty branch, so a stop with work outstanding is rejected 4 Two trials outstanding A trial decision based at a later head Refused. The base no longer equals the head immediately before the cohort's first decision

docs.title: The seven distributed-start refusals
docs.text:
Every row raises CapabilityError, naming its reason, before any claim or lease is issued. Single-process distributed resume ships in M11.2: prepare_resume admits a distributed run, re-runs admission against the recorded values, and Session.drive() rolls the epoch over as the explicit recovery step. There is no Dispatcher.resume — resume is Session.resume(...) followed by drive(). Cross-process re-read stays M11.3's.

Of the seven, one is genuinely re-checked on resume against a value that can drift: the cohort capability, because the program is re-resolved from the supplied registry. Context, experience, budget and codec are read from the committed start and cannot change, so their resume-side refusals are store-tampering backstops rather than admission re-checks; the codec row is enforced by check_declared_codec on every reader's path.

Six of the seven are enforced, and the seventh is a different KIND of rule. The fingerprint row is recorded and not compared — see environment fingerprint — and it could not be compared at start or at resume even once that lands, because a worker's fingerprint is not part of the run declaration and no worker exists yet. It is the one refusal that will fire when a worker CLAIMS, and it will refuse the worker rather than the run.

resumable means the run recorded enough identity to resume, not that it replays identically. For durable-local the two coincide, because its components are deterministic by admission. A distributed run may carry a non-deterministic component — a model-backed proposer is the ordinary case — and resuming one continues the search rather than reproducing the trajectory it would have taken uninterrupted. That is the schedule-sensitivity this record already states, made explicit at the flag that would otherwise imply more.

Refused Read at start from Re-read on resume from A declared context policy The run declaration's context policy The committed run start A declared experience access The run declaration's experience access The committed run start A policy without the cohort capability The supplied program's structural declaration The re-supplied program's declaration, cross-checked against the recorded configuration A finite token, wall-time or spend ceiling The effective budget: task and run declarations narrowed The committed task and run capabilities A custom codec The declared artifact codec The committed run capabilities A component not declaring retry_safe Every resolved component manifest The manifests re-resolved for the recorded refs An environment fingerprint mismatch Not at start: a worker's fingerprint is not in the run declaration and no worker exists yet Not at resume either. This one will be checked when a WORKER CLAIMS, against the recorded run fingerprint, and refuses the worker rather than the run

Resume is the strictly harder direction: a run admitted under a conforming program can be resumed with a program that no longer declares the capability, or in an environment that has drifted since, and neither is visible from committed history alone.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text:
Ranking keeps score primary: evaluations are pre-ordered by their producing trial's logical step, then stably sorted by score, with the evaluation id as a final tiebreak — so a later better score still wins and only exact ties are decided by logical order. On sequential streams logical order equals completion order, so existing runs are unchanged.

A cohort barrier makes the set of results visible at the next boundary independent of arrival order, but not the policy's view of them, because policy-facing collections remain in commit order. Either those collections are canonicalized by logical step, or the cohort suite carries a completion-permutation-invariance law. This record chooses canonicalization, for the same reason width is kernel-derived: a structural guarantee beats a trust-based one, and a policy should not become schedule-sensitive by accident.

Canonicalization lands where each collection is built, not where it is read. The completed trials and evaluations are ordered at insertion by their producing trial's logical step, with the evaluation id as the final tiebreak.

The artifact list is ordered later than the others, and for a structural reason: an artifact is committed before the completion that attributes it, so at insertion there is no producing trial to order by. The completion carries both the artifact ids and the logical step and lands in the same batch immediately after, so that is where the list becomes canonical -- and the seed attributes to the bootstrap at step zero. Reading order out of the projection instead would put a sort on the fold's hot path, which the reserved-budget fold already showed is where cost accumulates.

Retry exhaustion remains a genuine divergence no ordering rule removes, since scheduling decides whether a completion lands inside or outside its deadline:

A distributed run reproduces every decision and named random choice from its committed history. Repeating the same declaration and seed reproduces the same trajectory only when every outcome is itself deterministic and no attempt is abandoned — a non-deterministic provider or a lease that expires under load will diverge. A cohort barrier guarantees that the set of results visible at the next boundary does not depend on arrival order.

docs.title: Environment fingerprint
docs.text:
A versioned digest over the interpreter implementation and version, the platform, the resolved distribution set, and the installed Meta-Evolve source digest, recorded on the run's capabilities and declared by every worker; mismatch refuses the worker.

The comparison is unimplemented as of M11.2. Distributed start refuses a run with no fingerprint, and Dispatcher copies the run's onto every WorkerRegistration it builds — but neither broker's acquire reads worker.environment_fingerprint, so nothing compares the two. The value is carried and never used as a guard. The refusal message says so rather than claiming a check that does not happen, because AGENTS.md names misleading reproducibility claims an anti-pattern, and a user reading a refusal is entitled to believe it.

It becomes real with M11.4's durable worker table, which is the authority that admits a worker in the first place: comparing fingerprints is part of admitting one, not part of handing out a lease.

A RESUME-TIME comparison is a different question, and it is deferred for a different reason. On resume both values are already in hand — the recorded fingerprint on RunCapabilities, and the current one from environment_fingerprint() — so nothing about worker-table authority blocks comparing them. What blocks it is what the digest covers: the installed meta-evolve SOURCE and every installed distribution. Measured: changing the source digest, adding one unrelated package, or a patch-level Python bump each move the fingerprint. A strict resume-time comparison would therefore refuse every legitimate resume across a code change or a uv sync — which in this repository is the ordinary case, not the exception, since evolving the source is the point.

So the open question is not authority but POLICY: which dimensions must match for a resume to be safe. Platform and interpreter plausibly must; the source digest plausibly must not, or the flag means "resume only the exact build that started this run". Whoever implements #203 should decide that before writing a comparison, rather than discovering it from a refused resume.

It is a version-set fingerprint, not environment identity. Name and version pairs do not identify installed bytes, so two editable or locally patched installs can match, and the platform string omits OS release and libc ABI. It reliably detects drift; it does not prove sameness. Content-hashed distributions are the exit.

docs.title: Byte compatibility and frozen fixtures
docs.text:
M11.1 changes durable folds while leaving every recorded byte where it is, so the anchors that would catch a regression are named here, before the first code slice begins.

Anchor What it pins tests/fixtures/v3_durable_run/ A real SQLite store frozen before Usage.spend_micros existed. Every stored envelope must re-serialize to its exact stored bytes, and reopening must replay identical accounting _FROZEN_V3_TRIAL_COMPLETED in tests/test_durable_format.py One TrialCompleted envelope captured verbatim, not synthesized by stripping fields from today's object GOLDEN_EVENTS in tests/test_event_serialization.py The bare event bodies for the recorded event types serialization.identity_content at schema version 1 Task and run identity, frozen to the v1 envelope while the durable schema version moves independently SearchSpec.configuration The policy's durable configuration map, which cohort width joins

The technique is the one #143 established for money, and it is why the record schema stayed at v3 (CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION): a new field omitted at its default moves no existing byte. The store-schema ladder in durability.py is an independent one and it does move in M11.2, for the work and epoch tables -- additively, adding tables and touching no existing row or column, unlike v1 to v2 which had to backfill a digest. Stated as "the ladder moves" rather than as a rung number, because naming one is how this sentence rotted twice: it read "stayed at v3" before the work tables landed, and then a specific rung one migration after they did. durability.py is where the current rung lives. Two ladders, two answers; conflating them points a future migration at the wrong file. Cohort width follows it exactly — absent from the configuration map and from the kernel's identity contribution at width one — so every existing run identity, SearchSpec encoding and event stream is unchanged by construction rather than by inspection.

One obligation these fixtures cannot see. Width must survive policy rebinding: a preset that reconstructs itself when bound drops any field the reconstruction omits, and a silently narrowed width would run wide under a narrow identity. That is a code obligation for M11.1, and only a test that binds and then reads the width back will catch it.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Central decision authority with generational execution — one dispatcher is the sole caller of the policy and the sole writer of the stream. Two ledgers, with lease state durable but outside the event stream. Attempts distinct, not secret, with the lease token and fence carrying authority. Reserved budget as a fold, every release a committed fact. One evaluation disposition, pinned at completion, consumed by all five callers. Cohort width declared on the policy and contributed to run identity by the kernel. Policy-facing collections canonicalized by logical step. The sequential path refuses a width above one.

docs.title: Deferred and rejected
docs.text:
Deferred. Steady-state refill, which admits new work while earlier work is outstanding: it does strictly more than cohorts, is not asked for by #10, and costs a general pending-work capability, a post-stop drain rule, a changed completeness definition, and per-policy conformance. Distributed context and experience, which need a cohort-aware prerequisite grammar, a reconciled cutoff, and an endpoint carrying an operation ordinal with attempt and resolution appended atomically. Concurrency for further presets, each behind proved pending-work semantics. Paid concurrency, behind conservative per-trial allocation.

Rejected. Decentralized policy decisions; leases in the event stream; workers appending envelopes; reservation rows outside the stream; releasing capacity without a terminal fact; redefining what a decision's recorded head means; cohort width as an execution overlay; truncating a returned cohort; mixed-kind cohorts; archive updates inside a cohort; policy-specific coordinator branches; a trial id serving as both work identity and lease credential; secret or random attempt identities; completion-order tiebreaks; running every policy concurrently by default; adding a distributed mode to the synchronous callable path; actors or timestamps on the event envelope; external queue dependencies; multi-dispatcher consensus or failover.

docs.title: M8 harness-evolution design brief
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This is a retained design record. The programming model and project status identify shipped behavior; proposals below do not extend those contracts. This retained decision brief records the design that preceded M8 implementation. Current executable semantics live in the shipped programming model and architecture; official-SDK validation closed the M8.6 gate on retained authorized captures.

Design one bounded experiment: start from a worker harness containing a planner prompt and context policy; let an outer proposer change only those surfaces; score each candidate on fresh held-out repository tasks under equal budgets; compare it with the unchanged harness; leave promotion external.

The deterministic demonstration is examples/research/harness_evolution/.

Its execution boundary is decision-complete: the example accepts a user-owned proposer callable, CI drives it with a deterministic fixture-backed SDK client, and an opt-in maintainer driver may invoke a real SDK through the same callable shape. See the user-owned SDK boundary. The first authorized live run is captured once and sanitized without dropping regressions, ties, or failures. Evaluation, equal budgets, mutation authority, and promotion remain outside the wrapper.

docs.title: Map onto current seams
docs.text: M8 concept Current seam HarnessArtifact Artifact codecs, registries, component identity, and lineage MutationSurface Proposal validation, policy violations, and workspace capture Held-out evaluation Evaluators launching bounded fresh inner runs Harness comparison Run summaries, usage, failures, and comparison validity External promotion A governance decision after search selection SDK execution A user-owned callable returning a candidate or ProposalResult

docs.title: Locked executable decisions
docs.text:
• Search evaluates development episodes. Held-out episodes evaluate only the unchanged baseline and selected candidate, each with Greedy(max_trials=0).
  • Candidate encoding is followed by generic core-side successor validation before artifact commit. MutationSurface.apply() is convenience only.
  • The parent declares mutable surfaces. Successors cannot change parameter names/types, component references, interfaces, or non-surface state.
  • Planner text and context policy are independent implementations governed by one published conformance suite.
  • Evaluator identity includes exact suite content, worker/model declaration, budgets, timeouts, environment, and scoring/aggregation rule.
  • Resume guarantees begin at a committed outer evaluation. Uncommitted inner work may repeat.
  • One held-out fixture demonstrates the boundary; it is not statistically strong promotion evidence.

docs.title: Implemented artifact and identity
docs.text: The built-in artifact is agent-harness / harness-manifest-v1, with exactly one TextParam planner and one PolicyParam context policy. Existing artifact occurrence identity, content digest, lineage, and component references apply.

docs.title: Mutation authority
docs.text: Only text and policy configuration change. The codec returns InvalidOutput for malformed/no-op transitions and PolicyViolation for authority expansion; the proposal, evidence, and typed failure commit without a successor artifact.

docs.title: Held-out evaluation
docs.text: Portable episode values and fresh inner runs are implemented. Hidden tests and process controls remain evaluator-only; captured attempts, diagnostics, diffs, failures, and counts become outer evidence.

docs.title: Comparison and promotion
docs.text: compare_harnesses enforces the full equality gate and reports quality, actual usage, failures, verdict, and eligibility. best() never deploys anything.

docs.title: Replay and extensions
docs.text: Outer episode capture is ordinary durable evidence. Fault injection proves a committed outer evaluation is not repeated. Both built-in surfaces pass the same published suite without a coordinator branch.

docs.title: The blocker, and how it was closed
docs.text:
The first authorized official-SDK result is committed without dropping its failures or tie: strict output-schema validation rejected both proposal calls, so no native mutation reached decoding or successor validation. That was the blocker, and it stood until a second separately authorized capture exercised the boundary -- two complete manifests through decoding and the trusted successor path, retained unimproved in experiments/08_harness_evolution_live/capture-openrouter.json. The failed result remains part of the record beside it.

Closing the blocker is the whole of the claim. It is not paper reproduction, not statistical generalization, and not a claim that the live run should have promoted anything: its private split scored every candidate 0.0, so selection fell back to the seed and the held-out comparison tied.

docs.title: Acceptance evidence
docs.text:
• Valid prompt and context-policy mutations use one ordinary coordinator path.
  • Authority violations are typed rejections with no successor artifact.
  • Composite identity, lineage, component provenance, nested usage, and failures replay.
  • Held-out inner runs are fresh and comparison fails closed on mismatched controls.
  • Resume performs no committed episode twice.
  • Promotion remains an explicit external outcome.

Final review must make candidate authority, distinct causal identity, parent lineage (the parent lineage invariant), effective budget, every typed failure, replay, comparison validity, and promotion ownership explicit.

docs.title: Meta-evolution
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This is a retained design record. The programming model and project status identify shipped behavior; proposals below do not extend those contracts.

M9's deliberately small trusted policy-artifact slice is shipped and owned by the policy-evolution guide and canonical architecture. This page now records only future generalization beyond that slice; it defines no additional shipped classes.

docs.title: Inner and outer loops
docs.text:
Future outer candidates may describe broader harnesses or policies. Their evaluators would run fresh, bounded inner meta.run() episodes against an experiment-controlled suite. Inner artifacts, trials, evaluations, failures, evidence, and usage would retain their own identities while linking to the outer evaluation.

The candidate could change only a declared mutation surface. It could not change the suite, hidden splits, evaluator, enclosing budget, permissions, cache semantics, or promotion rule.

docs.title: Broader policy meta-evolution
docs.text: M9 already compares its two-field policy artifacts under exact controls. Any broader policy space must remain compatible across task distribution, model, evaluator, environment, seeds, and budgets. Aggregation must preserve uncertainty and typed failures rather than average missing measurements into low scores. Held-out results remain unavailable until the relevant evaluation permits them.

docs.title: Nested budgets
docs.text:
Outer and inner evaluation, trial, token, and wall limits require explicit reservation and settlement. Inner exhaustion cannot consume undeclared outer authority. Cache reuse is valid only when every behavior-affecting declaration matches.

M8 and M9 used decision-complete designs and the harness_evolution and policy_evolution examples. See the M8 design and milestone roadmap.

docs.title: Distributed and network direction
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This is a retained design record. The programming model and project status identify shipped behavior; proposals below do not extend those contracts.

The shipped execution profiles are local and durable-local. Distribution begins only after local semantics remain stable under concurrency and failure.

docs.title: Trusted distribution
docs.text:
The M11 trusted-concurrency design is the subordinate record for that step. A trusted worker design needs durable attempts, leases, renewal, expiry, cancellation, idempotent result submission, capability matching, and a budget reservation fold over committed facts. Delivery retries retain one logical trial. Out-of-order wall-clock completion cannot change logical random choices or reveal future experience.

Isolation and placement are separate axes. Where a candidate's code runs is the sandbox and workspace boundary and needs nothing from distribution; which machine claims which work item, and how a result is accepted exactly once, is the distributed concern. A platform may own placement and isolation. It may never own work identity or result acceptance: platform-internal retry is acceptable only when contained within one attempt and bounded by the same idempotency key, never creating an attempt the ledger does not know about.

docs.title: Federation
docs.text:
Cross-institution exchange additionally needs scoped identities, signed manifests, visibility, licensing, attribution, embargo, retraction, disputes, and task-specific trust. Policy-filtered subgraphs may preserve causal shape while redacting content.

Worker liveness, service health, queue estimates, and caches are ephemeral. Accepted artifacts, evaluations, budgets, authority changes, and promotion decisions remain durable. No network design may weaken candidate authority or failure honesty.

docs.title: Partial execution budgets: implementation plan for #315
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 18, 2026 for #315, under #313. The budget contract owns the proposed semantics; this page specifies the implementation, tests, and migration for that contract. This page retains the pre-implementation plan; the current contract, canonical acceptance gate, and implementation verification now record the separate #315 source change.
