docs.title: Starting point and dependency
docs.text:
The inspected checkout is c04ec6b4b949b8a2702779107e25acd24feb8020 plus the uncommitted #297 reference/docstring work and API design documents. Preserve that work and identify its exact integration revision before implementation. The programming model and architecture remain the shipped contract owners.

The local #314 plan records a pre-1.0 compatibility reset with 0.2.0 as the working release target. At this issue check, #314 remained open with its foundation checklist unchecked and no dated decision comment. Planning can proceed now; landing runtime work requires its foundation contract/release checkpoint and the named Author API revision gate in the canonical roadmap. It does not require all optional API comparisons to finish or #314 itself to close.

Keep #315 as one focused PR: a private resolver at the existing preparation boundary, observable regression coverage, and matching documentation. Preset defaults, counting names, per-trial allocation (#206), callback dispatch, summary redesign, and M11 concurrency remain separate work.

docs.title: 1. Freeze the concrete behavior
docs.text:
Within the execution override, omitted or explicit None means inherit the task ceiling. A standalone Budget still uses None to mean unlimited. Zero is a real supplied value. A finite override above a finite task ceiling is invalid, even when a different dimension tightens. Removing a task ceiling requires changing the task declaration; no execution-time escape is added.

For a task with Budget(trials=4, evaluations=5), require:

Execution override Resolved outcome None Four trials, five evaluations Budget() Four trials, five evaluations Budget(evaluations=2) Four trials, two evaluations Budget(trials=4, evaluations=2) Identical to the preceding partial override Budget(trials=0) Zero trials, five evaluations; seed-only execution Budget(evaluations=0) Four trials, zero evaluations; existing seed admission refusal Budget(trials=3, evaluations=6) Explicit widening error before work or run facts

Apply the same resolution rule to tokens, billed micro-USD, and elapsed work. Without a task ceiling, a finite supplied dimension introduces one; two absent dimensions remain unlimited. Search still has its own stopping configuration.

With Greedy(max_trials=None), the partial two-evaluation example binds a policy limit of four, evaluates the seed, makes one proposal, and stops with budget_exhausted. Its usage is one trial and two evaluations, and history has two records. The resolved ceiling is not a promise that all four trials run.

docs.title: 2. Change one preparation seam
docs.text:
application/session_preparation.py:prepare_start() currently chooses budget or task.budget or Budget() and then checks the whole value against the task ceiling. Replace that choice/check with a small private _resolve_run_budget(task_budget, override) in the same module.

The operation has three steps:

  1. If one declaration is absent, use the other; if both are absent, use Budget(). Do not use resource truthiness to detect omission.
  2. For each of the five dimensions, reject when both values are finite and the explicitly supplied override exceeds the task ceiling.
  3. After validation, return task_budget.narrow(override) to inherit omitted dimensions and retain supplied tighter ones.

Keep Budget.narrow() unchanged. Intersection alone would silently clamp an explicitly excessive request, which is not the proposed contract. Keep the existing ValueError("run budget cannot widen the task budget") for widening and the existing non-Budget type check; changing error taxonomy or messages is unnecessary for this slice.

Preserve the current validation order: storage/codec/seed validation and the mode/random-seed/budget type checks precede resolution. Resolution then precedes component execution, proposer run validation, policy binding, distributed admission, identity construction, and commitment. Do not promise that constructing a storage handle or encoding the seed has no side effects.

The resolved budget must reach all existing consumers unchanged:

  • validate_proposer_run() and prepare_search();
  • distributed admission when that mode is requested;
  • run_id_for() and RunStarted.run_budget;
  • the coordinator's existing accounting and work-admission paths.

run() and Session.start() already share this preparation boundary. Add no independent resolver in those entry points or in CLI factories. Do not change improve()'s signature or preset constructors. The module is currently 450 lines with an existing rationale and a 478-line ceiling; a small helper should fit that allowance. Recheck the size after implementation rather than growing the baseline or creating a new module for this operation.

docs.title: 3. Specify observable regression coverage
docs.text:
Put focused coverage in tests/test_run_budget_overrides.py if the existing files cannot accommodate it cleanly. Existing test_experiment.py, test_session.py, and test_preset_budget_inheritance.py retain their relevant contracts; avoid copying their full fixture matrices.

Case Required assertion Resolution table across all five dimensions Literal expected ceilings for absent, equal, tighter, wider, newly bounded, and zero values; inputs remain unchanged Absent/empty budgets No task budget, empty task budget, no override, and empty override have the specified meanings Mixed dimensions Tightening one dimension cannot conceal an explicit widening elsewhere Validation timing Invalid widening invokes neither proposer nor evaluator and commits no run facts; preserve existing type/constructor failures Entry-point parity Typed run, retained keyword run, and exhausted Session agree on resolved declarations, usage, stop, and history Effective-budget consumers Proposer validation and preset binding see the inherited ceilings, not the sparse override Seed/zero handling Partial zero trials produces seed-only work; partial zero evaluations raises BudgetUnavailable with no calls or run facts Genuine unbounded inheritance max_trials=None still fails when neither declaration supplies a finite trial ceiling Resolved preset limit A task trial cap survives an evaluation-only override and persists as the same concrete integer in search configuration Authority in distributed mode A count-only partial override remains admissible when otherwise valid; inherited finite measured ceilings, including zero, retain the current capability refusal

Private resolver cases may cover the full value table cheaply; public-entry cases must prove validation timing, binding, and recording. Test expected values/outcomes rather than reproducing the resolver algorithm in a test. Reuse test_domain.py's constructor/intersection guarantees; do not expand the issue into a new numeric validation design.

The most important equivalence test runs a partial override and its fully specified equivalent in separate stores with the same task, seed, components, policy, and random seed. Require identical run IDs, serialized events, occurrences, search configuration, final usage, and stop reason. The raw override is not a new identity input or durable fact. In the same storage, ordinary duplicate-run refusal should still apply.

Retain stop-reason distinctions: an inherited trial allowance can end with trial_limit_reached; an evaluation ceiling reached earlier ends with budget_exhausted. This issue neither changes stop precedence nor treats failure as a low score. Keep unrelated callback/result API expectations owned by #316/#317 when their changes later integrate.

docs.title: 4. Prove recorded budgets survive recovery
docs.text:
No event field, durable type, schema version, or identity formula needs to change. application/transitions.py must keep validating that recorded run budgets fit the recorded task. prepare_resume() must continue passing start.run_budget to policy reconstruction, component validation, admission, and the coordinator; it must not call the new start-time resolver.

Use registered, deterministic, retry-safe components and existing tests/_faults.py helpers. Add a small dedicated recovery test file if needed rather than further enlarging the existing resume suite.

  1. Run an uninterrupted reference using the full effective budget.
  2. Start the equivalent partial-override run, interrupt at real committed frontiers, close/reopen its store, and resume without a new budget argument.
  3. Assert the recorded effective budget and bound integer are unchanged, and the final event stream, identities, counts, resources, and stop match the reference. Do not truncate records to manufacture a crash.
  4. Use #314's captured old fully specified run to distinguish old-runtime resume, new-runtime read, and new-runtime resume with matching manifests. Historical partial overrides that were rejected have no run to migrate.
  5. Keep unknown spend, failed-work costs, and historical post-call overages correct. In particular, a partial override must not lose a task's monetary ceiling and thereby allow evaluation after a proposal reports unknown spend.

Reuse the existing monetary, unknown-spend, historical-overage, and distributed resume suites for their established guarantees. Add the targeted inherited monetary-ceiling case; do not duplicate every recovery matrix across every budget dimension or mode.

Compare built-in component manifests before and after the isolated #315 patch. No policy/registry change is planned. Keep any source-digest effects explicit, including user-declared dependencies that include edited documentation source. Separate them from #297's already observed digest changes. An old history may remain readable while incompatible execution correctly refuses; weakening verification is not a remedy for a failed compatibility check.

docs.title: 5. Migrate the reference and current contracts together
docs.text:
The local #297 work deliberately documents the old replacement behavior. Update those same owners when the runtime change lands; do not discard that work or leave contradictory current-behavior prose behind.

Owner Change in the implementation PR Budget and run() docstrings; Session.start() parameter guidance Explain override-specific inheritance, explicit widening refusal, and one resolved allowance docs/programming-model.md Replace the whole-budget replacement contract with partial restriction semantics docs/guides/evaluation-and-budgets.md, docs/guides/limits.md Show a sparse restriction and preserve accounting/seed/admission explanations docs/guides/budget-override-migration.md, examples/learn/budget_overrides.py, and the API reference cases Replace the dataclasses.replace workaround with the actual partial override and print the resolved ceiling tests/test_api_reference_examples.py Replace the assertion that partial tightening raises with success/equivalence coverage; retain a real widening refusal docs/implementation-plan.md Correct the shipped #163 explanation that quotes the old resolution expression, preserving its historical milestone and preset semantics docs/milestones.md, relevant architecture text, migration guide Record #315's acceptance under the #314 gate and its release-specific behavioral difference

For the reference example, retrieve limited.inspect().declaration.effective_budget to print the retained trial ceiling. Reading .trials from the sparse request would print None, which would misrepresent the allowance. Retain the useful output: ceiling four, one proposal, two evaluations, budget_exhausted. Remove the replace import only if no other example needs it. Keep the existing snippet/route anchors.

The current example test rejects Budget(evaluations=2). Replace that rejection with Budget(evaluations=6) against the task's five-evaluation ceiling; assert that the immutable task still has its original limits.

Migration notes must state that Budget() and sparse overrides which formerly raised can now execute work. Existing valid full declarations and dataclasses.replace(task.budget, ...) calls remain valid. Explicit None cannot remove a task ceiling. Do not add a compatibility flag, sentinel, new budget class, or schema migration for this behavior.

docs.title: 6. Verify and complete one slice
docs.text:
1. Run the focused resolver/entry-point/equivalence tests, then existing experiment, Session, preset-inheritance, and domain budget tests.
  2. Run targeted recovery and monetary/unknown-spend/overage checks, plus the relevant distributed admission and recovery coverage.
  3. Execute the migrated reference cells and printed outputs; run reference, evaluation/limits guide, ownership, route, and file-length checks with a strict documentation build.
  4. Validate the example against a fresh installed package outside the checkout through the maintained Docs workflow's download checks.
  5. Run the required integrated CI/Docs selection once the slice is stable; use .github/workflows/ci.yml and docs.yml as command owners. Repeat for subsequent relevant changes or unresolved failures.
  6. Record the exact implementation revision, package/environment, real pass/fail/skip counts, before/after compatibility outcomes, and any limits.

Close #315 only when the new partial call works, explicit widening still refuses before work, normalized facts/recovery are correct, all five dimensions are covered, and canonical docs/examples teach the same behavior. The wider coordinated release and hosted meta-evolve-docs publication remain #318/#319 work; this PR does not independently publish a package or site.

docs.title: Planning evidence, September 18
docs.text:
The unchanged runtime passed 110 tests from test_experiment.py, test_session.py, and test_preset_budget_inheritance.py. A temporary probe at /private/tmp/meta-evolve-315/baseline_probe.py confirmed that empty/partial overrides currently fail with zero component calls and no stored run. Full tightening executes one proposal/two evaluations; zero trials is seed-only; zero evaluations refuses seed admission. Its results are saved beside it in baseline-probe.json.

These observations validate the starting behavior and the test design. They do not demonstrate that the proposed resolver, migration, or compatibility gate has been implemented.

docs.title: Practical journey and newcomer handoff: plan for #336
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This is the integration plan for #336, under #330. It prepares one complete practical journey and the existing independent-review handoff. It does not implement an API, publish a package, or certify a newcomer session.

The source implementation now follows this plan; the verification record owns actual results and remaining independent reviews.

The programming model, architecture, author UX gate, and implementation plan remain authoritative.

docs.title: Outcome and entry gate
docs.text:
Keep the credential-free first run. Make the existing routing-prompt journey show one continuous story: define independent checks, authorize development feedback, try bounded revisions, inspect measurements and typed failures, capture a useful snapshot, save history, reopen in a fresh process, and adapt the evaluator. A completed, understood experiment is success even when the seed stays best.

Use the accepted contracts from these dependencies:

Dependency Contract #336 consumes #331 Short entrance, matching install instructions, existing newcomer packet #332 context.evidence.latest(kind), enabled/truncated state, RecentAncestors #333 Capture RunSummary inside storage lifetime; render it afterward #334 One objective and explicit context on the small callable path #335 with meta.open_run(...), explicit or only-run selection

Planning and partial rehearsals may precede dependency acceptance. Before #336 acceptance, all five need their accepted source, canonical contracts, and focused verification on the chosen integration revision. Open issues and concurrent local implementations are not proof of a matching installed package. Record that revision, dependency evidence, and any remaining limitations before integration. This work does not add a blocker to #319 or select a new release version.

docs.title: Reuse the routing journey
docs.text:
Use examples/learn/llm/prompt.py, prompt_cases.py, and openai_client.py as the canonical complete journey. Its independent Python grader, request journal, development/final separation, and provider-replacement tests already exercise the difficult boundaries. Keep the three-file download and existing commands.

The short SDK notebook remains the low-request introduction. The full journey continues to use 40 development cases, at most three revisions, and 12 separate final cases: at most 163 development requests plus 12 final requests, without retries. A preview remains a preview; it does not measure model accuracy. Do not change datasets, request defaults, or claim live improvement as part of this integration. The parser remains an alternative example, with its existing coverage retained rather than a second overhaul.

docs.title: Keep the two authoring paths honest
docs.text:
Use #334's improve(objective=..., context=...) in the existing credential-free feedback lesson and the own-evaluator adaptation exercise where those declarations are sufficient. Keep an explanatory link to the equivalent expanded declaration; reuse the lesson's callables and tests rather than add a second implementation.

Both SDK examples record model/request configuration in Task.environment; the complete driver also accepts an execution budget. Keep their explicit Task → Experiment → run path. Replacing it with improve() would discard identity or budget declarations. Do not add environment, budget, search, registry, mode, or pull-access keywords to make this example fit the small path.

docs.title: Make feedback complete and attributable
docs.text:
Today the full routing evaluator emits one routing-case per ticket, and the proposer groups records by maximum logical step. latest("routing-case") would return only one ticket. Introduce one lesson-owned routing-feedback evidence report per returned evaluation outcome, containing the evaluated prompt's SHA-256, completed checks, completion state, and typed failure kind if present. Keep existing per-request/per-case evidence for inspection and partial-work receipts. This small, bounded duplication avoids a new grouping API or loss of diagnostics.

Emit the report last, including when an evaluation returns a known typed failure. An interrupted evaluation has partial observations and no score; it must not pretend to have evaluated the remaining tickets. An accounting-unknown escape retains its existing receipts instead of manufacturing a completed report.

The proposer reads context.evidence.latest("routing-feedback") under RecentAncestors, with explicit record/rendering bounds. Reserve this label for the trusted evaluator; SDK response evidence uses its existing distinct label. Check the report's prompt digest against the supplied parent before using it. This checks the report's subject, not evaluation-occurrence identity: equal prompt bytes can occur more than once, and the accessor's exact ref remains the source occurrence. Do not claim the accessor authenticates a producer.

  • Required feedback with disabled context raises ContextDisabled before a rewrite request. An enabled selection with no report, or a mismatched report, produces an actionable CapabilityError before dispatch; no silent empty or stale-feedback fallback. Known failed seed evaluations still have their report so a repair attempt can proceed.
  • Surface the aggregate truncation flag. Continue when a usable report for the parent remains selected; the flag alone does not prove that report is partial. Record omission and rendered-text clipping are different possible causes.
  • A deliberate feedback-off comparison uses an explicit optional-feedback guard in the existing feedback exercise. Do not weaken the full driver's requirement.
  • Render the selected structured report into the request. max_chars bounds bundle text, not item.data or SDK request size; the fixed development suite bounds the report. Never query omitted history or use final checks to fill gaps.

Keep the first integration's existing context allowances unless focused tests justify a smaller bound. Tests must establish parent feedback after several revisions and rejected siblings; do not infer that a preset guarantees it.

docs.title: Show results and preserve storage ownership
docs.text:
Capture and display result.summary() while the store is open. Retain a small attempt/evidence view and selected-prompt export beside the summary: aggregate counts alone cannot explain a failed attempt. Render the captured summary again after closing storage, without reading a live Run or re-executing an evaluator.

Replace the manual read-only-store/Run construction in --inspect with open_run(directory / "history", run_id=...). Preserve run-id.txt for explicit identity, plus the chosen directory. Demonstrate only-run selection in the existing persistence guide, without inventing chronological ordering of IDs. Catch only the expected no-run case for an interrupted first request; missing or corrupt stores and ambiguous selection retain their typed diagnostics.

Final evaluation stays after development selection and outside search history. Its results and usage remain in final.json. requests.jsonl overlaps history; their totals must not be added. Reopening performs no SDK calls and grants no resume capability. In-memory SDK notebook output says history is not saved durably.

docs.title: Three reviewable implementation steps
docs.text:
Step Changes Completion evidence 1. Integrate the complete journey Routing evidence report and proposer, recent context, snapshot output, explicit reopen; update live guide snippets in the same change Real driver/evaluator/accounting/storage tests with synthetic provider responses, including failures and final isolation 2. Align the entrance and installed artifacts Add feedback/accessor and summary to the short SDK notebook; use #334 in the existing feedback lesson; align persistence/discovery links and generated downloads Copied cells with real SDK and simulated HTTP; extracted lesson with a non-editable package outside the checkout; strict docs checks 3. Deliver the existing review handoff Extend newcomer prompts and regression scenarios, record engineering evidence and repeated SDK glue Maintained packet linked from #275/#277 coordination material, exact setup and limitations, input for #337

For step 2, the short SDK evaluator already emits a complete routing-checks report. Add the parent marker and consume that report, preserving its six-ticket batch evaluation, at most three requests, explicit SDK settings, and accounting. The full journey owns final evaluation and the complete persistence story; do not inflate the short notebook with all of those operations. Keep notebook cells below 40 lines and hand-written files normally below 300 lines.

Primary files and their responsibilities:

  • examples/learn/llm/prompt.py: integrate the existing driver and evaluator. Leave provider settings/accounting in openai_client.py and data in prompt_cases.py; no coordinator or core-package change is expected.
  • docs/guides/live-prompt.md, docs/guides/providers.md, docs/learn/05-use-experience.md, docs/learn/06-persist-run.md: complete, runnable instructions; update links and reference examples only where affected.
  • Existing routing, SDK-notebook, feedback, persistence, and download tests: extend behavioral checks at their current owners; add a narrowly named test file only if the coverage needs its own responsibility.
  • docs/hooks/entrance.py and .github/workflows/docs.yml: retain generated canonical downloads; change the installed rehearsal only if coverage requires it.
  • docs/project/capability-walkthrough.md: extend the current packet and preserve dated evidence. Add docs/project/practical-journey-verification.md when actual integration results exist; link it from the existing evidence/navigation pages.

docs.title: Deterministic acceptance scenarios
docs.text:
Extend existing fixtures; substitute the provider or HTTP transport, not the grader, coordinator, accounting, or storage. Synthetic scores are test evidence only. A single live run is not required to happen to exhibit a failure.

Scenario Required observation Improvement, tie, regression, satisfied seed Correct parent retained; complete parent report used; stop reason and proposal/evaluation counts agree with history Seed remains best Completed experiment and useful summary; no promised positive delta Missing required metric or all evaluations fail Typed evaluation failures, no invented score/winner; inspectable summary and retained usage; no final check without selection Disabled required feedback ContextDisabled before rewrite dispatch; enabled/no-match is a distinct case Missing or stale selected report Clear configuration diagnostic before rewrite; no reach outside the selected bundle Record truncation and text-only truncation Test separately, including max_records=0 and max_chars=0; flag is truthful and intact structured reports remain usable Rejected or failed sibling, repeated parent text Latest authorized report remains correctly associated; a digest does not replace occurrence provenance Wrong completed answer versus unavailable output Wrong labels remain measured mistakes; empty/incomplete output keeps typed failure with no score Failed rewrite or partially failed evaluation Known usage/evidence retained; failed rewrite skips evaluation; partial evaluation produces no fabricated full-suite score Unknown spend or token accounting Unknown spend stays None; unknown required accounting escapes with receipts, committed prefix, and no hidden retry Snapshot and reopen Snapshot renders after close; fresh process uses only installed package and saved files; queries make zero SDK calls Empty/multiple-run stores and explicit selection Expected typed diagnostics, explicit ID works, no lexical-recency assumption or hidden fallback Final evaluation succeeds or fails No final case/result in development history or rewrite requests; final failure never reopens search; usage remains separate

Reuse #332/#333/#335's focused contract tests rather than reproduce their whole matrices. New checks here must prove the examples use those contracts correctly.

The installed archive test currently makes routing's seed perfect. It exercises no rewrite and therefore cannot establish the new feedback path. Extend that existing rehearsal with an imperfect seed, a revision, and an injected failure; verify the exact generated archive in a fresh directory and new interpreter. Keep test providers outside the public ZIP; no imports from tests or examples may be needed by the installed journey.

docs.title: Verification and retained evidence
docs.text:
Start with the focused routing files:

uv run --locked pytest -q tests/test_llm_prompt_lesson.py tests/test_llm_prompt_persistence.py tests/test_llm_prompt_docs.py tests/test_llm_openai_client.py

Then run changed feedback/persistence lessons and SDK notebook tests, the latter with the existing pinned SDK environment and simulated HTTP. Build docs strictly and run rendered/download checks through .github/workflows/docs.yml, including META_EVOLVE_LESSON_PYTHON pointing at a non-editable install of that build's meta-evolve.zip. Confirm the import path is outside the checkout. Follow the broader required checks in .github/workflows/ci.yml; packaging/release evidence remains with #272/#319. No package publication is part of this issue.

Record source SHA plus any dirty patch, package version/hash, docs revision, Python/OS, commands, results, fixture identity, saved-history locations, and remaining failures. Version text alone cannot establish revision agreement. Distinguish local source checks, installed-artifact checks, hosted CI, live captures, and independent review. A skipped SDK test is not a passed SDK check.

Planning baseline, September 19, 2026: the existing routing lesson and persistence tests passed 29 tests in the shared working tree at HEAD 1607afbb81f7c5e457f97eb437b13ffb9ad63267, with concurrent dependency edits. Command: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_llm_prompt_lesson.py tests/test_llm_prompt_persistence.py. This supports reuse of the existing journey; it is not a clean-commit reproduction, installed-package check, or #336 acceptance.

docs.title: Newcomer and QA handoff
docs.text:
Extend the existing packet, which already separates setup time, own-evaluator completion, and unprompted feedback problems. Keep participant prompts separate from observer answers. Observe an unaided adaptation first, then use controlled fault scenarios; a diagnostic task does not establish that a problem occurred spontaneously.

  1. Start at the homepage, install matching artifacts, and finish the first run.
  2. Build a bounded experiment for the participant's small problem using their own evaluator; inspect the result, including when no revision improves it.
  3. Observe whether they independently discover, enable, and consume useful feedback. After recording that outcome, ask them to diagnose disabled, missing, and truncated feedback in prepared credential-free scenarios.
  4. Ask them to explain a typed failed attempt, a low measured score, proposal versus evaluation counts, and unknown spend using the recorded result.
  5. Save, restart, reopen, and inspect without the original callbacks; explain the snapshot's lifetime and why saved local history is not resumable.

Add only missing observation fields: first unprompted feedback consumption; diagnosis of each feedback state; count/failure interpretation; successful reopen; abandonment and reason; and baseline/after docs, package, task, and assistance conditions. Time the own-evaluator task from its prompt to a completed run and inspected result; record setup separately. Record independent, assisted, blocked, abandoned, and not-attempted outcomes rather than reporting only successful times.

Bhasker and Salah agree session stopping rules and any timing/comparison thresholds before interpreting sessions. Preserve #275's requirement that three unfamiliar users complete the required journey without maintainer intervention after fixes. Report individual observations and retest exposure; three sessions do not estimate confusion prevalence. The same participant's learned retest is not a fresh baseline.

docs.title: 277 receives reproducible scenarios from the matrix, exact installed setup,
docs.text: expected/actual outcomes, retained histories, and defect links. #275 retains independent sessions and Salah's acceptance; #269 retains independent SDK and accounting review; #274 retains documentation coordination. #270/#271 own paid protocols and live captures. This handoff neither contacts participants nor runs paid experiments. #336 can close on complete engineering and handoff evidence while those owner-specific reviews remain explicitly open.

docs.title: Remaining SDK glue and difficulty
docs.text:
Inventory repeated author work for #337 with exact source locations: request configuration, token validation, typed output handling, Resources conversion, unknown/billed/estimated spend, partial-request receipts, and request journaling. Compare the short notebook with openai_client.py and the full driver. Record what differs and why; shared spelling alone does not justify a library helper.

Estimated difficulty is medium, approximately 3–5 engineering days once dependency contracts are stable, including example/docs changes and installed rehearsals. This excludes external review, release work, live experiments, and participant scheduling. The main risks are incomplete/stale feedback, loss of SDK identity/accounting while simplifying, source/download drift, and mistakenly counting automated checks as independent usability evidence. A defect requiring new runtime semantics returns to the owning dependency; #336 stays integration.

docs.title: Selected API behavior contracts
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

These contracts support the implementation plan. They describe selected behavior and acceptance cases, not the current package. The review contains the observed failures and rationale. The September 18 foundation decision freezes these contracts for the coordinated pre-1.0 release. Implementation remains in #315–#317.

docs.title: API-2: compose budget overrides
docs.text:
The #315 implementation plan specifies the shared resolution seam, test matrix, recovery checks, and documentation migration. The implemented slice is now covered by the programming model and verification record; this section retains its design and acceptance rationale.

Keep Task.budget as the experiment-owned ceiling. Treat the budget= execution argument as a partial restriction, resolving every dimension independently. Within this argument, None means inherit, including when explicitly written; it cannot remove a task ceiling. A Budget value on its own still uses None for an unlimited dimension.

Task dimension Override dimension Effective value / outcome None None None finite c None c None finite r r finite c finite r <= c r finite c finite r > c Validation error before proposer/evaluator work or committed run facts

Apply the table to evaluations, trials, tokens, spend_micros, and wall_seconds. Zero is a real ceiling, never a falsey synonym for omission. Constructor validation of types, non-negative values, and finite values remains in force. budget=None and an empty Budget() both preserve task ceilings. With neither task nor execution ceilings, the result is Budget(); search's own stopping behavior remains a separate concern.

For example, a task capped at four attempts and five evaluations plus Budget(evaluations=2) resolves to four attempts and two evaluations. Before

docs.title: 315 that call was rejected. The migration guide
docs.text: explains that previously rejected partial overrides can now execute work.

docs.title: Implementation boundary
docs.text:
Use one private resolution operation at application/session_preparation.py's shared start boundary. Do not reimplement it separately in run, Session, CLI factories, or policy binding. Validate before committing the run or calling components; do not promise that declaration construction, codec validation, or storage-handle creation has no side effects.

Resolve before policies consume the effective budget. Record the result in the existing run-start data. Replay and resume consume recorded values, never reapply current defaults or a new override. Keep the fold's invariant that the effective budget cannot exceed the recorded task ceiling.

Budget.narrow() remains mathematical intersection; do not change it to this stricter override-validation operation. Keep post-call resource enforcement, seed accounting, exact counts, unknown spend, and failure-cost retention intact. An external resource ceiling does not become a hard interruption guarantee.

docs.title: Required cases
docs.text:
• Cover every row for each dimension, including zero, an absent task budget, multi-dimension overrides, and invalid constructor inputs.
  • Reject an explicitly wider dimension even when another dimension tightens; no proposer/evaluator call and no initial durable run facts may result.
  • Exercise typed and compatibility run() forms and Session.start() with identical declarations and normalized effective budgets.
  • Exercise inherited preset limits after resolution, zero attempts with seed evaluation, and an evaluation ceiling that disallows evaluation entirely.
  • Read and resume a captured run without re-resolving its allowance. Existing valid explicit declarations keep their normalized identity and trajectory unless an independently documented manifest change prevents resume.
  • Preserve unknown-spend refusal/propagation, post-call overage outcomes, and non-rankable failures with retained resource usage.

Extend test_experiment.py, test_session.py, and test_preset_budget_inheritance.py; use existing monetary and durable tests for cross-cutting guarantees. Update the budget/limits guides, reference cases, and programming model in the same slice.

docs.title: API-3: make callback context explicit
docs.text:
The #316 implementation plan specifies route-aware binding, automatic invocation-source verification, migration, and recovery tests.

For plain callables, supply the parent positionally. Supply framework context only when a named keyword-only context parameter opts in. Choose and validate the call shape once, before component execution; never execute a callback to discover its signature or retry after its body raises TypeError.

Callable shape Proposed invocation / outcome f(parent) f(parent) f(parent, *, context) f(parent, context=context) f(parent, *, context=None) Framework context is supplied; the default does not disable opt-in f(parent, factor=2) f(parent); ordinary configuration keeps its Python default f(parent, *, factor=2) f(parent) f(parent, *args, **kwargs) Parent only; variadics do not opt in f(parent, context) or positional-only second context Reject at preparation; explain the keyword-only migration f(parent, context=None) Reject the positional context spelling rather than silently remove its framework input f(parent, required_setting) Reject unless the caller has already bound the setting f(parent, *, missing_setting) Reject unless the caller has already bound the setting Signature cannot be inspected Require an inspectable wrapper or the explicit structural proposer port

The positional context rejection concerns an additional parameter after the parent, not the name chosen for the parent itself. No inference from type annotations or parameter-count heuristics remains in the final convention. Other optional positional names, including _context or ctx, retain normal Python defaults; their previous inferred-context behavior requires migration. The library cannot infer whether an arbitrary optional argument was intended as configuration or context.

docs.title: Separate author callbacks from the structural port
docs.text:
The explicit structural contract remains .propose(parent, context) behind the adapter boundary. Do not apply the plain-callable rule indiscriminately to repository proposers or SDK adapters that implement this port. Keep existing dispatch precedence for objects that are both callable and structural, document it, and require an explicit wrapper when the author's intended role differs.

Bound methods, partials, and callable instances may work locally when their effective signatures satisfy the rule. They do not become durable components: registered durable functions must still meet source-verification requirements. An inspectable module-level wrapper with declared dependencies is the migration route for registered code. Local wrappers must not be advertised as resumable.

Keep validate_run hooks, context grants, named random streams, workspace lifetimes, derivation validation, and failure normalization unchanged. Context delivery does not grant broader feedback or access to held-out evaluation. Component-body errors execute once and retain their existing typed outcome; infrastructure/capability exceptions continue to escape where required.

docs.title: Migration and resume
docs.text:
The selected pre-1.0 release policy permits one coordinated cutover without an intermediate compatibility release. Use preparation-time errors to explain rejected positional-context and uninspectable forms. Document every previously inferred two-input case, including optional arguments and variadics whose behavior can change without a binding error. Do not introduce a permanent legacy dispatch mode or warn once per proposal.

Inventory repository functions, examples, registered fixtures, and integrations before the cutover. A scan can identify ambiguous shapes; it must not silently rewrite factor=2 into a context parameter. Migrate actual context consumers to keyword-only context; preserve configuration parameters and bind required configuration explicitly. Include _context, ctx, optional context, callable objects, partials, and unused second arguments in manual review.

Changing the adapter can change an unchanged registered function's behavior. For new runs, bind the invocation implementation into the registered proposer manifest using the existing source-dependency/digest machinery. Include this framework dependency automatically; users must not remember to declare the library's adapter themselves. Resolution and reconstruction must calculate it identically. Prefer this to introducing a new durable type or schema solely for a callback spelling. Confirm the final seam around registry_support.py's component-manifest construction during API-1.

An old manifest without the required invocation guarantee must not silently resume through the new adapter. Reject it before work unless an explicitly verified historical implementation is supported. Read-only reopening remains available. No manifest backfill, source-hash weakening, or automatic component version substitution is part of this migration.

docs.title: Required cases
docs.text:
• Test every signature row, positional-only parent, bound methods, partials, callable instances, structural proposers, and objects supporting both roles.
  • Assert callback body invocation counts, ordinary default values, exact context identity, and clear preparation-time errors without evaluation.
  • Retain tests proving that internal TypeError is not retried and that failure usage/evidence survive normalization.
  • Test migration diagnostics and the final invocation contract, including formerly inferred optional/variadic input; retain no permanent legacy mode.
  • Capture an old incomplete run whose unchanged proposer accepts an optional second argument or variadics. New resume must reject incompatible invocation even if that function's own source digest is unchanged.
  • Prove new registered keyword-context runs resume from the correct frontier with verified dependencies, and altered dependencies still refuse execution.

Start in adapters/proposers.py, registry_support.py, and the existing callable adapter, proposer-seam, manifest, resume, and conformance tests. Migrate callback examples and docstrings together; do not require a new public adapter type if an ordinary explicit wrapper already meets the requirement.

docs.title: API-4: report runs without requiring a winner
docs.text:
The #317 implementation plan specifies record invariants, one-snapshot queries, pending-seed reporting, comparison, and CLI migration.

Evolve the existing frozen, storage-independent RunSummary rather than add safe_summary() or another competing reporting method. Preserve its current policy, seed, configuration, usage, random-seed, and provenance fields. The selected minimal shape change is:

Field Proposed contract lifecycle "complete" only when a committed stop exists; otherwise "incomplete" rankability "rankable" when a successful evaluation is selectable, otherwise "unrankable" stop_reason Recorded reason, or None before stop primary_score Best primary-objective measurement, or None when unrankable winning_lineage Existing decoded lineage when rankable; empty tuple when unrankable usage, evaluation_count, experience_usage Keep their existing accounting meanings, including failed-work cost; do not reinterpret counts to match a renamed method

Do not introduce a numeric sentinel, invent an improvement score, or treat the initial artifact as a successful measurement when its evaluation failed. A complete run may be unrankable; an incomplete run may already be rankable; a rankable completed run may still select its seed. Direct construction of this public record must reject contradictory lifecycle/rankability fields.

Build the summary from one validated replay/snapshot and reuse private query building blocks with inspection where appropriate. Avoid the current repeated queries through best() and lineage(). Keep the result usable independently of its storage handle; do not embed a storage-bound TrialView merely to obtain an optional score. Missing stores/runs and corruption still raise typed errors.

docs.title: Comparison remains a stricter operation
docs.text:
best() and best_trial() still raise NoSuccessfulEvaluation when nothing ranks. compare() explicitly requires a successful measurement on both sides; the changed summary must not make an unrankable side a tie, an automatic loser, or a generic declaration mismatch. Preserve existing error precedence.

Retain the comparator's existing controls: evaluator, artifact kind, primary metric/direction/threshold, task and effective budgets, seed representation / schema / digest, and authorized proposer. Random seed and feedback declaration differences remain reported separately. winner is None means equal successful scores; retain winner identity as one of the two summary objects. Preserve the current treatment of rankable incomplete runs; do not silently add a requirement that both runs have stopped.

If API-8 later supports comparing different proposers, this strict comparator is not automatically that scientific comparison. Such an experiment must declare its controls explicitly; relaxing Run.compare() is a separate decision.

docs.title: Required cases and consumers
docs.text:
• Summarize all four lifecycle/rankability combinations, seed-only success, ties/regressions, proposal failure, evaluator failure, and unknown spend.
  • Include admitted distributed genesis before seed evaluation. Summary, inspection, and usage must report the valid committed prefix without requiring a bootstrapped search state; pending work has no completed usage.
  • Assert one coherent snapshot, no evaluator/proposer execution during queries, and preserved typed errors for missing or damaged history.
  • Keep maximize/minimize comparisons, all independent incompatibility cases, cross-store comparisons, winner identity, and exact ties covered.
  • Migrate CLI run/resume rendering and any browser/report consumers; show lifecycle, rankability, and an absent score explicitly. Recommended CLI rule: run/resume prints the summary but retains exit 1 for an unrankable result; successful read-only inspection returns 0 even for such a run. Keep usage errors at 2 and existing domain-error behavior. A reportable failure must not silently become command success merely because summary() no longer raises.
  • Update exact public dataclass-field/signature tests and examples intentionally; document optional-score handling for user code and positional construction.

Start in application/comparisons.py, application/inspection.py, application/results.py, cli.py, and browser presentation. Extend test_run_comparisons.py, test_run_inspection.py, and relevant CLI/browser tests. The migration guide must show how callers replace exception-only reporting with a rankability/optional-score check.

docs.title: Public API design comparisons
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

The September 18 comparisons are complete; see the decision record and retained execution evidence. This page preserves the comparison questions and acceptance boundaries.

This is API-1's bounded comparison plan, supporting the implementation sequence. The three behavior contracts are the proposed foundation. The choices below still need evidence; a sketch is not an accepted API. The #314 decision plan owns the foundation checkpoint, selected pre-1.0 release direction, comparison order, and implementation handoff.

docs.title: Use the same real journeys
docs.text:
Preserve a runnable baseline for each journey. Compare it with the proposed declaration while keeping algorithms, evaluator cases, seeds, budgets, and held-out checks fixed. An authoring comparison must not claim a gain caused by secretly changing the search or its allowance.

Journey Existing material What must become clearer First callable run Duration parser and improve() What to write, what executes, how many proposals run, and how to retrieve the selected value SDK callback and feedback Provider guide, executable reference cases Explicit context, opt-in observations, usage reporting, and typed failure without an SDK-specific coordinator Search comparison Policy-comparison lessons and preset inheritance examples One predictable allowance, seed accounting, voluntary stopping, and equal external controls Failed-run diagnosis Reference cases and inspection lesson Report cost and failure before asking for a winner; distinguish incomplete from unrankable Reopen and resume Durable operations example and registered fixtures Which objects need registration, what source is verified, and when history can be read but execution refused Composition and meta-evolution Policy evolution, AutoResearch, and ACE Reuse one loop where appropriate; keep multiple stages, actual retained results, private checks, and cost attribution explicit

For the final journey, exercise all three methods rather than choosing only the one that fits a proposed object. Policy evaluation retains inner histories; AutoResearch currently reduces inner outcomes to summaries; ACE has development, search, consolidation, and final checking. Preserve those distinctions.

Keep exploratory code isolated from the shipped package. Notebooks belong only under gitignored notebooks/. Retain small runnable comparison scripts and their results with the decision record once useful; do not add new destination packages or production protocols just to make a sketch look complete.

docs.title: Compare contracts, not just syntax
docs.text:
For every journey, record required author decisions, concepts encountered, configuration duplicated, wrapper code written, location of authority, and how an expected failure is diagnosed. Include setup/imports and migration effort; a shorter call that hides another required configuration object is not a win.

Use identical deterministic inputs to check outcome, trajectory, counts, failure classification, resources, retention, and authority. When a proposed default intentionally changes the trajectory, show that case separately from the equal-configuration comparison. Track ID/manifest differences explicitly.

Adopt a choice only when it removes a demonstrated ambiguity or repeated work, keeps the first callable path at least as understandable, and preserves the invariants under the difficult journey that motivated it. A new abstraction should earn its place in more than one real use case. Record tradeoffs rather than inventing an aggregate usability score. Internal traces are engineering evidence; independent reader sessions remain a separate activity.

Each decision record contains the baseline and alternative code, observed friction, selected rule and spelling, discarded option, migration examples, identity/resume consequences, acceptance tests, and source revision. If evidence does not favor a change, retain the current design and close that comparison. Do not let exploration prevent the three specified fixes from proceeding once their contracts and release boundary are settled.

docs.title: API-5: allowance and counting
docs.text:
Compare the current preset-led allowance with a budget-led ordinary path. Favor the latter if the same finite amount no longer needs to be repeated in the task budget and preset. External authorization and a procedure's voluntary early stop remain different concepts even if the common spelling gets smaller.

Resolve these cases before choosing a constructor/default:

Case Decision required improve() with no allowance Keep one documented finite default; currently 20 attempts after seed evaluation. Bare built-in preset with a finite effective attempt ceiling Decide whether to inherit by default in the breaking release; preserve historical recorded limits. Bare preset without an attempt ceiling Choose one resolution site for a finite default; avoid a hidden unlimited loop. Only an evaluation/resource ceiling exists Failed proposals may consume no evaluations or billed resources; state the independent attempt termination rule. Explicit smaller policy limit Allow a voluntary early stop without widening external authority. Explicit policy limit above the external cap Keep the hard cap authoritative; specify the existing/changed refusal or stop behavior. Custom search, BestOfK, or candidate-policy interpreter Preserve the policy's own meaning; do not inject a preset default into every SearchProgram. Population, Specialists, TreeSearch, or BestOfN cohorts Verify policy-specific branching, width, and zero-work cases; preserve trial and occurrence identities.

Record concrete resolved configuration before work. Never store “inherit from whatever today's default is.” Pin stop reasons when a policy limit and hard budget coincide. Session, run, and improve must not each invent a default.

Review attempts and history() as a separate naming decision after resolving semantics. If accepted, account for improve(trials=...), Budget.trials, Usage.trials, preset max_trials, Run.trials(), CLI labels, and examples together. A partial rename would make counting harder. Explain that proposal attempts exclude the seed, history contains the bootstrap record, evaluations may include the seed, and delivery retries are not new logical attempts.

Public aliases may lower to current durable records during migration. Do not rename internal trial identities, fields, and stored schemas merely to match author vocabulary. Default recommendation: first fix allowance placement; rename counts only if the complete mapping is materially easier to use.

docs.title: API-6: primary objective and additional metrics
docs.text:
Compare objectives=(Maximize("quality"), Minimize("cost")) with a singular primary-objective declaration plus explicit additional-metric declarations. The exact spelling for additional metrics is an output of this comparison.

The alternative must preserve these distinct capabilities:

  • One primary metric/direction controls ordinary ranking and satisfaction.
  • Required additional measurements are validated rather than quietly dropped.
  • A recorded metric can have an explicit direction for alternate winner queries; the query does not retrospectively change search decisions.
  • Scalar evaluators remain simple when exactly one metric is required. Missing required metrics stay typed invalid output; optional extra metrics remain available without acquiring a hidden optimization direction.
  • Custom search can inspect declared measurements. Specialists' current per-metric frontier uses the primary direction; neither spelling promises mixed-direction or Pareto optimization.

Prototype a quality/cost evaluator, scalar score, missing metric, threshold, alternate query, and specialist search. Prefer a small declaration over three mandatory measurement/ranking/stopping objects. Keep the current ordered tuple if the alternative merely moves its complexity elsewhere. Preserve historical objective ordering on replay and comparison even if new calls lower from a different surface.

docs.title: API-7: resource reports and nested accounting
docs.text:
Compare current rich returns using Usage(...).without_counts with a proposed resource-only value for components. Its scope is tokens, billed micro-USD, and elapsed work. Run usage still owns logical proposal/evaluation counts; components must not invent or forward inner counts into an outer run.

Exercise a plain candidate return, scalar/mapping evaluation, SDK response, failed proposal with billable work, unknown spend, and a nested evaluator that forwards inner resources. Keep proposal claims separate from independent measurements, and keep direct returns available without wrapping every result.

Decide conversion ownership once at the adapter boundary. An outer evaluator must report its own work plus intended inner work exactly once; an archive of inner results must not implicitly charge those results again. Demonstrate partial failure costs and show which methods still report outer-only usage.

Preserve None for unknown spend through conversion, aggregation, and replay. Current Usage(tokens=7) implies known-zero spend; changing that default is a separate decision requiring explicit migration and budget-refusal tests. Do not smuggle it into a new resource type. Do not equate summed elapsed work with wall-clock duration or claim hard preemption of external calls.

Adopt the split only if components become harder to misuse and the nested examples lose bookkeeping without acquiring equivalent conversion ceremony. Keep durable accounting types unchanged unless actual stored meaning changes.

docs.title: API-8: a reusable improvement procedure
docs.text:
Compare the current Experiment plus dataclasses.replace against the review's working Improver idea. Run the same procedure on two tasks/seeds, compare two procedures under fixed controls, and use bounded candidate configuration θ to construct Iθ in policy evolution and AutoResearch.

Settle membership and placement explicitly:

Concern Proposed boundary to test Proposal strategy, search, feedback-selection strategy Reusable procedure configuration Evaluator, objectives, task suite and private splits Task / trusted enclosing evaluator Seed and chosen procedure Experiment declaration Requested allowance Choose one ordinary declaration site and define any execution-time narrowing; keep hard caps external Observation grant, pull permissions and access bounds Experiment/governance-owned authority, never enlarged by the procedure candidate Storage, execution mode and component resolution Explicit execution wiring; compare registry placement without introducing ambient state

If adopted, replace the corresponding Experiment fields in the breaking release instead of retaining two complete declarations indefinitely. It should be an immutable configuration value that lowers through existing preparation; it gets no new coordinator, scheduler, run identity, or durable serialization merely because it has a name. Trace mutable registries and live callable state honestly: a frozen outer declaration does not freeze its dependencies.

Do not treat the object as automatically serializable or evolvable. Candidate data selects permitted settings; trusted interpretation constructs behavior. Feedback-selection configuration cannot widen the observation grant. Keep ACE's stages explicit and AutoResearch's outer evaluation and final checks external.

Prove the first-use cost is justified by reuse in at least two existing compositions. If dataclasses.replace is equally clear, keep Experiment and teach the conceptual procedure without adding a class. If different-proposer comparisons are demonstrated, declare an explicit experimental protocol; Run.compare() currently requires the same authorized proposer.

docs.title: API-9: imports after semantics
docs.text:
Inventory public names by author role: ordinary declarations/callbacks, returned inspection records, extension protocols, and specialized domains. Start with the imports actually required by the six journeys. Keep frequently handled failures discoverable, including the distinction between failure values and exceptions.

Prefer existing namespaces for advanced APIs; avoid mandatory imports from kernel modules or a new directory per concept. Move public imports only when the discovery/migration improvement is clear. Preserve underlying durable type identity even when an import path changes. Specify the old-to-new import table, warning/removal release, reference links, and installed-package checks.

The number of root exports is not an acceptance target. A small root namespace that forces ordinary users to learn several internal modules is not simpler. Keep the final cleanup separate from algorithmic or persistence changes so reviewers can assess its real cost.

docs.title: Public API revision: implementation plan
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 18, 2026, following the API review. The inspected baseline is c04ec6b4b949b8a2702779107e25acd24feb8020 plus the local #297 documentation patch. That patch and this plan are not evidence of a published release. This plan specifies work; it introduces no runtime behavior or importable API.

docs.title: Outcome and scope
docs.text:
Make the ordinary story predictable: declare what can change, propose a revision, evaluate it independently, search within a known allowance, and inspect the outcome even when nothing succeeds. Make the same pieces easy to reuse when evaluating an improvement procedure.

Keep improve() small. Preserve the responsibilities of Task, Experiment, Session, and Run, and the shared execution path underneath them. A new procedure object is justified only if real compositions become easier to author and explain. Completing this work does not require adopting every sketch in the review.

Recommendation Implementation disposition Preserve omitted task ceilings in run budget overrides Specify and implement. Explicit keyword-only context for plain proposer callbacks Specify, migrate, and implement as a behavior break. Summarize failed and incomplete runs without requiring a winner Specify and implement; retain strict winner queries and comparisons. One ordinary attempt allowance and clearer counting Compare alternatives, then select one rule. An explicit primary objective Prototype without losing additional-metric validation or query directions. Resource-only component reports Adopt only if nested accounting improves without complicating simple callbacks. A reusable improvement-procedure declaration Adopt only if it beats reusing Experiment with dataclasses.replace. Root export cleanup Follow the selected API; avoid a package reorganization for its own sake.

The behavior contracts specify the first three changes. The design comparisons specify how to decide the remaining choices. Those pages own the detail; this page owns sequence, deliverables, compatibility, and completion.

docs.title: Implementation gate
docs.text:
The roadmap still bounds runtime work: M11.0–M11.2 are shipped and distributed execution is serial. The separately named Author API revision gate now owns this work. It neither completes M11.3 nor introduces concurrent workers.

The gate records accepted decisions, excluded alternatives, compatibility policy, and tests. docs/milestones.md owns scope and acceptance; docs/implementation-plan.md owns technical seams. Update the shipped programming model and architecture with each implemented behavior, not with prototype signatures.

The user selected an explicit pre-1.0 compatibility reset on September 18. Use one coordinated breaking release for accepted default, constructor, and spelling changes, with 0.2.0 as the working target. The #314 decision plan owns this release direction. Amend the existing through-1.x commitments for keyword run(), dictionary CLI factories, and preset inheritance explicitly in the foundation checkpoint; the current 0.1.0 package version alone does not erase them. Enumerate actual removals rather than assuming every old spelling must go.

Do not ship a succession of incompatible intermediate declarations. Independent implementation slices can be reviewed separately against the agreed target. No intermediate compatibility release is required. Provide migration diagnostics at the cutover and disclose source-manifest effects separately.

docs.title: Work breakdown and dependencies
docs.text:
Tracked by #313 — Author API revision with six initial subissues and the two adopted follow-ups #320/#321. API-0 and API-1 share the decisions issue; the comparison dispositions below settle API-5–8 for this release. Every behavior slice includes focused tests, its migrated examples, reference docstrings, and the affected canonical contract.

Work item Depends on Deliverable and acceptance gate API-0 — Pin the baseline and release contract (#314) Existing #297 work Identify exact source, lock, package, and durable fixtures; preserve #297's current-behavior reference and its source-manifest qualification. Add the named roadmap gate. API-1 — Compare declarations and freeze decisions (#314) API-0 Run the bounded comparisons; record chosen spelling, rejected alternative, migration, authority, identity, and resume consequences for each decision. API-2 — Compose budget overrides (#315) API-1 foundation contracts Implement the per-dimension table in the contracts page; typed and keyword entry points and Session.start() agree. API-3 — Make callback context explicit (#316) API-1 foundation contracts Implement signature binding, migration diagnostics, structural-port separation, and verified invocation semantics for resume. API-4 — Make summaries independent of a winner (#317) API-1 foundation contracts Failed/incomplete runs summarize; CLI consumers migrate; strict comparison and winner behavior remain intact. API-5 — Unify ordinary allowance/counting, if selected API-2; API-1 decision Resolve once, record explicit policy configuration, preserve externally bounded voluntary stopping and historical defaults. API-6 — Clarify primary objectives, if selected API-1 decision Preserve scalar/mapping normalization, alternate metric queries, and explicit policy-specific capabilities. API-7 — Separate component resource reports, if selected API-1 decision Preserve exact engine counts, failure costs, and unknown spend through nested runs and replay. API-8 — Add a reusable procedure, if selected API-3; accepted API-5–7 Lower to existing declarations and execution; migrate real compositions; keep evaluator, grants, budgets, and promotion external. API-9 — Consolidate imports and reader journeys (#318) All selected behavior slices One recommended authoring path, runnable examples, migration table, and updated contributor map. Remove only imports explicitly scheduled for the breaking release. API-10 — Verify and release the integrated revision (#319) API-9 Pass behavior, historical-store, installed-package, and documentation gates; record actual compatibility outcomes and publication revision.

The September 18 decisions select API-5's budget-led preset defaults in #320 and API-7's resource-only reports in #321. Counting names, ordered objectives (API-6), and Experiment (API-8) stay for 0.2; there is no new Improver implementation prerequisite. API-9 therefore integrates #315–#317, #320, and #321 before API-10's single release.

API-1 has two exits: first freeze the three foundation contracts and their release treatment; then resolve each larger comparison before its conditional implementation. The foundation fixes need not wait for every optional design. API-2, API-3, and API-4 are independent after their target contracts are fixed. API-6 and API-7 need no new procedure object. API-8 must not begin by creating a destination package tree. If a conditional change is rejected, its dependent work uses the existing contract and the decision record explains why.

API-9 is integration, not the first documentation pass. No individual API change is complete while its examples or canonical documentation still teach the old behavior. Give each work item a small reviewable diff; split by independently testable responsibility when a hand-written file exceeds the normal 300-line limit.

docs.title: Documentation and repository structure
docs.text:
The #318 integration plan maps the selected release to migration routes, page/source owners, six reader journeys, and verification.

Build on the completed improvement-loop framing rather than replacing it. The conceptual reading path remains: first working loop → components → composition → a procedure as the candidate → research evidence and limits. Notation stays optional and follows the existing definitions: I is the procedure, E independent evaluation, B external allowance, H authorized observations, and R retained results. Do not reuse E for experience or imply that every composed method returns one Run.

Owner / surface Required revision docs/start-here.md, parser lesson source, README entry Preserve a complete callable example without credentials; expose new machinery only when the reader needs it. docs/programming-model.md Own the final authoring story, execution overlays, defaults, and compatibility contract. docs/reference/api.md, source docstrings, executable reference cases Render real signatures, defaults, inputs, outcomes, and failures; remove superseded examples with the behavior change. Budget, evaluation, limits, feedback, and durability guides Explain resolved ceilings, explicit observation opt-in, counting, and read-versus-resume migration. Result lesson, CLI and optional browser presentation Show incomplete, unrankable, and seed-selected runs honestly; diagnose failure without invoking best(). Composition worksheet and method walkthroughs Map actual stages and retained results to I, E, B, H, and R; show bounded Iθ only where the candidate is a procedure configuration. Policy, AutoResearch, and ACE examples Preserve their distinct inner-history, held-out-check, and resource-reporting contracts. Avoid presenting outer-only usage as total inner cost. Contributor tour and examples/README.md Map each role to current source/test owners and the simplest use/compose/evolve example. New versioned migration guide Give before/after calls, changed defaults, automatic versus manual migration, and durable-store outcomes for the selected release.

Organize Python by responsibility: declarations and execution in application, durable meaning in domain, contracts in ports, call normalization and external integration in adapters, search implementations in policies, and candidate-policy interpretation in policy. Do not mirror the conceptual ladder with evolution/, meta_evolution/, and rsi/ runtime packages.

Preserve existing guide URLs, historical anchors, and artifact/example paths unless a selected change supplies an explicit redirect or migration. Link to canonical definitions instead of copying signatures across guides. The API reference work from #297 remains the rendering and runnable-example foundation.

Keep research positioning precise: reusable declarations and nested runs are tools for experiments, not evidence of accelerating self-improvement. Preserve the externally owned survival test and separate selection from promotion. No new literature review or RSI rebranding is needed for this API change.

docs.title: Compatibility and migration
docs.text:
Evaluate each selected change along four independent axes:

Axis Required outcome Python calls and imports List every changed binding, default, field, and return shape. Provide a replacement and a bounded deprecation where a compatibility release is used. Recorded facts and identities Keep existing durable types/identities where semantics are unchanged. Explain intentional changes; version schemas only when stored meaning requires it. Read-only reopening Existing supported stores remain inspectable, including failed and incomplete runs. Never require new callback execution merely to read history. Executable resume Resume only with verified equivalent invocation, policy configuration, source dependencies, and capabilities. Otherwise refuse before further work and explain the mismatch.

Already observed: #297's docstring edits change exact-source manifests for Greedy, BestOfN, AncestorsOnly, and BestSibling. An old Greedy history reopened successfully while resume refused the changed policy source. Retain that qualification in the verification record. Do not drop docstrings from hashing or backfill a new manifest over old work.

Capture historical fixtures with the identified old package before changing semantics: completed success, failed seed, incomplete registered context-aware run, inherited limit, pushed feedback, unknown spend, and a distributed serial run. Reuse existing fixtures when they already prove the case. Record source, component manifests, effective budget, resolved policy, IDs, and expected reopen/resume outcome; do not regenerate them with new code and call them old.

Callback dispatch needs particular care: an unchanged source function can behave differently under a new adapter. API-3 must bind invocation semantics into verification, as specified in its contract. A function-source hash alone does not prove that the caller still supplies the same arguments.

Prefer a migration table and ordinary Python edits over a new migration tool. Mechanical import/keyword renames may be automated only when unambiguous. Optional positional callback parameters and changed metric intent require review. Keep old environments available to finish old runs; inspect them with the new reader when supported, or start a new run with explicit lineage/evidence under the existing derivation rules. Never relabel new work as continuation.

docs.title: Verification and completion
docs.text:
The #319 release plan owns the remaining coordinated package-publication sequence and links its distribution/compatibility checks.

Start each slice with the concrete cases in its contract. Add regression tests for observable outcomes, invalid authority changes, and actual compatibility risks. Do not add tests that merely freeze prose, directory names, or the number of exports.

Gate Evidence required Behavior Focused callable, budget, summary/comparison, and selected redesign cases; seed/attempt counts, failures, ties, targets, and resource accounting are exact. Shared execution improve, typed/compatible run, and Session lower consistently; memory/durable-local agree where admitted; existing serial distributed restrictions remain enforced. Authority and composition Candidate configuration cannot enlarge budgets, observations, private evaluation access, or promotion; nested costs and actual retention remain explicit. Historical compatibility Old histories reopen; expected resume refusals happen before execution; unchanged supported implementations continue from the recorded frontier. Package and reference Build/install the identified package outside the checkout, run canonical examples, render signatures and failure cases, validate root and namespace imports. Documentation integration Strict MkDocs build, ownership and route checks, executable snippets/downloads, desktop/narrow review of changed reference surfaces, and actual source/site revision alignment. Release CI and the maintained Docs workflow pass for the integrated revision; release/migration notes identify remaining resume restrictions and each deliberate behavior break.

Use .github/workflows/docs.yml and the maintained runtime CI configuration as the command owners; inspect them when implementing instead of copying a stale command inventory into this plan. Keep fake SDK responses deterministic and separate from any optional live experiment. Broad regression runs belong at integration after focused tests pass, and repeat only for relevant changes or unresolved failures.

Record the exact revision, environment/lock, package hash, pass/fail/skip counts, and the limits of manual review. In particular, an internal authoring comparison is not an independent user study, and a deterministic nested example is not an empirical RSI result.

Release only when the simplest example is still simple, every adopted change removes demonstrated friction, all four compatibility outcomes are explicit, and documentation teaches the implemented API. Publish meta-evolve-docs from that identified source revision and verify the deployed routes/signatures; a local build is not proof that the hosted site has updated.

The foundation and comparison decisions complete API-0/API-1's design handoff. The specified behavior slices proceed without a new procedure object as a prerequisite.

docs.title: Public API redesign review
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This September 18, 2026 review considers breaking changes beyond #297. It was checked against c04ec6b4b949b8a2702779107e25acd24feb8020 plus the local #297 documentation patch. Proposed spellings below are sketches, not importable APIs.

The programming model still owns shipped behavior. Architecture owns its invariants, and the roadmap retains the implementation boundary: M11.0–M11.2 are shipped; concurrent workers are not. This review does not expand that gate.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Keep the callable entry point and independent evaluation. Change behavior where the current API requires users to memorize exceptions. Start with budget composition, explicit context delivery, and a summary that handles failed runs. Then compare the existing declarations with an explicit reusable improvement procedure, using the same real examples.

Measure how many decisions a user must understand and repeat, not the number of exports or the length of a fluent expression. Accept a breaking change when it removes a demonstrated ambiguity or repeated work.

docs.title: What the current code demonstrates
docs.text:
These are observations from source and deterministic probes, not a usability study. Temporary probe scripts and results are under /private/tmp/meta-evolve-api-review-2026-09-18/.

Observation Consequence Proposed direction A task bounded by Budget(trials=4, evaluations=5) rejects a run override of Budget(evaluations=2) before evaluation. Tightening one resource requires reconstructing the complete allowance. Preserve unspecified task ceilings. def propose(parent, factor=2) receives ProposerContext as factor. The tested run retained its seed and recorded a proposer failure. Ordinary Python configuration is mistaken for framework input. Deliver context through an explicit callback convention. def propose(parent, *, context) is rejected at startup. The explicit keyword convention is unavailable. Support this as the canonical context-aware callable. Greedy() with Budget(trials=25) made 20 attempts; Greedy(max_trials=None) made 25. The ordinary allowance has two declarations and an inheritance switch. Give common runs one obvious place to set the allowance. Those runs had 21 and 26 history records respectively. trials() includes the seed while usage().trials excludes it. Review public counting vocabulary without changing durable identities. A failed seed remained inspectable, but summary(), best(), and best_trial() all raised NoSuccessfulEvaluation. A reporting operation requires a winner. Make summary available for every existing run; retain strict winner queries. Nested examples repeatedly forward usage().without_counts. Component resources and engine-owned counts share one type. Prototype a resource-only component report. Policy examples reach into run._projection() to decide whether to resume. Author code still depends on internal machinery. Use the existing public inspection lifecycle, then assess remaining friction.

Relevant seams are application/session_preparation.py, adapters/proposers.py, policies/_trial_budget.py, application/results.py, and ports/callables.py. Relevant examples are AutoResearch, policy evolution, and ACE under examples/research/.

docs.title: 1. Compose budget limits safely
docs.text:
Proposed run(experiment, budget=Budget(evaluations=2)) semantics:

  • An unspecified dimension preserves the task ceiling.
  • A supplied finite dimension may tighten it or introduce a new ceiling.
  • A supplied finite value above a task ceiling remains an error, before work.
  • Removing a task ceiling requires changing the task declaration explicitly.
  • Record the resolved effective budget; replay never resolves it again.
