Budget remains a ceiling value; this changes how the run argument composes with the task. It does not change accounting, unknown-spend propagation, post-call enforcement, or candidate authority. Budget.narrow() already provides mathematical intersection, but accepting an explicitly looser finite override would change the current refusal contract further.

This is a behavior break: some calls that currently fail will execute. Migration notes must say so. No new configuration container is needed.

docs.title: 2. Make callback context explicit
docs.text:
Compare these proposed callable forms:

def propose(parent):
    ...

def propose(parent, *, context):
    ...

def propose(parent, factor=2):
    ...  # factor retains its ordinary Python default

Only a named keyword-only context parameter opts into context delivery. Variadic parameters alone do not request it. Validate the invocation before execution; never call twice to discover a signature. Uninspectable callables need an explicit adapter. The structural proposer port can retain its explicit two-input contract behind that adapter boundary.

Existing positional-context functions require migration. Do not retain arity-based inference indefinitely beside the new convention. Callback identity, registered source manifests, callable instances, and partials need coverage.

docs.title: 3. Make reporting independent of successful selection
docs.text:
Redesign Run.summary() to report lifecycle, rankability, stop reason, usage, and an optional best measurement. Keep best() strict when no value ranks. Use inspect() for detailed history and decisions. This avoids requiring a winner just to report a failed experiment or its cost.

Keep lifecycle, rankability, and improvement distinct: a stopped run can be unrankable; a rankable run can select its seed. Missing runs and damaged storage still raise typed errors. Changing the summary also affects RunComparison; migrate both deliberately rather than adding another synonym.

docs.title: One ordinary allowance, explicit search behavior
docs.text:
Search chooses which candidate gets work. External budgets bound how much work is authorized. A procedure may also stop voluntarily, which matters when a policy artifact evolves its own stopping behavior.

Compare a budget-led authoring path with the current preset-led path. In the budget-led version, bare Greedy() inherits the resolved attempt allowance; the entry point supplies a documented finite default only when none is given. An explicit smaller policy limit may still stop early. Resolve defaults once and record them. Test zero attempts, failed proposals, evaluation-only limits, targets, custom search, population search, and cohorts before choosing a rule.

Consider attempts for public proposal-attempt limits and history() for all retained attempts including the seed. This is worthwhile only if it makes counts consistently predictable. Preserve internal trial identities, seed evaluation, stop reasons, and stored schemas unless a separate migration needs to change them. A new spelling alone does not justify a release break.

docs.title: State the primary objective explicitly
docs.text:
The ordered objective tuple requires all named metrics, but the first controls ordinary ranking and satisfaction. It does not request joint or Pareto optimization. Prototype singular objective=Maximize("quality") alongside an explicit way to declare additional measured metrics and their query directions. Compare it against retaining the ordered tuple.

Exercise scalar evaluators, alternate winner queries, missing measurements, Specialists, and custom search. Specialists currently applies the primary objective's direction to its metric frontier; it is not a general mixed-direction multi-objective solver. Do not imply a capability by renaming the declaration. Separating measurement, ranking, and stopping may help, but three mandatory configuration objects would make simple runs worse.

docs.title: Separate component resources from engine counts
docs.text:
A proposed resource-only report would contain tokens, billed micro-USD, and elapsed time. Components could not supply trial or evaluation counts. Run usage would still expose those engine-owned counts, plus recorded resources. Nested callers would forward resources without remembering to zero counts.

Keep direct candidate/scalar returns and optional rich result records. Proposal claims and independent measurements remain distinct. Unknown billed spend stays unknown, including after failures. Usage(tokens=7) currently defaults to known-zero spend; changing that default is a separate behavioral decision, not something to hide inside an accounting wrapper.

docs.title: Should the improvement procedure become an object?
docs.text:
The notation suggests a reusable procedure I applied to a task and seed. Today its configuration spans Experiment.proposer, search, context, and experience. That makes this a serious design candidate:

# Proposed sketch only; Improver and these field changes are not shipped.
task = meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate, objective=meta.Maximize("quality"))
improver = meta.Improver(
    proposer=propose,
    search=meta.Greedy(),
    feedback=meta.AncestorsOnly(),
)
experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed=seed,
    improver=improver,
    budget=meta.Budget(attempts=20),
)
result = meta.run(experiment)

The attraction is independently reusing and comparing the procedure. The cost is another object and more nesting for a single run. Compare this with reusing an existing Experiment through dataclasses.replace; do not assume the new object wins. If selected, it should replace the relevant declaration fields, not add a second complete spelling. Settle run-allowance placement and registry wiring as part of that comparison.

Improver is a working name for one search-loop recipe. ACE includes development, search, consolidation, and held-out phases. AutoResearch evaluates a recipe by running several inner experiments. Neither becomes one ordinary search by wrapping its components. Retain explicit Python orchestration where those stages carry the algorithm's meaning.

A callable-containing declaration is not automatically a portable or evolvable artifact. A candidate can supply bounded configuration θ; trusted code constructs I_θ. Evaluators, private splits, hard budgets, grants, and promotion remain external. Feedback selection may be configurable, but it cannot expand the observation grant. Reification alone demonstrates no RSI.

docs.title: Keep the useful boundaries
docs.text:
Task, Experiment, Session, and Run separate evaluation, declaration, execution, and inspection. Keep these responsibilities even if a later design changes a constructor. Preserve plain callables, provider independence, replaceable components, distinct identities, immutable facts, and typed failures.

Pushed feedback and pulled access can have clearer names, but remain different capabilities. Source and policy artifacts retain domain codecs and validated mutation surfaces. Git can present file history; it does not replace evaluation identity, occurrence lineage, accounting, or promotion authority.

Review the 79 root exports by authoring role. Advanced views and protocols can use documented namespaces; frequently returned failure types deserve an obvious import path. Prefer existing namespaces over a directory for each concept. Keep the runtime organized by responsibility and the documentation organized by the improvement loop and its compositions.

docs.title: Compatibility is more than call syntax
docs.text:
The #297 docstring edits leave executable syntax unchanged, but exact-source manifests change for greedy, best-of-n, ancestors-only, and best-sibling. A probe wrote an incomplete Greedy run with the base package: current code reopened and inspected it, while resume raised CapabilityError for the policy implementation digest mismatch. See the reference verification record.

Distinguish Python source compatibility, recorded bytes and identities, read-only reopening, and executable resume. Moving a public import need not move the underlying durable type. Historical resolution must use recorded policy configuration, never new defaults. Keep exact-source checks; discarding docstrings from a hash is not proof that component behavior agrees.

The reviewed contract promises declaration-keyword run() through 1.x. The user subsequently selected an explicit pre-1.0 compatibility reset and one coordinated breaking release; the #314 decision plan records the policy amendment work. Provide a migration table and deliberate cutover, without permanent parallel APIs. Do not rewrite old stores or weaken manifest checks to make an upgrade appear compatible.

docs.title: Sequence and decision gates
docs.text:
1. Retain #297 as documentation of current behavior, with the source-digest qualification above. It remains useful whichever redesign is chosen.
  2. Specify budget composition, explicit callback context, and failure-safe summaries as separate behavior changes, each with its migration cases.
  3. Compare existing declarations and the reusable procedure on six journeys: first callable run; SDK usage and feedback; bounded search-policy comparison; failed-run inspection; registered reopen/resume; nested policy, AutoResearch, and multi-stage ACE composition.
  4. Use those traces to decide limit placement, primary-objective declaration, resource reporting, and whether Improver earns its existence.
  5. Schedule accepted changes in a named milestone/release gate. Update canonical contracts, examples, conformance, and migration documentation together.

Measure required author decisions, repeated declarations, concepts encountered, and failure diagnosis. Use code traces rather than line counts alone. Require unchanged authority and lineage, exact counting, retained failure cost, honest unknown spend, and explicit compatibility outcomes. Use the shared coordinator and add no provider-specific branch or dependency.

This recommends behavior changes and a bounded architecture comparison; it does not select all proposed spellings or replace independent usability tests.

The implementation plan develops this review into proposed work items, behavior contracts, comparison gates, and release verification.

docs.title: Saved-run reopening: plan for #335
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 19, 2026 for #335, under #330. This design record is retained alongside the source implementation. The canonical API owns shipped behavior; the verification record tracks acceptance. The remainder records the selected design and its rationale.

The programming model owns public API contracts, the architecture owns invariants, the roadmap owns acceptance gates, and the implementation plan owns technical boundaries. Implementation depends on #331 establishing the author-UX gate. That gate is present in the working tree inspected here; this is not evidence that #331 has merged. This slice adds no requirement to #313/#319's current release scope.

docs.title: Recommended experience
docs.text:
Add one context-managed function that returns the existing Run:

import meta_evolve as meta

with meta.open_run("runs/example/history") as run:
    snapshot = run.summary()

print(snapshot)  # Captured while storage was open.

The path is the directory originally passed to Storage.durable(), not its SQLite file or a parent directory containing several stores. In a shared store, pass the saved identity explicitly:

with meta.open_run("runs/shared/history", run_id=saved_run_id) as run:
    inspection = run.inspect()

The public callable has this proposed shape:

open_run(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    run_id: RunId | str | None = None,
    registry: Registry | None = None,
) -> AbstractContextManager[Run]

Use open_run because it names both the resource lifetime and the object being opened. Reuse Storage.read_only() and Run; no new result or handle class is needed. Authors already holding storage continue to use Run(run_id, storage, registry=...) and retain responsibility for that storage.

Keep this path-only API small. Writable mode, automatic migration, resume, directory discovery, a run catalog, and a "latest" selector are outside it.

docs.title: Selection and errors
docs.text:
Enter the context in this order: validate arguments, open read-only storage, select one identity, validate that history, construct Run, then yield it.

Input or store state Outcome on context entry Explicit RunId or valid ID string Open that identity only; do not enumerate or substitute another run. Explicit identity has no event stream Existing RunNotFound, even if another run exists. Omitted ID; no recorded runs RunNotFound with an actionable message naming the store. Omitted ID; exactly one recorded run Select it and validate its history. Omitted ID; several recorded runs New RunSelectionRequired containing the available identities. Missing/inaccessible directory or database Preserve DurableStoreError and its underlying cause. Older, unstamped, or future schema Preserve SchemaVersionRejected; perform no migration. Damaged schema, selected stream, or referenced artifact Preserve DurableCorruption; never fall back to another run.

RunSelectionRequired subclasses RunError and exposes run_ids: tuple[RunId, ...]. Its message explains run_id=... and lists the available IDs in deterministic lexical order. The structured tuple makes a choice possible without parsing an exception string. Widen RunNotFound's docstring to include an existing store containing no runs; do not change its existing callers or inheritance.

ID strings follow existing RunId validation: nonempty, without surrounding whitespace. Accept a saved run.id directly or its .value from a file. Reject other values, including a different domain ID type, with TypeError; reject malformed strings with ValueError. Do not trim, coerce arbitrary objects, or introduce a hash-format requirement. An invalid registry raises TypeError before storage opens, matching Run's current Registry requirement.

Omitted-ID selection reads Storage.runs() once. Its lexical order is only a stable presentation order, never a creation order. If another run is committed after that listing, the selected identity remains fixed. Listing and later queries are not one long transaction. Explicit selection avoids unrelated stream replay, although the existing opener still validates the store schema.

docs.title: Validation and custom artifacts
docs.text:
Before yielding, call the existing load_validated_run(storage, selected_id, require_existing=True). Construction of Run alone is lazy and would otherwise admit a missing or damaged history. Do not substitute a version check, best(), or a summary for authoritative loading: valid incomplete and entirely unsuccessful runs must also open.

Entry validates the committed framework records and artifact references; it does not require a winning evaluation, verify executable component manifests, or promise that every custom artifact can be decoded. Preserve custom-value decoding at the existing query boundary:

  • registry= is passed to Run, retaining built-in codecs and adding supplied custom codecs through its current per-run index.
  • A custom history can open without its codec, and usage() remains available. A value-decoding query such as best() raises the existing actionable CapabilityError when that codec is absent.
  • A reconstructed codec registry enables decoded queries in another process; the original proposer and evaluator are unnecessary for inspection.
  • Supplied codecs remain trusted Python extensions. Reopening does not invoke their encode/decode methods on entry; queries that decode values can do so. Codec decode failures keep their existing DurableCorruption translation.

Discard the entry validation result. Subsequent Run queries use their existing validated reads, so a live WAL writer remains observable. Each captured summary or inspection keeps its own single-frontier guarantee; the with block does not freeze all its queries to one version. The extra initial replay is the deliberate cost of rejecting invalid selections before yielding. Do not add a cache or change Run internals to avoid it in this slice.

docs.title: Ownership and read-only guarantees
docs.text:
Implement the function with the standard-library contextmanager. Calling it creates a context manager; argument validation and I/O happen on __enter__. It opens one storage handle inside with Storage.read_only(path) as storage. That scope closes the handle after normal exit, a body exception, or an error during selection, validation, or Run construction. Exceptions propagate with their existing types and causes. Failed storage opening retains the opener's existing connection-cleanup responsibility.

Capture summaries, inspections, usage, or selected values inside the block. These detached results remain available afterward. The yielded Run is still a live reader: later storage-dependent queries fail through the existing store error path. Add no hidden reopen, cached fallback, finalizer, Run.close(), or new closed-handle exception. A run's identity remains usable after exit.

docs.title: 333 owns safe summary formatting and the I/O-free Run repr; #335 does not
docs.text:
depend on its richer display fields to implement reopening.

The helper grants inspection authority: no event/artifact/work commits, schema changes, migration, repair, proposer/evaluator/search execution, provider calls, or resume. A missing store directory is never created.

The issue's "no writes" criterion needs precise acceptance wording. A planning probe against the current Storage.read_only() preserved the closed store's database and artifact hashes but created meta-evolve.sqlite-wal and meta-evolve.sqlite-shm. SQLite documents this behavior for read-only WAL databases. Define the guarantee as no mutation of committed history and no framework writes, directory creation, or migration; SQLite may maintain WAL sidecars. Document that qualification in the durability guide and #335's acceptance record before closure. Preserve live-WAL behavior; immutable=1, copying stores, and deleting sidecars are not fixes for this convenience API.

docs.title: Implementation sequence
docs.text:
Keep this one bounded implementation PR, with three reviewable steps:

  1. Contract and opening. Add application/reopening.py containing the context manager and minimal private selection logic. Add the typed selection error in errors.py; export both public names from the root package and follow existing application exports where appropriate. Add core selection and lifetime tests with the implementation. Record the API and durability contract in canonical docs in the same change.
  2. Integrity and compatibility. Exercise real durable histories, custom codecs, failed/incomplete runs, historical fixtures, and exception cleanup. Reuse durable_loading.py, existing read-only adapters, and their error translations. No schema, event, identity, coordinator, or search changes.
  3. Complete user journey. Update the persistence lesson and its extracted download, covering save in one process and reopen in another. Add an explicit selection example for a multi-run store, preserve path discovery, and check source-generated reference coverage. Hand the verified path to #336.

Do not add another general storage factory, selector protocol, location record, or shared validation subsystem. Existing direct construction remains supported. Keep new handwritten modules and tests below 300 lines by splitting tests into selection/integrity and lifetime responsibilities if needed.

docs.title: Focused acceptance checks
docs.text:
Concern Required evidence Only-run convenience A real saved run opens without an ID; its identity and queries match direct Storage.read_only() plus Run. Explicit selection Typed ID and string work in one/many-run stores; missing explicit ID raises without fallback or enumeration. Zero/many Empty current store raises RunNotFound; several runs expose all IDs through RunSelectionRequired. Use real runs whose insertion order opposes lexical order and assert that premise. Arguments Wrong ID types, empty/padded strings, and invalid registry fail before acquiring storage. Creating the context manager performs no I/O. Lifecycle Completed, incomplete, pending-seed, and entirely unsuccessful histories open. Winner queries retain NoSuccessfulEvaluation. Codecs Reconstruct a custom codec registry; preserve built-ins. Missing codec permits entry/usage, fails on decoded query. Decoding faults retain existing errors. Integrity Missing directory/database, damaged events, missing artifacts, malformed current schema, and old/future schemas preserve typed errors and causes. No automatic repair or migration. Cleanup Observe connection closure on success, body exception, selection error, missing ID, corrupt stream, and failure while constructing the codec index. Body exceptions are not swallowed. Detached results Capture summary/inspection/usage, close storage, then use them. Explicit queries on the retained Run surface the existing store error. Authority Proposer/evaluator/search/provider/resume tripwires remain untouched. Verify unchanged schema, committed events, and artifact bytes; distinguish SQLite sidecars. Missing paths remain absent. Live reader Queries can observe a later valid committed frontier through the same handle; entry validation does not become a cache or retarget the selected ID. Historical read Copy retained fixtures; current-schema supported histories remain readable. An older schema is refused until a separate explicit writable migration of the copy; historical event bytes remain unchanged. Fresh process Save and record path/ID, remove access to original local callbacks, exit, then reopen in a separate process outside the checkout. Exercise single-run inference and explicit multi-run choice.

Start with new tests/test_open_run.py and a lifetime test module only if needed. Use the existing custom artifact in test_run_reopening.py, state fixtures from summary/inspection tests, and retained historical fixtures. Regression coverage includes test_run_listing.py, test_run_reopening.py, test_read_only_storage.py, and the relevant durable/history tests. Existing lower-level contracts should be reused rather than duplicated exhaustively.

docs.title: Documentation integration and completion
docs.text:
• In docs/programming-model.md, specify the new entry point, exact selection behavior, error types, codec boundary, and context lifetime. In docs/architecture.md, retain live read-only projection and authority rules.
  • In docs/implementation-plan.md, record the small application boundary. Update #335's status in the roadmap only after its acceptance evidence exists.
  • In docs/guides/durability.md, lead reopening with the convenience, then retain explicit storage ownership for advanced use. Explain WAL sidecars and preserve the separate save, reopen, resume, and exported-artifact reuse contracts.
  • In docs/learn/06-persist-run.md, replace manual only-run selection with the helper. Keep last-duration-run.txt: choosing within a known store does not locate that store after a restart. Add explicit ID selection for shared stores and capture values before closing. Keep notebook cells below 40 lines.
  • Add both exports to docs/reference/api.md's persistence/errors tier and generated member list. Update reference and persistence tests with the API; build the docs strictly and run the extracted lesson in a fresh process.

Completion requires the focused behavior tests, unchanged supported historical reads, strict docs/reference checks, and the executable save/reopen journey. The integrated model journey and independent newcomer evidence remain in #336.

docs.title: Effort and planning evidence
docs.text:
Estimated difficulty remains low–medium. The runtime change is a small composition of existing operations. Most work is proving error timing, resource cleanup, compatibility, and the cross-process documentation path. The estimate assumes the existing storage format, live-reader semantics, and the qualified WAL sidecar contract above; a zero-filesystem-change reader is separate scope.

Inspected base: 1607afbb81f7c5e457f97eb437b13ffb9ad63267, together with ongoing local #331/#332/#333 work. Planning probes used disposable stores only and confirmed lexical listing, lazy direct Run construction, missing-run rejection by authoritative loading, codec-free validation/usage, custom-codec query errors, detached summary access, DurableCorruption on a query after close, and the WAL sidecar distinction. These probes establish existing behavior; they are not acceptance tests for the helper; implementation evidence is recorded separately.

docs.title: Readable run snapshots: plan for #333
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 19, 2026 for #333, under #330. The inspected source is 1607afbb81f7c5e457f97eb437b13ffb9ad63267. This planning record is retained alongside the source implementation. The canonical API owns behavior; the verification record tracks acceptance. Release and first-run documentation work remain separate.

The programming model owns the public contract, the architecture owns invariants, the roadmap owns acceptance gates, and the implementation plan owns technical boundaries. The author-UX gate records the follow-up scope. This is the bounded notebook/report portion of the post-M10 presentation follow-up. It adds no requirement to #313/#319's current release gate.

docs.title: Recommended public experience
docs.text:
Keep the existing RunSummary; introduce no new result class or display API. Capture explicitly while storage is available, then display the captured value:

with meta.Storage.durable("runs/example") as storage:
    result = meta.improve(
        seed=0,
        proposer=lambda parent: parent + 1,
        evaluator=lambda value: value,
        trials=2,
        storage=storage,
    )
    snapshot = result.summary()

print(snapshot)  # Concise text, including after storage closes.
snapshot        # Rich display when this is a notebook cell's final expression.

Illustrative text for that completed run:

Run <run id>
Status: Complete
Measurement: Available
score (maximize): baseline 0 → selected 2
Improvement: Improved over baseline
Proposals: 2
Evaluations: 3 (includes baseline)
Failed attempts: 0
Stop: Proposal limit reached
Task spend: $0.000000
History at capture: Saved at <absolute directory>
Recorded resume support: No (local execution)

Saving local history does not make local callables resumable. Default in-memory execution instead says History at capture: Not saved durably. Display remains a historical snapshot; it makes no claim that the directory still exists.

repr(result) shows only a bounded run identifier and directs readers to summary(). It never queries storage or caches a hidden summary. A fresh result.summary() after storage closes still surfaces the storage error.

docs.title: Findings that constrain the implementation
docs.text:
Inspected behavior Decision application/comparisons.py already builds each summary from one validated event frontier. Extend that builder; preserve #317's consistency and comparison failure ordering. The summary stores decoded initial_artifact and winning_lineage values. Its generated dataclass repr can call their display methods. Supply an explicit safe repr; keep decoded fields for programmatic access but never traverse them for display. Baseline, failure count, persistence, and execution capability are absent from RunSummary. Capture the selected facts explicitly; formatting cannot query for them later. Storage declares durability but has no general location contract. Carry optional built-in location metadata; unknown custom-store locations remain unknown. Artifact presentation already separates inert payload records from escaped browser markup. Preserve that boundary; compact run output needs no artifact or evidence bodies. Core dependencies are empty; browser dependencies are optional. Use standard-library formatting and HTML escaping; no notebook/browser dependency on core import.

The earlier #317 plan explains the existing state, accounting, and history-compatibility contracts. This issue preserves them.

docs.title: Capture the missing facts
docs.text:
Add the following keyword-only fields to RunSummary, each defaulting to None. Existing positional fields and the three required state keywords keep their binding and meaning. None means unavailable, never zero or false.

Proposed field Source and meaning primary_objective: Maximize \| Minimize \| None First objective from the captured run declaration; reuse the existing immutable type. baseline_score: int \| float \| None Successful primary-objective measurement of the bootstrap trial, otherwise absent. failure_count: int \| None Number of distinct attempts with a committed typed proposal or evaluation failure, including the baseline if it failed. storage_is_durable: bool \| None Capability of the handle used to capture this report. storage_location: str \| None Optional display path known to that handle; never recovered from a backend or the filesystem during rendering. capabilities: RunCapabilities \| None Existing recorded execution declaration, not a fresh resume authorization.

For a summary built by Run.summary(), objective, failure count, durability, and capabilities are populated. Baseline and location may legitimately be absent. Old-style manual construction remains valid and displays unknown metadata honestly. Validate supplied types and finite non-boolean scores; failure counts must be nonnegative integers. Reject a supplied baseline with an unrankable summary. Do not authenticate manually assembled history or compare decoded artifact values during validation.

Derive the baseline using projection.bootstrap.trial.id and projection.evaluation_for(...). Do not select an arbitrary evaluation by artifact digest, lineage position, or score equality: repeated content has distinct occurrences. A pending or failed seed evaluation has no baseline.

Count the union of trial IDs whose committed TrialOutcome.failure or Evaluation.failure is present. Count a failed attempt once. Pending work, an unevaluated candidate, a rejected revision, and a low measured score are not failures merely because they did not improve the run.

Keep usage.trials as the proposal-attempt count and evaluation_count as committed evaluations. These include failed outcomes, exclude pending work, and differ in their treatment of the seed. Preserve the separate task and experience accounting; label displayed spend as task spend, not total cost. Show a separate context/pull usage row when present, without inventing a combined cost or measured elapsed duration.

Add private, optional, keyword-only display-path metadata to Storage, excluded from its repr and equality. Built-in durable() and read_only() capture an absolute path while opening their handle. in_memory() and compose() leave it absent. No new backend protocol, adapter introspection, public constructor option, or persisted field is needed. Snapshot construction only copies it.

All run facts come from the same validated projection already used by _summary_inputs; handle metadata is copied from the frozen storage facade. Do not call inspect(), best(), trials(), usage(), or load a second projection to enrich a summary. This retains an event-frontier guarantee, not a new cross-store transaction guarantee.

Keep normal dataclass equality for the added summary facts. Manually omitting facts does not make an incomplete report equal to a populated report. Update the current exact-field/equality tests deliberately; separately verify that the old constructor still binds and gives the documented unknown defaults. This is a nondurable record extension with no schema or identity change.

docs.title: Presentation rules
docs.text:
RunSummary.__repr__ supplies a compact, safe identifier/state/score summary. __str__ supplies the readable text report; _repr_html_ supplies equivalent notebook HTML. All three use the same bounded, inert display fields. They read only captured values, never storage, codecs, component functions, clocks, environment verification, network resources, or custom artifact display hooks.

Condition Required wording or behavior Complete/incomplete Complete or Incomplete, determined only by the recorded stop. Never infer that an incomplete run is currently executing. Rankable/unrankable Available or No successful measurement. Completion alone does not imply success. Baseline and selected scores present Show both, preserve zero and negatives, and identify maximize/minimize. Classify improvement with the objective's exact comparison; ties mean no improvement. Either score or the objective absent Report the available facts; improvement is unavailable. Do not manufacture a zero baseline or a percentage. Seed remains selected Report no measured improvement. Do not imply that the last proposal won. No stop yet Not stopped; recognized stop codes get ordinary wording, while unfamiliar codes remain visible as bounded text. Unknown task spend Unknown, never $0. Reuse the existing exact integer-microdollar formatter for known spend. Durable location absent Saved; location unspecified. A missing path is not evidence of memory-only execution. Durability metadata absent Unknown; do not label an old manual summary as saved or unsaved. Recorded resume support Identify the recorded mode and capability. Say that compatibility is not checked when support is declared; a complete run has no continuation pending.

Use baseline → selected and the direction-aware verdict in this slice. Numeric deltas, percentages, secondary-objective panels, and target-achievement badges add no necessary information and are deferred. A failed baseline followed by a successful candidate remains rankable, with improvement unavailable.

Keep full artifact values, evidence bodies, manifests, failure messages, and lineage lists out of compact output. The existing explicit inspection and frozen-payload artifact presentation remain their detail paths. In particular, never fall back to str, repr, _repr_html_, or equality on a decoded value. The frozen dataclass alone does not make a custom decoded value inert.

Bound dynamic text to 200 Unicode characters per field with visible truncation and at most 16 display rows. Preserve exact values on the public record. Escape terminal control characters, and HTML-escape every dynamic value. HTML uses a small semantic label/value layout that wraps on narrow screens; no scripts, external fonts, fetched images, active links, or automatic artifact previews. Test bounds with multibyte text and very large numeric values as well as long paths and custom stop reasons; output must not depend on payload size.

docs.title: Implementation sequence
docs.text:
Keep this as one focused issue and PR, with three reviewable slices. Do not create additional sub-issues for ordinary implementation steps.

  1. Capture and plain text. Enrich the existing summary builder, add the optional storage path metadata, and implement safe Run/summary repr and summary text. Prove closed-storage rendering, exact counting, constructor compatibility, and one-frontier capture before adding HTML.
  2. Notebook rendering. Render the same inert fields as escaped HTML and verify hooks cannot reach decoded values or optional packages. Use the existing PresentationField record in the private outer renderer meta_evolve/_run_display.py. Keep its scalar field builder alongside the markup renderer: presentation/ retains its stricter frozen-artifact-only dependency boundary. Runtime imports must remain acyclic.
  3. Documentation and review. Update the canonical contract and examples, exercise notebook desktop/narrow layouts, and record acceptance evidence against the actual integration revision before closing #333.

Keep formatting out of application/comparisons.py, which is already near the file-size guideline. If record validation makes a split necessary, extract the run-summary record by responsibility and retain its existing import/export locations; do not reorganize the application package. Keep individual new files below 300 lines. Reuse _formatting.dollars; do not route through the CLI renderer, whose detailed output currently formats decoded artifact values.

docs.title: Verification and documentation handoff
docs.text:
Acceptance area Focused evidence required Snapshot lifetime Capture while open, close, make the store unavailable, and render text/repr/HTML. Tripwires prove no later reads, codecs, or components run. Repeat for reopened read-only storage. Minimal Run repr Closed and unavailable stores remain representable; explicit queries still raise their real integrity/storage errors. Snapshot consistency Extend the existing advancement-during-capture test to the new fields. One load per summary and per comparison side, with no public-query recursion. Outcome semantics All four lifecycle/rankability states; pending distributed seed; failed seed then success; zero, negative, maximize, minimize, ties, and seed-selected cases. Counting Proposal failure, evaluation failure, failed baseline, pending/unevaluated work, unknown spend, and no double-counted failed attempt. Persistence/capability Memory, saved local-callable run, registered resumable run, completed run, read-only reopening, third-party durable storage without a path, and old-style manually constructed summaries. Safe/bounded output Hostile HTML/control strings and decoded objects with failing display/equality hooks; large artifacts, evidence, paths, and numbers; semantically equal text/HTML fields. Dependency boundary Core-only import and text/HTML generation without notebook or browser extras. New safety tests must not sit behind pytest.importorskip("starlette"). Historical behavior Reuse historical read fixtures without rewriting bytes. Preserve strict comparison and winner queries; test same-runtime continuation separately from expected source-drift refusal. Visual review Actual notebook display at desktop and approximately 360px width; long labels wrap, states remain legible without color, HTML and plain-text fallback convey the same facts.

Extend test_run_summaries.py, test_run_summary_snapshots.py, and the current constructor/comparison tests. Put dependency-free rendering tests in a focused new module; assert behavior and escaped structure rather than full-page golden screenshots. Existing optional browser routes and CLI output are outside this change. Source-manifest changes may affect verified resume compatibility even though durable record schemas are untouched; preserve that distinction in the verification receipt.

Update these sources with implementation:

  • docs/programming-model.md: capture lifetime, selected fields, safe display.
  • docs/architecture.md: inert snapshot rendering and unchanged authority.
  • docs/milestones.md and docs/implementation-plan.md: #331's follow-up gate, bounded presentation completion, and remaining post-M10 work.
  • docs/learn/03-inspect-results.md: lead with the compact snapshot, then detail.
  • docs/learn/06-persist-run.md: capture inside the storage block and display outside it; coordinate reopen wording with #335 without implementing it.
  • Canonical example/snippet sources and generated notebook material used by those pages; keep examples complete and code cells below 40 lines.
  • API reference/docstrings and summary migration guidance for optional fields and the deliberate repr change; do not duplicate signatures in guides.

Run the focused behavior suites, core dependency checks, affected example and documentation checks, and the repository's required integration checks once the implementation exists. Record visual review separately from automated tests. Hand the captured-report example to #336; do not expand #333 into the feedback accessor, improve() options, reopening convenience, or SDK work.

docs.title: Difficulty and completion
docs.text:
Low–medium complexity; estimated two to four focused working days, excluding the #331 dependency, review queues, and publication. The main risk is truthful capture and compatibility, rather than HTML styling. No coordinator, storage schema, search, budget, or provider overhaul is needed.

Close #333 only after behavior, focused tests, canonical documentation, and desktop/narrow notebook review agree. The verification record distinguishes source implementation, automated checks, and visual review; this plan alone is not acceptance evidence.

docs.title: Run summaries without a winner: implementation plan for #317
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This planning record is retained for design history. The implemented source contract now belongs to the programming model, with verification tracked separately.

Prepared September 18, 2026 for #317, under #313. The summary contract owns the proposed behavior; this page specifies its implementation and tests. The programming model and architecture remain the shipped contract owners.

docs.title: Starting point and release boundary
docs.text: The inspected HEAD is c04ec6b4b949b8a2702779107e25acd24feb8020, with local #297,

docs.title: 314, and #315 work. #316's callback implementation began changing during this
docs.text:
review. Preserve those edits; identify the actual integration revision before implementation and reconcile callback fixtures with the accepted #316 contract. This plan changes no runtime source or tests.

The local #314 foundation decision and Author API revision gate now freeze the summary, comparison, CLI, and pending-seed contracts. They select a coordinated pre-1.0 compatibility reset, working target 0.2.0. Bind implementation to the reviewed foundation revision and finalize the constructor/private seams below in its handoff. Other API redesign implementations are not prerequisites.

Keep #317 as one focused implementation PR with query behavior, consumers, tests, migration guidance, and canonical documentation. It changes reporting, not execution, search, budget admission, or M11 concurrency. Do not combine it with callback migration or opportunistic namespace cleanup.

docs.title: Findings that determine the design
docs.text:
Source tracing and deterministic probes establish:

Current behavior Consequence for #317 A successful summary() performs four validated loads; compare() performs ten across its two runs. Build each summary and its comparison inputs from one captured event frontier. A failed seed with one evaluation, two tokens, and seven billed micro-USD raises from summary, both before and after stop. Make reporting independent of rankability without hiding cost. All four lifecycle/rankability combinations occur through ordinary Session.start() and stepping. Test real execution boundaries without truncating event streams. Distributed Session.start() can retain the seed while its evaluation is pending. Summary raises; inspection and usage currently raise SearchNotStarted. Committed-usage reporting must not require a ready policy view. Failed-left/missing-right comparison raises NoSuccessfulEvaluation before reading the right side. Keep left-to-right failure precedence when summaries stop raising. Missing summary raises generic RunError; inspection raises RunNotFound. Deliberately align missing-summary behavior with the typed read boundary. CLI run failure produces exit 1 and only an error line. Preserve exit 1 while making the actual summary available on stdout. Browser detail already uses inspection; comparison consumes strict RunComparison. Preserve those routes and refusal behavior; no new summary endpoint is needed.

The source-hashed probe and output are in /private/tmp/meta-evolve-317/probe.py and probe.json. These observations are baseline evidence, not a result for the proposed implementation.

docs.title: 1. Freeze the public record and invariants
docs.text:
Retain RunSummary as the same root-exported, frozen, slotted application view. It remains outside durable serialization. Preserve its current field names, decoded seed/lineage values, provenance, and count/resource meanings.

Change Required meaning Add lifecycle complete iff a committed stop exists; otherwise incomplete Add rankability rankable iff a successful primary-objective measurement is selectable Add stop_reason The recorded reason when complete; None when incomplete Change primary_score to int \| float \| None Actual selected measurement or None; zero and negative scores remain valid Permit empty winning_lineage Empty iff unrankable; otherwise the existing decoded causal lineage

Make the three new fields required keyword-only fields, without defaults that would guess the lifecycle of a manually constructed record. Preserve the binding order of existing positional fields; callers constructing summaries directly add the new keywords. Run.summary() itself gains no parameter.

Validate the new relationships in RunSummary.__post_init__: accepted state values; non-empty string stop reason iff complete; finite numeric, non-boolean score and non-empty tuple lineage iff rankable; None score and empty tuple lineage iff unrankable. A rankable summary must have at least one completed evaluation. Type errors and contradictory values should fail clearly. Do not try to authenticate arbitrary user-constructed history or compare decoded artifact objects merely to validate these relationships.

evaluation_count continues to count committed evaluation outcomes, including failed evaluations and the seed when evaluated. Pending evaluations do not count. Proposal attempts, bootstrap records, and worker deliveries remain distinct. Keep usage, experience totals, and name_only_components unchanged. Do not add an improved flag: selecting a seed or an exact tie is still rankable.

Keep best(), best_trial(), and default lineage() strict when nothing ranks. Detailed typed failures remain in inspect()/trials(); a compact summary does not become a second full inspection aggregate.

docs.title: 2. Build from one validated snapshot
docs.text:
Keep summary/comparison ownership in application/comparisons.py unless the final size requires a responsibility-based split. Use a private load/build seam so summary() and compare() reuse the same projection and seed metadata:

  1. Call load_validated_run(..., require_existing=True) exactly once for this run. A nonexistent run raises RunNotFound; corrupt nonempty history keeps its existing typed integrity failure.
  2. Use the retained declaration and ViewBuilder for primary ranking, seed decoding, and causal lineage. Handle only the expected absence of a successful evaluation; do not catch corruption, decoding, or infrastructure failures.
  3. Derive lifecycle from projection.stop, not from score, budget, or a live Session object. Preserve ranking direction and stable logical tie order.
  4. Aggregate recorded usage/experience and build the storage-independent value. It must remain usable after storage closes, including custom-codec values.

Do not call public best(), lineage(), or inspect() inside this builder. They would trigger fresh loads or construct unrelated detailed views. Reusing the existing ViewBuilder retains ranking and lineage semantics without a new query framework or public snapshot object.

One snapshot means one validated event frontier per run. It does not promise an atomic transaction across two independent stores. The browser already checks versions before and after comparisons; preserve that stronger UI behavior.

docs.title: Include the pending seed evaluation
docs.text:
Use an actual admitted Session.start(..., mode="distributed") fixture. Before driving it, its valid genesis contains one seed trial and zero evaluations; summary should be incomplete/unrankable, with no score, stop, or winning lineage. Preserve its decoded seed and aggregate only committed usage. Pending external work is not an estimated or settled cost.

RunProjection.search_state intentionally rejects this frontier. Keep that execution guard. Separate the existing recorded-usage fold from its readiness requirement with one small private helper, reusing SearchState.usage's exact calculation/order. Share it with the summary and, as a bounded supporting fix, Run.usage() and inspection's usage field so those read paths agree on this valid state. Do not add a scheduler path, force bootstrap execution, duplicate numeric aggregation, or return guessed zero usage on a caught exception.

Normal bootstrapped usage must stay exactly equal, including unknown spend, post-call overages, failed work, and floating-point elapsed-work aggregation. The policy-facing view's readiness and recovery rules remain unchanged. Record the newly supported pre-bootstrap inspection/usage case in migration guidance.

docs.title: 3. Preserve strict comparison and error order
docs.text:
Perform these steps in order, reusing each side's loaded inputs:

  1. Validate that other is a Run.
  2. Load/build the left summary and require a successful measurement.
  3. Load/build the right summary and require a successful measurement.
  4. Apply the existing declaration-compatibility checks in their existing order.
  5. Compare actual numeric scores using the primary objective's direction and return the existing comparison record.

This uses at most one validated load per side and short-circuits before reading the right run if the left is unrankable. A missing/corrupt left side still wins over a failed right side; an unrankable side still wins over declaration incompatibility. The deliberate missing-run change is the more specific RunNotFound, which remains a RunError.

Retain evaluator, artifact kind, metric/direction/threshold, task/effective budget, seed representation/schema/digest, and authorized-proposer controls. Random seed and context/experience differences remain reported separately. Do not add a requirement that a rankable run has stopped, or relax proposer equality to compare different improvement procedures.

Harden direct RunComparison construction for the newly optional scores: both sides must be rankable; winner is None means equal successful scores, never two missing scores. An explicit winner must still be exactly one of the two summary instances. Preserve existing consistency checks for comparison flags. Correct objective direction stays the builder's responsibility; adding another objective field solely to re-prove it in the record is unnecessary.

docs.title: 4. Migrate reporting consumers
docs.text:
Keep _render_summary() as the one text formatter. Add lifecycle, rankability, and stop rows; render an absent score and empty winning lineage explicitly (for example none). Continue omitting measured wall-clock values from stable CLI text. Render zero/negative scores as scores, not as absence.

The CLI needs text and exit status together. Use one small private command report value with those two fields, and let main() remain the only stream writer. A shared summary-report helper can choose status from rankability; do not use an exception to carry an ordinary unrankable report or execute a second query just to choose the exit code. Other commands retain their existing output/status semantics; no new public CLI result type is introduced.

Command outcome stdout stderr / exit run/resume, rankable, including seed-selected Summary Empty / 0 run/resume, unrankable Summary with state, absent score, and recorded cost Empty / 1 inspect, valid rankable or unrankable history Detailed inspection Empty / 0 compare, compatible rankable histories Comparison Empty / 0 Missing/corrupt run, inadmissible resume, or refused comparison No fabricated summary Existing typed error / 1 Usage/module error Existing usage behavior Existing error / 2

Unexpected defects keep their traceback. Keep factory compatibility, parser flags, UI server lifecycle, and capability decisions out of this change. Update AST boundary tests narrowly: allow the shared status helper to read rankability for control flow, while formatting remains confined to the existing renderers and stream writes remain confined to main().

Browser detail already displays lifecycle/rankability through RunInspection. Test the new pending-seed case there through the shared inspection fix. Strict comparison still returns HTTP 422 for an unrankable side; preserve escaping, inert artifact presentation, version checks, and cache behavior. No new route, report format, or browser-specific summary semantics is needed.

docs.title: 5. Regression and compatibility matrix
docs.text:
Prefer focused new test_run_summaries.py and CLI outcome coverage over growing the already-large comparison/CLI suites. Reuse existing fixtures and failure injection. Normally keep files below 300 lines; preserve the CLI's documented single-boundary exception and review any necessary exact length-ratchet update.

Case Required evidence Four lifecycle/rankability states Create through public sessions; state, stop, optional score, lineage, counts, and usage agree with inspection Pending distributed seed Real admitted start; zero evaluated outcomes, truthful committed usage; reporting executes no work Seed-only, tie, regression, maximize/minimize Selected measurement and lineage match strict queries; zero and negative scores remain present Failed proposer/evaluator; unevaluated successor Typed outcomes and spent resources survive; no score is invented Unknown spend and overages Summary/usage/inspection agree and never coerce unknown to zero Feedback and custom codecs Declarations/provenance/experience totals and decoded seed/lineage types remain intact Snapshot coherence One validated load per summary, at most one per comparison side; a commit after the captured frontier cannot mix old counts with a new winner Query purity No proposer/evaluator/search execution, event append, work claim, store migration, or durable mutation during reporting Strict comparison Failures on either/both sides, error precedence, incompatible controls, cross-store comparisons, exact tie, and winner identity Record construction Invalid states/combinations fail; required keyword-only additions and dataclass immutability are intentional CLI and browser Real subprocess output/exit tests and existing browser refusal/security/cache tests, including pending seed Historical stores Old success/failure/incomplete histories produce new views without rewriting records or relaxing resume verification

Reuse tests/_faults.py for interrupted durable prefixes rather than deleting SQLite rows. Reuse the old stores identified by #314's compatibility record, with their source and capture hashes. Hash stored records/artifacts before and after reads, and test matching-runtime resume separately from expected cross-version manifest refusals. Add no durable type, event field, store-schema version, or identity input for a derived summary.

Compare affected component manifest digests before and after any shared-source extraction. A reporting change is not proof of resume compatibility: preserve exact-source checks and record any fingerprint effect separately from schema compatibility and from #316's invocation changes.

Update existing tests that explicitly require summary failure, especially test_run_comparisons.py, test_monetary_accounting.py, and test_api_reference_examples.py. Their cost and strict-winner assertions must remain; replace only the obsolete summary expectation. Preserve existing custom codec reopening and artifact/source corruption tests at the read boundary.

docs.title: 6. Documentation, implementation order, and completion
docs.text:
Update Run, Run.summary(), Run.usage(), and RunSummary docstrings; the programming model/architecture; result inspection and CLI guides; budget guidance that currently warns against summary; and the executable failure reference case. Keep full failure diagnosis in the inspection lesson. Audit example reporting for optional-score assumptions without gratuitously rewriting successful-only studies or changing their algorithms.

Migration explains: absence now returns primary_score=None; strict winner queries still raise; direct constructors require the new keywords; missing runs use RunNotFound; unrankable CLI runs print a summary and exit 1; and pre-bootstrap usage/inspection becomes available. Do not advertise a successful summary call as successful evaluation, improvement, or resumability.

Implement in this order: record/constructor contract → shared recorded-usage and snapshot builder → strict comparison → CLI/browser consumers → canonical docs and executable examples. Each stage keeps its focused tests with the behavior. Review the combined diff as one #317 slice.

Run focused summary, inspection, comparison, accounting, reopening, CLI, and browser checks first. Then run applicable runtime CI and the maintained Docs workflow, including strict build, rendered reference, executable examples, and fresh installed-package downloads. Identify the final source/lock/package and record actual results and limits. #318/#319 own coordinated release/publication.

The planning-time baseline selection was not green while #316 was changing: 81 failures, 11 setup errors, and 27 passes. Inspected failures rejected older positional-context fixtures under the new callback rule. Do not treat that run as a stable baseline or fix sibling callback work inside #317; rerun after integration settles. The earlier source-hashed probes establish the reporting observations above independently of those in-progress fixture migrations.

docs.title: Scheduler showcase: plan for #350
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 20, 2026 for #350, under #343. The prerequisite #347 is closed. This plan builds on the existing documentation work in the working tree. The implementation verification now records the completed local Jupyter rehearsal. The user selected Jupyter for delivery; Colab remains unverified and is not advertised as supported.

The programming model owns public APIs, architecture owns invariants, and the B2 acceptance record owns the shipped study. M11 remains the runtime build boundary. This issue changes the study's presentation and installation route using its existing execution contracts.

docs.title: Reader outcome
docs.text:
A reader arriving from “improve a program” can explain the scheduling problem, read one proposed code change, run the complete study in a supported notebook, and interpret the measured result. The scheduler showcase is an optional next step after the introduction.

Open research/adrs.md with jobs of different sizes arriving at several workers. Round-robin takes turns assigning jobs without inspecting worker load; the fixture's repeated large jobs make that uneven. Show the small change: sample two workers, inspect their loads, and choose the less loaded worker. Explain a probe as one request for a worker's current load.

Use this compact development comparison, regenerated from actual run records:

Scheduler Load imbalance, lower is better Probes per job Combined quality, higher is better Starting round-robin 0.2071 0 0.7929 Inspect every worker 0.0381 7 0.8219 Inspect two workers 0.0464 2 0.9136

The two-worker version buys much better balance than the seed with two probes. It spends fewer probes than a full scan, accepting slightly worse balance. Explain the fixed quality formula beside the measurements: max(0, 1 - imbalance - 0.02 * probes_per_job).

Keep development, post-search selection, and final checking visibly separate. The final comparison currently measures quality 0.7912 → 0.8806, imbalance 0.2088 → 0.0794, and probes 0 → 2. These are simulator measurements. The proposer uses an authored sequence; actual candidate code produces the measurements.

Move the ADRS worksheet, component mapping, declared authority, complete phase report, and research qualifications below the runnable showcase. Retain the existing page and notebook URLs and any promised anchors. Correct the page's BestOfN description to the maintained Greedy configuration and its command to python examples/research/systems_optimization/main.py.

docs.title: Implementation order
docs.text:
1. Prove the downloaded runtime route first. Build the package and complete example archives from one source state, install into a fresh environment, and run outside the checkout. Establish a working Jupyter route before polishing cells. Attempt an actual Colab session separately and record its platform, Python version, confinement result, and exact failure if refused.
  2. Add the complete download and early capability check. Register systems in the existing docs/hooks/catalog.py archive mechanism. Preserve examples/research/systems_optimization/ and its package import names. Add visible notebook download/extraction and confinement-preflight cells.
  3. Rewrite the page and existing notebook around the measured change. Make the page the canonical lesson and register it in the existing notebook exporter in docs/hooks/entrance.py. Keep command.run_example() as its execution path. Derive compact tables, selected source, and phase summaries from that outcome. Reuse retained failures and replay checks for the advanced walkthrough; regenerate the existing evidence notebook from the same cells.
  4. Connect navigation and regression checks. Link the showcase from the existing “improve a program” choices in the homepage/README and appropriate next-step pages. Extend existing archive, notebook, and rendered-site tests; update affected Docs workflow selections.
  5. Rehearse and assemble the audit evidence. Execute the finished notebook with the matching installation/downloads, render it and the page, inspect them visually, and retain the exact output and runtime receipts. Salah's review is required before closing the issue.

docs.title: Notebook and runtime contract
docs.text:
State Python 3.12+ and platform requirements before installation. The current mechanisms are macOS sandbox-exec and Linux Landlock ABI 3 or newer, subject to successful enforcement on the actual host. Advertise a runtime only after the complete notebook has run there. If Colab refuses confinement, publish the reproducible limitation and the verified Jupyter route.

Aim for four required cells to the first measured table, each below 40 lines:

  1. Install the package from the documentation build's source ZIP.
  2. Download and extract that build's complete systems example automatically.
  3. Import the downloaded example and verify real confinement, with an actionable explanation if the runtime or extraction location is unsuitable.
  4. Run the maintained study and display the compact measured comparison.

Keep code inspection, detailed phase results, failure controls, accounting, and replay after that result. Publish the actual required cell count and elapsed setup/run time. This optional study has its own runtime requirements; the introductory five-minute result remains separate.

Confinement discovery alone is insufficient. Use the existing launcher for a small standard-library probe in a temporary workspace: verify that Python starts and that reading the downloaded protected workload file is denied. Confirm that file exists and is readable by the trusted notebook first, so a missing file cannot masquerade as successful protection. Handle launch denial, timeout, an unsafe path, and unavailable facilities before calling the study. This diagnostic is setup work, outside study evaluations and scenario counts. Prefer a visible cell over a new runtime abstraction.

The extraction layout matters: confinement.REPOSITORY is derived from the example's ancestors. Extract into a dedicated notebook working-directory child outside the interpreter installation and Linux readable exemptions such as /tmp and /usr. Keep child workspaces outside the protected download root. Validate canonical paths through the existing confinement checks. Choose a compatible rehearsal directory; retain the current allow-list.

Use lesson_notebook() to export the page's visible cells as downloads/systems-optimization.ipynb. Regenerate and execute the existing docs/notebooks/systems_optimization/systems_optimization.ipynb from that export, preserving its established evidence URL. Check cell-source equality between page, download, and executed notebook. Mark illustrative candidate source as nonexecuted excerpts so it does not become extra setup cells. Keep table rendering in the shared visible cells, with no second study driver or notebook renderer. Keep downloads and installation from one documentation build; retain their hashes and source revision for audit.

docs.title: Data and behavior to preserve
docs.text:
• run_example() retains development search, post-search selection, final comparison, decision persistence, and replay in their existing order.
  • Read tables from decision.development, decision.selection, and decision.comparison. Resolve the final selected source through its recorded identity and the run's artifacts. search.best() is not necessarily the post-search winner.
  • Display typed failures and absent comparisons explicitly. A failed attempt has no invented metric. Preserve cleanup even if a run or notebook cell fails.
  • Keep simulator execution, candidate surfaces, workload separation, policy identities, accounting, and evaluator independence intact. Presentation changes need no coordinator branch, new public API, or new artifact domain.
  • Preserve source-manifest verification. Editing an identity-bearing example module, even its comments, requires regenerating affected captured digests.

docs.title: Acceptance checks and evidence
docs.text:
Extend test_systems_optimization_notebook.py, test_catalog_examples.py, test_lesson_downloads.py, and the existing research/navigation checks. Replace assumptions that setup is the first run cell or that every saved output is byte-identical when installation logs/timings are variable; keep exact checks for deterministic study results. Test visible behavior rather than specific explanatory sentences.

The focused checks must prove:

  • The archive is complete, preserves relative paths, and matches maintained files. A fresh noneditable installation runs the downloaded notebook outside the checkout without PYTHONPATH or earlier notebook state. Assert package and example import origins. On Linux, ordinary pytest /tmp extraction is unsuitable for this example; provision a compatible isolated location.
  • Notebook cells and the displayed measurements agree with a fresh governed run. Table rows cannot mix workload phases. All replay checks still pass.
  • Changing the two-worker comparison from <= to >= changes observed measurements. Reuse the existing wrong-comparator candidate as the control, and retain invalid-schedule/off-surface typed refusals as failure evidence.
  • Unsupported enforcement stops before study execution with a useful remedy; successful capability detection followed by failed launch is covered too.
  • A missing or unrankable final comparison renders without a score or crash; output-directory cleanup still runs on exceptions.
  • A strict documentation build and rendered-link checks cover the notebook, source archive, source links, optional program navigation, and advanced study.

Run the affected notebook/download tests and existing systems-optimization measurement, failure, confinement, accounting, decision, and replay tests. Retain a rendered page, executed notebook, copied-cell transcript, source revision and dirty-state qualification, archive hashes, installation origin, OS/kernel/Python details, setup/run times, cell count, and manual interventions. Record Jupyter and Colab outcomes separately. Agent rehearsal supplies execution evidence; Salah's audit and the separate newcomer-review gate retain their owners.

docs.title: Planning evidence
docs.text:
Inspected working tree: 9077011776a9b3cf6d2df57e798288e58a9c486c, with existing documentation edits. A fresh fixture run on Python 3.12.13/macOS 26.6.2 reproduced the numbers above, development/selection/final evaluation counts of 9/5/2, scenario counts of 13/15/4, and all eleven replay checks.

The outer tool sandbox refused nested sandbox-exec with “Operation not permitted”; running with approved local process permissions succeeded. This supports testing actual launch in preflight. It does not establish hosted notebook compatibility. A fresh installed-download notebook rehearsal and actual Colab check remain implementation acceptance work.

docs.title: Scientific direction
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This is a retained design record. The programming model and project status identify shipped behavior; proposals below do not extend those contracts.

Meta-Evolve may eventually represent hypotheses, protocols, datasets, simulations, analyses, claims, replications, and retractions as typed artifacts. That direction does not make software evaluation equivalent to validated science.

Scientific use requires explicit provenance, preregistered or otherwise governed evaluation, uncertainty, leakage controls, independent replication, negative results, and human/institutional authority. Model-generated novelty or an improved benchmark score is evidence only within the declared experiment.

Training views, semantic retrieval, learned search, and model-weight updates must be derived from immutable authorized records. They cannot become an unrecorded source of experience or retroactively alter a historical decision.

Current shipped semantics provide useful ingredients—immutable artifacts, typed failures, evidence, budgets, causal lineage, and replay—but do not ship a scientific artifact domain or make generalization claims.

docs.title: Agent SDK accounting support: study plan for #337
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This plans #337, under #330. The outcome is an evidenced decision about reusable SDK accounting support. A maintained recipe, retaining the existing wrappers, or deferring a helper can satisfy the issue. A lightweight implementation and decision provides runnable recipes and focused offline comparisons. The requested practical scope closes the decision with experiment-local reuse and no public helper. The broader matrix below is retained as optional follow-up guidance; its full runtime acceptance is not claimed or required for this closure.

The programming model, architecture, author UX gate, and implementation plan remain authoritative. The SDK boundary reference owns the existing failure and accounting rules. The study does not expand #313/#319's release scope.

docs.title: Question and starting point
docs.text:
After #336, can a small reusable recipe remove repeated accounting work from Codex, Claude Code's Agent SDK, and Pi integrations without hiding decisions about agent execution, paid work, unavailable measurements, or valid output?

Use #336's completed journey and glue inventory. It shipped in source through #338. Planning baseline, September 19, 2026: a6ac22e7aab7239dd4adf777d43995d07bbcf5b8. Unrelated local release and harness planning edits were present; this is not a clean installed-artifact claim. Pin the actual source revision and SDK dependencies again when running the study.

Codex, Claude Agent SDK, and Pi are the three required study targets. The issue's minimum of two materially different integrations is a floor; this plan uses all three to test the requested agent workflows. The short notebook and full lesson both use OpenAI Responses and serve as a simple regression control. No new live capture or newcomer session is needed to start this study; those remain distinct evidence under #269–#271 and #275/#277.

docs.title: Scope and comparison cases
docs.text:
Compare a bounded agent invocation through each programmatic interface, including multiple model steps, tool execution, terminal events and partial failure. Use deterministic process/protocol/model fixtures and synthetic billing reports; keep outputs and tool observations fixed when comparing each wrapper to its candidate revision. Native event streams and asynchronous SDK consumption are in scope even though Meta-Evolve's outer callable path remains synchronous.

Integration Starting implementation and meaningful difference Codex Use the official Python openai-codex SDK and its pinned CLI/app-server runtime. Start from CodexProvider in experiments/_live_support/providers.py and experiments/08_harness_evolution_live/codex_boundary.py. Trace thread/turn identity, tool activity, terminal status and the actual scope of reported usage. Claude Code via Claude Agent SDK Use Python claude-agent-sdk and its matching CLI. Start from AgentSdkProvider and experiment 11's accounting probes. Trace asynchronous assistant/tool/result messages, query versus session totals, terminal errors and auxiliary work. Pi Use Pi's programmatic agent interface. For this Python study, choose the documented JSON-over-stdio RPC path; consult the TypeScript SDK's session/event contract. Pin the Pi package/runtime and record the bridge's code and lifecycle cost. This is an agent integration, not a direct pi-ai model call or a claimed native Python SDK.

Read the official Codex SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Claude accounting, Pi SDK and Pi RPC contracts. Sources checked September 19, 2026; pin package/runtime versions and recheck their field semantics before constructing fixtures.

Two concrete traps justify this scope. Claude's ResultMessage.usage excludes nested work; model_usage covers more calls, and its streaming-input totals are cumulative. The documented coverage still excludes some helper calls. Its reported dollars are estimates, not billing statements. See the Python result contract. Pi's session statistics include reported tool and compaction work; its contextUsage describes the current context rather than consumed work. These are different aggregation problems from decoding one model response.

The existing agent probes mostly constrain turns and tools and contain historical zero defaults for missing usage. Treat those as findings to review, not current accounting guarantees. Known zero monetary charge never proves zero token work. Use current Resources reports at the author boundary rather than copying their historical author Usage spelling or silently changing old capture claims.

Keep the existing Responses lesson and openai==2.54.0 notebook as a lightweight control: an agent-oriented recipe must not complicate a single model call. A new direct Anthropic Messages wrapper is unnecessary for this study.

The existing experiments/_live_support/accounting.py is a supporting reference. It already consolidates exact decimal conversion and a paid-call boundary, but its experiment policy requires a bill. The lesson allows spend_micros=None. Do not merge these policies or import this experiment module into core or the downloadable lessons as a shortcut.

Meta-Evolve concurrency, a generic agent runtime, provider registries, pricing services, package publication and historical-capture migrations remain outside the comparison. Pi accounting findings can inform the separately planned SoL-Pi experiment;

docs.title: 337 does not implement its mechanisms or depend on its live campaign.
Common agent task and execution boundary
docs.text:
Use a small temporary workspace with an editable text artifact, fixed task instructions and independent Python checks. Each agent must read relevant files, perform a permitted tool action and produce a candidate that the wrapper can extract. A success fixture includes multiple model steps and a tool result; disabling every tool and asking for one string cannot satisfy the agent gate.

Exercise both roles: an agent proposes an artifact for independent grading; an evaluator runs an agent against a fixed task and grades its artifact or trace. Agent self-reported success is never the metric. Preserve the development/final split and declare which authorized Meta-Evolve feedback reaches the agent.

Use fresh workspaces and sessions per independent attempt, with explicit runtime settings, tool/permission bounds and resource-loading policy. Check that project or user configuration cannot silently alter the fixture. A continuation/resume scenario separately tests attribution to the current invocation; it must not charge prior history again. SDK session IDs do not replace Meta-Evolve lineage.

docs.title: What the author must still own
docs.text: Responsibility Study treatment Request settings, credentials, model, SDK and runtime identity Remain in client construction and Task.environment; record permission, tool, session and resource-loading settings without credentials. Events, token categories and accounting scope Remain SDK-specific; declare deltas versus cumulative totals, duplicate identities, resets, disjoint categories and included auxiliary work. Output validity and grading Remain explicit in the wrapper and independent evaluator; an accounting utility cannot decide a score or candidate acceptance. Billed versus estimated cost and its source Remain explicit; a price calculation is evidence, not a bill. Exact conversion and accounting assembly Candidate reuse seam, subject to the comparison below. Reuse Resources validation/addition rather than inventing a second accounting type. Process/session lifetime, timing, retries and cancellation Wrapper retains SDK lifecycle and policy; a budget outside the callable is not a proven hard limit on its internal model/tool loop. Tool access and partial-work aggregation Preserve tool outcomes, terminal status, receipts and authorized feedback. Custom experience tools delegate to the existing audited reader. Request journal and final-check separation Remain journey-owned; these persist observations that may never reach a history commit.

docs.title: One minimal candidate
docs.text:
First establish working baselines for all three agents, with explicit guarantees. Do not make the new baseline deliberately verbose to favor the candidate. Retain the short notebook's unknown-spend path as a simplicity check; it must not acquire mandatory billing setup merely to use a shared recipe.

The initial hypothesis is an example-owned recipe for retaining observations and finalizing one agent invocation. Each wrapper interprets its own events first. Only then prototype one small shared function for the repeated accounting assembly, if the inventory supports it: explicitly scoped token work, elapsed work, cost provenance and partial receipts become existing Resources and EvidenceDraft values, or an accounting-unknown escape. Do not force streams into a universal event schema, a new public receipt class or a result hierarchy. The exact seam is provisional; a final-number formatter alone may earn no helper.

Meta-Evolve proposer or evaluator
    -> user-owned Codex / Claude / Pi invocation
    -> native model/tool/session events and final artifact
    -> wrapper-owned attribution and failure classification
    -> candidate accounting seam -> existing Resources + evidence + result

The wrapper still encloses startup, iteration, tools, terminal decoding and cleanup in the work-accounting boundary. A function called only after success cannot recover a lost stream or discover unreported internal calls. The candidate neither imports an SDK nor dispatches requests, retries, fetches prices, grades output, adds engine counts, or supplies missing measurements.

Keep ProposalResult and EvaluationResult at their current owners. The study must exercise both roles; returning a provider's self-assigned score cannot replace the independent evaluator.
