If reuse requires callbacks for every field, provider modes, or a generic adapter protocol, record that as evidence against this candidate rather than enlarging it during the study.

docs.title: Deterministic evidence matrix
docs.text:
Run applicable cases before and after for all three targets, then through real Meta-Evolve callables, storage and budgets. Native transports/parsers must be exercised where the SDK is used, with scripted process or model responses; Pi's RPC probe also exercises its pinned runtime against deterministic model/tool fixtures. A fake complete() result alone proves only reducer logic. Record adapter-level and runtime-level evidence separately, including telemetry gaps. Use controlled clocks and synthetic billing strings; no paid calls are needed.

Case Required observation Completed tool-using agent, proposer and evaluator Correct artifact or independent metric; equivalent resources, evidence and engine counts before/after. Multiple internal model steps do not become Meta-Evolve trials/evaluations. Cached and reasoning categories Follow each pinned runtime's disjoint/subset rules; preserve breakdowns without adding them twice. Repeated events, final totals and per-model breakdown Count each execution once; never add a final aggregate to the steps it summarizes. Duplicate text/tool events are not additional billed calls. Continued/resumed session and reset Attribute only this invocation's work. Apply verified delta/cumulative/reset rules; retain prior receipts without charging them again. Compaction, internal retries and nested agents/tools Include observable auxiliary work once, preserving attribution. If required work is unobservable, expose the gap rather than calling a partial total complete. Do not fabricate an equivalent capability in another runtime. Wrong completed answer Measured low score under the declared grader, not an infrastructure failure. Empty, incomplete, malformed or unsupported artifact with known usage Typed failure without a score; keep tokens, bill if known, elapsed work and diagnostic evidence. Final assistant text alone is not proof the artifact is valid. Tool failure, permission denial or exhausted turn limit Preserve native terminal status and costs. A recoverable tool error can precede a valid final artifact; an unsuccessful overall execution has no invented score. Cancellation, timeout or process death mid-tool/stream Retain completed-prefix receipts, stop/close the owned process or session, record incomplete work and do not promote a partial artifact as success. Failure proven before dispatch No model/tool work dispatched and no invented paid usage; distinguish this from an ambiguous process or transport error. Transport failure after possible work, unusable body, or missing required accounting ExecutionAccountingUnknown escapes; available receipts and cause survive; no fabricated zero or automatic retry. Missing/null/negative/boolean token category Follow the pinned provider contract; absent required counts escape. Never turn absence into zero by convenience defaulting or lose a bad component inside a valid sum. Exact bill, explicit zero, fractional micro and high-precision amount Count billed spend exactly under the existing round-up rule; preserve raw amount/source. Reject lost float precision rather than claiming to reconstruct it. Tokens known, bill absent or estimate only Successful output stays usable; spend is None, estimates remain evidence. SDK-reported dollar fields alone do not establish a bill. A monetary ceiling stops subsequent work under shipped rules. Independently established no per-invocation charge Explicit zero spend is valid only with that basis recorded. A subscription label or absent cost field alone is insufficient; missing required tokens still escape. Optional billing lookup fails Preserve model output and known resources; record unknown spend and a safe diagnostic. Distinguish an unavailable bill from an exception announcing unknown required work. SDK retry controls and explicit caller retry Record actual runtime retry policy and observed attempts. Disable retries for the basic fixture where supported; test internal retries separately, exposing unobservable work or an unavailable control. Later decoding error after usage was recovered Preserve already known costs in a typed failure or available receipt; never fall through to an ordinary exception that books zero usage. Multiple requests, then known failure Aggregate completed and failed-request resources once; retain partial evidence, with no invented full-suite score. Multiple requests, then unknown accounting Keep completed-prefix receipts plus available failing-request facts; no fabricated complete result or charge. Distinguish the journal from committed history. Nested run Forward inner.usage().resources once; do not forward inner engine counts. Add only outer work not already represented in the nested resources. Timing and post-run inspection Include the declared invocation/cleanup work once; overlapping tool/model durations are evidence, not extra outer elapsed time. Reading history invokes neither SDK nor cost callback. SDK limits versus Meta-Evolve budget Demonstrate the actual enforcement boundary; do not claim an outer admission check interrupts in-flight agent work or that an estimated SDK cost cap is a billed-spend ceiling.

For partial and nested cases, test known-plus-known and known-plus-unknown spend. The journey's request journal overlaps committed history; adding their totals would double count. Final evaluation remains outside development usage and feedback. The helper does not add a new durable unknown-token representation.

For features unavailable on one target, document the native limitation and verify honest rejection or incomplete accounting. This does not waive the shared tool-using success, interruption and attribution cases. An SDK with insufficient telemetry can be a valid finding against a reusable helper, not a passing claim of complete accounting. No new durable accounting model is implied.

Baseline bugs are findings, not behavior to preserve. Use canonical contracts as the oracle and record any mismatch separately before claiming equivalence. Do not silently fix a production wrapper inside the comparison and attribute that correction to the helper's ergonomics.

docs.title: Three reviewable steps
docs.text:
Step Work Exit evidence 1. Freeze and reproduce Pin SDKs, bundled runtimes, Pi/Node and transport dependencies. Adapt existing Codex/Claude probes to the common agent task; add Pi RPC. Inventory native usage scope and the simple Responses control. Three offline baselines, native event traces, required author decisions and baseline defects/telemetry gaps. 2. Compare one candidate Keep SDK lifecycle/extraction local; test one shared accounting seam against all three. Run tool, interruption, partial/nested and attribution cases through real storage/budgets. Keep fixture facts identical across arms. Before/after source and event-to-resource traces, both callable roles, repeatable outcomes and documented unsupported cases. 3. Decide and hand off Review correctness first, then the friction scorecard. Choose retain, recipe/example-local reuse, defer, or public-helper follow-up. A decision with evidence, remaining costs and rejected alternatives; input for #269 and the #330 parent.

When executed, keep the runnable comparison under experiments/sdk_accounting/, with a small README, pinned optional dependencies, deterministic fixtures and focused tests. Create files as each responsibility needs them, not a destination package tree. Keep hand-written files normally below 300 lines. Use a separate environment so study SDKs/runtimes do not enter core dependencies or change the lesson's installed SDK baseline. Block external traffic in the fixture harness; use controlled temporary workspaces and isolated agent configuration.

Write actual results to docs/project/sdk-accounting-study.md when they exist; link it from this plan and the practical-journey handoff. Retain exact commands, source SHA/dirty patch, Python/Node/SDK/runtime versions, fixture identity, outcome counts and representative traces. A skipped integration is not comparison evidence. The first implementation's record separates native SDK shape checks from scripted agent execution and the remaining runtime work.

docs.title: Friction scorecard and decision rule
docs.text:
For each agent integration, retain a side-by-side worksheet with:

  • Decisions the author must understand before and after, identifying which were eliminated, merely relocated, or still essential provider semantics.
  • Repeated validation, monetary conversion, evidence construction and failure branches removed, including the shared implementation and its configuration in the code-size comparison. Shorter call sites alone are insufficient.
  • Concepts and indirections added, including how an author locates a bad token field, distinguishes unknown spend from free work, and diagnoses partial work, session attribution or process cleanup. Include Pi's language/process bridge.
  • Edits needed to change tool permissions, session policy, an artifact check, billing reporter or agent runtime. Keep these as concrete edit traces, not ratings unsupported by examples.

All accounting/failure gates must pass before a benefit counts. Favor a maintained recipe or example-local function if it removes recurring error-prone work across the three agents while leaving required decisions visible. Report a narrower benefit as narrower support, not universal agent compatibility. Reject a candidate that simply renames constructors, moves the same branches behind hooks, requires provider special cases, or complicates the notebook's unknown-spend path.

Disposition What closes the study Retain existing wrappers Evidence shows insufficient shared work or greater complexity; record the best recipe and why a helper was rejected. Recipe or example-local reuse Name its owner and bounded supported cases; describe the concrete migration and verification needed without promising a public import. Defer helper adoption Complete the bounded comparison, then name the additional evidence or SDK capability needed to revisit adoption. An unfinished required baseline is not a completed study. Public helper warranted Open a separate implementation issue specifying the proposed contract, placement, compatibility/release gate and migration tests. #337 alone authorizes no public helper shipment.

Keep findings with the existing #269 accounting review and #330 coordination. Fixture results establish accounting behavior; author edit traces support an engineering usability judgment. Neither substitutes for live-provider evidence or the independent newcomer sessions.

docs.title: Difficulty and completion boundary
docs.text:
This is a medium-to-high difficulty study, larger than comparing two text APIs. Most effort is in lifecycle, tool/stream failures, cumulative attribution and SDK telemetry gaps. Start with Codex and Claude, then require Pi's different process/session boundary before the final decision. Reuse existing fixtures; estimate any public helper and its maintenance separately after the evidence.

The original full-study gate required all three agent integrations to have before/after evidence and every applicable matrix case resolved. The accepted lightweight scope instead closes #337 with three reporting comparisons, focused failure/accounting checks, runnable recipes, and a retain-local-reuse decision. The decision record identifies the evidence and deferred runtime cases; it does not claim that the full matrix passed. No model-quality improvement, easier onboarding, or live reproducibility is claimed from these deterministic checks.

docs.title: Future search policies
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This is a retained design record. The programming model and project status identify shipped behavior; proposals below do not extend those contracts.

Meta-Evolve currently ships deterministic Greedy, BestOfN, BestOfK, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch presets. The ideas below are roadmap direction, not importable names or accepted semantics.

docs.title: Pareto and quality-diversity archives
docs.text: Multi-objective archives would need explicit dominance, constraint, tie, capacity, and admission decisions. Quality-diversity additionally needs a versioned behavior descriptor and deterministic binning. Archive membership must be replayable from recorded evaluations rather than recomputed under a new definition.

docs.title: Islands and migration
docs.text: An island design must distinguish artifact identity from island membership. Migration is a recorded search decision, not artifact copying or Git history. Timing, topology, migrant selection, admission, and random streams must remain deterministic at the logical level.

docs.title: Other bandits and tree allocation
docs.text:
TreeSearch ships fixed progressive widening, best-descendant backup, and deterministic UCT descent; it does not imply the broader allocation ideas below are importable names or accepted semantics. Any other allocation policy may use uncertainty, cost, or upper-confidence estimates only when their observations, update rule, and random choices are explicit. Retry delivery must never become an extra logical trial.

No future policy may erase failed outcomes, widen budgets, inspect hidden evaluation, or require a coordinator special case.

docs.title: User-owned SDK boundary
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. This retained decision record preceded the deterministic M8 flagship and opt-in driver; the M8.6 validation gate subsequently closed on retained authorized captures. The callable boundary itself and the hard-removal migration it gates are shipped. The programming model owns the current contract; the removal history is retained below. This page adds no agent runtime, provider adapter, or M8 domain type.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Meta-Evolve accepts an ordinary callable or an object with a structural propose() method. The user invokes and configures any model SDK inside that boundary. The SDK owns authentication, sessions, tools, permissions, structured decoding, and provider telemetry. Meta-Evolve owns candidate validation, independent evaluation, budgets, durable records, lineage, experience auditing, and promotion authority.

There is no provider ABC and no generic agent runtime. A direct candidate return remains the smallest path; ProposalResult is the typed path when a wrapper has usage, evidence, metadata, or derivation to report.

SDK wrapper output Meta-Evolve destination Decoded artifact value ProposalResult.candidate Total tokens and elapsed time Usage.tokens and Usage.wall_seconds Charged monetary cost Usage.spend_micros Raw response, estimated cost, model, granular tokens, provider telemetry EvidenceDraft or metadata Audited observations actually used derived_from

Trial and evaluation counts are coordinator-owned. A wrapper that reports either count is normalized to typed InvalidOutput, and completion overwrites both counts independently as defense in depth. Granular token categories remain provider evidence. Charged monetary cost was promoted to the shared Usage.spend_micros field by issue #143; estimates still remain evidence with their price basis.

Ordinary SDK exceptions become ProposerFailure. Framework failures that state a fact about durable state, accounting, or run capability escape unchanged: EventStreamConflict, DurableCorruption, InvalidSearchHistory, ExperienceStoreUnavailable, ExecutionAccountingUnknown, and CapabilityError.

docs.title: Audited agent pull
docs.text:
A user wrapper may register an SDK custom tool whose handler delegates to the scoped context.experience reader. The handler returns only the authorized observation and retains the observation references that the SDK actually used; the wrapper returns those references in ProposalResult.derived_from.

SDK tool call
  -> user handler
  -> context.experience.search/open/ancestors/siblings/compare
  -> audited, bounded observation
  -> SDK
  -> ProposalResult(derived_from=used_references)

The callback can be in-process or forwarded through a user-owned RPC bridge. Meta-Evolve adds no process or tool protocol for that bridge. Access denial, exhaustion, audit-store failure, and unknown accounting keep their existing semantics because the handler delegates to the scoped reader rather than copying or bypassing it. SDKs without custom-tool support may receive pushed context.bundle content, but that is not agent-directed pull.

docs.title: M8 flagship execution
docs.text:
The examples/research/harness_evolution/ demonstration accepts a user-owned proposer callable. CI uses a deterministic fixture-backed SDK client. The opt-in maintainer driver invokes a real SDK through the same callable boundary, without a package dependency or a shipped provider example.

The first authorized live M8 run must be captured once, sanitized, and retained honestly. The capture must preserve ties, regressions, typed failures, and unsuccessful attempts rather than rewriting them into a success narrative. It must identify the wrapper declaration and the controls that affect behavior.

The wrapper may propose only manifest-declared planner and context-policy changes. External evaluators run fresh held-out episodes under equal effective budgets. Candidate code cannot change evaluation, grants, hidden inputs, budgets, promotion rules, or mutation authority. best() selects a recorded result; promotion remains a separate governed action.

The provider removal was gated on this boundary and the audited experience bridge being complete, and shipped in the same change as both. The M8 types are implemented elsewhere; this decision still adds no provider ABC, agent runtime, or core SDK adapter.

docs.title: Removal and evidence policy
docs.text:
The removed imports and extras were:

from meta_evolve.claude import Claude
from meta_evolve.codex import Codex
meta-evolve[claude]
meta-evolve[codex]

Install and authenticate your chosen SDK in your application, then call it from an ordinary proposer or evaluator. Use your model SDK is the complete current notebook guide.

The pre-1.0 migration is a hard removal: first-party Claude and Codex imports, extras, adapters, fixtures, and live tests receive no compatibility shim. Historical experiments and milestone records remain accessible and are labeled superseded. Their original claims are evidence of what was tested at the time; they are not current package instructions or shipped fixtures.

The repository boundary applies to current src/, examples, and shipped guides. Provider names remain legitimate in historical experiments, milestone records, design decisions, and migration material.

docs.title: Worker processes: stabilization plan for #353
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 21, 2026 for #353, the third M11.3 slice. Planning assumption: finish the existing implementation and prepare it for another review. This record does not authorize merging or change runtime behavior.

The roadmap owns scope and acceptance; the programming model owns the public API; architecture owns invariants; and the implementation plan owns technical boundaries. The M11 design supplies the subordinate admission, lease, and reattachment rules.

docs.title: Inspected baseline
docs.text:
Item Observation and consequence PR #353 Draft; changes requested on 170e4a26b8401b6d6560d9b18b459cac60595791. Three inline findings remain the initial repair scope. Base PR #341 Open draft targeting main, head f48e04f6ffd231f9d9b6db9ce2f77cf7a68de7b1; changes requested and merge conflicts reported. Settle its review and integration before landing #353. Stack ancestry The inspected #353 head includes that #341 head and current main 9077011776a9b3cf6d2df57e798288e58a9c486c. Its description's promise to inherit the base fixes is older than the source. Verify the fixes instead of implementing them twice. Parent #202 Closed, while its body still leaves #341/#353 unfinished. Reconcile tracking with integrated acceptance; issue state alone is not proof of completion. Evidence The review reports three isolated reproductions on this exact head. The PR's earlier full-suite claim is historical; this planning pass ran no runtime tests. Hosted checks were still in progress when inspected.

The local main working tree contains unrelated in-progress documentation and example changes. Implementation should use an isolated checkout of the PR, preserving that work. Recheck branch heads and reviews when execution starts.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Preserve the existing spawned-worker and listening-host entry points, one lease per worker process, shared settlement path, and explicit reconnect behavior. The required change is three bounded fixes with regression coverage, followed by integration and documentation verification.

Keep admission before spawned-run epoch rollover; authenticate before sending run details or lease secrets; build executors from the recorded start; retain at-most-once acceptance and store-authoritative Duplicate/Stale answers. Reconnect must preserve acknowledgment recovery without promising recovery of an old live call across epochs. Failures retain their existing domain meaning.

Worker respawning, capacity above one, durable worker administration, a general load-testing framework, paid-budget admission, distributed experience, TLS implementation, and the full M11.6 example remain outside this repair.

docs.title: 1. Refuse malformed authentication envelopes locally
docs.text:
Finding: malformed MAC aborts the dispatcher.

In distributed/handshake_envelope.py, validate the MAC's type, ASCII encoding, and SHA-256 hexadecimal format before comparison. Translate malformed peer input into the existing handshake refusal, without quoting supplied payloads. Keep MAC verification before body decoding. Do not broadly catch application exceptions and relabel them as authentication failures.

Acceptance:

  • Drive the real host handshake with the reported non-ASCII MAC, plus wrong type, wrong length, and non-hex variants; each returns Refused.
  • A pending-admission/dispatcher regression proves another valid worker can still join and perform work after a malformed peer is refused.
  • Existing wrong-key, nonce, frame-bound, and verify-before-parse tests pass.

docs.title: 2. Preserve results through write-side connection loss
docs.text:
Finding: worker exits before retaining its result.

In distributed/worker.py, retain Completed and its lease before attempting transmission. If encoding or frame validation converts it to CompletionFailed, clear the pending result before transmitting that replacement. Only completed results participate in the existing acknowledgment/reconnect path.

Route socket OSErrors through Lost(holding, run_id) for reads, initial pulls, initial resends, outcome writes, and subsequent pulls. Keep this boundary specific to transport operations: protocol violations, encoding failures, and component interrupts must retain their existing classifications. In distributed/worker_process.py, ensure the connected socket closes when serve() returns or raises. Reuse the existing reconnect loop; retain its backoff on connect/admission failures without adding a new retry policy.

Acceptance:

  • With a socketpair and explicit synchronization, close the host while the evaluator is running, then release the evaluator. The worker returns Lost carrying the exact result and lease; the evaluator was called once.
  • Fail the first pull, a resend repeatedly, and a pull after acknowledgment. Pending state is preserved only while a completed result remains unanswered.
  • A failed fallback write after an unsendable result retains no completed result. Attempt failures, completion failures, and interrupts remain distinct.
  • Exercise the real external-worker reconnect path: preserve incarnation, advertise the held lease, resend before pulling, recover the answer, and exit on Goodbye. A spawned worker still exits when its dispatcher is lost.

Adjacent follow-up: probe reconnecting to a different run. Source inspection shows the handshake filters advertised leases by issuing run, while the caller passes its pending result to serve() unconditionally. Reproduce and classify that gap separately before extending this three-finding repair; an old result must never acquire a new run identity.

docs.title: 3. Reserve worker identity at final admission
docs.text:
Finding: overlapping handshakes admit duplicate identities.

Keep ownership in the existing HostAdmission, HostHandshake, and listener handoff. After manifest and held-lease validation, recheck identity and reserve ownership before sending Admitted. The reservation must be visible before another handshake advances in the same PendingHandshakes.advance() batch. Rechecking a live map populated only after the batch does not satisfy this.

Preserve same-incarnation reconnects, the live-owner rules, and minted IDs' single-admission rule. Any temporary reservation belongs to its connection; refusal, disconnect, timeout, host shutdown, or failed handoff releases only that reservation. A successful handoff transfers ownership to the existing live-endpoint tracking. Add no durable registry or coordinator special case.

Acceptance:

  • Stage two real handshakes with the same worker ID and different incarnations: both Hellos pass before either manifests message completes. Admit exactly one.
  • Repeat through the production pending-handshake batch. The refusal must not release or steal the first worker's healthy lease.
  • Retain legitimate same-incarnation reattachment and stale-owner replacement; refuse overlapping reuse of a minted worker ID.
  • Abort between reservation and handoff; later legitimate admission succeeds, and cleanup cannot erase another connection's ownership.

docs.title: 4. Verify the integrated slice and align its claims
docs.text:
Make each defect a separate reviewable fix with a regression that fails on the inspected head. Then restack as needed after #341 is settled and rerun against the resulting commit. Verify #341's settling-lease protection, completion-failure subclass round trip, and guarded exception formatting remain intact.

Use existing handshake, worker-answer, reattachment, host, process, cleanup, CLI-signal, cohort, liveness, and broker suites. Preserve real-process proofs: simultaneous execution in distinct processes; worker termination during proposal and evaluation; dispatcher termination and resume; duplicate acknowledgment after restart; deterministic cohort barriers; exact accepted count accounting. Use explicit synchronization instead of timing assumptions for new regressions.

After focused checks pass, run the integrated deterministic suite, Ruff, mypy, source compilation, canonical CI examples, strict docs build, and experiment 17's no-provider dry run. Record exact source commits, commands, outcomes, and any skipped process capabilities. A dry run proves its declared contract, not live provider quality or complete paid-spend accounting.

Align programming-model.md, architecture.md, milestones.md, implementation-plan.md, project/status.md, the CLI guide, and the M11 design. At the inspected head, the API describes opt-in processes while architecture still says execution is serial and the status page implies distributed mode alone starts processes. State the actual distinction: default inline execution versus explicitly selected process backends. Keep the broader M11 gate open until its remaining slices pass. Do not repeat signatures outside their owner.

The completion gate is three demonstrated repairs, preserved base behavior, passing checks on the integrated commit, consistent availability claims, and a fresh review of that exact revision. Updating GitHub tracking, requesting reviews, or merging is a separate authorized action.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Start with one complete improvement experiment, then choose the task you need. Each guide supplies its own setup, definitions, code, and expected observations. Use a fresh Python 3.12+ notebook; no checkout or earlier lesson is required. The SDK guide makes billable model requests and needs an API key; the other guides use handwritten examples with Python grading.

Run each guide's setup before its task cells. Some guides place definitions under Required setup for a fresh notebook; expand and run those cells even though they start closed. Each page explains the change, shows its output, and offers an exercise and adaptation advice. Saving examples mark where to restart.

Unsure where to go next? Start with Define what better means to adapt the scoring to your own task. Choose Use your model SDK to replace handwritten revisions with model requests, or Save and reopen a run to keep your results. For an explanation of how the pieces fit, read the concepts overview. For help choosing a tool and identifying what you need to write, read When to use Meta-Evolve.

Upgrading an existing experiment? Follow Migrate to 0.2 for the five API changes and supported-history guidance.

docs.title: Apply, compose, or evolve a method
docs.text:
• Use a method: choose an implemented workflow and adapt its artifact and evaluation to your task.
  • Compose a method: choose proposal, search, and experience components and define their actual stage schedule.
  • Evolve a method: make a declared part of the procedure the candidate and evaluate the outcomes it produces.

For a small example of the inner and outer roles, follow policy evolution. The meta-evolution concept explains the boundary.

docs.title: Build an experiment
docs.text: You want to… Guide Score revisions and decide what counts as better Define what better means Compare revising the best version with exploring another branch Choose what to try next Use failed checks to guide the next revision Give the proposer feedback Call your own model from a proposer or evaluator Use your model SDK

docs.title: Control and understand a run
docs.text: You want to… Guide Bound work and stop at a target score Set limits and stopping conditions Read selected versions, regressions, and failed attempts Inspect results and failures Keep history and read it after restarting Save and reopen a run

docs.title: Advanced composition
docs.text:
• Improve an agent's harness: change one instruction and measure the answers it produces in a complete notebook. Continue to the governed repair study for independent final checks and typed configuration export.
  • Improve a search policy: measure policy settings through bounded inner experiments and inspect their saved histories.
  • Add an artifact domain: define how your own value type is validated, encoded, improved, and reopened from saved history.

For complete applications and their setup requirements, choose an example. For detailed behavior, use the API reference, run and search reference, or evaluation and budget reference.

docs.title: Local run browser
docs.text: Inspect saved runs, view artifacts and their differences, and compare results in an optional local browser. It reads Storage without changing history or executing experiment components.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text:
Install the optional dependencies, then point the command at an existing durable store:

uv sync --extra browser
meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --port 8000

Runs using a custom artifact codec can reconstruct it through the ordinary experiment-module convention:

meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --module experiments.my_run

The optional module is loaded only after browser dependencies are available. Only its experiment().registry enters the browser reader; proposers, evaluators, policies, sessions, and execution are never invoked. Without the module or codec, the run is an ordinary actionable codec-unavailable 422 state rather than corruption.

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The host is fixed to loopback and the server uses one worker. The browser has no write, run, resume, cancellation, promotion, or deletion controls. It has no authentication. Loopback binding limits its intended scope; it is not a claim that the application is safe to proxy or publish remotely.

The pages are complete server-rendered HTML. Search, detail, comparison, lineage tables, and navigation work with JavaScript disabled. A small same-origin script only polls committed stream versions and reloads after facts change. A complete run page with a stable version carries no polling attributes at all; only the catalog and incomplete or unstable pages poll.

docs.title: What appears
docs.text:
The catalog is ordered lexicographically by content-derived run ID; it makes no chronological claim. Cards show task identity, lifecycle, rankability, policy, the primary objective and available score, artifact kind, and usage. Search filters those recorded fields.

A detail page follows the recorded story: overview, declaration, lineage, trials, evidence and failures, recorded artifact history, and decision timeline. The SVG lineage diagram has a semantic table containing the same parent edges. The history table preserves recorded occurrence order without calling it time, keeps occurrence identity separate from content digest, and offers one explicit diff choice for every parent.

Artifact pages show identity, parents, bounded specialized presentation, exact canonical attachment, and every available parent diff. Text, source trees, skill sets, canonical Python values, harnesses, and policy artifacts have fixed views. A custom kind receives deterministic canonical-payload text and an explicit no-specialized-view notice. All content originates in the frozen payload; decoded ArtifactView.value is never read, stringified, or passed to templates. Evidence URIs remain inert text, never links.

Direct-parent diffs support Text, SourceTree, and SkillSet. They identify added, removed, modified, and unchanged files and label added, removed, and unchanged lines textually as well as visually. A file whose content is identical on both sides reports its unchanged status without lines and consumes none of the shared diff budgets. Foreign-run views, non-parent edges, and incompatible families are refused with 422. Multi-parent occurrences never acquire an arbitrary default parent.

Bounds apply in this order: lexicographic path sorting; first 100 entries; 64 KiB UTF-8 per retained preview document; 256 KiB aggregate preview input; 64 KiB per diff side and 256 KiB aggregate diff input before invoking the diff algorithm; then 4,000 output lines. Final partial and omitted states remain visible. Canonical downloads are not truncated.

Comparison always receives an explicit ordered pair and invokes the public Run.compare() contract. It reports score, usage, winner or tie, and the three declaration flags. Incompatible or unrankable pairs remain visible as typed refusals; the browser does not pre-filter candidates or turn failure into a score.

docs.title: Replay and caches
docs.text:
One dedicated thread creates Storage.read_only(), performs every listing, version query, inspection, and comparison, and closes the handle. Route handlers and Starlette's general threadpool never receive it. This preserves SQLite connection affinity while concurrent HTTP requests queue safely.

The first catalog request performs one validated replay for every discovered run. It keeps one lightweight card per run, stamped with the exact run_version it observed and replaced when a newer version appears, plus a 32-entry LRU of full inspections. Comparisons use a separate 32-entry LRU keyed by the ordered IDs and both exact versions. Eviction discards only derived views, never durable facts. Inspections retain each frozen payload beside the decoded object, without eagerly storing an additional serialized byte copy; payload-heavy runs therefore consume proportionally more memory inside the bounded LRU. A comparison cache miss pays the public API's full multi-replay cost.

Before replay, the reader polls exact versions. Exact hits avoid replay; completed cached runs are not polled again. Catalog polling still calls Storage.runs() to discover additions and checks versions of incomplete runs.

Inspection reads a version before and after replay. A mismatch is retried once. If commits continue, the valid inspection snapshot is served without a version label or cache entry. Comparison is stricter: both versions must remain stable across the complete public comparison. A second mismatch returns retryable 503 rather than presenting a mixed observation.

docs.title: Failures and safety
docs.text:
Unknown or concurrently missing runs and artifact occurrences return 404. Comparison and diff refusals and codec capability gaps return escaped 422 pages. Transient store failures and unstable comparisons return 503. Corruption and unexpected defects return a safe 500 without a traceback or durable detail. A corrupt or codec-unavailable run becomes an isolated catalog error card so healthy runs remain reachable.

Store-open and schema failures happen before the server binds and use the ordinary CLI domain-failure path. Responses include a restrictive content security policy, nosniff, no-referrer, and frame-denial headers. These defenses do not expand the browser beyond its local, unauthenticated scope.

Raw artifact responses use application/json, nosniff, and Content-Disposition: attachment with a digest-derived filename. The bytes are the current digest encoding, canonical-payload-v1, not a native artifact export and not an unconditional promise for every future durable format.

docs.title: Manual visual review checklist
docs.text:
For changes to browser templates or CSS, review the catalog, run, artifact, diff, refusal, truncation, and codec-unavailable fixtures with JavaScript disabled at both fixed viewports:

  • desktop: 1440 × 900;
  • mobile: 390 × 844.

Record completion in the PR. Check heading order, landmarks, skip link, visible keyboard focus, native controls, textual status labels, contained wide tables and preformatted text, single-column mobile layout, and reduced-motion mode. The browser does not provide screenshot automation.

docs.title: Migrate execution budget overrides
docs.text:
For the complete upgrade path, start with Migrate to 0.2.

Execution budgets now inherit omitted task ceilings. This is the #315 source change in the Author API revision, whose working release target is 0.2.0. The package version and hosted documentation release remain separate integration work; this page describes the implemented behavior. The programming model owns the current contract.

docs.title: Tighten only what changes
docs.text:
Given a task with Budget(trials=4, evaluations=5), an execution can now pass Budget(evaluations=2). The resolved allowance is four trials and two evaluations. Previously this partial override raised ValueError because its missing trial dimension was treated as removing the task ceiling.

Execution override Effective allowance or outcome None or Budget() Four trials, five evaluations Budget(evaluations=2) Four trials, two evaluations Budget(trials=None, evaluations=2) Four trials, two evaluations Budget(trials=0) Zero trials, five evaluations; seed-only work Budget(evaluations=0) Seed admission raises BudgetUnavailable Budget(trials=3, evaluations=6) Explicit widening raises ValueError

The same rule applies to tokens, billed micro-USD, and reported elapsed time. Where the task has no ceiling, an override may introduce one. Explicit None cannot remove a task ceiling; changing that authority requires a different task declaration. A standalone Budget still uses None to mean no ceiling.

Existing valid full overrides and dataclasses.replace(task.budget, ...) calls remain valid. Empty or sparse overrides that formerly failed can now execute work; update tests or callers that relied on that rejection. Invalid explicit widening still fails before proposer/evaluator calls or committed run facts. Storage construction and seed encoding retain their earlier validation order.

The complete example below applies this restriction. Inspect result.inspect().declaration.effective_budget to see the resolved limits; the sparse request itself remains unchanged.

import meta_evolve as meta


def increment(parent):
    return parent + 1


task = meta.Task(evaluator=float, budget=meta.Budget(trials=4, evaluations=5))
experiment = meta.Experiment(task=task, seed=0, proposer=increment,
                             search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=None))
result = meta.run(experiment, budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=2))

print(result.inspect().declaration.effective_budget)
print("Proposals:", result.usage().trials)
print("Evaluations:", result.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# Budget(evaluations=2, trials=4, tokens=None, spend_micros=None, wall_seconds=None)
# Proposals: 1
# Evaluations: 2

Run it with python examples/learn/budget_overrides.py, or use the reference case.

docs.title: Existing runs and accounting
docs.text:
There is no store migration. Runs record the effective budget, and resume uses that recorded value. A partial override and its fully specified equivalent produce identical facts and identities; they cannot create separate runs in the same store. A previously rejected override has no run history to migrate.

Search presets retain their own defaults and stopping rules. Seed evaluations, failed-work costs, unknown spend, and post-call resource enforcement retain their existing accounting semantics; see evaluation and budgets.

Historical resume still requires matching registered components and source manifests. The #315 resolver alone preserved built-in manifests on its merge baseline. The integrated callback and reference changes intentionally alter source verification; old histories remain readable, but continuation requires matching source. The verification record identifies the isolated #315 baselines, and callback migration explains the subsequent boundary.

docs.title: Migrate proposer context
docs.text:
For the complete upgrade path, start with Migrate to 0.2.

Status: Shipped. This is the source implementation of #316, part of the coordinated pre-1.0 revision. The package remains version 0.1.0 until that release is published. The programming model owns the callback contract; this guide explains the transition.

docs.title: Make framework inputs explicit
docs.text:
Previously, the plain-callback adapter preferred two positional inputs whenever they bound. That made def propose(parent, factor=2) receive a context object as factor, and rejected the explicit keyword-context spelling.

Before:

def propose(parent, context):
    return parent + context.rng.choice((-1, 1))

After:

def propose(parent, *, context):
    return parent + context.rng.choice((-1, 1))

If context was unused, remove that argument entirely. Update direct Python callers too: propose(parent, context=context). No change is needed to the ordinary parent-only path.

Existing spelling New behavior and action f(parent) Receives the parent only. f(parent, *, context=None) Receives actual framework context, regardless of the default. f(parent, factor=2) factor stays 2; it is ordinary configuration. f(parent, context=None) Preparation raises TypeError; make context keyword-only or remove it. f(parent, ctx=None) or _context=None Receives parent only; the alias retains its default. Review manually if it previously used inferred context. f(parent, *args, **kwargs) Receives no extra arguments. Explicitly add keyword-only context when needed. f(parent, required) Preparation raises TypeError; bind configuration in a wrapper or partial. Uninspectable plain callable Wrap it in an inspectable callback or implement the explicit structural port.

The parent can be positional-only or itself named context. An additional positional parameter named context is reserved and rejected. Parameter annotations and aliases do not opt in. Invalid signatures fail before seed evaluation, validation hooks, or committed run facts. Callback exceptions remain typed failures under the existing failure rules; the framework never retries a body to discover how to call it.

Local bound methods, callable objects, decorated callables, and partials use their effective inspect.signature. If a partial still exposes keyword-only context, the framework supplies it even if the partial prefilled that keyword. Use a wrapper that hides it when you intend a fixed argument:

def configured(parent):
    return existing_function(parent, fixed_settings)

This is a signature pattern, not a complete runnable example. Durable registered wrappers must be plain module-level functions with declared source dependencies; local convenience does not make a closure or partial durably verifiable.

docs.title: Keep explicit adapter interfaces
docs.text:
These contracts are unchanged:

  • A structural object's .propose(parent, context) method receives two positional inputs, with the existing .propose(parent) convenience.
  • ProposerRunner.execute(parents, context) remains the explicit runner port.
  • PatchProposer owns its (tree, context) callback interface.

Normal execution chooses a declared runner first, then a structural .propose method, then a plain callable. Invalid runner metadata does not fall back to another route. A callable's valid configured .component preserves identity while retaining the plain-callback argument rule.

An explicit CallableProposer(obj) or local ComponentRef retaining a callable chooses its callable side, even if it also has .propose. Passing obj.propose as a plain callback therefore differs from passing obj as a structural object. Review the entry route before editing an adapter's method signatures.

docs.title: Registered runs and history
docs.text:
The registry now automatically includes framework binding, invocation, and registered adapter wiring in every registered proposer manifest. Continue to declare your own source dependencies. Evaluator manifests gain no invocation dependency from this change.

All pre-cutover registered proposer manifests differ, including parent-only callbacks whose behavior did not change. An unchanged function is insufficient evidence: an optional or variadic function could receive different arguments. Resume raises CapabilityError before runner construction, preflight, or new work. Policy factory setup may still execute while resolving manifests.

Use Storage.read_only(...) and Run(...) to inspect supported old histories. Continue unfinished runs with their matching package and component environment. Do not edit recorded manifests, backfill hashes, or treat a fresh run as a continuation. When intentionally changing component behavior, version the component and start a new run. Run IDs do not incorporate source manifests; an identical ID does not prove implementation equivalence, and an existing run cannot be overwritten.

The verification record covers captured old runs, same-runtime recovery, and migrated examples. Final package and hosted-site publication belong to #318/#319.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: Run two improvement experiments, compare their results, and reopen their recorded history from the terminal. The walkthrough uses deterministic local examples and requires no model credentials.

docs.title: Run and compare
docs.text:
From a checkout, install the package with uv sync --locked. This offline example needs no credentials. Its artifact is a number; the proposer changes that number, the evaluator measures distance from a fixed target, and only search changes between the two declarations.

The first factory fixes the target at 12, starts at 0, and permits eight successor attempts. Greedy keeps the best measured parent; BestOfN always proposes from the seed. Feedback is omitted and named randomness uses seed 35.

Complete experiment modules

experiment.py:

"""A CLI experiment module: one ``experiment()`` factory and nothing else.

This is the whole convention. The module defines its components and returns a
typed ``meta.Experiment``; importing it starts no run, opens no storage,
and prints nothing. The command line supplies the infrastructure it owns:

    meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/experiment.py --storage ./store

``examples/learn/number_search/main.py`` is the same search written as a script.
A script is not an experiment module: importing one runs it. That difference
is exactly what this file exists to show.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import meta_evolve as meta


TARGET = 12
MOVES = (-2, 1, 5)


def propose(parent: object, *, context: object) -> object:
    """Take one random declared move away from the parent."""

    return parent + context.rng.choice(MOVES)


def score(candidate: object) -> float:
    """Higher is better; reaching the target scores the maximum 0."""

    return -abs(candidate - TARGET)


def experiment() -> meta.Experiment:
    """The factory the command line calls. Plain callables, so this module
    runs under the default ``--mode local``. See ``resumable.py`` for the
    registered-component shape ``--mode durable-local`` requires."""

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=score,
            objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=0),),
            budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=9, trials=8),
        ),
        seed=0,
        proposer=propose,
        search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=8),
        random_seed=35,
    )

best_of_n.py (keep beside experiment.py):

"""The comparison variant: the same experiment under a different policy.

``meta.Run.compare`` refuses two runs that do not declare the same task,
initial artifact, budget, and proposer, so a comparable variant has to reuse
them rather than restate them. This module therefore uses
``dataclasses.replace()`` on ``experiment.py``'s declaration to change exactly
one field — the search policy:

    meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/best_of_n.py --storage ./store
    meta-evolve compare <greedy-run-id> <best-of-n-run-id> --storage ./store

The sibling import works because the command line appends an experiment
module's own directory to ``sys.path``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace

import meta_evolve as meta
from experiment import experiment as greedy_experiment


def experiment() -> meta.Experiment:
    """Greedy hill climbing swapped for independent best-of-N attempts."""

    return replace(greedy_experiment(), search=meta.BestOfN(max_trials=8))

Start with two runs in one durable store:

uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/experiment.py --storage ./store
# Selected output: score 0; evaluations 6; lineage 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 7 -> 12
uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/best_of_n.py --storage ./store
# Selected output: score -7; evaluations 9; lineage 0 -> 5
uv run meta-evolve list --storage ./store

run imports one side-effect-free experiment() factory returning meta.Experiment and prints the new run's summary. list returns the stored run IDs. Use those IDs next:

uv run meta-evolve inspect <greedy-run-id> --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve compare <greedy-run-id> <best-of-n-run-id> --storage ./store

inspect reports lifecycle, rankability, declarations, attempts, evidence, and decisions, including typed failures. compare first requires a successful measurement from each run, then checks that the task, initial artifact, budget, and proposer declarations are compatible. It reports both runs and their winner or exact tie. The BestOfN module reuses the first module's declarations so only search behavior changes.

For an optional server-rendered view over the same read-only public queries:

uv sync --extra browser
uv run meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --port 8000

The local browser guide documents its fixed loopback scope, exact-version caches, rendering exclusions, and absence of authentication.

The canonical examples/operations/command_line/ walkthrough pins this entire transcript through subprocess tests.

docs.title: Reports and exit status
docs.text:
run and resume print the summary to stdout, including lifecycle, rankability, stop reason, and recorded costs. An absent score or winning lineage prints none. A measured zero is still a score; retaining the seed still ranks. Wall-clock measurements remain omitted from stable text.

Outcome stdout stderr Exit Rankable run or resume Summary Empty 0 Unrankable run or resume Summary with absent score and retained costs Empty 1 inspect of any valid history, including pending seed evaluation Detailed report Empty 0 Compatible rankable compare Comparison Empty 0 Missing/corrupt run, refused comparison, or inadmissible execution Empty Typed error 1 Usage or experiment-module error Empty Error 2

Unexpected defects keep their traceback. The migration guide explains the changed failure report; commands and factory declarations keep their existing inputs.

docs.title: Resume is a declared capability
docs.text:
Create a reconstructable run, then resume it:

uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py \
    --storage ./store --mode durable-local
uv run meta-evolve resume <run-id> \
    --module examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py --storage ./store
Complete resumable module 
"""The experiment-module shape ``--mode durable-local`` requires.

Same convention as ``experiment.py`` — one ``experiment()`` factory, no
import-time side effects — but the factory registers its components and
returns the registry, so the run is recorded resumable:

    meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py \\
        --storage ./store --mode durable-local
    meta-evolve resume <run-id> \\
        --module examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py --storage ./store

Two modules rather than one because the library requires different component
shapes for the two modes: local mode drives live callables, durable-local
drives registered, source-digestible module-level functions so a resumed run
can verify it is replaying the code that was recorded. The command line does
not choose between them and does not check either — it passes ``--mode``
through and lets ``meta.run`` enforce its own contract.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import meta_evolve as meta


TARGET = 6


def climb(parent: object, *, context: object) -> object:
    """Deterministic and retry-safe: the same parent always yields the same
    child, so replaying it during recovery reproduces the identical candidate.
    ``context`` is unused because this climb has no randomness in it."""

    return parent + 1


def score(candidate: object) -> float:
    """Higher is better; the target itself is the ceiling."""

    return -abs(float(candidate) - TARGET)


def experiment() -> meta.Experiment:
    """Register the components and hand back the typed declaration plus the
    registry ``meta.run`` and ``meta.resume`` both resolve against."""

    registry = meta.Registry()
    proposer = registry.register_proposer(
        "example:climb", "1", climb, deterministic=True, retry_safe=True
    )
    evaluator = registry.register_evaluator(
        "example:score",
        "1",
        score,
        deterministic=True,
        retry_safe=True,
        configuration={"target": TARGET},
    )
    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(evaluator=evaluator, budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=8)),
        seed=0,
        proposer=proposer,
        search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=8),
        registry=registry,
    )

The module registers source-digestible proposer and evaluator functions. On resume, its factory rebuilds the registry and the library verifies the recorded component identities. A local run may use durable storage and remains listable and inspectable, but it is not resumable.

The command line adds no capability rules. It passes --mode to meta.run and lets meta.resume accept or refuse the recorded run. The programming model owns the five report-verb mappings, factory convention, modes, and exit codes.

For a real interrupted-process workflow, continue with the examples/operations/durable_operations/ walkthrough.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text: Run the two commands above, then inspect the IDs printed by list. Compare their parent choices as well as their best scores. These commands report recorded results; a different search policy does not guarantee a higher score. Try resuming the local run: expect CapabilityError. The registered durable-local example can resume; repeating resume after completion adds no work.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text:
The CLI is a thin translation over the public run and durability contracts.

meta-evolve run MODULE --storage STORAGE [--mode local|durable-local|distributed]
meta-evolve list --storage STORAGE
meta-evolve inspect RUN_ID --storage STORAGE
meta-evolve resume RUN_ID --module MODULE --storage STORAGE
meta-evolve compare LEFT_RUN_ID RIGHT_RUN_ID --storage STORAGE
meta-evolve ui --storage STORAGE [--port PORT] [--module MODULE]

Each verb makes one public call:

Verb Public call Result run meta.run(...) Run ID and summary list storage.runs() Reachable content-derived run IDs inspect run.inspect() Overview, declaration, trials, decisions resume meta.resume(...) Verified missing durable-local or distributed work compare run.compare(other) Compatible comparison and winner

The module's side-effect-free experiment() factory returns Experiment. Dictionary factories remain functional under the pre-1.0 release policy, but each load emits DeprecationWarning naming the module and factory and asking for meta.Experiment(...). Unknown keys and the execution-owned storage, mode, and call-level budget remain usage errors; those overlays belong to the command line and run().

Failures in the RunError hierarchy become concise CLI errors without tracebacks. Unknown arguments, invalid factories, missing runs, capability gaps, and incompatible comparisons fail closed.

The CLI does not add an artifact history, registry, evaluator, or promotion authority of its own. Git may be ingress or egress for source, but durable Meta-Evolve artifacts and transitions remain the experiment record. Inspection includes failures, artifact occurrence identity and digest, evidence, decision rationale, and named randomness. Measured wall-clock values remain omitted so equivalent deterministic runs produce byte-identical output.

docs.title: Read-only local browser
docs.text:
ui is the one long-running lifecycle exception to the five deterministic report verbs. Install it explicitly and serve an existing durable store:

uv sync --extra browser
meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --port 8000

The host is fixed to 127.0.0.1, the worker count is fixed to one, and valid ports are 1..65535. There is no host or worker override. The command owns no domain query or HTML logic: it conditionally imports and delegates to the browser server. Uvicorn retains its operational logging. Missing browser dependencies give installation guidance and exit 2; store-open and schema failures remain typed CLI domain failures and exit 1 before a socket binds.

The browser is read-only, local, and unauthenticated. Loopback scope is not a remote-safety or authentication claim. See the browser guide for the replay, cache, polling, and rendering boundaries.

For a run using a custom artifact codec, ui --module MODULE loads the same side-effect-free experiment() convention and passes only its registry to the read-only browser. Browser dependencies are imported first. No proposer, evaluator, policy, session, execution, or mutation surface is invoked. Missing custom codecs remain actionable 422 capability states.

docs.title: Durability
docs.text:
For a complete notebook walkthrough, start with Save and reopen a run.

Storage composes artifact and event storage. In-memory storage is isolated to the process. Durable storage uses a verified filesystem artifact store plus an append-only SQLite event stream.

import meta_evolve as meta

storage = meta.Storage.durable(".meta-evolve/example")

docs.title: Store
docs.text: Pass durable storage to meta.run() to preserve committed artifacts, evidence, decisions, lineage, usage, and failures. mode="durable-local" additionally requires registered reconstructible components and their verified manifests. Validation happens before the first event is written.

docs.title: Reopen
docs.text:
open_run opens existing history for a with block:

with meta.open_run(".meta-evolve/example") as reopened:
    snapshot = reopened.summary()

print(snapshot)

Pass the directory used for Storage.durable(). Without run_id=, it opens the only recorded run. An empty store raises RunNotFound; several runs raise RunSelectionRequired with a run_ids tuple of available IDs. Choose explicitly with meta.open_run(path, run_id=saved_id), using a RunId or its saved string. IDs are listed lexically; their order does not establish which run is newest. An explicit missing ID never substitutes another run.

Calling open_run() creates a context manager. Entry validates the arguments, opens storage, and validates the selected history before yielding Run, including incomplete and unsuccessful runs. Storage closes on success or error. Capture summaries, inspections, usage, and selected values inside the block; those results remain usable afterward. A subsequent query on the live Run still requires open storage and surfaces a store error after close.

Reopen performs no proposal or evaluation and never resumes work. Local callable and SDK histories can be durable and inspectable even when their live components cannot be rebuilt. For custom artifacts, supply registry= with reconstructed codecs to decode values. Without the required codec, entry and usage() still work, while a decoded query such as best() raises CapabilityError naming the missing codec. Supplied codecs are trusted Python extensions invoked by decoded queries, not by opening the run.

For explicit storage ownership, keep using Run directly:

with meta.Storage.read_only(".meta-evolve/example") as storage:
    version = storage.run_version(run_id)
    inspection = meta.Run(run_id, storage).inspect()

is_durable and is_read_only answer different questions. The first says committed facts live on durable media; the second says this handle cannot commit. Storage.durable(...) reports True, False, while Storage.read_only(...) reports True, True. Artifact, blob, event, and unit-of-work writes all raise CapabilityError. Passing the handle to run(), improve(), or resume() is rejected before a codec, registry component, proposer, evaluator, provider, or subprocess runs.

run_version(run_id) is the maximum committed event sequence. It returns 0 for a well-formed id with no events and uses a new deferred transaction on each call, so a long-lived reader observes successive atomic commits from a WAL writer. It is deliberately a cheap polling query, not a full integrity check. An open_run() block also permits fresh reads: it selects the identity once, but does not freeze subsequent queries to the entry-time history. Run(run_id, storage).inspect() performs authoritative loading and still raises RunNotFound when that run is required but absent.

The optional local run browser owns one long-lived read-only handle on one dedicated thread. It calls runs() to discover additions, polls exact versions before replay, and never polls a cached completed run again. Its bounded caches are disposable observations; append-only storage and validated replay remain authoritative.

Read-only open requires an existing current store. It uses SQLite mode=ro plus query_only, and never creates a directory, changes journal settings, executes DDL, stamps a schema, or migrates. For an older or unstamped store, close readers and reopen it once with writable Storage.durable(...), then use Storage.read_only(...) again. Future schemas raise SchemaVersionRejected, malformed current schemas raise DurableCorruption, and missing or inaccessible database/filesystem/WAL state raises DurableStoreError with the underlying cause.

Read-only means no changes to committed history and no framework writes or migration. SQLite can create or maintain -wal and -shm sidecars even through a read-only connection; see its WAL documentation. The reader preserves live WAL visibility and does not use SQLite's immutable mode. It never creates a missing store directory or repairs an incomplete one.

docs.title: Resume
docs.text:
resume verifies manifests, declarations, store integrity, and the recovery frontier before doing missing work. It retains the same run ID and never re-executes a committed operation. A non-resumable local history raises CapabilityError.

Registered proposer verification includes the framework's invocation source. The explicit keyword-context cutover changes those manifests even for unchanged parent-only callbacks. Older histories remain readable; continuation requires their matching implementation. See the callback migration guide.

Use Session.resume to pace that same recovery:

with meta.Session.resume(run_id, storage=storage, registry=registry) as session:
    for decision in session:
        observe(decision)
result = session.run

A distributed run resumes through the same call and then drive(), because it is scheduled rather than stepped — iterating its decisions raises. resume() makes that choice for you; hold the session yourself and you make it:

with meta.Session.resume(run_id, storage=storage, registry=registry) as session:
    session.drive()

Preparation validates and classifies the committed frontier but does not finish pending work. The first step() either completes the already committed trial or evaluation, or records and completes one new decision. Resuming an already stopped run iterates zero times; an explicit terminal step() returns the existing stop view without changing events or artifacts.

docs.title: Complete registered-resume example
docs.text:
Run this as a Python file with meta_evolve installed. It compares saving a local run with reconstructing registered components for resume. The temporary stores are for this demonstration only; retain a persistent directory for real work. Omitting session.step() leaves both revisions for resume to perform.

resume_checklist.py · complete example
"""Registered resume demonstration, moved from the beginner persistence lesson."""

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
import meta_evolve as meta


def add_item(items):
    return (*items, ("outline", "draft")[len(items)])


def score(items):
    return len(items)


def declaration():
    registry = meta.Registry()
    proposer = registry.register_proposer(
        "checklist:add", "1", add_item, deterministic=True, retry_safe=True,
    )
    evaluator = registry.register_evaluator(
        "checklist:score", "1", score, deterministic=True, retry_safe=True,
    )
    return meta.Experiment(
        seed=(), proposer=proposer, task=meta.Task(evaluator=evaluator),
        search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=2), registry=registry,
    )


with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    root = Path(directory)
    with meta.Storage.durable(root / "saved") as storage:
        result = meta.improve(seed=(), proposer=add_item, evaluator=score,
                              trials=2, storage=storage)
        saved_id = result.id
    with meta.Storage.read_only(root / "saved") as storage:
        reopened = meta.Run(saved_id, storage)
        print("Reopened:", reopened.best().value)

    with meta.Storage.durable(root / "continued") as storage:
        with meta.Session.start(declaration(), storage=storage, mode="durable-local") as session:
            session.step()  # Finish one revision, leaving one to perform.
            run_id = session.run.id
            print("Before resume:", session.run.usage().trials)
    with meta.Storage.durable(root / "continued") as storage:
        resumed = meta.resume(run_id, storage=storage, registry=declaration().registry)
        print("After resume:", resumed.usage().trials)
        print("Selected:", resumed.best().value)
# Output:
# Reopened: ('outline', 'draft')
# Before resume: 1
# After resume: 2
# Selected: ('outline', 'draft')

docs.title: Compare
docs.text: Reopened completed runs use the same comparison contract as live results. Declaration mismatches raise RunsNotComparable before ranking.

docs.title: Replay and reproducibility
docs.text:
Replay is a pure fold over immutable transitions and artifacts. It reconstructs logical decisions, projections, context selection, access audits, and usage without calling external systems. Named random streams reproduce deterministic local choices. Provider output is not promised to regenerate byte-for-byte; the durable guarantee is the exact committed transcript and declarations.

Usage records retain unknown billed spend as explicit null; omitted spend still means the historical default of zero. Existing zero and integer records keep their canonical bytes. Readers predating nullable spend cannot read these new unknown values. Inspection and replay reuse cost evidence without rerunning user callbacks; recovery may repeat external work whose outcome never committed.

Corrupt bytes, unknown schemas, gaps, mismatched IDs, and incomplete atomic batches fail explicitly rather than falling back to a partial interpretation.

docs.title: Open a store from an earlier version
docs.text:
The current durable store schema adds the work and lease tables that distributed mode uses. No recorded event byte changes, and the upgrade is one-way: an earlier release refuses a migrated store as a future schema. A store an older release migrated from v1 has its events table rebuilt with the same rows, and one holding an event with no digest is refused as corrupt. A store written by an earlier release must be opened once with writable Storage.durable(...), which migrates it; until then Storage.read_only(...) and the run browser refuse it with SchemaVersionRejected.

A durable-local run that uses BestOfN and was recorded by an earlier release does not resume. Its RunStarted manifest records a digest of the policy's module source. The current release changes that module, and resume compares the digest exactly, so it refuses with CapabilityError. Finish such runs before upgrading. The run id and the stream's other bytes are unchanged.

Exact source matching also includes docstrings and other text in a hashed module. The reference refresh changes the source digests of Greedy, BestOfN, AncestorsOnly, and BestSibling, even though their execution logic is unchanged. Runs with those earlier manifests remain inspectable, but resume requires matching component source. Complete unfinished work with its matching package before upgrading; do not bypass the manifest check.

An artifact read that meets damaged durable state -- including a committed artifact the store no longer has -- now raises DurableCorruption with the original fault on local and durable-local runs. Earlier releases stopped the same run with InvalidDecision wrapping the cause, so code that catches InvalidDecision for this case no longer sees it.

docs.title: Evaluation and budgets
docs.text:
For a complete notebook walkthrough, start with Define what better means or Set limits and stopping conditions. This reference covers detailed evaluation, accounting, and failure behavior.

A Task declares the evaluator, artifact representation, objectives, and optional budget ceiling. The evaluator—not the candidate—owns what better means.

import meta_evolve as meta

task = meta.Task(
    evaluator=lambda text: {"quality": len(set(text.split()))},
    objectives=(meta.Maximize("quality"),),
    budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=6, trials=5),
)

Maximize and Minimize identify ordered objectives. A run-level budget may narrow the task ceiling but cannot widen it. Omitted or None dimensions inherit task limits, so Budget(evaluations=2) retains the task's other ceilings. Budget() preserves them all; zero is a real limit. An explicitly wider finite value raises ValueError before work starts. See the budget override example and migration notes.

Task.environment is an immutable evaluator-owned declaration. Its empty default preserves ordinary runs; when supplied it contributes to task and run identity, so changing a nested episode environment invalidates its RunId.

docs.title: Exact accounting
docs.text:
Seed evaluation consumes one evaluation and no successor trial. Each attempted successor consumes one trial; a valid evaluated successor consumes one evaluation. Token, monetary-spend, and wall usage come from the component action that actually performed the work. Rich callbacks return Resources; the engine adds its own counts to durable Usage, aggregated in the run summary.

Run.summary().usage, Run.usage(), and inspection report the same committed costs even when nothing ranks or seed evaluation is pending. Prefer run.usage() when accumulating resources across nested runs: it reads the costs directly without constructing the rest of a report. Unknown spend remains unknown, and failed work remains charged.

Rolling a nested run's usage into an outer one also means dropping its counts, since trials and evaluations belong to the run that minted them. Project the inner resources and add the outer evaluator's own work exactly once:

total = own_resources + inner.usage().resources

run.inspect().overview.task_usage reports the same figure and remains available, but it builds a whole aggregate to reach one field; prefer the accessor.

Search checks the effective budget before starting more work — for counts, tokens, and wall time. Monetary spend is knowable only once a call returns, so it is enforced post-hoc instead. Exhaustion is a recorded stop reason. Components never grant themselves additional work.

docs.title: Money
docs.text:
Resources.spend_micros, recorded in Usage, reports charged monetary spend in integer micro-USD (1 unit = one millionth of a US dollar). A wrapper reports the amount its provider actually billed; estimates keep their status and price basis in evidence instead of appearing as exact bills. Core never infers money from tokens and never converts currencies.

Report spend_micros=None when billed spend is unavailable. A successful result can still carry its measured tokens and score. Aggregating any unknown amount produces an unknown total; known individual charges remain in history. The default 0 means known free work, including ordinary local callables. Neither missing telemetry nor the choice of subscription or API-key login establishes a bill or its absence. SDK-calculated prices remain estimates.

With no monetary ceiling, token and trial limits continue to work normally. With a run, task, or trial monetary ceiling, an unknown charge makes that ceiling unverifiable. The completed result is retained, further work is refused, and built-in policies report accounting_unavailable when this causes their stop. An unknown proposal's candidate is saved but its evaluation is skipped. Budget.allows returns false for unknown spend under a monetary ceiling; remaining_after rejects that subtraction. Inspection shows spend=unknown.

Budget(spend_micros=...) sets a ceiling with post-hoc enforcement: spend is known only after a call returns, so the first action that crosses the ceiling is billed, recorded as a typed ResourceExhausted failure, and halts the run. There is no hard cap — reservation-based preflight is future work. A ceiling of 0 means free work only: unpaid components run normally, and the first paid action fails typed and stops the run.

A ceiling can also sit on an individual trial. When a trial spends past its own spend_micros, the run halts — including for subsequent free work, since a breached ceiling is a property of the run's history, not of the next action. A trial with no ceiling anywhere, neither aggregate nor per-trial, stays unbounded, exactly as trials=None means unlimited trials.

spend_micros is wrapper-self-reported and not independently verified by the framework: a wrapper that omits or understates its provider's charge understates trusted accounting, and the round-up conversion convention is advisory. The framework guarantees exact aggregation of known reports and propagates unknown totals. User-owned cost reporters can price tokens or look up a receipt. Estimates remain evidence and do not satisfy or consume a billed-spend budget; use token/trial bounds when a bill is unavailable.

Enforcement bounds the framework's paid actions, not a provider's billing. Under durable execution a crash between a paid call and its commit leaves the charge real but unrecorded, and recovery re-executes the call; bounding that requires provider-side idempotency, which is future work.

docs.title: Evidence and uncertainty
docs.text: An evaluation can return scalar or objective-keyed metrics, uncertainty, immutable evidence, and action usage. Evidence records what was observed; it is not a candidate-controlled score. External evaluators also record environment and bounded process evidence where available.

docs.title: Typed failures
docs.text:
Invalid candidate shape, proposer failure, evaluator failure, timeout, resource exhaustion, policy violation, and infrastructure failure retain their distinct types and details. A trial with no valid evaluation is non-rankable. It never becomes zero, negative infinity, or a fabricated metric.

Run-level capability and durability errors use the shipped error hierarchy, including CapabilityError, BudgetUnavailable, and InvalidDecision.

docs.title: Authority
docs.text: The candidate may propose artifact content and declare causal observations. The task/evaluator owns hidden data, environment, metrics, and failure translation; the coordinator owns effective budgets and commitment; governance owns permissions and promotion.

docs.title: Define what better means
docs.text:
A parser that gets "30s" right can still get "2h" wrong. Before improving it, you need a way to measure its answers and decide which revision to keep. An evaluator computes measurements; an objective says which measurement to improve and whether higher or lower is better. The measurements come from the evaluator, independently of a proposer's claims; see evaluation authority.

You want to… Use Grade answers An evaluator returning a score Track several measurements A dictionary of metrics Choose what determines the winner Maximize or Minimize

The revisions are handwritten. Python executes and grades them; no model, SDK, or credentials are needed.

To run this page: expand the required setup and run its cells from top to bottom, then run the examples below in order. Every definition is here; no other page needs to be executed. Rerunning the cells repeats the same results.

Required setup for a fresh notebook

Install. Use Python 3.12 or newer. Download the package ZIP into your notebook's working folder. For hosted notebooks, upload it through the file browser; %pwd shows the working folder. The ZIP is also included in offline docs builds. Install once; restart the kernel if asked before continuing.

%pip install ./meta-evolve.zip

Starting source. SEED reads a duration's number but ignores its unit. CONTRACT tells the proposer what the parser should do.

import meta_evolve as meta

CONTRACT = """Implement parse_seconds(text) for whole-number durations.
Inputs contain a number followed by s, m, or h, such as '30s' or '2h'.
Return the duration in seconds as an integer. Return only Python source.
"""

SEED = '''def parse_seconds(text):
    return int(text[:-1])
'''

Revisions. MINUTES adds minutes support; COMPLETE adds hours as well.
