Only after selection do we evaluate the empty baseline and selected library on held-out questions, in fresh sessions with the same executor configuration. These scores never enter the proposal context or choose another winner. Inspect per-question answers, tool use and failures in the two held-out JSON files. Six questions demonstrate the mechanism; they do not establish benchmark improvement or reproduce EvoSkill's Pareto selection.

In [ ]: Copied! 
def save_report(run, baseline, selected, data):
    usage = run.usage().resources + baseline.usage + selected.usage
    observations = [item for trial in run.trials() for item in trial.evidence]
    observations += list(baseline.evidence) + list(selected.evidence)
    costs = [item.data["result"].get("total_cost_usd") for item in observations
             if item.kind == "evoskill.agent"]
    report = {
        "run_id": str(run.id), "controls": data.identity,
        "development": [{"step": trial.logical_step, "state": trial.state,
                         "metrics": dict(trial.metrics)} for trial in run.trials()],
        "held_out_baseline": dict(baseline.metrics), "held_out_selected": dict(selected.metrics),
        "held_out_failures": [asdict(result.failure) if result.failure else None
                              for result in (baseline, selected)],
        "resources": asdict(usage),
        "estimated_cost_usd": sum(costs) if costs and all(cost is not None for cost in costs) else None,
        "selected_digest": run.best().digest,
    }
    (data.root / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    for label, result in (("baseline", baseline), ("selected", selected)):
        (data.root / f"held-out-{label}.json").write_text(
            json.dumps([dict(item.data) for item in result.evidence], default=dict, indent=2) + "\n")
    return report
def save_report(run, baseline, selected, data): usage = run.usage().resources + baseline.usage + selected.usage observations = [item for trial in run.trials() for item in trial.evidence] observations += list(baseline.evidence) + list(selected.evidence) costs = [item.data["result"].get("total_cost_usd") for item in observations if item.kind == "evoskill.agent"] report = { "run_id": str(run.id), "controls": data.identity, "development": [{"step": trial.logical_step, "state": trial.state, "metrics": dict(trial.metrics)} for trial in run.trials()], "held_out_baseline": dict(baseline.metrics), "held_out_selected": dict(selected.metrics), "held_out_failures": [asdict(result.failure) if result.failure else None for result in (baseline, selected)], "resources": asdict(usage), "estimated_cost_usd": sum(costs) if costs and all(cost is not None for cost in costs) else None, "selected_digest": run.best().digest, } (data.root / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n") for label, result in (("baseline", baseline), ("selected", selected)): (data.root / f"held-out-{label}.json").write_text( json.dumps([dict(item.data) for item in result.evidence], default=dict, indent=2) + "\n") return report In [ ]: held-out Copied! 
if run.summary().primary_score is None:
    print("No rankable candidate; held-out checks skipped. Inspect failures above.")
else:
    winner = run.best().value
    materialize(winner, RUN_DIR / "selected")
    baseline = await evaluate(seed, data, "held_out")
    selected = await evaluate(winner, data, "held_out")
    report = save_report(run, baseline, selected, data)
    print("Held-out baseline:", report["held_out_baseline"])
    print("Held-out selected:", report["held_out_selected"])
    print("Tokens and elapsed work:", report["resources"])
    print("Estimated USD (not billed spend):", report["estimated_cost_usd"])
    print("Saved report:", RUN_DIR / "report.json")

Inspect failures above.") else: winner = run.best().value materialize(winner, RUN_DIR / "selected") baseline = await evaluate(seed, data, "held_out") selected = await evaluate(winner, data, "held_out") report = save_report(run, baseline, selected, data) print("Held-out baseline:", report["held_out_baseline"]) print("Held-out selected:", report["held_out_selected"]) print("Tokens and elapsed work:", report["resources"]) print("Estimated USD (not billed spend):", report["estimated_cost_usd"]) print("Saved report:", RUN_DIR / "report.json")

run.usage() includes executor, proposer and generator work during search; report["resources"] also includes both final checks. The SDK's total_cost_usd is retained as an estimate, while billed spend_micros remains unknown. If a dispatched call loses trustworthy token accounting, the run stops without an automatic retry and points to its receipt. Earlier receipts remain on disk.

Search history in this notebook is in memory; files and JSON receipts are saved under RUN_DIR. The equivalent CLI additionally writes durable Meta-Evolve history. Re-running live cells creates more provider calls. To begin a new experiment, restart the kernel and Run All. Model aliases and provider behavior can change; replaying saved artifacts is distinct from reproducing live answers.

Try a different development/held-out split only as a new experiment. Keep the original final check untouched when interpreting its result.

docs.title: EvoSkill: improve a native Claude skill folder¶
docs.text:
Status: Experimental/live-only. This notebook calls real Claude agents: Haiku executes, Sonnet proposes a skill, and Sonnet invokes a skill-builder to write it. Meta-Evolve scores and selects the resulting folder versions.

Run cells in order in a fresh Python 3.12+ kernel on macOS or Linux. No repository checkout, local dataset, or companion download is needed. A matching Meta-Evolve source package is embedded because the public release predates the feedback API used here. Two bundled Python helpers handle transport, files and grading; the agent declarations and evolution loop are visible below. Setup downloads about 4.6 MB of pinned public data.

Authenticate locally with claude auth login, or configure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the kernel environment before starting. Do not write a credential in a cell. Allow up to 19 SDK sessions (15 Haiku, 4 Sonnet). Per-call SDK estimate limits sum to $10.50 at the maximum run length; they can overshoot and are not a billed-spend cap. No score or improvement is promised. Saved outputs are intentionally empty.

Walkthrough · Example source · Official EvoSkill sample

"""Compare two workers and take the less loaded one.

def choose(cluster, size):

    second = cluster.pick()
    if second == first:
        second = (first + 1) % cluster.size
    return first if cluster.load(first) <= cluster.load(second) else second

docs.title: Improve a scheduler¶
docs.text:
Jobs of different sizes arrive at a group of workers. Where should each job go? Our starting program takes turns: worker 0, worker 1, and so on. That is cheap, but when large jobs arrive at regular intervals, the same workers get overloaded.

Try a small change: look at two workers and choose the less busy one. Here is the proposed function. load() asks for a worker's current load; each request counts as one probe:

def choose(cluster, size):
    first = cluster.pick()
    second = cluster.pick()
    if second == first:
        second = (first + 1) % cluster.size
    return first if cluster.load(first) <= cluster.load(second) else second

The fixed simulator actually runs this Python code. Its development workloads produce this comparison:

Program Load imbalance ↓ Probes per job ↓ Quality ↑ Starting round-robin 0.2071 0 0.7929 Inspect every worker 0.0381 7 0.8219 Inspect two workers 0.0464 2 0.9136

Two probes buy much better balance than the starting program. Inspecting every worker balances jobs a little better, but takes seven probes per job here. The two-worker program offers the better tradeoff under the fixed score: quality = max(0, 1 - imbalance - 0.02 * probes_per_job). Imbalance is zero for an even distribution and one when a single worker gets everything. These measurements describe this simulator, not hardware speed.

The proposer tries handwritten revisions, including mistakes. The measured scores come from running those programs, not a lookup table or a live model.

docs.title: Run it in Jupyter¶
docs.text:
This is an optional next step after your first improvement. Use a fresh Jupyter kernel with Python 3.12 or newer, on macOS with usable sandbox-exec, or Linux with usable Landlock ABI 3+. The runtime must allow confined child processes. The third cell checks that they really work before the study starts. Hosted notebooks, including Colab, are not verified here.

Save the notebook in an ordinary project folder, outside your Python installation and, on Linux, outside /tmp, /var/tmp, /usr, and other system directories. Its downloaded code needs a protected location; temporary execution workspaces are created separately. No model key, GPU, or repository checkout is needed.

Run these four cells in order. Installation and download use the same published documentation build. An archived copy also works: put its meta-evolve.zip and systems-example.zip beside the notebook; the cells find them automatically. Source installation may download build tools. If you have already imported Meta-Evolve or the example, restart the kernel before starting again.

docs.text: This probe starts a confined Python process and checks that it cannot read the downloaded workload file. It is setup, outside the study's measured work. If it fails, the following cells leave the study stopped and explain the remedy.

docs.text: The study tests the starting program and eight revisions, then selects a program on a separate workload and checks it once more on a final workload. This cell shows the development comparison from its recorded measurements.

docs.text: Development feedback helps propose changes. Selection tests eligible programs on a different, published workload after proposing ends. docs.text: What if the comparison used >= instead of <=, choosing the busier worker? Change the selected source and run it through the same fixed development evaluator. This optional check runs separately from the recorded study above.

docs.title: Capability-lesson newcomer walkthrough
docs.text:
This is the revised task handoff from #281 to #275. Use #277's exploratory findings and reusable regression checklist to record each scenario's cells or commands, expected and actual result, environment, tested commit, assistance needed, outcome, and linked defects.

This page is a facilitator's handoff. Give participants the prompts below one at a time, without the expected results in the observer checklist. The walkthrough checks whether someone can find, explain, and adapt an experiment, as well as execute its cells.

docs.title: Run a session
docs.text:
1. Start with a reader who can use Python functions and notebooks but has not used Meta-Evolve. Record their relevant experience and any prior exposure to these docs. Use an empty notebook and working folder, without a checkout.
  2. Record the documentation source/build revision, package version, installation URL or archive hash, and imported package location, then open the homepage. Let the reader choose links; do not supply a direct guide link unless help is needed.
  3. Ask them to think aloud. Record the first point where they hesitate, their interpretation, and the page, heading, or cell involved. Ask neutral questions such as “What do you expect this to do?” Avoid explaining the API for them.
  4. If they ask for help, record their attempted approach before helping. Mark that task as assisted even if it succeeds afterward. Stop at a blocker when continuing would only repeat the same problem.
  5. Use a new notebook for the chosen task guide. Observe whether the reader finds and executes required setup, including any folded cells, without prompting. Record time to find the guide, first successful task result, and independent adaptation; separate installation delays from reading and coding time. Complete further guides in later sessions; preserve code and outputs for every attempted task.
  6. For their own evaluator, measure time to a completed bounded experiment and an inspected result. The seed may remain selected; a positive score delta is not required. Observe feedback problems before asking the diagnostic questions below, and distinguish an unprompted discovery from a prompted task.

docs.title: Participant prompts
docs.text:
Give only the current prompt to the participant. The first four form the common entrance walkthrough; the last prompt checks transfer after a task guide.

  1. Find and run: “Starting on the homepage, find a first example you can run without a model account. Set it up in your notebook and run it.”
  2. Explain: “Point to what changes, what proposes a change, and what decides whether it is better. Explain what happened between the printed scores.”
  3. Predict and adapt: “Allow just one revision. Before running, predict the number of evaluations and which inputs will still fail. Run it and use the selected parser on a new input.”
  4. Find a task: “You want to keep the result and inspect it after restarting Python. Find the relevant instructions, then try them in a fresh notebook.”
  5. Transfer: “For a small problem of your own, implement a starting value, revision function, and measurement function. Use the documentation to run a bounded experiment and use its selected result. Explain which rules stay outside the revision.”

For another guide, state the desired outcome in ordinary words before giving its title: for example, “Use failed test cases to guide the next revision.” Then use that page's change-and-predict exercise. Record the prediction before execution, the explanation afterward, and any help required.

After the exercise, ask a question relevant to that guide without naming the answer's location: “Why didn't my new metric change the winner?”, “Why did search revise a weaker version?”, “Why isn't feedback reaching my proposer?”, “Why wasn't the last attempt selected?”, or “Do I need the original functions to reopen?” Record their route, answer, and any assistance. Returning readers should also find the relevant operation with shared setup closed.

After the parser walkthrough, ask: “Find how to configure the same example explicitly. Explain what Task, Experiment, Session, and Run each need and do. Show where you would change scoring, generate different revisions, choose a different parent, or pause execution. Predict what has run immediately after constructing an experiment, starting a session, and taking its first step.” Then ask the reader to execute that example and inspect its selected parser. Record their navigation, prediction, explanation, and assistance separately.

docs.title: Tasks for an unfamiliar reader
docs.text:
For the tool-choice page, add these unaided retrieval tasks:

  • Starting at the homepage, decide whether Meta-Evolve fits a small idea of your own. Identify the starting value, revision function, and independent grader; find a guide you could adapt. Explain one reason to choose a bundled optimizer.
  • Find whether closing Python preserves a default run, whether saving makes it resumable, and whether a spending ceiling prevents every overrun.
  • Find what evidence would support a live improvement claim. Separate the handwritten parser's measured scores from model performance.

Record time to find each answer, navigation or search route, interpretation, and assistance. These tasks extend #275/#277; agent checks are not human results.

Observer checklist: use these outcomes to interpret the session, without reading them to the participant. Reproducing output alone does not demonstrate that the reader understands why it occurred.

Task Starting page Expected observable result Install and run the homepage cells Homepage Seed 33%, selected 100%; one proposal, two evaluations; 4m gives 240 seconds Continue to the full parser walkthrough Start here Scores are 33%, 67%, 100%; no SDK request or lesson-file import Identify the artifact, proposer, evaluator, search, feedback, and limits Parser and routing prompt Reader separates simulated responses from actual independent grading Explain declarations, execution, and inspection Core objects Reader distinguishes the evaluator from Task, reuses the task in Experiment, predicts no execution at declaration, one seed evaluation at local start, and two evaluations after the first parser step; Run queries add no work Inspect results in a fresh notebook Inspection One history keeps the 67% revision after a 33% regression and a failure with no score; four attempts give a two-version winning lineage Define measurements and choose an objective in a fresh notebook Evaluation Reader reports hours separately and predicts how changing the objective changes the winner Change one search declaration Search Reader traces Greedy to 5 and TreeSearch to 10 using six proposals and seven evaluations each; five proposals select 5 for both with six evaluations; the constructed score table is not a benchmark Inspect and retain a search history Search Reader identifies the seed retained on a tie and the failed evaluation with no score, then reopens the saved tree history without callbacks or new evaluations Supply and use feedback in a fresh notebook Feedback Failed checks drive the handwritten fixes to 100%; disabling feedback leaves 33% with the same three evaluations Explain early stopping and exhaustion in a fresh notebook Limits Reader distinguishes attempt limits, score satisfaction, and evaluation ceilings; predicts zero proposals when the seed suffices Save, restart, reopen, and export from a fresh notebook Persistence Fresh kernel reads 33%, 67%, 100% and three evaluations without lesson functions; exported source parses 4m and 2h; an earlier run survives a new save Connect an SDK in a fresh notebook Use your model SDK Reader runs required accounting setup, locates the separate request cell, explains the three-request maximum, and inspects labels and usage without requests; identifies where to replace the SDK and finds the explanation of unknown spend Improve and reuse an agent configuration in a fresh notebook Harness Reader explains 2/3 → 3/3 through the polite password answer, reuses the selected instruction, and predicts that zero proposals retain 2/3; distinguishes this simulation from the linked governed repair study Improve and reuse a search policy in a fresh notebook Policy Reader explains scores 6, 7, 8 through inner traces, distinguishes three outer evaluations from twenty inner evaluations, and predicts why a candidate limit of 99 cannot raise the fixed inner budget Add a value type in a fresh notebook Artifact domain Reader separates valid recipe structure from checklist scores, sees a plain tuple rejected without evaluation, and reopens saved values with a rebuilt registry; reopening does not grant resume capability Transfer the component map Discovery Reader separates an optimized skill artifact from proposer feedback

Reading declarations and running deterministic checks do not require paid calls. Live execution and retained transcripts remain subject to #270's protocol and #271's validation. If live evidence is unavailable, record it as unavailable; test fixtures are not model transcripts and do not fulfill a live validation gate.

docs.title: Evidence and acceptance
docs.text:
Record the exact source commit, OS, Python version, installation method, commands, expected/actual output, and every point requiring maintainer help. Run from an empty working directory so accidental repository imports cannot hide missing definitions. For the live guides, also rehearse extracted downloads. Retain history directories and their original run IDs for fresh-process inspection.

Existing ownership and acceptance remain with #275: three independent newcomers, participants coordinated by Salah, defects reproduced and fixes verified by the QA owner, and Salah's acceptance of the findings. Completing automated example tests does not complete those walkthroughs or the integrated release gate.

docs.title: Practical-journey handoff for #336
docs.text:
The integration verification supplies the exact engineering setup, regression commands, outcomes, and remaining SDK glue. Use the short SDK notebook for three-request wiring and the complete routing journey for development feedback, known failed-work usage, detached snapshots, final separation, and saved history. These live guides remain Experimental/live-only; the engineering rehearsals substitute providers or HTTP responses and authorize no paid calls.

For #275, first give the existing unaided transfer prompt. Start its timer when the task is presented, and stop when the participant has completed a bounded run with their own evaluator and inspected its outcome. Record setup time separately. A seed that remains best counts; a positive score delta is not the success gate. Observe whether feedback is discovered, enabled, and consumed without prompting before asking the following diagnostic prompts, one at a time:

  • “This run has no useful feedback for its revision function. Find why, and explain whether the feedback was disabled or no matching report was selected.”
  • “This run says context was truncated. Determine whether its selected checks are still usable, and explain what the bounds control.”
  • “Compare this failed attempt with a completed wrong answer. Explain the measurements, work counts, and retained usage.”
  • “Keep the result, restart Python, and inspect it without the original functions. Explain which values remain usable after the store closes.”

Facilitator setup uses the credential-free feedback and persistence guides first. context=None exercises deliberate feedback off; RecentAncestors(max_records=0) exercises enabled but empty selection; a large record allowance with max_chars=0 clips only text and leaves structured evidence intact. The optional parser proposer returns its parent without checks. Contrast this with the routing proposer's required-feedback diagnostic using the offline tests below. Do not send a diagnostic SDK request during an unauthorised paid session.

Bhasker and Salah agree session stopping rules and any timing/comparison thresholds before the first scored session. Retain each participant's outcome and assistance, including abandonment. Keep baseline and after conditions explicit; a familiarized retest is not a fresh participant. Three observations do not estimate prevalence. The existing three-user unaided completion and Salah acceptance gates still apply.

For #277, extend the maintained checklist with these scenarios. Each row needs commands/cells, expected and actual results, environment and tested source/package identity, assistance, retained output/history, and linked defects or limitations.

Scenario Expected result and regression owner Improvement, tie, regression, failed seed Correct selected parent, complete or explicitly partial report; test_llm_prompt_lesson.py / test_llm_prompt_feedback.py Disabled, missing, stale, truncated feedback No silent fallback or lookup outside selection; intact report survives text clipping; test_llm_prompt_feedback.py / test_sdk_notebook_feedback.py Missing metric, malformed output, failed rewrite No fabricated score; failed rewrite skips evaluation; known usage remains; routing feedback and SDK failure tests Unknown accounting and final failure Receipts survive; final failure triggers no new search; test_llm_prompt_persistence.py Restart, wrong ID, multiple runs, snapshot lifetime Explicit selection, typed diagnostics, detached display, no SDK calls; routing persistence/reopening tests and #335's contract checks Installed ZIP and copied notebook No checkout imports; real driver or SDK transport, imperfect seed and failure exercised; test_lesson_downloads.py / SDK notebook tests

This is maintained handoff material for #275/#277, not completed independent sessions or a release recommendation. #269 retains independent SDK/accounting review, #274 docs coordination, and #270/#271 live evidence. Participant coordination remains with Salah; no outreach follows from this packet.

docs.title: Regression handoff for #295
docs.text:
Use #277's existing checklist and owner to track these scenarios against the final implementation commit:

  • Copy every core guide from an empty notebook, including folded setup, and compare the visible cells with the rendered output. Also run the whole sequence.
  • Follow each chooser and historical section link; check that task links reach visible instructions and setup links reach the expandable setup control.
  • Rerun and change the objective, search allowance, feedback policy, or seed as instructed. Retain scores, work counts, failures, and winning lineage.
  • Save, exit Python, and reopen using only the reopening cell. Export and use the source. Save with one proposal, then reopen both folders separately; their original run IDs and histories must remain intact.
  • Exercise expansion, copying setup and task cells, keyboard focus, search, and narrow layouts. Record friction separately from execution failures.

Automated checks and agent observations belong in preflight evidence below; independent participant records remain with #275. This handoff supplies updated scenarios and does not close either QA issue.

docs.title: Agent preflight of the rewritten guides
docs.text:
This review identifies documentation defects and checks executable examples. It is not an independent newcomer session; no participant results are recorded here. The three human walkthroughs remain pending.

Reviewed on September 15, 2026, against the uncommitted documentation working tree based on 97ab240, using macOS arm64 and Python 3.12.13.

Finding Change The homepage's Guides card opened the detailed run reference Route it to the task guide index The first lesson used library terminology before explaining the loop Lead with starting values, revision functions, measurement, and history Start here introduced improve(), trials(), and best().value after their first use Explain the calls before their cells Start here printed the selected source without showing how to use it Load the selected parser and call it on 4m A downloaded ZIP may be on the reader's computer rather than in a hosted notebook Explain upload and the notebook's working folder at installation Guide discovery assumed readers knew terms such as candidate and parent Use concrete task descriptions and offer routes for scoring, SDK calls, and saving Three policy-guide calls used the compatibility spelling of run Use Experiment consistently, with execution storage and budget on run

docs.title: Documentation audit and editorial conventions
docs.text: Lead with improving solutions and the methods that produce them. The use, compose, and evolve journeys connect that idea to implementations and research directions. The complete duration parser teaches the common API; task guides and examples provide next steps. Keep instructions beside code and evidence.

docs.title: Ownership and navigation
docs.text:
Section Reader's question Content owner Start here How do I run and understand an improvement loop? One complete parser walkthrough Methods Which method can I use, compose, or evolve? The existing research catalog and its canonical walkthroughs Guides How do I perform this task? Build an experiment; control and understand a run; advanced composition Examples How does this apply to my problem? One catalog of maintained runnable examples Concepts Why does it work this way? Explanations under the architecture contract Reference What does this API accept and return? Source signatures, detailed contracts, tools, and programming model Development (secondary) What exists, and how do I contribute? Contribution routes, canonical contracts, status, roadmap, design and evidence indexes

The homepage remains accessible through the logo. Group guides by reader task and link related pages by purpose. Keep historical URLs or explicit redirects when moving their navigation entries. Source repair, integer demonstrations, and evidence notebooks are additional examples rather than competing introductions.

Development links to indexes and canonical overviews; detailed designs and historical notebooks remain accessible at their existing URLs. Methods are primary destinations and Examples groups applications by purpose. The homepage and Start here link installation, comparison, SDK integration, limits, and persistence.

Open the programming model with the mental model and callable API. Ordinary guides and concepts explain current behavior without milestone chronology; project status and evidence records retain development history. Preserve decision-relevant limitations beside the behavior they qualify. Navigation checks protect reader routes and historical destinations, not an exact submenu layout or leaf count.

The homepage and README share the opening “Improve solutions. Improve the methods that produce them.” Keep use/compose/evolve links visible and code reachable without reading theory. Both entrances contain a complete parser experiment: installation, every definition, one handwritten revision, independent evaluation, and verified output. Explain the roles and how to use the selected code. The homepage includes canonical source; literal README cells and shared setup are checked against their owners. Test both outside the checkout with the installed package. The full tutorial adds revisions using the same parser and checks. Keep scores beside their handwritten-fixture explanation. Route readers to methods, tutorials, SDK integration, tasks, concepts, and reference before project history. Distinguish notebook, checkout, and credentialed entry points.

The programming model owns the shipped API; architecture owns domain semantics; milestones owns scope and acceptance gates; and the implementation plan owns technical staging. Design records remain subordinate, including records whose decisions later shipped.

docs.title: Comparisons and positioning
docs.text: The comparison explains method reuse, structured artifacts, composition, and evaluating improvement procedures through concrete examples. It answers fit, authoring responsibilities, and next steps. Support external capability claims with versioned primary sources, check dates, and the material actually inspected. Name uncertainty instead of inferring absence; preserve unrelated source dates. Compare complete setup and responsibilities, not call-site argument counts. Qualify storage, recovery, accounting, and execution guarantees beside their benefits. Live performance claims must link retained evidence; tutorial scores remain teaching evidence. Conceptual roles, availability, autonomy, and strength of evidence answer different questions. Keep the survey's attributed autonomy map on its research page. Distinguish empirical evidence, conditional proofs, and bias-relative search guarantees; a practical estimator does not inherit an idealized oracle's guarantees. Keep historical comparison anchors.

docs.title: Method walkthroughs
docs.text:
The catalog at research/index.md owns method discovery; Examples owns application and execution-mode discovery. Both link to one canonical page per method. Show usable implementations before proposed mappings and adjacent references. Keep availability aligned with research/catalog.json; use only Shipped, Experimental/live-only, and Design—not shipped as status labels.

After the problem, answer the four method questions: what changes, what generates the change, what judges it, and what is retained? Name fixed controls and actual stages, including search and feedback. Keep exact algorithm scope, complete setup, supported execution, result interpretation, adaptation, and evidence together. Identify whether the candidate is an output, generator, policy, or research procedure.

State which results are returned, persisted, or produced by later calls. Capturing inner histories and forwarding physical usage are explicit choices; nesting supplies neither automatically. The nested-evaluation comparison shows the different policy and AutoResearch boundaries. An outer Run need not capture or resume the whole method.

Implementation scope and evidence are separate from availability. Preserve the distinction between a mechanism fixture, live integration, and a reproduction. A search preset does not establish a complete research method. Scientific discovery belongs in the framework's application scope, while unimplemented scientific methods retain their Design—not shipped status. New method releases update the canonical walkthrough, catalog, source/download links, and evidence together; composition claims point to code showing actual compatible reuse.

docs.title: Concept conventions
docs.text:
Concepts start with the duration parser. Offer the path: improvement loop → artifacts → meta-evolution → evaluation and authority → experience → deeper semantics. Keep search, history, budgets, failures, identity, domains, and conformance discoverable. Evaluation and authority also appear in introductions.

The loop owns optional base notation; meta-evolution adds the procedure candidate. Link those definitions after concrete examples. They are teaching notation, not new API types or a prerequisite for the quickstart. Diagrams label mutable candidates, fixed controls, and optional feedback. Keep overviews compact; show branching, rejection, and seed evaluation in detailed traces. Use text as well as color and preserve offline readability. Selection may retain the seed; it promises neither a gain nor promotion.

Open each primary page with a plain-language definition, what the reader supplies, and what they can do with it. Explain declaration fields for values such as Task and Experiment, and public methods for active or inspectable objects such as Session and Run. Keep evaluator measurements distinct from the task's evaluation contract. The programming model owns the core-object progression; link there instead of repeating full contracts. Use an example, then link a runnable guide and its owned reference. Concept pages need no full notebook; supplemental scripts name repository setup. Distinguish evaluator and proposer authorship from permission to read evidence. Keep simulated proposals and measured behavior explicit, and use only verified example results.

Use recognizable navigation names and links by purpose. Preserve URLs and heading fragments when retitling; navigation supplies the reading order.

docs.title: Lesson conventions
docs.text:
Make rewritten instructional pages self-contained: purpose, prerequisites, setup, code, expected observations, explanation, and one focused exercise. Links offer optional depth, not missing steps. A discovery page helps readers choose a tutorial; it need not reproduce every tutorial.

The limits guide established the pattern used by evaluation, search, feedback, inspection, and persistence: open with the problem and a short task chooser, then put complete prerequisites in one collapsed section labeled Required setup for a fresh notebook, before the executable task cells. Tell readers to expand and run setup first, then run the examples in order. Folding required setup does not make it optional. Keep the actual change, output, interpretation, and exercise visible. Explain each API before use and link to Start here for the full parser explanation. Reuse canonical snippets; all definitions must be copyable from the page. Use inline settings in the chooser instead of duplicate executable previews. Fold shared preparation, keeping the guide's new concept visible: evaluation teaches the grading function; feedback teaches evidence and its use; inspection prepares a mixed history before querying it. Persistence keeps saving, the kernel restart, reopening, and export visible. Its reopening cell is self-contained. Include a focused answer to a likely question and explain what to replace for the reader's own task. Update the newcomer and regression handoff with changed cells, setup discovery, question retrieval, and transfer tasks. Agent preflight does not establish independent human understanding. Test each rewritten guide in a fresh namespace and from outside the checkout with the installed package; executing a prerequisite page first is insufficient.

The evaluation guide consolidates the earlier metrics lesson. The limits guide consolidates the earlier threshold and budget lessons. Their previous URLs and fragments redirect to the relevant sections. One SDK notebook guide owns setup and real request wiring. Its accounting and tool details are in Reference; larger SDK applications are in Examples. The old migration URL redirects to the retained removal history. CLI, browser, and extension contracts are in Reference. The SDK introduction keeps installation, credentials, request controls, both callables, declaration, execution, and inspection visible. Only the complete request-accounting wrapper is folded as required setup before use. Keep the request cell separate, explain its bound and rerun behavior, and link deeper failure/accounting details from the point where the reader needs them. Feedback, inspection, and saving also run in fresh notebooks. The saving guide additionally verifies reopening after the original Python process exits, with no proposer or evaluator definitions and no exported source file required. The SDK notebook is tested through the official SDK with simulated HTTP responses, including failed requests and missing usage. Those checks establish the wiring and accounting, not live model performance. The harness guide uses a handwritten help assistant to teach both configuration changes, independent answer checks, fresh held-out evaluation, and export/reload. Tests execute its displayed cells and exercise failures and incompatible grading. The policy guide runs inner number searches to grade candidate search settings. Its notebook retains and reopens every inner history, separates inner and outer work counts, compares fresh held-out runs, and tests the fixed budget ceiling. The artifact-domain guide defines a recipe value and codec in visible cells. It separates structural validity from useful steps, rejects foreign proposals, and reopens saved recipes in a fresh process with only the type and codec. The displayed codec also passes the published conformance suite.

Extract focused code from canonical scripts, keeping required cells in execution order and definitions before use. Start here keeps installation and Python cells visible without CLI drivers or companion lesson imports; its folds contain optional explanations. Tests execute required folded cells, preserve indentation, and match rendered copyable code. Preserve historical fragments; setup links land at the visible fold so readers can expand it. Continuations name their prerequisite page and define each addition. Put verified output beside the command, preferably as comments; longer transcripts can use adjacent output blocks. Explain what changed and why, including failed attempts. Prefer readable fields and response evidence to raw object dumps.

Use consistent roles: artifact/seed, proposer, evaluator, task and objectives, search, experiment, session, run, explicit feedback/experience, and external controls. Introduce only the roles the current question needs. Selection never grants deployment authority. A failed measurement has no score; a measured wrong response may have a low score. Persistence does not imply resumability, and recorded replay does not rerun a model.

docs.title: Evidence and compatibility
docs.text:
Use only Shipped, Experimental/live-only, and Design—not shipped as status labels. Describe deterministic fixtures, dry runs, and retained live captures separately as evidence modes. Shipped lessons need no repeated banner. Never replace missing live evidence with a transcript that looks like a model run. Label illustrative output explicitly; exercises predict qualitative behavior, not guaranteed live scores. Live claims must match retained authorized evidence.

Example pages name editable content, independent grading, selection data, separate final checks when present, replacement points, and evidence limitations. Notebook mirrors remain byte-identical to their canonical sources. Site builds publish saved outputs without executing notebooks. Keep unique historical measurements and research decisions even when beginner prose is superseded.

docs.title: Destination coverage
docs.text:
Each maintained page should answer a distinct reader question. Extend an existing page when the explanation belongs there. Keep unique measurements and design decisions accessible through Development; a historical inventory entry does not require a page in the learning path.

Add a guide: write the task, setup, runnable cells, expected observations, and adaptation advice. Link it from the appropriate index or navigation and add relevant execution/output checks. No history or redirect entry is required.

Edit a guide: run its affected executable checks and the rendered-link checks. Tests protect results, complete copyable setup, actual destinations, and evidence. They do not prescribe sentences, cell counts, or submenu layouts. Review explanations and claims against the canonical contracts; use the newcomer walkthrough to assess understanding, answer-finding, and adaptation.

Move or retire a page: inspect repository links, known published routes, and the fixed tests/fixtures/documentation_routes.json compatibility baseline. Preserve supported anchors with explicit IDs or add a source, destination, and explicit fragment mappings to docs/redirects.json. Remove the obsolete source file; the existing MkDocs hook generates its route, working fallback links, and search exclusion. Point current internal links directly to maintained pages. Missing destinations, collisions, and redirect chains fail the build; rendered checks catch broken links and fragments. Keep unknown existing promises until there is evidence for a deliberate retirement, recorded with its reason and replacement in the review. Repository privacy does not establish lack of use.

The compatibility fixture is a fixed set of promises, not a current page or heading inventory. Add entries only for deliberate compatibility commitments. docs/project/documentation-migration.json is the frozen pre-#299 migration snapshot, excluded from the build and never read by its hooks or tests. docs.title: Agent SDK accounting: first implementation for #337
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

The requested lightweight first slice of #337 is implemented under experiments/sdk_accounting/, with usage instructions in its README. Run it from the source checkout with:

uv run --locked python -m experiments.sdk_accounting.run

The plan retains the broader study matrix as optional follow-up guidance. The accepted lightweight scope closes the decision with usable small recipes and focused offline evidence. Full runtime acceptance and a live SDK campaign are not claimed. No public provider API is added.

docs.title: Disposition
docs.text:
Keep the three wrapper recipes and the small experiment-local reporting function. A public helper is not justified by this slice. Shared result construction is useful, but Resources and the existing rich results already cover much of it. SDK-specific usage scope, lifecycle and failure handling remain the larger work.

The comparison retains a plain constructor baseline in comparison.inline_report and compares it with accounting.finish after identical native extraction. This is a narrow before/after reporting comparison, not proof that the complete new wrappers are equivalent to historical live drivers. Historical captures and their assumptions remain unchanged.

Target Concrete accounting trace Before/after reporting Codex Thread snapshots 8 → 17 contribute 17 once; a prior thread total is explicitly subtracted on continuation. Failed-turn notifications remain available. Same candidate/failure, resources and receipt evidence. Claude Agent SDK Main-loop fields describe 14 tokens; the two model entries describe 14 + 3 = 17. The last query snapshot contributes 17, not the sum of snapshots or both accounting views. Same candidate/failure, resources and receipt evidence. Pi Session total 100 → 117 contributes 17 after settlement; context size 9,999 is not consumed work. Compaction events can follow agent_end. Same candidate/failure, resources and receipt evidence.

These numbers are synthetic fixtures. All three runnable examples retain unknown spend, one proposal and two evaluations. The fixed Python grader assigns 2 to durable typed records; this is not a model-improvement measurement.

docs.title: What was simplified, and what was not
docs.text:
Author work Result of the first slice Build a rich result without dropping failed-work costs One local finish() consistently preserves resources and omits the candidate keyword on failure. Explicit candidate=None is not the same as omitting it. Validate/convert an exact bill, preserve its source, retain unknown spend Shared reporting handles this small repeated operation; estimates and bill lookup policy remain with the caller. Decide which token totals mean this invocation's work Still different in all three wrappers. No universal event decoder is warranted. Start, consume, interrupt and close the SDK Still native: Codex turn handles, Claude async iterators, Pi subprocess/RPC. Pi's bridge is materially larger than its result constructor. Change tools, permissions, models, session policy or grading Remains explicit caller configuration and independent evaluation. There is no new provider registry or coordinator branch.

The benefit is consistent reporting, not an elimination of the important author decisions. The shared function also adds code for bills and diagnostics that the unknown-bill constructor baseline does not need. A shorter call site therefore does not establish a total reduction in complexity or justify a public API.

Codex's pinned convenience collector can raise on a failed turn before returning its collected usage; the recipe consumes notifications directly. Claude's richer model totals still have a documented coverage boundary: some internal helper calls are excluded. Pi's bridge requires a settled event and a final statistics reply. An unavailable measurement escapes with a receipt rather than becoming zero usage or a low score. These wrappers report runtime-reported invocation work, without certifying otherwise unobservable calls.

Documentation checks include a strict build and rendered internal links. Clean-checkout verification also fixes test discovery through the direct pytest entry point and removes a link to an unmerged SoL-Pi planning anchor.

Checks cover both callable roles, failed/empty output, exact and unknown spend, missing/invalid counts, duplicate snapshots, continuation/reset handling, monetary admission, nested resource forwarding and durable reopen. They validate accounting against real Meta-Evolve records, not only return-object shapes.

docs.title: Remaining boundaries
docs.text:
The first slice does not establish real runtime/tool-loop compatibility, credential/authentication behavior, hidden helper-call completeness, arbitrary subagent/compaction accounting, background work, cross-platform process isolation or a complete agent budget reservation protocol. These need targeted follow-up only when a concrete use case requires them. The existing #269 review and SoL-Pi work can reuse the recipes without treating these fixtures as live evidence.

Protocol references: Codex SDK, Claude Agent SDK accounting, Claude Python results, and Pi RPC. The pinned installed source also informed the native fixtures. This decision completes #337's accepted lightweight scope and the remaining #330 study gate. The broader matrix remains deferred;

docs.title: 269's independent reviews, release work and live evidence retain their own gates.
Project status
docs.text:
The callable improvement loop, configurable experiments, bounded search, explicit experience, durable history, and local inspection are Shipped. The task guides show how to use them; the examples apply them to prompts, source, skills, harnesses, search policies, and a systems simulator.

The programming model owns the public API contract; the roadmap owns milestone status and scope.

docs.title: Author API revision
docs.text:
The integrated source Shipped partial budget restrictions, keyword-only plain callback context, winner-independent summaries, budget-led preset limits, and component Resources. Follow Migrate to 0.2. The package still reports 0.1.0 pending the coordinated 0.2.0 release; use this documentation's source download or matching commit. The version string alone does not identify this source revision. Package publication remains #319's separate gate.

The integration verification identifies source, tests, installed examples, history compatibility, and deployment.

docs.title: Distributed execution
docs.text:
M11.0–M11.2 are merged: the design record, concurrency-ready fold, durable work table, dispatcher, and generational cohorts are available. A run started with mode="distributed" still executes work serially, one worker at a time. Single-process recovery is available; multiprocess concurrency remains Design—not shipped.

The current scope requires a cohort-capable search policy (BestOfN is the shipped example), no pushed context or pull experience, and budgets whose finite dimensions are trial and evaluation counts. Finite token, elapsed-time, and monetary ceilings are refused; worker environment-fingerprint matching is not implemented yet. See the trusted-concurrency roadmap for the remaining acceptance gates and storage upgrades before opening older stores.

Federation and the post-local-author notebook/browser presentation follow-up also remain Design—not shipped.

docs.title: Implementation history
docs.text:
Milestones 1–8, 9, 9.5, and 10 are complete. Immutable source trees, exact patches, bounded processes, and independent command evaluation shipped in Milestone 5; Milestone 7 established the cross-domain extension boundary. External SDKs are user-owned callables, with no first-party provider adapter in the package.

The deterministic harness implementation runs through M8.5. The historical M8.6 captures closed its named blocker without adding harness code beyond M8.5 to main; provider evidence retains the outcomes and their limits. Milestone 9 added policy artifacts and nested improvement. M9.5.3 added Specialists and TreeSearch; M9.5.4 added the unified five-policy comparison.

Milestone 10 completed the local author experience on August 14, 2026: Experiment, improve(), functional @search, Run.inspect(), read-only storage, paced and resumable Session, and the optional browser with artifact presentation. The roadmap records the individual slices and acceptance criteria.

docs.title: Measured local-author design target
docs.text: The M10.0 design scorecard measures a runnable shipped full-protocol search at 15 scaffolding lines and the statically counted proposed functional syntax at 1: a 93% reduction. The historical labels and counts remain unchanged; the M10.3 after-side now executes in deterministic unnumbered local fixtures. This measures authoring friction, not optimization quality or runtime performance.

docs.title: API examples and edge cases
docs.text:
These small deterministic examples answer questions about the API reference. They use numbers so counting, selection, and failure behavior are easy to see. The duration-parser tutorial provides the complete installation-to-result introduction.

Run the setup once, then the cells in order. Only an installed meta_evolve package is required; there are no model calls or credentials. The same code is available in reference_cases.py.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
The proposer adds one to its parent; the evaluator measures the resulting value. The default objective maximizes that measurement as score.

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import EvaluatorFailure


def propose(value):
    return value + 1


def evaluate(value):
    return value

docs.title: Seed evaluation and proposal counts
docs.text:
improve(trials=0) evaluates the seed without asking for a revision. trials=2 allows two successor attempts, in addition to the seed. Run.trials() includes the seed record, while Usage.trials counts only successor attempts.

seed_only = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=evaluate, trials=0)
counted = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=evaluate, trials=2)
for result in (seed_only, counted):
    print([attempt.artifact.value for attempt in result.trials()])
    print("proposals:", result.usage().trials, "evaluations:", result.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# [0]
# proposals: 0 evaluations: 1
# [0, 1, 2]
# proposals: 2 evaluations: 3

A failed proposal consumes an attempt without requiring an evaluator call. A failed evaluation still consumes an evaluation. Therefore proposal counts, evaluation counts, and the number of history records need not be equal.

docs.title: Ties, regressions, and the selected result
docs.text:
Greedy proposes from the best measured artifact so far. It keeps an earlier successful evaluation on an exact tie. Regressions remain in history, and the seed can remain the selected result.

selection_cases = {}
for label, measure in (("ties", lambda value: 0), ("regressions", lambda value: -value)):
    result = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=measure, trials=2)
    selection_cases[label] = result
    selected = result.best_trial()
    print(label, "winner:", selected.artifact.value, "score:", selected.metrics["score"])
    print("history:", [attempt.artifact.value for attempt in result.trials()])
# Output:
# ties winner: 0 score: 0
# history: [0, 1, 1]
# regressions winner: 0 score: 0
# history: [0, 1, 1]

Both successors contain 1: neither replaced the seed as Greedy's parent. best() returns an artifact view with decoded .value; best_trial() returns the producing attempt with its artifact, metrics, evidence, and usage. Neither means “the last attempt.”

BestOfN always proposes from the seed, even when a successor ranks better. Enabled feedback can still carry earlier observations; independent parent selection does not imply statistically independent model calls.

docs.title: One objective on the short path
docs.text:
Pass one Maximize or Minimize as improve(objective=...). A scalar evaluator measures that objective's named metric. Here the evaluator returns distance from three; minimizing error stops as soon as that distance reaches zero:

def distance(value):
    return abs(3 - value)


closest = meta.improve(
    seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=distance, trials=5,
    objective=meta.Minimize("error", satisfy=0),
)
print("selected:", closest.best().value)
print("error:", closest.best_trial().metrics["error"])
print("proposals:", closest.usage().trials, "evaluations:", closest.usage().evaluations)
print("stop:", closest.summary().stop_reason)
# Output:
# selected: 3
# error: 0
# proposals: 3 evaluations: 4
# stop: objective_satisfied

A mapping or EvaluationResult must instead contain the exact declared metric. A missing measurement is a typed evaluation failure. objective=None keeps the default Maximize("score") with no satisfaction target. If the seed meets an explicit target, search stops after its evaluation, even with trials=0.

docs.title: Ordered objectives and satisfaction
docs.text:
Task.objectives defaults to (Maximize("score"),) with no target. A scalar evaluator is valid only with one objective. With several, return a mapping containing every objective's metric; additional metrics are retained without changing the selection rule.

The first objective controls default ranking and built-in satisfaction stopping. Maximize(..., satisfy=x) accepts values at least x; Minimize accepts values at most x. A target on a secondary objective is not another stopping condition.

def measure_tradeoff(value):
    return {"quality": value, "cost": value}


tradeoff = meta.run(meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(
        evaluator=measure_tradeoff,
        objectives=(meta.Maximize("quality", satisfy=2), meta.Minimize("cost", satisfy=0)),
    ),
    seed=0,
    proposer=propose,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
))
print("primary winner:", tradeoff.best().value)
print("lowest cost:", tradeoff.best("cost").value)
print("proposals:", tradeoff.usage().trials)
print("stop:", tradeoff.inspect().overview.stop_reason)
# Output:
# primary winner: 2
# lowest cost: 0
# proposals: 2
# stop: objective_satisfied

The seed already meets the secondary cost target, but the run continues until quality reaches two. Querying best("cost") afterward ranks the retained history by that declared objective; it does not rerun search or change its decisions. This declaration does not request Pareto or joint multi-objective optimization.

docs.title: Tighten one budget dimension
docs.text:
Budget controls allowed work independently of search. run(experiment) uses the task budget. In a supplied budget=, omitted or None fields inherit task ceilings; supplied finite limits cannot exceed them.

When the task bounds both proposals and evaluations, passing only Budget(evaluations=2) tightens evaluations and retains the trial ceiling. Inspect the resolved budget to see both limits:

task = meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate, budget=meta.Budget(trials=4, evaluations=5))
experiment = meta.Experiment(task=task, seed=0, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(4))
tighter = meta.Budget(evaluations=2)
limited = meta.run(experiment, budget=tighter)
print("retained proposal ceiling:", limited.inspect().declaration.effective_budget.trials)
print("proposals:", limited.usage().trials, "evaluations:", limited.usage().evaluations)
print("stop:", limited.inspect().overview.stop_reason)
# Output:
# retained proposal ceiling: 4
# proposals: 1 evaluations: 2
# stop: budget_exhausted

Budget() retains every task limit. Explicit widening, such as Budget(evaluations=6) against this task's five-evaluation ceiling, raises ValueError before component calls or committed run facts. See the migration notes for previously rejected partial overrides.

docs.title: Preset defaults follow the allowance
docs.text:
Greedy, BestOfN, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch inherit finite effective Budget.trials when max_trials is omitted or None. Without that ceiling, they use 20, or 100 for TreeSearch. An explicit integer is a voluntary stop. improve(trials=...) keeps its integer-only default of 20.

allowance = meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate, budget=meta.Budget(trials=25))
for search in (meta.Greedy(), meta.Greedy(max_trials=20)):
    result = meta.run(meta.Experiment(task=allowance, seed=0, proposer=propose, search=search))
    print("proposals:", result.usage().trials, "evaluations:", result.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# proposals: 25 evaluations: 26
# proposals: 20 evaluations: 21

See Migrate to 0.2 to retain earlier work amounts.

docs.title: Proposer arguments and feedback
docs.text:
A plain proposer accepts (parent) or explicitly requests ProposerContext with (parent, *, context). Ordinary optional arguments retain their Python defaults:

def scale_candidate(parent, scale=2):
    return parent * scale


scaled = meta.improve(seed=1, proposer=scale_candidate, evaluator=evaluate, trials=1)
print(scaled.best().value)
# Output:
# 2

Request framework state explicitly:

def advance(parent, *, context):
    return parent + context.step


advanced = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=advance, evaluator=evaluate, trials=2)
print(advanced.best().value)
# Output:
# 3

To receive feedback, pass context=RecentAncestors(...) to improve() or Experiment and accept the keyword-only context in the proposer. Read context.evidence.latest(kind) or the bundle's bounded .rendered text. Pushed feedback is off by default; recording evidence alone does not enable it. PullAccess separately supplies an audited reader as context.experience. Follow the feedback guide for a complete example. The migration guide covers existing positional callbacks and registered histories.

This bounded loop uses exact evaluator evidence to propose the next value. Two records hold one evidence item and its evaluation in this example; a different evaluator may need a larger bound. One rendered character deliberately demonstrates that structured evidence remains available when text is clipped.

def feedback_score(value):
    return meta.EvaluationResult(metrics={"score": value}, evidence=(
        meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="feedback", data={"value": value}),
    ))


def feedback_revision(parent, *, context):
    item = context.evidence.latest("feedback")
    if item is None:
        return parent
    return meta.ProposalResult(candidate=item.data["value"] + 1,
                               derived_from=(item.ref,))


feedback_run = meta.improve(
    seed=0, proposer=feedback_revision, evaluator=feedback_score, trials=6,
    context=meta.RecentAncestors(max_records=2, max_chars=1),
)
print("selected:", feedback_run.best().value)
print("proposals:", feedback_run.usage().trials,
      "evaluations:", feedback_run.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# selected: 6
# proposals: 6 evaluations: 7

latest() raises meta_evolve.errors.ContextDisabled with pushed context off; an enabled policy with no selected match returns None. Check .enabled when feedback is an optional dependency. The experience guide explains selection order, provenance, and upgrading durable histories.

docs.title: Plain values and result records
docs.text:
A proposer can return a candidate directly; an evaluator can return a scalar or metric mapping. Use ProposalResult and EvaluationResult when you also need observations, usage, or typed failures. Their maps are frozen on construction.

def propose_with_usage(parent):
    return meta.ProposalResult(
        candidate=parent + 1,
        hypothesis="A larger value should score higher.",
        usage=meta.Resources(tokens=5, spend_micros=None),
    )


def evaluate_with_evidence(value):
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": value},
        evidence=(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="measurement", data={"value": value}),),
    )


recorded = meta.improve(
    seed=0, proposer=propose_with_usage, evaluator=evaluate_with_evidence, trials=1,
)
selected = recorded.best_trial()
print("value:", selected.artifact.value, "score:", selected.metrics["score"])
print("evidence:", selected.evidence[0].data["value"])
print("tokens:", recorded.usage().tokens, "spend:", recorded.usage().spend_micros)
# Output:
# value: 1 score: 1
# evidence: 1
# tokens: 5 spend: None

The token amount above is a declared fixture, not measured provider activity. Rich results take Resources, containing tokens, billed micro-USD, and elapsed seconds. The engine owns counts and records Usage. Passing the old Usage value to a rich result raises at construction.

docs.title: Forward nested resources
docs.text:
Project inner.usage().resources, then add the evaluator's own costs once. Here each outer evaluation runs one inner proposal reporting five tokens and unknown spend, then adds two tokens of its own. Inner counts remain inner:

def evaluate_procedure(value):
    inner = meta.improve(seed=value, proposer=propose_with_usage, evaluator=evaluate, trials=1)
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": inner.best().value},
        usage=meta.Resources(tokens=2) + inner.usage().resources,
    )


nested = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=evaluate_procedure, trials=1)
print("outer proposals:", nested.usage().trials, "evaluations:", nested.usage().evaluations)
print("tokens:", nested.usage().tokens, "spend:", nested.usage().spend_micros)
# Output:
# outer proposals: 1 evaluations: 2
# tokens: 14 spend: None

docs.title: Unknown spend and monetary ceilings
docs.text:
Resources(spend_micros=0) means known free work. None means an unknown bill; adding an unknown amount makes the aggregate unknown. Estimates belong in evidence. One micro-USD is one millionth of a US dollar.

With no monetary ceiling, the preceding run can evaluate its successor. Under a monetary ceiling, an unknown proposal charge prevents further work:

unknown_spend = meta.run(meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate_with_evidence, budget=meta.Budget(spend_micros=100)),
    seed=0,
    proposer=propose_with_usage,
    search=meta.Greedy(2),
))
print("states:", [attempt.state for attempt in unknown_spend.trials()])
print("candidate retained:", unknown_spend.trials()[-1].artifact.value)
print("best measured:", unknown_spend.best().value)
print("stop:", unknown_spend.inspect().overview.stop_reason)
# Output:
# states: ['evaluated', 'unevaluated']
# candidate retained: 1
# best measured: 0
# stop: accounting_unavailable

The proposed value is retained, but was never evaluated. It cannot replace the measured seed. If the evaluator instead reports unknown spend, its completed measurement is retained and further work stops.

Resource reports are checked after calls return. A reported monetary overrun is charged and recorded as a typed ResourceExhausted failure. A zero spend ceiling permits known free work. These ceilings neither interrupt an in-flight SDK request nor guarantee a provider hard spending cap. See evaluation and budgets for accounting details.

docs.title: No successful evaluation
docs.text:
Failures such as EvaluatorFailure, ProposerFailure, and InvalidOutput are data from meta_evolve.domain, not exceptions to raise. Return them directly, or attach one to a result record. A failed proposal omits candidate; a failed evaluation omits metrics. Contradictory records raise ValueError.

def unavailable(value):
    return meta.EvaluationResult(failure=EvaluatorFailure(message="grader unavailable"))


failed = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=unavailable, trials=0)
try:
    failed.best()
except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
    print("No successful evaluation")
print("state:", failed.trials()[0].state)
report = failed.summary()
print("evaluations:", report.evaluation_count)
print("rankability:", report.rankability)
print("score:", report.primary_score, "lineage:", report.winning_lineage)
print("lifecycle:", report.lifecycle)
# Output:
# No successful evaluation
# state: evaluation_failed
# evaluations: 1
# rankability: unrankable
# score: None lineage: ()
# lifecycle: complete

NoSuccessfulEvaluation is an exception: best(), best_trial(), and default-winner lineage() raise it when nothing ranks. summary() returns state, absent score, and recorded costs; trials(), usage(), and inspect() also remain available. See the summary migration guide.

Invalid output and ordinary exceptions inside a proposer or evaluator become typed outcomes. Declaration errors, unsupported capabilities, and infrastructure faults can raise instead of returning a Run; they are not candidate scores.

docs.title: Retained history and resume
docs.text: Passing Storage.durable(path) to improve() or local run() saves history. Reopen it with Run(run_id, storage) to inspect facts without executing components. Resuming unfinished work additionally requires a supported mode and registered, reconstructible components. Follow save and reopen and recovery for those separate workflows.

docs.title: Shipped API reference
docs.text:
Signatures and descriptions come from the package source used for this build. Start with the declarations below, then use the complete import inventory and extension contracts when you need them.

Your task Start with Run a small experiment improve() Configure evaluation and search Task, Experiment, and run() Inspect a result and its costs Run and Usage

For a complete example, use Start here. The core-object walkthrough explains declaration, execution, and inspection. API examples cover counts and edge cases; Migrate to 0.2 explains the coordinated API changes.

docs.title: Generated entries
docs.text:
The common declarations below show the inputs you construct. Returned views describe the values you inspect; their private constructors are not needed. Search binding and cohort methods belong to the extension protocol.

The following four tiers cover every root export.

docs.title: improve
docs.text:
improve(
    *,
    seed,
    proposer,
    evaluator,
    trials=20,
    storage=None,
    random_seed=0,
    objective=None,
    context=None,
)

Run a bounded greedy improvement loop with a callable evaluator.

This constructs Task, Experiment, and Greedy, then calls run. By default it maximizes score with no satisfaction target and supplies no pushed feedback. Declare one objective or an explicit context policy here. Use the expanded path for multiple objectives, custom artifacts, budgets, search, pulled experience, execution mode, or registry components.

The seed is evaluated before successor attempts. A tie or regression keeps the earlier best result; an attempt need not improve anything. Supplying durable storage preserves local history but does not make this run resumable.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default seed

Initial immutable JSON-like value, such as a string or number.

required proposer

Callable accepting (parent) or (parent, *, context), or a local proposer adapter. Return a candidate or ProposalResult.

required evaluator

Independent callable returning a finite scalar measured under the objective's name, a mapping containing that metric, or EvaluationResult. Missing measurements become typed evaluation failures, not scores.

required trials int

Maximum number of successor proposals; defaults to 20. Zero evaluates only the seed. Failed proposals still count. Must be a non-negative integer; booleans and None are rejected.

20 storage

Artifact and event storage; defaults to isolated memory.

None random_seed int

Integer seed for recorded deterministic choices, default 0; does not make external providers deterministic.

0 objective Maximize | Minimize | None

One Maximize or Minimize; None uses Maximize("score") without a satisfaction target. A satisfied seed needs no proposals.

None context ContextPolicy | None

Explicit policy for bounded pushed feedback, such as RecentAncestors. None and NoMemory disable it. This never enables pull access. The proposer reads evidence through its keyword-only context.

None

Returns:

Type Description Run

A Run, even if all evaluations failed. Winner queries then raise NoSuccessfulEvaluation; trials(), inspect(), and usage() remain available.

docs.text:
Task(
    *,
    evaluator,
    artifact=None,
    objectives=(Maximize("score"),),
    budget=None,
    environment=FrozenMap(),
    artifact_kind="python-value",
    artifact_representation="canonical-json",
)

Define independent evaluation, objectives, artifact type, and budget.

Construction declares the rules without evaluating a candidate. The seed belongs to Experiment. Candidate proposals cannot revise this contract.

Malformed declarations raise TypeError or ValueError. During a run, invalid returned measurements become typed outcomes, not fabricated scores.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default evaluator ComponentRef | Callable[..., object]

Callable receiving the decoded candidate, or a registered evaluator reference. Return a finite number for exactly one objective, a mapping covering every objective, EvaluationResult, or a typed failure from meta_evolve.domain. Booleans are not scores.

required artifact InitVar[type | None]

Optional artifact type, such as Text, with declared kind and representation; an instance is rejected. Omit it for ordinary immutable JSON-like values, including strings.

None objectives tuple[Objective, ...]

Non-empty ordered objectives with unique metric names. Defaults to (Maximize("score"),) with no satisfaction target. The first controls default ranking and built-in satisfaction stopping. Extra reported metrics are retained without changing that selection.

(Maximize('score'),) budget Budget | None

Optional Budget; None adds no task ceiling. Search can still impose its own finite attempt limit.

None environment Mapping[str, object]

Evaluator-owned JSON-like metadata, frozen on construction and included in task identity. It does not configure an OS environment.

FrozenMap() artifact_kind str

Advanced codec kind; defaults to "python-value".

'python-value' artifact_representation str

Advanced codec representation; defaults to "canonical-json". Prefer artifact= for declared artifact types; conflicting explicit kind or representation values are rejected.

Experiment(
    *,
    task,
    seed,
    proposer,
    search=None,
    context=None,
    experience=None,
    random_seed=0,
    registry=None,
)

An immutable evaluated-search declaration.

Execution starts only when passed to run or Session.start. Construction does not invoke components; execution validates their compatibility. Storage, mode, and a narrowing budget are execution options. Use dataclasses.replace to make a new declaration while reusing unchanged components.

Equality is ordinary dataclass equality over these eight fields. In particular, no structural equality is promised for live proposer or registry objects.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default task Task

Evaluation contract, artifact type, objectives, and optional budget ceiling.

required seed object

Initial value accepted by the task's artifact codec.

required proposer ProposerLike

Callable accepting (parent) or (parent, *, context), adapter, or registered proposer component. Only keyword-only context requests ProposerContext; other defaults remain unchanged.

required search SearchProgram | None

Search policy; None means budget-led Greedy() at execution time.

None context ContextPolicy | None

Policy-pushed feedback, such as AncestorsOnly. None and NoMemory select no records.

None experience ExperienceAccess | None

Bounded agent-pulled access, such as PullAccess. None provides no reader. Recording evidence does not enable either feedback channel automatically.

None random_seed int

Integer seed for recorded deterministic search choices; defaults to 0.

0 registry Registry | None

Extra artifact codecs and registered durable components; None uses built-ins and live local callables.

None

docs.title: run
docs.text:
run(
    experiment: Experiment,
    /,
    *,
    storage: Storage | None = None,
    budget: Budget | None = None,
    mode: ExecutionMode = "local",
) -> Run

run(
    *,
    task: Task,
    seed: object,
    proposer: ProposerLike,
    search: SearchProgram | None = None,
    context: ContextPolicy | None = None,
    experience: ExperienceAccess | None = None,
    storage: Storage | None = None,
    budget: Budget | None = None,
    random_seed: int = 0,
    mode: ExecutionMode = "local",
    registry: Registry | None = None,
) -> Run

Run one evaluated improvement search and return its inspectable history.

Pass an Experiment as the positional argument. The source-compatible keyword form accepts its declaration fields instead; supplying both forms raises TypeError. The keyword form retains the effective defaults search=None, context=None, experience=None, random_seed=0, and registry=None. The default Greedy() inherits finite trial allowance, falling back to 20 when unbounded. Both forms use the same Session as paced and resumed execution.

storage=None creates separate in-memory storage. A durable storage handle preserves local history; resumability additionally requires registered, reconstructible components and a supported execution mode.

budget=None uses the task budget, or an unrestricted resource allowance if the task has none. In a supplied Budget, omitted or None dimensions inherit task ceilings. Finite values may tighten or introduce ceilings; exceeding a finite task ceiling raises ValueError before work starts. Budget() preserves all task ceilings.

mode="local" accepts live Python callables and provides no isolation. "durable-local" adds reconstructible execution and recovery. "distributed" uses the durable dispatcher and currently executes serially, one worker at a time; it does not provide multiprocess concurrency. The latter two modes require durable storage, registered components, and their declared capabilities. See the programming model's execution profiles.

Invalid proposals and ordinary proposer or evaluator failures are recorded as typed trial outcomes; they are not converted to low scores. Capability and infrastructure exceptions can abort execution instead of producing a Run.

Returns:

Type Description Run

A Run for result, history, usage, and comparison queries, including when no evaluation succeeded.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If a declared public input has the wrong type.

ValueError

If a declaration is invalid or the task budget is widened.

BudgetUnavailable

If the seed cannot be admitted.

CapabilityError

If the requested execution requirements cannot be satisfied.

Returned by improve, run, or resume; session.run also reads an active session. Queries do not advance execution. Construct a Run from its ID and storage to read retained history; this neither reruns components nor resumes work.

Use best().value for selected content, best_trial() for that attempt's measurements, and trials() for all completed attempts. summary(), inspect(), and usage() work even when nothing ranks. A returned Run does not guarantee a successful evaluation or an improvement over the seed.

Every committed attempt in logical order, seed trial first.

Includes regressions, ties, failed proposals, failed evaluations, and attempts whose evaluation was not authorized. Read TrialView.state to distinguish them. Unlike usage().trials, this tuple includes the seed. Like inspect() and usage(), it remains available when no evaluation succeeded. In-progress attempts without a committed outcome are not yet included.

summary()

Report lifecycle, rankability, declarations, and committed usage.

Reads one validated snapshot, including incomplete runs and pending seed evaluation. If nothing ranks, primary_score is None and winning_lineage is empty. Use inspect() for detailed failures.

Capture while storage is open, then print or display the returned summary even after storage closes. Rendering never reads storage or displays decoded artifact objects. This method still performs a read and surfaces storage, integrity, and decoding failures.
