docs.title: Budget dataclass
docs.text:
Budget(
    *,
    evaluations=None,
    trials=None,
    tokens=None,
    spend_micros=None,
    wall_seconds=None,
)

Immutable resource ceilings, checked against recorded Usage.

Every field defaults to None (no ceiling for that resource). Counts must be non-negative integers; booleans are rejected. A budget bounds work independently of a search preset's own attempt limit.

Resource reports are checked after actions return; an in-flight SDK call is not interrupted. A monetary overrun is charged and recorded as a typed failure. This is not a hard provider spending cap.

In run(..., budget=...), omitted or None fields inherit task ceilings. Supplied limits may tighten or introduce ceilings, but exceeding a finite task ceiling raises ValueError before work starts. Budget() retains every task ceiling; zero remains a real limit. run documents execution defaults; the limits guide supplies complete examples.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default evaluations int | None

Maximum evaluator invocations, including the seed. Zero cannot admit the seed and raises BudgetUnavailable at run start. Failed evaluations still consume this allowance.

None trials int | None

Maximum successor proposal attempts; the seed consumes none. Zero permits seed evaluation only.

None tokens int | None

Ceiling on component-reported tokens.

None spend_micros int | None

Ceiling on billed micro-USD; zero permits known free work. Unknown spend makes a monetary ceiling unverifiable and stops more work.

None wall_seconds float | None

Ceiling on reported non-negative finite elapsed seconds.

None

docs.title: Greedy dataclass
docs.text:
Greedy(max_trials=None)

Expand the best evaluated artifact for at most max_trials attempts.

The seed is evaluated separately. A strictly better successor becomes the next parent; unsuccessful attempts remain in the record. Satisfaction or exhaustion can stop search before the attempt limit.

Exact ties retain the earlier successful evaluation. If no evaluation has succeeded yet, the seed remains the proposal parent. Default ranking and satisfaction use the first task objective.

The resolved limit is recorded for replay. An explicit limit can stop search sooner but never widens the effective budget. Pass this declaration as Experiment(search=Greedy(max_trials=3), ...); execution binds it for you. The methods below support the search extension protocol.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default max_trials int | None

Optional non-negative successor attempt limit. Omitted or None inherits finite Budget.trials at execution start, falling back to 20 when unbounded. Zero allows only seed evaluation.

None

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If the limit is not an integer or None; booleans are rejected.

ValueError

If the limit is negative.

docs.title: BestOfN dataclass
docs.text:
BestOfN(max_trials=None, cohort_width=1)

Expand the seed independently for at most max_trials successor attempts.

Every proposal starts from the same seed. Explicitly enabled experience can still communicate prior observations between attempts. The seed can remain the winner; a successor need not improve it.

Exact ties retain the earlier successful evaluation. Default ranking and satisfaction use the first task objective. A target or budget can stop the run before all attempts are used.

The resolved limit is recorded for replay. An explicit limit never widens the effective budget. Pass this as Experiment(search=BestOfN(3), ...); execution binds it for you. The methods below support search extensions.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default max_trials int | None

Optional non-negative successor attempt limit. Omitted or None inherits finite Budget.trials at start, falling back to 20 when unbounded. Zero allows only seed evaluation.

None cohort_width int

Positive number of attempts planned from one committed history, default 1. Widths above one require mode="distributed" and its admission requirements. Current execution is serial; a cohort is not a promise of concurrent model calls.

1

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If limits have unsupported types; booleans are rejected.

ValueError

If max_trials is negative or cohort_width is below one.

docs.text:
Resources(*, tokens=0, spend_micros=0, wall_seconds=0.0)

Immutable component costs, additive with +.

Use in ProposalResult and EvaluationResult. Plain candidates, scalars, and metric mappings need no wrapper. The engine owns trial/evaluation counts; these are only available on returned Usage.

Forward inner.usage().resources from a nested evaluator, adding its own costs exactly once. Failed work still costs resources. Unknown spend stays unknown when added; estimates belong in evidence.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default tokens int

Non-negative integer token count, default zero.

0 spend_micros int | None

Billed micro-USD, default 0 for known free work; explicitly use None when unknown. Booleans are not counts.

0 wall_seconds float

Non-negative finite elapsed work, default 0.0. Aggregation sums reported work, not concurrent wall-clock duration.

0.0

A normalized candidate or typed proposer failure.

candidate is a value in the task's artifact type, not a durable payload: the registered codec is the one authority for that translation, and it runs where the task's kind and representation are known.

Plain proposers can return the candidate directly. Use this record when reporting usage, observations, or a failure from meta_evolve.domain.

Malformed records raise TypeError or ValueError on construction. During a run, ordinary exceptions raised inside a proposer become typed proposer failures; capability and infrastructure errors can abort the run.

Required for success; even None can be a valid value. The displayed _MISSING default means omitted. Omit this argument entirely when supplying failure.

Typed proposer or shared failure, such as ProposerFailure or InvalidOutput. A failure cannot also carry a candidate.

Optional non-empty explanation of the proposed change.

    failure=None,
    uncertainty=FrozenMap(),

Independent measurements or a typed failure, plus evidence and usage.

Successful metrics must cover the task objectives. A failed measurement has no rankable metrics. Return this explicitly to attach evidence, uncertainty, tokens, monetary spend, or elapsed usage; plain evaluators may return a scalar or metric mapping when no extra observations are needed.

Invalid field shapes raise TypeError or ValueError on construction. Missing task metrics are detected during execution as InvalidOutput. docs.title: Text
docs.text:
Bases: str

An immutable UTF-8 text artifact, usable as a Python string.

Use Task(artifact=Text, ...) for prompt or document candidates. The proposer can return a plain string; the codec decodes retained values as Text. Ordinary string seeds also work with the default task codec, so this wrapper is optional when a distinct text artifact kind is unnecessary. Empty strings are valid. The codec validates text; the evaluator defines quality, and constructing Text does not run an evaluation.

docs.title: ProposerContext dataclass
docs.text:
The candidate-facing state authorized for one proposal.

A plain callback requests this with def propose(parent, *, context). A default on that keyword does not disable delivery. Ordinary optional arguments keep their Python defaults; variadics alone do not request context. Structural objects retain their explicit propose(parent, context) port.

rng supplies recorded per-attempt randomness. step is the successor's logical step, starting at one; objectives is the task's ordered tuple. bundle.records contains pushed feedback and bundle.rendered its bounded text. evidence.latest(kind) reads its last matching evidence; evidence.enabled distinguishes disabled context from a missing match. With no context policy the bundle is empty. experience is an audited reader only when pull access is enabled; otherwise None. Repository adapters may supply workspace with controlled execution and history information; ordinary callables receive None there.

docs.title: evidence property
docs.text:
Evidence in this bundle, with explicit enabled/truncated status.

Manually constructed contexts must supply context_policy to enable lookup; neither an empty bundle nor its reason proves policy status.

NoMemory()

Select no pushed feedback; equivalent to Experiment(context=None).

This is the default. It does not disable separately declared pull access or erase retained history; the proposer simply receives an empty bundle.

docs.title: Selected evidence views
docs.text: ProposerContext.evidence returns an EvidenceSelection; latest(kind) returns an EvidenceItem or None. These supporting types live in meta_evolve.ports.evidence; ContextDisabled lives in meta_evolve.errors.

docs.title: meta_evolve.ports.evidence.EvidenceSelection dataclass
docs.text:
Read selected evidence without queries, I/O, or additional authority.

enabled describes the pushed-context declaration, not the presence of records. Use it to make feedback optional in intentional no-context runs. The full selection remains available through context.bundle.

docs.title: truncated property
docs.text:
Whether the policy omitted records or clipped its text rendering.

This flag cannot distinguish those causes. A text-only truncation does not remove structured evidence or bound the contents of item.data.

docs.title: latest
docs.text:
Return the last matching evidence in the selected canonical order.

kind is an exact, nonempty evidence label. Same-step matches follow bundle order. The result may describe an older ancestor or sibling; it need not describe the current parent or a successful evaluation. Proposer and evaluator evidence both qualify. No missing records or pull observations are fetched. None means no selected match, not that no evidence exists in the run. Disabled context raises instead.

docs.title: meta_evolve.ports.evidence.EvidenceItem dataclass
docs.text:
Selected evidence with its exact occurrence and recorded position.

data is recursively immutable. ref can be explicitly cited in a proposal's derived_from; reading this view records no derivation itself. A label identifies evidence, not whether its producer was an evaluator.

docs.title: meta_evolve.errors.ContextDisabled
docs.text:
Bases: CapabilityError

Evidence lookup requires explicitly enabled pushed context.

Check context.evidence.enabled when feedback is optional. An unhandled lookup aborts at the call site, possibly after seed evaluation, rather than recording a proposal failure or repeatedly consuming the attempt budget.

docs.title: Presentation records
docs.text: Only ArtifactPresentation and ArtifactDiff are root-exported records. Their minimal immutable supporting records live in meta_evolve.presentation: PresentationSection groups labelled PresentationField values and PresentationDocument text; each document has an optional path and explicit truncation state. FileDiff carries its path, added/removed/modified/unchanged status, typed DiffLine values with optional old/new line numbers, and an optional refusal or truncation notice. These records contain inert data only, not HTML, SVG, URLs, or trusted markup.

docs.title: drive()
docs.text:
Run a distributed session to its stop, through the dispatcher.

A distributed run's unit of progress is a WORK ITEM, not a decision: the frontier has to empty before a generation can be produced, because every member is drawn from one complete committed history. So it cannot be iterated as decisions, and this is the loop instead.

Serial in M11.2. The concurrency delivered is structural -- cohorts, the work table, leases, fences, retries and their terminal facts -- with one worker running each call inline. Thread-parallel execution needs the design's renewal-deadline wait, which arrives with the futures it exists to bound.

docs.title: Storage dataclass
docs.text:
Paired artifact and event storage, plus one all-or-none commit.

is_durable and is_read_only are independent capabilities. Durability says committed facts live on durable media; read-only says this handle has no commit authority. A writable durable handle therefore reports True, False while :meth:read_only reports True, True.

docs.title: durable(path) classmethod
docs.text: Wire durable storage into path (created if missing): one SQLite connection (events + artifact occurrence rows) shared with a content-addressed filesystem blob store under path/artifacts.

docs.title: read_only(path) classmethod
docs.text:
Open an existing durable directory with inspection authority only.

The directory and current schema must already exist. This path never creates, stamps, migrates, or otherwise repairs durable state.

docs.title: compose(artifacts, events, *, commit_strategy, close=None, bind_event_store=False) classmethod
docs.text:
Compose independently implemented stores behind one atomic commit.

The strategy declares whether its commit survives process restart; callers cannot separately forge is_durable. Composed storage is always writable: Storage cannot verify that third-party stores genuinely refuse writes, so read-only inspection handles come only from :meth:read_only, which pairs the declaration with stores built to fail closed.

events reaches the read path only, unless the strategy binds it. A commit strategy carries its own event-store reference, so by default a wrapped event store sees reads and not writes.

bind_event_store=True hands the strategy event_store= on every commit. A strategy whose commit does not declare that parameter -- including a **kwargs one -- is refused by name, and one that answers can_bind may refuse the store for its own reason: the durable strategy needs _append_in_txn on its own connection, the in-memory one the _snapshot/_validate/_install triple, the local one only the port, and read-only storage binds nothing.

A bound store is part of the commit. The in-memory strategy installs artifacts, then the stream, and on a stream failure restores the stream through the bound store's _install, re-reads it, and only then rolls artifacts back. If the re-read stream is not the snapshot, whether or not the restore raised, the commit raises a BaseExceptionGroup, keeps the artifacts so no event references a missing one, and the storage refuses every later commit.

For example:

storage = Storage.compose(
    base.artifacts, AuditedEvents(base.events),
    commit_strategy=base._commit_strategy, bind_event_store=True,
)

docs.title: work_broker()
docs.text:
The broker over this store's work table.

Only a store whose commit strategy DECLARES the capability has one. Work rows live in transactional tables beside the event stream, and a transition has to be atomic with the logical batch that authorizes it -- which needs a real transaction, not a copy-on-write swap.

Checked with isinstance against a declared Protocol, as runs() and run_version() check theirs. is_durable is not the question: ReadOnlyUnitOfWork declares itself durable and has no work table, so the two capabilities are independent.

docs.title: commit(run_id, expected_version, *, events, occurrences, work=())
docs.text:
Commit events, occurrences and work as one all-or-none unit.

EventStreamConflict on a stale expected_version propagates unchanged, and nothing is written. See unit_of_work.py for the per-backend guarantee (durable: one SQLite transaction; in-memory: a locked copy-on-write swap; hand-built pair: local-only fallback).

work defaults to empty, and an empty work is the call this method has always made -- same arguments, same strategy method -- so a strategy supplied through :meth:compose before work rows existed keeps working untouched. Passing a non-empty work to a strategy that does not declare the parameter is a CapabilityError naming the strategy, decided from its signature and never from a raised exception.

Declaring the parameter and committing the rows are separate: only DurableUnitOfWork writes them, and the other shipped strategies declare it to refuse with their own CapabilityError.

docs.title: runs()
docs.text:
Every run this storage holds events for, sorted by id.

Identities, not Run objects: opening a run validates and replays its whole stream, and detail is already Run.summary()'s job. A listing exists so those queries stay reachable once the ids have scrolled out of a terminal, so it returns exactly what reopening one needs. The order is lexicographic by id and identical across backends; run ids are content-derived, so it is not chronological.

Enumeration is an optional store capability (ports.RunIndex), declared by implementing it. A paired event store that does not is refused explicitly here — never reported as an empty store, which would be a silent capability downgrade.

docs.title: resume(run_id, *, storage, registry)
docs.text:
Complete unfinished work in a validated durable session.

Recorded component identities and the recovery frontier are checked before execution. An already stopped run performs no more work. Replay reads committed facts; resume may execute components for unfinished work. Each mode drives through its own loop, the same branch run makes: a distributed session refuses step().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default run_id RunId

The retained run to continue.

required storage Storage

Writable durable storage containing that run.

required registry Registry

Components needed to reconstruct its declarations.

required

docs.title: open_run(path, *, run_id=None, registry=None)
docs.text:
Open a saved run for inspection within a with block.

Without an ID, select the only run in the store. With several runs, pass run_id=... explicitly; lexical ID order does not establish recency. Context entry validates the selected history before yielding the existing Run type, including incomplete or unsuccessful runs.

Validation and I/O start on context entry. The owned read-only storage closes on normal exit or error. Capture summary() or inspect() inside the block to use a detached result afterward; later queries on the live Run still require open storage. Queries can observe new WAL commits. Reopening never resumes work, migrates a schema, or creates a missing store. SQLite may maintain WAL sidecars without changing committed history.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str | Path

Existing directory originally passed to Storage.durable.

required run_id RunId | str | None

Saved RunId or nonempty ID string without outer whitespace; None selects the only run. A missing explicit ID never falls back.

None registry Registry | None

Optional reconstructed registry of custom artifact codecs. Needed by value-decoding queries, not by entry validation or usage().

None

Returns:

Type Description Iterator[Run]

Context manager yielding a read-only Run backed by owned storage.

Raises:

Storage is missing or inaccessible.

SchemaVersionRejected

docs.text:
Use these methods when implementing or registering a search program; ordinary runs construct the presets above and let the engine bind them. The extension guide owns the protocol laws, and component composition explains adapter wiring.

The namespaced Specialists and TreeSearch presets (meta_evolve.policies.Specialists, meta_evolve.policies.TreeSearch) are documented in the programming model and search guide; neither is a root export.

docs.title: meta_evolve.BestOfN.next_cohort
docs.text:
next_cohort(state)

A generation produced from one committed history.

Composition is either a tuple of trial decisions or a singleton stop, never mixed: a stop is the whole answer, so the sequential decision answering Stop IS the cohort. That also gives the coherence law for free -- at width one this returns exactly next(state), because it is next(state), rather than a second implementation that has to be kept agreeing with it.

Sizing is this policy's job. The record is explicit that the coordinator commits the whole cohort or refuses it entirely, as trial validation refuses rather than trims, so producing more than fits would be producing a batch designed to be rejected. The state to size it is right here: the trial ceiling this program declares, and the run's remaining allowance.

Members differ only in their randomness, which is the whole point -- best-of-n expands the SAME parent independently, so identical seeds would make a generation one trial done N times. No member can reference another's artifact because none of them looks anywhere but the seed; that is why this policy can declare a width and Greedy, which chains, cannot.

docs.title: Compose an improvement loop
docs.text:
Start with a seed, a proposer, and an evaluator. Add a search policy when you need to choose what to try next. This page explains how the components fit; the programming model owns the public contract, the architecture owns semantics, and the generated API owns exact signatures.

A method assembles these components and, where needed, several runs or evaluation stages. The method library shows concrete implementations; the composition guide explains how to reuse their parts. A search preset supplies selection behavior within a method. It does not supply every stage of an algorithm such as AutoData.

The four method questions map to existing public objects: the seed artifact says what changes, the proposer generates revisions, and a Task declares evaluation and objectives. An Experiment combines these with search and authorized experience. The task owns the budget ceiling; run(..., budget=...) may restrict it per dimension. The resulting Run exposes the retained versions and observations.

Component Receives Produces Authority Proposer Selected parent value; optional ProposerContext Candidate or ProposalResult Proposed content only Evaluator Candidate value Scalar, metric mapping, EvaluationResult, or failure Independent measurement Search Retained search state Parent choice, admission, stopping What to try next within bounds Context policy Authorized prior history Pushed ContextBundle What records to show a proposer Experience reader A bounded query from a proposer Audited prior records or source Read access within its grant

docs.title: Replace a proposer or evaluator
docs.text:
The duration-parser example uses two plain functions. An SDK wrapper uses the same boundary: it owns its client and session, then returns candidate content. Return ProposalResult to report provider usage, evidence, or a hypothesis. Return EvaluationResult when measurements need supporting evidence or uncertainty. Failures live in meta_evolve.domain and remain unrankable; they are never converted into zero scores.

For files, PatchProposer applies exact patches and CommandEvaluator runs independent checks. For new domains or advanced search, use the extension contracts and conformance suites. No provider or domain branch is needed in the execution engine.

docs.title: Separate push from pull
docs.text: Experiment(context=AncestorsOnly(...)) selects bounded records before a proposal. Experiment(experience=PullAccess(...)) gives the proposer an audited reader. They can be enabled separately or together; PullAccess is not a context policy. ProposerContext exposes the selected bundle, optional reader, randomness, objectives, step, and any adapter-provided workspace. Source access follows the same bounded read grant.

docs.title: Separate execution from results
docs.text:
Experiment declares the loop. run executes it; Session lets you pace the same execution. A Run reads retained facts. best().value gives the winner; inspect() and usage() also work when measurements failed. Persistent history is useful without resume capability; durable-local reconstruction adds the explicit component declarations needed to continue unfinished work.

A method can return more than one run or a different result object. ACE returns a study containing outer search and other phase results; the separate SealQA Feedback Descent lab returns an in-memory LabResult. The SVG adaptation retains an ordinary Run plus its initial generation record. Read each method's retention description before assuming that one saved Run captures or resumes the whole procedure.

Search selection never approves deployment. Keep evaluator authority, budgets, and final acceptance outside candidate content.

docs.title: Advanced experience provenance
docs.text:
This reference follows the outcome-first experience lesson.

Pushed and pulled observations enter one ordered ledger. Each entry records the run, occurrence kind and ID, logical step, event sequence, operation, result, and exact usage. A proposal's optional derived_from tuple must be an ordered subsequence of references that this proposer actually observed.

Validation rejects a reference that is missing, duplicated contrary to its ledger position, out of scope, from the future, content-inconsistent, or ordered differently from observation. Rejection is typed invalid output and creates no successor artifact.

Committed context selections and pull audits are facts. Replay rebuilds the experience projection and validates derivation without calling the selector, reader, renderer, proposer, or provider. Logical time—not wall-clock completion— decides what was prior.

This strict layer preserves causal claims while leaving everyday proposals free to declare no derivation. Experience remains bounded, explicit, and unable to change evaluation, budgets, permissions, or promotion.

docs.title: SDK accounting and tools
docs.text: For a complete runnable notebook, start with Use your model SDK. This reference covers richer return values, exact billing conversion, and audited tool callbacks. SDK-specific snippets below are patterns to adapt to your own client.

docs.title: Understand the notebook's results
docs.text:
The introductory notebook uses ask_model for both the rewrite and evaluation requests. It returns a ProposalResult carrying either text or a typed failure, plus Resources and EvidenceDraft observations. The evaluator forwards the same usage and evidence into its EvaluationResult. Its fixed expected answers and grading rule stay outside candidate authority.

Observation Notebook behavior Completed, nonempty text The proposer returns a candidate; the evaluator grades returned labels. Wrong labels or label count A valid measurement: incorrect labels fail checks; a wrong count fails all checks. Empty or incomplete response with known usage InvalidOutput, no score, retained tokens and response evidence. A failed rewrite has no successor to evaluate. Request exception, missing/invalid token counts, or unusable response structure ExecutionAccountingUnknown escapes with the original error as its cause; execution stops without invented zero usage or an automatic retry. Tokens known, exact bill absent Tokens remain usable; spend_micros=None propagates as unknown spend. This alone does not make a response fail.

Input plus output tokens enter shared usage; cached input is already included. The notebook retains elapsed request time, response ID, returned model/status, request text, output, and token counts. Evidence records describe one execution, not a guarantee that another request will reproduce it. The official SDK tests use simulated HTTP responses; their scores and token counts are not live results.

max_trials=1 allows at most three requests: seed evaluation, rewrite, then revision evaluation. Each evaluation batches the six tickets into one request. The notebook disables automatic retries. Its output allowance is per request, not a cap on total tokens or money; its timeout is not a hard run deadline. trials(), inspect(), best(), and usage() read recorded history without requests. Rerunning meta.run() performs another experiment.

docs.title: Replace the SDK boundary
docs.text:
Replace the client construction and ask_model on the introductory page. Keep the proposer and evaluator as ordinary callables; there is no first-party provider adapter or generic provider runtime to configure.

The notebook records the SDK version, request settings, and client options in Task.environment, making them part of experiment identity. The API key stays in client construction, outside configuration and evidence. When adapting the example, record behavior-affecting settings without credentials and rerun the declaration after changing them. store=False controls provider response storage; it does not disable the local evidence retained by the wrapper.

Preserve usage and failure reporting when changing clients. Use the three paid-call failure cases below rather than dropping accounting to return plain text. See the Responses API reference for the introductory client's request and response fields.

docs.title: Return a typed result
docs.text:
Use ProposalResult when the wrapper has more to report. This and the my_sdk tool example below are user-supplied SDK pseudocode:

def propose(parent):
    response = my_sdk.generate_structured(input=parent)
    return meta.ProposalResult(
        candidate=response.artifact,
        usage=meta.Resources(
            tokens=response.input_tokens + response.output_tokens,
            # Charged spend is shared usage; estimates stay evidence.
            spend_micros=response.charged_micros,
            wall_seconds=response.elapsed_seconds,
        ),
        metadata={"model": response.model},
        evidence=(
            meta.EvidenceDraft(
                kind="sdk-response",
                data={"estimated_cost": response.estimated_cost, "raw": response.raw},
            ),
        ),
    )

Total tokens, charged monetary spend, and elapsed time enter Resources, then recorded Usage with engine-owned counts. Model identity, estimated cost, granular token categories, and raw provider telemetry belong in evidence or metadata: only a figure the provider actually billed may become spend_micros. When no bill is available, explicitly report spend_micros=None. Keep input and output tokens; cached input and reasoning output are generally subsets, so use the SDK's documented totals without counting those subsets twice. A valid response remains usable. Unknown spend propagates through sums and stops further work under a monetary ceiling, as described in Money.

When a paid call fails, a wrapper has three cases, and the last is the one that is easy to miss:

  1. tokens and other required measures are known — return a typed failure carrying that usage, with unknown billed spend represented by None;
  2. the failure happened before any paid work — return a typed failure with zero usage;
  3. work may have started and required measures such as tokens are unavailable — raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown.

The names come from two submodules:

from meta_evolve.domain import InvalidOutput          # and the other failures
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown

Known spend_micros is an integer, so convert before reporting — a float raises. Round up, so the framework never under-reports a charge, and keep the raw provider figure in evidence as provenance.

Convert through Decimal, not by multiplying the float. Binary floats do not hold decimal amounts exactly, and the error goes the wrong way at exact micro boundaries: 0.000123 * 1_000_000 evaluates to 123.00000000000001, so a math.ceil of that produces 124 micro-USD for an amount that is exactly 123. Over-reporting money is a defect, not a safe direction.

from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, InvalidOperation, localcontext

def charged_micros(cost_usd: object) -> int | None:
    """Exact micro-USD, rounded up, or an explicitly unknown amount."""

    try:
        # str() first: it yields the shortest decimal that round-trips the
        # value, so Decimal("0.000123") -- not the binary approximation.
        amount = cost_usd if isinstance(cost_usd, Decimal) else Decimal(str(cost_usd))
    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError, TypeError):
        return None
    if not amount.is_finite() or amount < 0:
        return None
    with localcontext() as context:
        context.prec = max(28, len(amount.as_tuple().digits) + 6)
        return int((amount * 1_000_000).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING))

For an unreadable amount, retain a cost-reporting failure in evidence and report unknown spend. Missing token accounting still requires the case-3 escape.

Decode the amount exactly, before it becomes a float. The conversion above is only as exact as its input, and str(float) recovers just the digits the float kept — by then 0.0001230000000000000000001 is already 0.000123, and rounding up gives 123 micro-USD instead of 124. A float cannot be repaired after the fact. So read the charge from the raw body:

import json

body = json.loads(response.text, parse_float=Decimal)
micros = charged_micros((body.get("usage") or {}).get("cost"))

If your client hands you a decoded object rather than text, take the amount from somewhere exact — a Decimal, an integer, or a decimal string — rather than a float that has already been rounded.

The duration-parser example supplies an optional cost_reporter(response) callback on its example-owned SDK wrapper. It accepts a function or bound method, so users can calculate a token-price estimate or call their own billing API. Its CostReport explicitly labels estimated versus billed, retains the source, and records the reporter's version in configuration. These are example types; core needs only ordinary ProposalResult/EvaluationResult, Resources, and evidence. A committed report is read back during inspection, without invoking the callback again.

Never raise an ordinary exception after billing, and never return a bare Failure: both paths reach the adapter with no usage field, so the framework records zero and the charge is lost. This is a framework guarantee about those channels, not something conformance can detect on your behalf.

Trial and evaluation counts are coordinator-owned; reporting either at the proposer boundary produces typed InvalidOutput. The meeting-notes evaluator rejects response-wrapper counts as a failed measurement, retaining known usage.

At the proposer boundary, ordinary SDK exceptions become ProposerFailure. Framework failures about durable state, accounting, or run capability escape unchanged: EventStreamConflict, DurableCorruption, InvalidSearchHistory, ExperienceStoreUnavailable, ExecutionAccountingUnknown, and CapabilityError.

docs.title: Give an SDK audited pull tools
docs.text:
When an SDK supports custom tools, register a user-owned handler that delegates to context.experience:

used = []

def search_experience(arguments):
    if context.experience is None:
        raise meta.ExperienceAccessDenied("pull access was not granted")
    observation = context.experience.search(**arguments)
    used.extend(record.ref for record in observation.records)
    return observation

response = my_sdk.run(tools={"search_experience": search_experience})
return meta.ProposalResult(
    candidate=response.artifact,
    derived_from=tuple(dict.fromkeys(used)),
)

The exact observation API is defined by ExperienceReader. The callback may run in process, or a user-owned RPC service may forward each request to this scoped handler and return its result. The RPC service must not cache or broaden the reader capability. Meta-Evolve adds no generic tool server or agent process.

Access denial, exhaustion, audit-store failure, and unknown accounting retain their normal semantics because the SDK tool calls the authoritative reader. SDKs without custom-tool support can receive pushed context.bundle data, but that is context injection rather than agent-directed pull.

The credential-free 06_user_owned_sdk example contains a complete deterministic fake SDK and audited tool callback. An acceptance-gated milestone may own an opt-in real-client experiment, as M8 does for harness validation. There is no generic provider smoke directory: a live script must serve a current gate, add no package dependency, and retain its single authorized outcome honestly.

docs.title: Authority and reproducibility
docs.text:
The wrapper may propose candidate content. It cannot choose the evaluator, change the run budget, grant itself experience, edit audit history, or promote a result. External evaluation and durable storage remain the sources of score, accounting, and lineage truth.

Committed requests, evidence, usage, failures, and artifacts support inspection and replay. Meta-Evolve does not claim that a later external SDK call will regenerate byte-identical output.

API details: ProposalResult, ProposerContext, and EvidenceDraft.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Apply, compose, and evolve methods for optimization, research, and scientific discovery. Start from your problem: what can change, what observations can guide it, and how will you evaluate the result? The same programming model supports artifact improvement and experiments that evaluate an improvement procedure.

Use a method · Compose a method · Evolve a method

docs.title: Compose and evolve methods
docs.text:
For a worked progression, start with the duration parser: source changes under a fixed method. Next, policy evolution moves search settings into the candidate and traces their inner outcomes. Then AutoResearch evaluates research recipes across task splits, with a different retention and final-check boundary.

Use the component worksheet to identify proposal logic, search or stage scheduling, evaluation, and experience. The method comparison shows how existing implementations assemble those pieces. Reuse components where their interfaces and semantics fit; method-specific stages remain explicit code.

To improve the procedure itself, follow AutoResearch or policy evolution. The candidate becomes a recipe or policy, and its evaluator measures bounded inner experiments. Search presets are reusable building blocks; selecting one does not implement an entire research method.

docs.title: Scientific discovery

Scientific applications can define candidates such as models, hypotheses, simulation programs, or experiment procedures, then supply their own observations and evaluation. Custom artifact domains let the representation carry the validation rules the application needs. The domain and scientific method remain the author's responsibility.

The dedicated methods mapped here are Design—not shipped: Model Discovery Agent studies which experiment separates candidate mechanisms; AI co-scientist studies hypothesis generation and comparison; AI Scientist studies research workflows; FunSearch and AlphaEvolve study executable search for mathematical and algorithmic discoveries. Their pages identify the method-specific work still required. See the scientific direction for broader scope.

docs.title: ACE: improve an itemized playbook
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Evidence: deterministic mechanism demonstration; no live model gains or cross-task transfer claim.

docs.title: The concrete problem
docs.text:
An agent tags a company's financial disclosures. The note says “cash paid for interest,” but the company requires nwi:InterestPaidNetOfCapitalized rather than the generic taxonomy element. The starting playbook contains the wrong interest convention and no lease convention. Improving the context should change the answer while the company's grading rules remain fixed.

For a smaller notebook introduction, start with Improve a support agent's playbook: six support tickets, three named rules, and one revision per recorded mistake.

docs.title: Component worksheet
docs.text:
Question This implementation What changes? A Text JSON playbook with stable item identities, content, section, and status What generates the change? ace_curation.revise(lessons) corrects an entry, then adds a missing convention, using published development lessons What judges it? playbook_suite(agent) independently grades private task answers; Greedy(max_trials=2) maximizes solved and stops at 1.0 What is retained? Outer search records, selected playbook, failures, and usage; in-memory study results hold the other phases and their inner captures

Split membership, the agent declaration, inner budgets, and the neutral-only consolidation rule remain fixed. Private answers do not enter the curator's development lessons. Saving the outer search does not persist or resume the whole study; study.usage accounts for all phases, while study.run is search only.

docs.title: What the paper does
docs.text:
ACE, §3 separates a Generator's task trajectories, a Reflector's lessons, and a Curator's context updates. It edits individual identified bullets rather than rewriting the whole context. Incremental deltas and a grow-and-refine process maintain useful context while controlling redundancy. The paper supports repeated and online adaptation.

Here the agent is a deterministic fixture. Python extracts authored lessons, curates entries, and performs one consolidation after search. This preserves an itemized-update demonstration, not the paper's learned reflection, semantic retrieval/deduplication, helpful/harmful counters, or online adaptation algorithm.

docs.title: Follow the two levels
docs.text:
OUTER: seed playbook → curate/add → private score → select
                          ↑              │
                development lessons      │
                                         ↓
INNER: playbook + fixed agent + input → task answer
                                            ↓
                                     independent check

After selection: consolidation check → held-out evaluation

Outer work allows three evaluations and two revisions. Each inner rollout allows two evaluations, one revision, and 120 seconds. At most fourteen fixture agent calls cover development, private search, matched consolidation, and held-out work.

docs.title: The actual experiment
docs.text:
The declaration below is extracted from the maintained search function. Its proposer already closes over the allowed development lessons; the evaluator owns the private split. Storage is an execution choice, not candidate authority.

ace_search.py · search · experiment (excerpt)
experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(
        evaluator=playbook_suite(agent),
        artifact=meta.Text,
        objectives=(meta.Maximize("solved", satisfy=1.0),),
        budget=PLAYBOOK_BUDGET,
    ),
    seed=encode(SEED_PLAYBOOK),
    proposer=proposer,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=PLAYBOOK_TRIALS),
    random_seed=random_seed,
)
Mechanism User-owned implementation What it supplies Representation playbook.py, playbook_codec.encode Item identity and transition validation over Text Reflection and revision ace_curation.py, revise Deterministic edits from published lessons Execution and grading ace_episodes.py, playbook_suite Bounded inner rollouts and independent checks Stage ordering ace_study.py, study_playbook Development, search, consolidation, held-out order Consolidation ace_consolidation.py Prune retired entries only on neutral matched evidence

docs.title: The revision mechanism
docs.text:
The curator returns a proposer that changes one identified entry at a time. Its input is the published development lessons, so private answers cannot be added by a context policy behind the reader's back. The actual edit logic is:

ace_curation.py · curate
def curate(playbook: Playbook, lessons: Sequence[Lesson]) -> Playbook | None:
    """Amend items a lesson can rescue; retire the ones nothing supports.

    Returns ``None`` when every active item is already aligned, which is the
    signal to generate instead. Retired items are left in place rather than
    dropped: pruning them is consolidation's job, and consolidation acceptance
    belongs to the evaluator.
    """

    pending = list(uncovered(playbook, lessons))
    revised: list[PlaybookItem] = []
    changed = False
    for item in playbook.items:
        if item.status != "active" or aligned_with(item, lessons) is not None:
            revised.append(item)
            continue
        rescue = next(
            (lesson for lesson in pending if lesson.section == item.section), None
        )
        if rescue is not None:
            pending.remove(rescue)
            revised.append(item.amended(rescue.content))
        else:
            # Nothing published supports this entry, so stop telling the agent
            # it. Retiring keeps the record readable; deleting would not.
            revised.append(item.retired())
        changed = True
    return Playbook(tuple(revised)) if changed else None

If curation finds no change, generate adds the first uncovered lesson:

ace_curation.py · generate
def generate(playbook: Playbook, lessons: Sequence[Lesson]) -> Playbook | None:
    """Append an item for the first lesson the playbook does not state yet."""

    pending = uncovered(playbook, lessons)
    if not pending:
        return None
    lesson = pending[0]
    item = PlaybookItem(
        identity=lesson.identity, section=lesson.section, content=lesson.content
    )
    return Playbook(playbook.items + (item,))

The independent playbook_suite executes each candidate with a fixed agent and checks its answers against evaluator-owned company conventions. study_playbook collects development lessons before search, tests neutral consolidation after selection, and then checks the held-out split. The complete download includes each stage.

docs.title: Setup and run
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12+ on macOS or Linux. Download the source package and complete context example into a new directory. The ZIP retains the example's directory structure and all sibling modules.

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./meta-evolve.zip
python -m zipfile -e context-example.zip .
python examples/research/context_evolution/main.py --sibling ace
# Output excerpt (other study phases are also printed):
# trial scores: ['0.0', '0.5', '1.0']
# solved: 1.0

From a checkout, use uv sync --locked and uv run python examples/research/context_evolution/main.py --sibling ace. No model credentials or provider requests are involved in this fixture.

Verified fixture excerpt
trial scores: ['0.0', '0.5', '1.0']
solved: 1.0

The first edit corrects interest tagging; the second adds the lease rule. The retired scale entry remains in history until consolidation removes it. The fixture's final held-out solved fraction is 1.0, demonstrating the split boundary on these authored cases. An incomplete split is unrankable, never an average of only its successful rollouts.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text: Disable the lease lesson in a scratch copy of the development fixture. Predict which private task cannot improve and inspect the proposed entries. Restoring that lesson should restore the two-step progression. Changing the agent requires an explicit InnerAgent model, revision, and non-secret configuration.

docs.title: Evidence and limitations
docs.text:
Context tests verify the transcript; companion tests cover split isolation, transition failures, identity, and replay. The notebook is an existing supplement. #194 owns the implemented example; #192 owns later research scope. Nothing here reopens its completed migration.

Durable replay covers outer search. Development, consolidation, and held-out outcomes remain in-memory study results; saved search does not make them resumable.

docs.title: Research question
docs.text:
Can a meta-agent invent agent designs by programming new arrangements of model calls?

The primary source motivates this question. The worksheet below is a proposed Meta-Evolve translation, not a runnable implementation or a claim that the library implements the complete upstream algorithm.

docs.title: Component mapping

docs.title: Improve a scheduler
docs.text:
Jobs of different sizes arrive at a group of workers. Where should each job go? Our starting program takes turns: worker 0, worker 1, and so on. That is cheap, but when large jobs arrive at regular intervals, the same workers get overloaded.

Try a small change: look at two workers and choose the less busy one. Here is the proposed function. load() asks for a worker's current load; each request counts as one probe:

def choose(cluster, size):
    first = cluster.pick()
    second = cluster.pick()
    if second == first:
        second = (first + 1) % cluster.size
    return first if cluster.load(first) <= cluster.load(second) else second

The fixed simulator actually runs this Python code. Its development workloads produce this comparison:

Program Load imbalance ↓ Probes per job ↓ Quality ↑ Starting round-robin 0.2071 0 0.7929 Inspect every worker 0.0381 7 0.8219 Inspect two workers 0.0464 2 0.9136

Two probes buy much better balance than the starting program. Inspecting every worker balances jobs a little better, but takes seven probes per job here. The two-worker program offers the better tradeoff under the fixed score: quality = max(0, 1 - imbalance - 0.02 * probes_per_job). Imbalance is zero for an even distribution and one when a single worker gets everything. These measurements describe this simulator, not hardware speed.

The proposer tries handwritten revisions, including mistakes. The measured scores come from running those programs, not a lookup table or a live model.

docs.title: 3. Check this runtime
docs.text:
This probe starts a confined Python process and checks that it cannot read the downloaded workload file. It is setup, outside the study's measured work. If it fails, the following cells leave the study stopped and explain the remedy.

import subprocess
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

runtime_ready = False
protected = study_root / "examples/research/systems_optimization/workloads.py"
probe = """import errno, pathlib, sys
try:
    pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_bytes()
except PermissionError as error:
    if error.errno not in (errno.EACCES, errno.EPERM):
        raise
    print('protected')
else:
    raise SystemExit('Workloads were readable: confinement did not hold.')
"""
try:
    protected.read_bytes()
    if not Path(command.__file__).resolve().is_relative_to(study_root):
        raise RuntimeError("An older example is imported; restart the kernel.")
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="scheduler-check-") as workspace:
        checked = subprocess.run(
            [*confinement.launcher(Path(workspace)), sys.executable,
             "-I", "-B", "-c", probe, str(protected)],
            cwd=workspace, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
        )
    if checked.returncode or checked.stdout.strip() != "protected":
        raise RuntimeError((checked.stderr or checked.stdout).strip() or "Probe failed.")
    runtime_ready = True
    print(f"Ready: Python {sys.version.split()[0]}, {confinement.mechanism()} enforced.")
except (OSError, RuntimeError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as error:
    print(f"Study stopped: {error}")
    print("Use local Jupyter on macOS or Linux with the confinement listed above.")
    print("Keep the notebook outside system/temp folders and the Python installation.")

docs.title: 4. Run and compare
docs.text:
The study tests the starting program and eight revisions, then selects a program on a separate workload and checks it once more on a final workload. This cell shows the development comparison from its recorded measurements.

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

def show_measurements(attempt, label):
    if attempt is None:
        print(f"{label}: no measured candidate")
        return
    if not attempt.rankable:
        print(f"{label}: {attempt.failure_kind}/{attempt.outcome}")
        return
    metrics = attempt.metrics
    print(f"{label:24} {metrics['imbalance']:9.4f}"
          f" {metrics['work']:7.1f} {metrics['quality']:9.4f}")

result = None
selected_source = None
if runtime_ready:
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="scheduler-run-") as output:
        result = command.run_example(Path(output))
        chosen = result.decision.selection.chosen
        if chosen is not None:
            trial = next(item for item in result.search.trials()
                         if item.logical_step == chosen.logical_step)
            selected_source = trial.artifact.value["scheduler.py"]
    development = {item.candidate: item for item in result.decision.development}
    print("Development workload       Imbalance  Probes   Quality")
    for name, label in (
        ("round-robin (seed)", "Starting round-robin"),
        ("least-loaded-scan", "Inspect every worker"),
        ("power-of-two-choices", "Inspect two workers"),
    ):
        show_measurements(development.get(name), label)
else:
    print("Study not started. Resolve the runtime check above first.")

Rerunning this cell starts a fresh study. Its temporary store is cleaned up even if execution raises; the comparison and selected source remain inspectable below.

docs.title: Check the selected program
docs.text:
Development feedback helps propose changes. Selection tests eligible programs on a different, published workload after proposing ends. Final checking tests only the starting and selected programs after selection. Keeping those phases separate prevents treating a development score as a result on new jobs.

if result is not None:
    decision = result.decision
    print("Selected on the selection workload:", decision.selection.winner)
    comparison = decision.comparison
    if comparison is None:
        print("No program was selected; no final comparison was made.")
    else:
        print("Final workload             Imbalance  Probes   Quality")
        show_measurements(comparison.baseline, "Starting round-robin")
        show_measurements(comparison.selected, "Selected program")
        print("Final verdict:", comparison.verdict)
    if selected_source is not None:
        print("\nSelected scheduler.py:\n" + selected_source)
else:
    print("Run the study after the runtime check passes.")

The selected program is power-of-two-choices. On the final workload, imbalance falls from 0.2088 to 0.0794, using two probes instead of zero; quality rises from 0.7912 to 0.8806. These results do not establish production gains. The source above is the actual selected artifact. Selection does not deploy it.

docs.title: Change one line
docs.text:
What if the comparison used >= instead of <=, choosing the busier worker? Change the selected source and run it through the same fixed development evaluator. This optional check runs separately from the recorded study above.

from examples.research.systems_optimization import execution, surface

if selected_source is not None and "<=" in selected_source:
    edited_source = selected_source.replace("<=", ">=")
    measured = execution.evaluate(surface.with_scheduler(edited_source), "development")
    if measured.failure is not None:
        print("Edit rejected:", measured.failure.kind, measured.failure.message)
    else:
        print("Edited program on the development workload:")
        for metric in ("imbalance", "work", "quality"):
            print(f"{metric}: {measured.metrics[metric]:.4f}")
else:
    print("This exercise needs a selected program with the <= comparison.")

Both comparisons use two probes. Reversing the comparison lowers quality from 0.9136 to 0.7731. Change the replacement back to "<=" and rerun this cell: quality returns to 0.9136. You can also set edited_source = "not valid Python!" to see a typed rejection. Keep the evaluator fixed as you change the program.

docs.title: Research question and source
docs.text:
Agentic Harness Engineering attacks the same loop from the observability side, through three matched pillars: component observability gives every editable harness component a file-level representation so the action space is explicit and revertible; experience observability distills raw trajectories into a layered, drill-down evidence corpus an evolving agent can actually consume; and decision observability pairs every edit with a self-declared prediction, verified in the next round against task-level outcomes. Ten iterations lift pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2 from 69.7% to 77.0%, and its ablations localize the gain to tools, middleware, and long-term memory rather than the system prompt — which the authors read as factual harness structure transferring where prose-level strategy does not.

examples/research/harness_evolution translates the third pillar. Every proposal returns a closed manifest: the authorized observations it cites, one declared surface and its value, the development behavior the edit predicts will improve, and the regressions it puts at risk. The paper's manifest also carries an inferred root cause, and its loop intersects each prediction with the next round's task-level deltas to produce a per-edit verdict and roll back the edits that fail. This example does neither; a prediction here is recorded and auditable, not yet adjudicated.

Three properties are Meta-Evolve's stricter translation, not the paper's requirements: citations resolve only against an ordered ledger of observations the trusted adapter itself authorized, so a model-written identifier is never a derivation; exactly one surface may change per proposal; and a manifest that cannot state all five fields is a typed unrankable refusal rather than a low score.

This does not reproduce AHE's system, benchmarks, transfer results, or reported gains. It runs a model-free fixture over two repair episodes, evolves two declared surfaces rather than a file tree, and claims no cross-model, cross-benchmark, or cross-family transfer.

docs.title: Complete supporting source
docs.text:
accounting_evidence.py 
"""Recomputing a phase's spend from the evidence its trials committed.

Every total here is derived from committed records rather than counted at the
call site, and that is the point rather than an implementation detail: a total
the producer reported about itself cannot detect the producer having
under-reported. Separated from :mod:`phase_accounting`, which assembles those
totals into one value and states the laws they have to satisfy -- deriving a
number and judging it are different jobs, and the judging half is what a
promotion decision is read against.

Nothing here reads a file, opens a store, or knows what a phase is. Each
function takes finished runs and walks the evidence they already hold.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import Evidence, ExperienceObservation

import call_usage
import source_schema


CALL_EVIDENCE_KIND = "sdk-structured-output"
CAPTURE_EVIDENCE_KIND = "episode-capture"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class _Calls:
    count: int = 0
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0
    total_tokens: int = 0
    remainder: int = 0
    spend_micros: int = 0


def calls(runs: tuple[meta.Run, ...]) -> _Calls:
    """Every retained provider call, validated through :mod:`call_usage`.

    A retained call whose payload does not satisfy the one validation rule
    raises rather than being skipped: an unaccountable call is worse than a
    counted one, and this phase total is the number a promotion decision is
    read against.
    """

    count = 0
    totals = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    for run in runs:
        for trial in run.trials():
            for item in trial.evidence:
                if item.kind != CALL_EVIDENCE_KIND:
                    continue
                payload = item.data.get("call")
                if payload is None:
                    continue
                usage = call_usage.from_payload(dict(payload))
                count += 1
                totals[0] += usage.input_tokens
                totals[1] += usage.output_tokens
                totals[2] += usage.total_tokens
                totals[3] += usage.remainder
                totals[4] += usage.spend_micros
    return _Calls(count, *totals)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class _Episodes:
    episodes: int = 0
    attempts: int = 0
    evaluations: int = 0
    trials: int = 0


def episodes(runs: tuple[meta.Run, ...]) -> _Episodes:
    """Inner episode work, counted from the capture each evaluation published."""

    episodes = attempts = evaluations = trials = 0
    for run in runs:
        for trial in run.trials():
            for item in trial.evidence:
                if item.kind != CAPTURE_EVIDENCE_KIND:
                    continue
                for episode in item.data["episodes"]:
                    episodes += 1
                    attempts += len(episode["attempts"])
                    counts = episode["inner_counts"]
                    evaluations += counts["evaluations"]
                    trials += counts["trials"]
    return _Episodes(episodes, attempts, evaluations, trials)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class _Source:
    indexes: int = 0
    files: int = 0
    errors: int = 0
    total_bytes: int = 0


def source(runs: tuple[meta.Run, ...]) -> _Source:
    """Source records returned by successful opens, including repeated reads.

    The public Run view exposes aggregate pull usage, not individual opens.
    This example-local accounting edge reads the kernel's validated projection
    for those committed observations; it never queries a live reader. A
    truncated rendering still returned its structured records and spent bytes.
    Denied/exhausted opens and source publication alone contribute nothing.
    """

    indexes = files = errors = total = 0
    for run in runs:
        projection = run._projection()
        requests = {item.operation_id: item.request for item in projection.experience_attempts}
        for opened in projection.experience_successes:
            if requests[opened.operation_id].operation != "open":
                continue
            if not isinstance(opened.result, ExperienceObservation):
                raise ValueError("a successful open must return an observation")
            for record in opened.result.records:
                item = record.value
                if not isinstance(item, Evidence):
                    continue
                if item.kind == source_schema.INDEX_SCHEMA:
                    indexes += 1
                elif item.kind == source_schema.ERROR_SCHEMA:
                    errors += 1
                elif item.kind == source_schema.FILE_SCHEMA:
                    files += 1
                    total += int(item.data["bytes"])
    return _Source(indexes, files, errors, total)


def citations(runs: tuple[meta.Run, ...]) -> int:
    return sum(len(trial.derived_from) for run in runs for trial in run.trials())


__all__ = [
    "CALL_EVIDENCE_KIND",
    "CAPTURE_EVIDENCE_KIND",
    "calls",
    "citations",
    "episodes",
    "source",
]
call_usage.py 
"""Validated call-usage evidence: input/output/total tokens and spend for one
actual provider call.

The one rule this validates, stated once so both the fixture and a future
live retention path apply it the same way: a provider-reported total larger
than the input/output pair is accepted, and the remainder is named — a
correct reasoning-model response may report more total tokens than
input+output accounts for (reasoning tokens the provider bills but does not
itemize), and refusing that as malformed transport would refuse a good
response for a shape this validator, not the model, failed to anticipate. A
total *smaller* than input+output is refused: that is not a remainder, it is
an inconsistent report, and this validator runs before manifest decoding, so
letting it through would have a transport defect read as a bad model answer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass


_FIELDS = ("input_tokens", "output_tokens", "total_tokens", "spend_micros")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CallUsage:
    """One actual call's exact accounting. Never a hand-maintained total."""

    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    total_tokens: int
    spend_micros: int

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        for name in _FIELDS:
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"call usage {name} must be a non-negative integer, got {value!r}"
                )
        if self.input_tokens + self.output_tokens > self.total_tokens:
            raise ValueError(
                "call usage input+output "
                f"({self.input_tokens + self.output_tokens}) exceeds the "
                f"reported total ({self.total_tokens}); a provider-reported "
                "total may be larger than input+output but never smaller"
            )

    @property
    def remainder(self) -> int:
        """Tokens the total reports beyond input+output — e.g. reasoning tokens."""

        return self.total_tokens - self.input_tokens - self.output_tokens


def derive(
    *,
    input_tokens: int,
    output_tokens: int,
    total_tokens: int | None,
    spend_micros: int = 0,
) -> CallUsage:
    """Build a :class:`CallUsage`, deriving ``total`` when the provider
    reported none at all — distinct from a provider that reported a total
    and it happened to equal input+output; both are valid, and this is the
    one place either is turned into the same committed shape."""

    resolved_total = (
        input_tokens + output_tokens if total_tokens is None else total_tokens
    )
    return CallUsage(
        input_tokens=input_tokens,
        output_tokens=output_tokens,
        total_tokens=resolved_total,
        spend_micros=spend_micros,
    )


def to_payload(usage: CallUsage) -> dict[str, int]:
    return {
        "input_tokens": usage.input_tokens,
        "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens,
        "total_tokens": usage.total_tokens,
        "spend_micros": usage.spend_micros,
    }


def from_payload(payload: dict[str, object]) -> CallUsage:
    """The strict inverse of :func:`to_payload`: every field required and
    typed, never derived here — derivation is :func:`derive`'s job, for a
    live call that has not yet been normalized into a committed payload."""

    missing = [name for name in _FIELDS if name not in payload]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"call usage payload is missing fields: {missing}")
    return CallUsage(**{name: payload[name] for name in _FIELDS})
